title: BOOKING DATE ERROR WITHOUT ANY RESOLUTION
text: I booked a tour using the trip advisor app on my cell phone. I intended to schedule the tour for Tuesday, May 20th, in CORFU, Greece,  to align with my travel plans. However, due to what appears to be an error, possibly stemming from the app’s known occasional glitches, the booking was made for Tuesday, May 13th, which was exactly one week before I would be in Corfu, Greece.I was in Santorini, Greece on May 13th and was surprised when the tour operator contacted me that day to confirm my attendance for the tour in CORFU GREECE.This tour was not inexpensive ($159.16 USD).  I have consistently relied on TripAdvisor/Viator for travel experiences around the world. Upon realizing the date discrepancy, I immediately contacted your support team on May 13th to clarify the situation. I was advised to reach out to the tour operator directly. Unfortunately, they were unable to assist or offer a rescheduled tour for the correct date, leaving me without a tour and no clear path to a resolution.While I understand policies and limitations exist, I am disappointed by the lack of support in this case. Given my history as a repeat customer, I had expected that TripAdvisor/Viator would take greater initiative to assist in rebooking or offer a suitable alternative—particularly when it was clear I had not used the service on the incorrect date and made every effort to resolve the issue promptly.I respectfully request reconsideration of my case, whether in the form of a refund, credit, or rescheduling a comparable tour. It would go a long way in maintaining my trust in your platform and ensuring future bookings.People make mistakes, we are humans, not machines. I would think a company like Viator would make more of an effort to satisfy their customers. But after a number of emails and messages back and forth, they offered me a 5% discount which is unacceptable.

As I had already entered the museum, I attempted to use the tickets, only to find they were invalid for that time. I was forced to wait another hour, causing me to miss yet another planned activity.This entire experience was extremely frustrating. I wasted time, money, and nerves — and what’s most disappointing is that I could have easily purchased regular tickets at the museum for a lower price, without all this stress.The provider never informed me of the time change, nor offered any form of compensation or refund. text: I have used Viator many times and always been satisfied with the tour. We are in Egypt and booked a dessert safari with stargazing. We started off ok picked up on time in a vehicle which was a Lancruiser absolutely disgusting inside the back seated 8 people no working seat belts temperature 32 no air conditioning with the front passenger and driver and guide we were 11 in total. We drove about 15 minutes at reckless speeds up to 100 with the driver talking on his mobile phone sometimes no hands on the steering wheel veering from lane to lane. I told him off and I told the guide this driving was dangerous but they both ignored us. We then stopped at a scruffy area near a garage which was a meeting point for other vehicles to join the convoy. It was boiling hot in the vehicle we were told by the guide just 5 minutes waited 30 minutes for two people to arrive who they had forgotten to pick up. Then onwards in the same reckless driving way to a check point to enter the dessert. Again a shambles waiting 15 minutes for the control point to allow them to proceed. Then the journey to the Bedouin camp over rough terrain driving for about 45 minutes like a lunatic we were shaken around it was like being in a boiling hot Tin can. Arrived at the camp met Arabe the guide who was excellent. Lots of waiting around the entertainment amounted to about 5 minutes if guys singing and hand clapping the stargazing was really excellent everything else about the trip was absolutely awful. Then back in the jeep and a frightening drive to Hurghada during the journey they driver was on the mobile and then decided to show photos of his 17 month son to the passengers not looking at the road driving at reckless speeds and accident could have killed or severely injured everyone in the vehicle we were terrified. I told the guide but he did nothing. Second drop of was at the Citadel Hotel where the guide went into the hotel with two ladies from Macao to collect money for photographs they had purchased. We waited and waited eventually I told the driver to find the guide we had waited enough this was after 20 minutes of sitting in the hotel vehicle again.  The guide returned and started an argument with me that we had not been at the hotel pick up on time.  Our time was 4pm we were outside from 3.45pm and got into the vehicle as soon as it arrived.  He then calmed down and I told him again about the driver and the state of the vehicle he agreed.  So here is my warning be careful Viator use third parties for the trips they need to check that they are safe to transport people even in Egypt. We could have all been killed

title: INTEGRATE THE TWO COMPANIES MORE FULLY!I think it very unfortunate that Viator…
text: I think it very unfortunate that Viator and TripAdvisor are not, as yet at least, fully integrated. The former is supposedly owned by the latter and is its tour-booking branch. And yet I find tours, sometimes the same tour, booked by both “companies,” but, even more confusing, is the fact that the one might offer a given tour, and the other, not. The result is that if going, for example, on an overseas adventure, or a cruise, it’s not possible to collect all the adventures onto the same app, but instead one must sometimes book first with one app, then, perhaps for the next day of the tour, the other. This is very different from booking other things, hotels for example, with a company like Booking.com, which permits a person to book successive nights in successive hotels all on one app, with one single payee, rather than having to keep track between two apps provided by two companies that are supposedly the same company. Some efficiency expert should integrate the companies more satisfactorily for their customers.

The tour started with delicious pastries and ended with a chance to savour possibly the best grilled fish on earth at yet another beautiful location -  a restaurant he recommended by the beach. Knowing we were on the hunt for authentic handmade ceramic souvenirs, he also took us to his friend’s atelier where we found the loveliest pieces. He also recommended some restaurants and bars for us to check out in our neighbourhood- wanting us to make the most of our trip! title: Viator manipulated my review.
text: Viator manipulated my review on their website by deleting the pictures I uploaded. We booked a "5-star" cruise based on the description and images provided on Viator. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a scam. We were placed on a barely 1-star, outdated cruise that bore no resemblance to Viator’s description or the images advertised. Despite raising complaints to both the tour staff and the travel company at check-in, they refused to accommodate us on the originally booked cruise. We were told the images were just for show—meaning they were fake advertising. It appears they overbook and simply place people on whatever cruise is available to make more money. Our original booking was canceled two days prior, and we requested to reschedule for the following day—regretfully, as it was a terrible decision. When onboard, we were asked to sign a handwritten document stating we were satisfied with the cruise, “as per their policy.” When we refused, we were threatened and intimidated by the tour staff and the cruise owner, who said we would be kicked out at 10:30 PM if we didn’t sign. We felt forced to sign because we had already checked out of our hotel and couldn’t easily find an alternative, especially in an unfamiliar country. Viator was contacted, and the only option offered was to cancel the cruise. If you still choose to book this cruise, I strongly advise you to verify real images of the vessel beforehand—otherwise, you will be beyond disappointed. This has been my worst tour experience through Viator—if there was a negative 5 rating, I would select it. After the review was posted, Viator manipulated my review on their website by deleting the pictures I uploaded.

title: Boos Cruise
text: Booze Cruise Excursion – Honest Review (1/5)I recently went on a booze cruise excursion outside of the resort that I found through a link on TikTok. I’ll admit, I was a bit skeptical at first—and honestly, I wish I had trusted that instinct.My honest rating: 1 out of 5.While I tried to make the best of it (since I already paid $69), it just wasn’t what I expected.Here’s a breakdown:•	The Experience:The cruise lasted about three hours. First, we stopped for some snorkeling, then headed to an open water area where multiple boats were partying and mingling. It’s a fun spot to meet people and vibe. However, when we got there, it was cloudy, and heavy rain hit on the way back, which killed the mood a bit.•	Food:The included food was terrible—just fruit and chips with queso. They ran out quickly, and I think that’s unacceptable, especially on a drinking cruise. You could order food from a floating stand via a crew member walking around with a menu, but again, if I’m paying $69, I expect a decent snack included—not gourmet, but more than nachos.•	Drinks:The drink selection was mid at best. Only basic punch options like piña colada and rum punch. No variety and definitely not strong—I didn’t even catch a buzz. Bring your own bottle if you go. That probably would’ve made a big difference.•	Music:The music was played from a crew member’s phone, which felt super low-effort. The playlist was okay, but I had to request a few songs to get the vibe going for the group.Final Thoughts:I had a few fun moments, but overall, I wouldn’t recommend this booze cruise—at least not the one I went on. Better drinks, food, and music would’ve made a huge difference. Again, this is solely my opinion, and your experience might be different. But for me, it just didn’t deliver, especially for the price.

title: Disorganized, Misleading, and Not Worth the Pricev
text: I booked a Paris day trip from London through Viator, and unfortunately, the experience fell far below expectations. From the very beginning, there was confusion. The meeting instructions were vague—we were told to wait for someone from the company near a café, and while several of us were gathered, the representative arrived late. By then, I already had everything I needed and could have gone directly to the train myself. There was no “VIP access” to the train as advertised—we waited in line like everyone else. The guide simply handed out tickets and gave basic instructions.My package included lunch at the Eiffel Tower, but when we arrived in Paris, we met a different guide—also late—holding a sign that didn’t match the name of the company I booked through. That guide did not accompany us to any of the attractions and provided little assistance. At Notre Dame, we couldn’t even enter because we didn’t have skip-the-line access. The line was extremely long, so we skipped it and spent the time shopping until the next meeting time.At the Eiffel Tower, we were told the elevator line was over two hours long and were encouraged to take the stairs—nearly 400 steps. It was exhausting and definitely not what I expected or paid for.Our final stop was the Louvre. The guide, who initially said she would not accompany us, ended up following us to the ticket entrance—only to discover our tickets didn’t work. She argued with the staff, then left for 15–20 minutes. When she returned, the new tickets still didn’t work. After another long delay, she finally got valid ones. At that point, we only had time to rush in, see the Mona Lisa, and leave.This experience was incredibly frustrating and not worth the $500+ price tag. I will not be booking with Viator again, and I strongly discourage others from choosing this tour if they’re looking for a smooth, premium experience. What was advertised as a VIP, guided tour ended up being little more than a disorganized, self-led day with poor coordination and minimal support.

title: Missing on attraction due to last minute Viator cancellation
text: We purchased tickets to Alhambra and Generalife in Granada for April 21st, 2025 through Viator. On April 18th, which was the day of our departure to Spain, we got an email notifying us that the tour was cancelled. We immediately looked for other options to obtain tickets and all we could find for our dates were tickets at 400 CAD per person, while on the Alhambra official site the earliest date tickets were available for was May 11th (way beyond the dates of our stay in Spain). We called Viator to inquire if they can arrange a new booking for us and were advised that the cancellation was due to the tour operator closing its business, which Viator had no control over. What transpired in the conversation with the Viator representative was that the tour operator was no longer in business as of February 17th, yet they didn't notify us until 2 months later and 3 days before our scheduled tour. We knew that this attraction was in high demand hence booked our tour on February 2nd. The representative appeared to be helpful, spoke with a manager and offered to book us with a different tour operator, at a higher price, however no additional cost to us, which we gladly accepted as our stay in Granada was scheduled for only 2 days and visiting Alhambra was high on our 'things to do' list. Long story short, on April 20th we received another email indicating that the tour was not confirmed and we never got to see Alhambra.The lesson we learned is that if you are booking a tour/excursion that involves admission tickets to an attraction, you are better off purchasing from the official place rather than going through a third party like Viator. While we are not faulting them for what happened with the tour operator they were working with, we would have expected to be notified as soon as they became aware, not last minute and giving us no chance to re-book. Very disappointing and will never book with them again.

name: Linda S
title: The Best Way to Experience the Canal
text: Panama Canal Partial Tour - Southbound Direction with Panama Marine Adventures6 hours (approx.) From Gamboa to Flamenco Marina in Panama CityWe are so glad we traveled the canal with this team! The experience was excellent. The tour guide was multi-lingual and spoke both Spanish & clear English during the entire tour. We were comfortably bused from the Flamenco Marina in Panama City to our ship the Pacific Queen in  Gamboa and from there headed down the canal southbound. The tour guide narrated during much of the trip while we took in the breathtaking rainforests on either side of the canal. He was approachable with questions and very knowledgable. The boat has three decks (two air conditioned and the top is open air with half covered and half open to the sky). The top deck has 360 degree views and plenty of seating. Despite about 120 guests on the boat we were all comfortable and had plenty of room to move around. The boat traveled through the Gailard cut & three total locks. One at the Pedro Miguel Lock and two at the Moraflores Locks. We previously visited Moraflores Locks to enjoy the visitor's center but nothing compared to riding through the locks as the water drained and the gates opened. Seeing the canal in operation from this perspective is completely unique and worth the time! I highly recommend if you come to Panama you need to experience the canal with this crew!Beyond the experience itself, water and soft drinks were provided complimentary whenever requested during the voyage and the complimentary meal was authentic Panamanian, but both tasty and simple enough to work for most appetites. We also had cellular service during the entire voyage allowing us to video call friends and family to share the experience with them.

title: Hidden costs
text: On May 6, 2025, I purchased two airline tickets through the JustFly application. One day later, I requested to purchase seats from the same company. After selecting them, they charged my card $189.68. My surprise was enormous when days later they tried to charge me another $189.68, plus $466, plus $22. As a consequence, the card was blocked, fortunately denying these payments due to "fraudulent activity." Because of this, I had to change my card and call each of the companies that make recurring payments.They tried to charge me over 15 times.But my surprise was even greater when upon contacting them, they told me that the $189 was only to "secure" the seats, that the actual cost was the $466 they tried to charge me days later. I never knew what the $22 was for.This is openly deceptive and fraudulent to consumers. These hidden costs are a crude scheme to rob unsuspecting consumers, and someone should do something about it. One only needs to look at the ratings that the public gives this company to realize that this is something regular and recurring that they do to passengers.## JustFly's Deceptive PracticesBased on my experience and other customer reports, JustFly appears to engage in misleading pricing tactics. The company has been criticized for their predatory fees and poor customer service. In one documented case, a customer reported that JustFly didn't provide a final cost quote until after the transaction was completed, and when they tried to cancel, they faced significant cancellation fees even within minutes of booking.JustFly's website advertises "cheap flights" and claims to offer savings on flight and hotel bundles, but these promotions may mask additional charges that appear later in the booking process or after completion.**Customer Service Issues**When customers attempt to resolve issues, they often encounter difficulties reaching effective customer service. One customer reported having to navigate through multiple phone menu layers before reaching a live person, only to be stonewalled when asking to speak with a supervisor.Your experience with hidden seat charges aligns with the pattern of behavior reported by other customers. The practice of charging an initial fee to "secure" seats and then attempting to charge significantly more later appears to be part of a concerning business model that relies on unclear pricing and unexpected fees.

title: Overcharged and added unreasonable hidden fees on seat selection
text: I recently booked two flight tickets on Justfly.com At the time of booking, I paid $382 for seat selection. After my booking was confirmed, I received a confirmation email from Turkish Airlines, which stated that the seat selection fee was only $318.When I called Justfly’s customer service number and entered my confirmation number, the system repeatedly said it could not locate my booking. Therefore, I used the message/text function to contact them. Through the text system, they were able to find my booking number. However, all responses I received were from an automated AI system.The AI repeatedly instructed me to contact the airline regarding the seat selection fee. I called Turkish Airlines directly, and they confirmed that the total seat selection fee they received was $318, this is the price tag of their system, no additional charges are required.I messaged Justfly again, but the automated system kept insisting that everything was fine on their end by automated AI.Not only did JustFly charge me $382 for seat selection, but they also added $42.26 labeled as a “seat request fee,” resulting in a total of $424.26 paid on their website for seat selection alone. However, the airline only charge $318 in total.This clearly shows that Justfly.com overcharged and added unreasonable hidden fees. I will not use this website again, nor will I recommend it to anyone.

title: Justfly Deserves a ZERO
text: This was hands down one of the worst travel booking experiences I’ve ever had. Everything that could go wrong, did. I spent over an hour on the phone with a live agent booking a trip from BWI to San Jose, Costa Rica, then to Panama City, and back to BWI. Sounds simple enough, right? Wrong. When I received the itinerary, an entire leg of the trip was missing!I called Justfly immediately—less than 8 hours later—to report the issue and was told my cancellation request would be reviewed since I was still within the 24-hour window. After several days of waiting with no update, I called again and was forced to speak to a chatbot. When I finally got through to another human, I was told that because I said, “When will I receive my refund?” instead of explicitly saying “Yes,” my cancellation was denied. Are you kidding me?So now, I’m stuck having to buy a whole new ticket directly from the airline just to make my travel date. I’m 83 years old, on a fixed income, and this has caused me a completely unnecessary financial burden and a ton of stress.This company is disorganized, unhelpful, and seems to hide behind technicalities to avoid doing the right thing. I will never use Justfly again, and I strongly advise others to steer clear.

title: Dear JustFly Customer Support,
text: Dear JustFly Customer Support,I am writing to request a refund for baggage fees formally I was unexpectedly charged on my recent trip booked through your website.On Saturday, May 15, 2025, I purchased a ticket on JustFly that explicitly stated I was entitled to one free carry-on bag and one free checked bag. However, upon arrival at Atlanta International Airport on Friday, March 21, 2025, I was informed that I had zero checked baggage allowance and was required to pay for the first checked bag. My husband and I had to pay $330 to check in our luggage, which was not part of our planned expenses. To my surprise, the same issue occurred on our return flight from Antalya Airport on Friday, March 28, 2025, where we were again charged for checked baggage. As a result, I now owe approximately $700 on my credit card due to these unexpected charges.This situation has caused financial strain and disrupted our travel plans. I do not understand why this discrepancy occurred between the information on your website and the airline’s policy, but I expect a prompt resolution. I kindly request a full refund for the baggage fees paid on both of my luggage's trip.Please address this matter as soon as possible to prevent further escalation. I appreciate your prompt response and resolution.ATTENTION!!! NEW POSTEmail response from JustflyAs per our records, the checked-in baggage allowance is included per passenger. In order to proceed with the refund for the baggage amount you paid, we kindly require a receipt for each passenger and for each ticket individually.The receipts we have received so far are only linked to one ticket—Peter's. Therefore, we have processed and refunded the amount for the first checked-in baggage based on the receipt provided for his ticket.To complete the refund for your ticket, we will need the receipt that is specifically linked to your ticket.Should you have any questions or require further assistance, please do not hesitate to reach out.Dear Justfly Customer Service,Thank you for your email response above.However, I am confused and disappointed by how this refund issue is being handled. When I purchased our tickets through Justfly, it was clearly stated that checked baggage was included/paid for each passenger. I paid for both tickets—mine and my husband's—in a single transaction, which was accepted without issue.Due to a problem with the baggage allowance not being honored by Turkish Airlines at the airport, my husband was forced to paid for both his and my checked baggage. As travel partners, we handled the unexpected expense together. The receipt provided clearly shows that baggage fees were paid for both passengers, for both the outbound and return flights.Yet, I have only received a refund for one passenger—Peter—because the receipt was apparently linked to just his Name. This does not make sense, as the payment covered baggage for two passengers and should be refunded as such. The fact that the receipt was not split does not change the fact that the total amount paid includes baggage for both tickets.I kindly request that Justfly review this situation again. A full refund for both passengers' baggage fees is fair and expected. There is no reason why the second person refund should be denied.I look forward to your prompt assistance in resolving this matter.Best regards,FC[Reference # 272050311]

title: Terrible Experience with JustFly
text: Terrible Experience with JustFly – Do Not Trust This CompanyI purchased tickets from JustFly in October for my husband and me to travel to Lima, Peru. We had been planning this trip for six months and carefully chose a Delta flight from San Francisco to Lima with only one layover in LAX. Since we are older, shorter flights are important to us. Additionally, I am visually impaired and rely on my husband during the trip.One day before our flight, my daughter attempted to check in on JustFly’s website and received a message stating that our flight had been changed without any prior notification. They informed us that we had to modify our booking but assured us there would be no extra charges. They also mentioned that we would receive compensation for the change.Not knowing what to do, I decided to call a JustFly agent, who assured me that I needed to proceed with the change and that once I did, we would receive a refund for our original tickets. He even provided his direct number and email, guaranteeing that everything would be resolved. Trusting his word, my husband and I changed the flight.When we called back to confirm, they informed us that we would now be flying with LATAM instead of Delta and that we would not receive any refund because we had not purchased First Class tickets. I felt completely deceived by JustFly and strongly believe they reassigned our original Delta tickets to someone else.The worst part was their customer service. When I tried to express my frustration, the agent mockingly told us that if we weren’t happy, we could cancel our flight. But then he added that if we canceled, we wouldn’t receive our refund for at least two weeks, there would be a $500 deduction for canceling, and buying new last-minute tickets would be much more expensive. A complete scam.JustFly is an untrustworthy company with terrible customer service and highly questionable practices. I would not recommend anyone to buy tickets from them. One star is too much for this service.

title: Disappointed with Allianz after past positive experiences
text: We had a mediocre to poor experience with Allianz. My spouse had a serious medical emergency in Australia.The medical emergency turned into a nine-day extended stay in Australia. What started out fine with our Case Manager turned into disappointment when we were given conflicting information and instructions by the case management department; and then, from the trip cancellations claims department.  The Allianz system for tracking claims is either inefficient or employees are not doing their jobs or they require better training. Invoices were often lost and had to be resent.  Certain demands were being made for specific wording, such as, for "Refunds and Penalties" with regard to rebooked airline tickets.  I was instructed that if the words "refunds" and "penalties" were not in the letter from the airlines, the claim would not be honored.  As much as I explained that we didn't benefit from any refunds or incurred any penalties - and I uploaded every piece of documentation with explanations of the rebooking - I met with a brick wall. Instructions on where to e-mail or upload invoices/expenses in general were not clearly explained either.  In follow-up calls for status updates, I was told an adjuster or someone would call me back within 24 - 48 hours, but they never did.Frustratingly, our claim is still not fully completed, because of an "errant" medical invoice in Allianz's system. All invoices and expenses were uploaded to the dashboard or sent by emails between mid February and March 21. Some in duplicate.  Medical invoices were e-mailed to Case Management for the Guarantee of Payment letter.We have had positive experiences with Allianz in the past when submitting claims for simple flight cancellations for covered reasons. Perhaps the process for handling numerous invoices and expenses during complex medical emergencies might not be their strong point.Fortunately, Allianz sent checks at the end of April (for an ordeal that started February 7) for our trip interruption expenses per the policy and two of the three medical invoices, but in the end, the entire experience proved a struggle.

text: Unfortunately a disappointing week…especially for the price we paid. A bathroom that didn’t work, run down and shabby furniture, moldy walls….the office was hard to get hold of, no service etc.we cannot recommend this company to fellow travelers.

name: Britt Nateras
title: VRBO was very difficult to reach
text: VRBO was very difficult to reach. They have such limited support compared to AirBnb. They leave it all on the host and when the host is unresponsive, they can't or won't do anything.

name: Duwanda Laye
title: horrible business practices
text: My Experience with VRBO and Host Demetrice Brown – BewareI had an extremely disappointing experience with VRBO and one of their hosts, Demetrice Brown of DS Brown Investment, regarding a property located at 743 N 32nd St, Milwaukee, WI. I attempted to reserve a stay through VRBO, but the process was frustrating and ultimately unethical.The listing for this property did not display a cancellation policy, as VRBO claims should be standard. Due to the absence of this policy, I reached out directly to Mr. Brown and asked if I would receive a full refund should I choose to cancel. He clearly stated, “Yes.” Based on that assurance, I canceled the reservation. After doing so, Mr. Brown ceased all communication and refused to return my deposit.To make matters worse, VRBO then claimed that according to their cancellation policy—not the property’s—my refund was not eligible. They did refund taxes and fees, which only further contradicts their explanation and adds to the confusion. The conflicting information between VRBO and their host, along with the lack of accountability, was incredibly frustrating and unprofessional.This experience reflects poor business practices and a lack of integrity from both VRBO and Mr. Brown. I caution others to be extremely careful before booking with this company or this host. I will not be using VRBO again.

name: Laura
title: Villa was dirty and the VRBO Customer…
text: Villa was dirty and the VRBO Customer service couldn’t do anything about it.There was mold in a bathroom and they classed the issue as minor.Terrible customer service, I certainly wouldn’t use VRBO again.Edit - VRBO have now offered a solution.

name: Golspie
title: The most horrendous customer service I…
text: The most horrendous customer service I have ever experienced.. already 8 hours of calls in a week and 3 agents looking at why I have been underpaid and still getting moved around and hung up on.Absolute joke.Not to mention response below.. they don't even know who wrote this so has can they say they have requested more info?? Again lies.

name: Adam Wright
title: The host cancelled my reso because they double booked
text: I booked a place for two months from the Campo Real Estate Host on VRBO for a liberty Village area in Toronto and they just cancelled on me after having booked more than 3 weeks ago saying the place was double booked on another site. How did they not know after more than 3 weeks? I didn’t know VRBO allows this to happen because they told me they MAY be penalized. Now, I have to rush to find another place while on a vacation in an other country. Definitely not going to try VRBO out again as this was my first experience. On to another short-term rental site. And I’m staying away from Campo Real Estate as a host on other websites. -Adam W.

name: chun kim
title: Unpleasant experience
text: I realized the property was in the wrong location less than 30 minutes after booking and immediately asked to cancel. The host initially replied to confirm the booking, but once I mentioned cancellation, he went silent. He only responded the next morning, refusing to issue a refund, claiming he had just been asleep.On the check-in day, even though we never officially canceled the reservation, we were given no instructions or way to access the property — as if we weren’t expected to stay at all. The host took our money and offered zero support. He made no effort to help and showed no willingness to cooperate.Worse yet, VRBO completely failed us. When we reached out, they simply repeated that the host refused to refund, without investigating the situation properly. They ignored the timeline, the lack of access, and the host’s unprofessional behavior.Now I truly understand why so many people give low ratings. We were treated with zero empathy. Be very careful — or better yet, stay away from VRBO entirely

name: Meghan
title: How do you do zero stars?
text: How do you do zero stars? Our apartment was mouldy and the shower didn’t work. Claimed they offered us an exchange place but can’t send the email proof of this, because there isn’t any as they never offered it. Had to stay somewhere else and can’t get our money back. Don’t use - Air bnb are so much better!!!

name: Tsvetanka Peltekova
title: Charged $434 for Canceling Within hours No Support, Just Penalties
text: I canceled a reservation immediately after booking within hours for a stay 8 months in the future. In response, VRBO suspended my listing for 7 days and charged my credit card $434. I received an invoice with a past due date the same day they charged me without warning, notice, or any ability to dispute the fee.What’s worse: guests on VRBO can cancel almost anytime with no penalty, yet as a host, I was punished harshly for acting in good faith. This isn’t about protecting guests it feels like a revenue tactic targeting hosts.I’ve also previously dealt with a system glitch that showed a $4,000+ reservation that didn’t exist. VRBO blamed me, then admitted it was a system issue, and stopped responding when I asked for compensation for lost nights.I’ve lost trust in this platform. No accountability, no transparency, and policies that treat hosts as disposable. Due to hosts complaints many other reservation platforms are gaining popularity. Do not put your financial health in the hands of such a dishonest platform. They can and will ruin you.

name: Venice Hub
title: THE WORST EVER. POOR SUPPORT. I REMOVED MY LISTING
text: WE ARE A HOTEL AND HAVE LISTED OUR PROPERTY ON ALMOST DOZEN OF OTAS. WE NEVER HAD ANY ISSUE OF THIS KIND WITH OTA. THEY ALWAYS CARE ABOUT YOUR LISTING. THIS IS THE WORST LISTING PLATFORM EVER I HAVE SEEN. IF YOU ASK FOR A HELP FROM A SUPPORT TEAM, THEY SAY OK MY COLLEAGUE WILL SHORTLY CALL YOU BACK. AND THEY NEVER CALL YOU. IT WAS THIS WORSE THAT I REMOVED MY LISTING FROM THIS OTA

name: Coastal Print Solutions
title: Misleading listing and VRBO is a JOKE
text: We just had stayed at our  first VRBO listing in Storey Lake at 2945 Penelope Loop in Kissimmee. Do NOT rent this property! Pool did not look like pictures, broken back door lock leaving the house unlocked all night, broken smoke alarm, unresponsive homeowners, dirty etc. Also false listing info saying that the house has a fireplace and a sauna, hot tub, non of that even exist. Nasty coffee pot, DO NOT rent here! VRBO claims they weren’t in violation even though their listing is FALSE and subpar. So we are now handling with our cc company and will be getting compensation. Look at the listing photo compared to what we got!!! How TF is this even legal. VRBO is a joke. Never ever again. I would attach photos if I could!

name: Vigo
title: VRBO is barely a company
text: VRBO is barely a company.  The hosts do whatever they want.  They lie about their listings, the number of rooms, beds, amenities, they charge insane fees for things they don't do and when you complain VRBO does nothing.  Use Air B and B.

name: Weslyn
title: Host:Seagoville, Texas
text: Wyatt was our host in Seagoville, and he was fantastic.When I first started planning my trip, I was a bit skeptical, but Wyatt answered all my questions and made me feel comfortable. He walked me through the directions and made sure I understood everything clearly.When we arrived at the property, it was clean, sanitized, and very nice. Wyatt communicated with us regularly to ensure we were comfortable throughout our stay. On the last day, he provided detailed instructions for check-out, which made the process smooth and easy.We had no issues at all, and I definitely plan to contact Wyatt again the next time I book an Airbnb.

name: Lauren
title: Would not trust this company
text: Booked a stay through Vrbo with cottages.com as the host for the property. Upon booking they took half the money and stated they would take the second half at a later date. Two months later I received an email out of the blue to say that my booking has been cancelled and the first payment will not be refunded as I did not pay the remaining fee. I had received no reminders to pay the fee and lost £400.

name: Alex De souza
title: Don't trust to this company .
text: I have had a scammy and very bad experience with VRBO. I booked 2 days at Heaven Caravans in Hastings with my whole family. When we arrived, they couldn't locate our reservation. I had the booking confirmation email and everything. We had to travel all the way back to London without being able to go on our holiday.I wasted my time and my money.

name: Lee O
title: This awful company is not interested in…
text: This awful company is not interested in the people who rent properties, only the people who have properties to rent . . . mostly the pictures and descriptions are a total falsehood, the prices are ludicrous, and the amount vrbo pockets absurd, don't try and get any help from vrbo either if there is a problem, they just tell you to sort it with the owner.The vrbo website is a mess, difficult to navigate, and it's like a secret society, they won't let you give a telephone or email to the owner . . .It's much cheaper to use google maps for the area you wish to visit, then look up agencies in the areas to find good accomodation directly then no charges from vrbo and or direct with an owner !I received an email from Trustpilot saying I had to give booking's details etc etc otherwise my experience would not be published. . . I have done so, and only listed two properties that we have rented, but I must be not very wise because I have rented a few more from this company, and since it took over from HomeAway,it has just gone downhill,like I explained !I don't need an answer from some person who works in a call center or whatever from this company, it's always the same old same old,excuses, and there's nothing they can do etc etc . . .Unbelievable, an few hours after receiving from Trustpilot a message I had to give my bookings, which were various,I did and received a telephone call from some "dedicated team" in India of course, nice chap, and the result = they will look into it ! "They"=vrbo, have to look at themselves and work out what is wrong with "their" system , and the myriad of faults they make, and their service . . .

name: Kevin
title: Be careful
text: Vrbo reached out to me and refunded the cancellation charge so I’m updating the rating from a 1 to a 4. I’m rating them a 4 because of the stress and frustration in trying to resolve the issue. The phone number for the host was wrong and not verified apparently, and no email address is provided to contact the host.I booked an apartment through Vrbo in Mexico. The host was supposed to email check in instructions 24 hours before check in but they never did. I chatted with Vrbo support who said they could not reach the host and gave me a Vrbo support number to call. I called them and they tried to call the host but said the host didn’t speak English. I had a native Spanish speaker friend call the number for the host provided by Vrbo. The person who answered told my friend that it was the wrong number. I had to cancel the booking as there’s no way I’m going to fly to another country, travel to the apartment, and not be able to enter. This apartment building did not have a person for check in. Vrbo passed on the host cancellation fee and did not give me a full refund despite the fact that the host did not fulfill their obligation and Vrbo provided the wrong phone number. I called Vrbo customer support and I was told there was nothing they can do. I’m never using them again. The host stole my money and Vrbo will do nothing to protect renters.

name: Gareth o'reilly
title: SCAM COMPANY! Don't use these guys...they don't have your back but they will sure take your money
text: If I could give less stars I would..SCAM COMPANY !I wish I had read these reviews before trying to book through them.We booked an apartment then when we arrived the host did not give us the info to access property. I tried to get through to VRBO and they could only refund us and leave us to find alternatives last minute accommodation promising to refund us.When it came to securing the refund they stone walled us with terms and conditions.Mira, the representative I was in touch with was less than useful and kept regurgitating the company policy that we weren't informed of on the day.Don't use these guys...they don't have your back but they will sure take your money

name: Bewerter
title: It can't be worse - lost money - no feedback

name: Robert Reynolds
title: My complaint is not as bad as the…

name: Rebecca Leitch
title: So bad
text: So bad. I will never book a property from VRBO again. Didn't receive compensation or a refund on our stay. We a dreadful property with damp and mould with a broken shower. No offer of fixing or changing our accomodation. Went trying to approach customer service with our concerns and recieving compensation we received nothing.

name: Chasity Cooper
title: It's sad just how AWFUL this platform is!
text: It's sad just how AWFUL this platform is. They have all the crazy extra charges and fees. But really the customer service or should I say LACK of customer service is what takes the cake. It doesn't matter if its via chat, email or a call. They know you can't actually DO anything so they just make whatever decision benefits them and your just stuck with it. Oh and did you know you have absolutely no way of seeing reviews or any information about your guests? Yeah, and unless you pay some $60 fee PER STAY for damage protection you have NONE. AND the coverage is only up to $1500.00! They wrongfully charged me for a cancelation. They said they would refund me but never did. Every time I relied to call back once I realized they weren't going to refund me no one knew what I was talking about?! So I left the platform for about a year. I came back and here we go again! The GUEST wants to cancel their reservation I have to accept it but the only way I can is by selecting "ok" to a notice that pops up saying I will be charged. No way I was going through that whole thing again so I got online and chatted with a representative. Who advised me to just select ok?! Told me "I wouldn't be charged, ignore it"  I said NO WAY IM NOT AGREEING to a charge and getting right back into the same situation again. Guess what literally that's the only option! The clock still ticks away against me for "not responding" even thought I have been messaging the guest to keep them in the loop. My ratings go down. This whole thing is RIDICULOUS!

name: Tammy Duncan
title: Why I will now get the insurance.
text: I’m sorry for doing this but I have to say this.  I had a terrible experience and I don’t want to use Vrbo again.  We booked a place and there was a bad storm.  It was the hurricane that impacted a large majority of North Carolina.  I was told by the owner I couldn’t get a refund for a little rain.  The roads were washed out.  It was a natural disaster.  Vrbo was no help in this situation.  I did learn a very valuable lesson.  I will get the insurance. Vrbo has all the rules of what you have to do to protect the owner but nothing for us when we are not protected.  It truly hurt and we were out 1000$.  I’m sorry but it truly hurt the owner said a little rain.  The roads leading to our destination were washed out.  That was more than a little rain. Again a valuable lesson.  And I do understand business but I also understand decency.

name: Leslie Hjorth
title: Unexpected last minute cancelation
text: Our reservation was unexpectedly canceled just 48 hours before check-in—during graduation weekend in a small town with extremely limited availability. We were left scrambling, only to find that no hotels or rentals were available. VRBO claims to assist with last-minute cancellations, but after spending over three hours on the phone with their support team, we received no meaningful help and then hung up on and no return call. I’m incredibly disappointed by how poorly this situation was handled. What should have been a joyful and memorable weekend was completely derailed.

name: Spencer Brown
title: Low bookings and Scripted Customer Service provides no support…

VRBO provided no support and customer service can only read scripts. I found this to be true when even Supervisor level people have no ability to veer from the scripts.

name: Sabina

They have the worst customer service team, very unprofessional it seems as if they have been randomly selected on the streets. Awful to set up your property with too. Worst website and please do not use it!

name: Jeff McNiece
title: VRBO doesn’t take responsibility when a technical issue blocks home from being listed
text: I pay $700 a year to have my property listed in VRBO and have been a customer of theirs for almost 20 years. I recently discovered that my property was not showing up on any searches including the map function. My house is always getting rental Inquiries and reservations and has been quiet the last couple of months and I finally discovered why!!  I did a Service Case reporting this and honestly - they fixed it quickly. No idea of if this was a global issue or just mine?  I asked to know for how long this issue had been going on as I wanted a prorated refund on my annual fee for the property to be listed (isn’t this what the $700 is for???!!!).  They informed me that they do not provide any refunds for their technical issues and also, they had no idea how long this had been occurring. This is total bullshit as being in the Software Development for almost 40 years, configuration control can always show you when the bug was introduced. The bottom line is that they are NOT willing to take responsibility for their poor software quality. Really wish there were more customer focused responsible alternatives.

name: Mike

name: Corinna
title: Please read before you even think of booking with VRBO
text: Posting this just to get it out there. Vrbo is the absolute worst company to try and deal with from a customer support aspect. I am getting no resolution from them and now have no choice but to get my story out there anyway I know how. Here's my story:After a flood destroyed our home earlier this month, I had to relocate quickly with my kids — one of whom is autistic. As a single mom, all I wanted was a quiet, safe, private place to help my kids feel stable again.Instead, the rental I booked through VRBO was a disaster. The “stylish private bungalow in an upscale neighbourhood” as the add described it, turned out to be a run-down, noisy home on a major road, with two tenants and the host living in the basement. The space was unsafe — unstable beds that shifted while you slept, peeling floors, flimsy locks, and a security system that beeped loudly every time someone entered or exited any part of the "PRIVATE" home. This was overwhelming for me and I know it would be completely overwhelming for my autistic child.I packed up and left within 48 hours. The host refused any sort of refund on the month long stay, (over $6,000!) and accused me of trying to “scam” them — while taking zero responsibility for the lies in their listing. No empathy. No decency. VRBO customer service did nothing — no resolution, no accountability, no compassion.If you’re a parent, especially one raising an autistic child or dealing with crisis, please think twice before trusting listings on VRBO.And to the host: families deserve better.

name: Deborah Dennis
title: Serenity property in broken bow ok
text: Serenity property in broken bow ok. The cancellation policy is ridiculous. I booked on April 9. Had to cancel on April 21 related to an unexpected family event. Booked for May 1-3. “Read the cancellation policy” was their response. So I’m out $922.00.   No consideration for any circumstance. Won’t be using them again ever.

name: Judy
title: Extremely Unprofessional and Costing Me…
text: Extremely Unprofessional and Costing Me Money.I updated my short-term rental permit for my property weeks ago, but VRBO still has my listing pulled. Every single day I’m told the same thing — “be patient, it’ll be back up in 3 to 24 hours.” Every day, nothing happens. When I call back, I’m told I have to start the process over again.Updating an expired permit is extremely basic — it happens every year — yet VRBO has made it an absolute nightmare. I’ve been passed around endlessly, and shockingly, even the customer service agents claim there’s no way for them to contact the department that handles this. How is that even possible?Meanwhile, I’m losing money every single day and now have upcoming bookings that I’m being forced to cancel. This is unacceptable. VRBO’s lack of professionalism and internal communication is absolutely appalling, and they clearly have no regard for their hosts’ businesses.

name: Lisa Ashton

name: Paulina Shelley
title: Allows scammers
text: Will never book through VRBO again. They allow scammers and they scam. I booked a New York City apartment for 3 days. It was a two bedroom apartment that sleeps 13, according to the webpage, through a company called NYShortstays. I get there and it’s a one bedroom apartment that can only sleep maybe 2, no TVs, no bedding, no towels. Now the owner and VRBO will not give me a refund. All of my US Military comrades, stay away from this company.I also found out today that short term rentals are illegal in NYC. Why is VRBO allowing this?Edit: VRBO did reach out, but they sided with the owner again! They told me the owner said the description states a one or two bedroom apartment. Everyone, go look up property 4371034 on VRBO and tell me if you agree. The first description of the property in bold letters states it is a “2bedroom gem”. They also still have not addressed the fact that short term rentals are illegal in NYC and they allowed this company to advertise on their website. They are unwilling to deal with host who scam their customers and it’s a horrible shame!

name: Julian Kernohan
title: NEVER USE VRBO WEBSITE
text: I made a hotel reservation in April 2025 for a stay in Abu Dhabi in December 2025.  The website says that the "host" will confirm within 24 hours and in the meantime takes a deposit.  Within 24 hours the response came back that the hotel was no longer available and my deposit would be refunded within 72 hours.  I then made another reservation at another hotel.  Same thing.  They took a deposit and then told me that there was no room available.   I contacted VRBO chat room and spoke to "Elijah" who apologized.  I explained that I was also very familiar with Abu Dhabi as I had lived there for 30 years and knew the hotels very well.  I received a phone call from "Khalid" - possibly from a call center in the Philippines, but I cannot confirm that for sure.  He apologized and said he would email me with other hotels that were available. I reminded him that I knew Abu Dhabi and was only interested in 4 or 5 star hotels in the same areas of the city and at a similar budget.  His email arrived shortly thereafter with a) mainly apartments and b) the few hotels mentioned were approximately 3-5 times the price of the two hotels that I was interested in.  In addition, one of the hotels was on an island and not in Abu Dhabi City.  I am not interested in staying on an island and the hotel prices were not within the mentioned budget and, therefore, not acceptable.  Why would a website even list hotels that are not available and then take a deposit when the hotel is not available?

name: pbson
title: The website needs major work to keep…
text: The website needs major work to keep filters in place once a property is viewed.I find it so frustrating I need to keep resetting filters hat I have given up.Perhaps Verb should spend some time on this rather than reducing reward scheme amounts

name: Paulo Dias
text: 444 / 5 000My name is Paulo Dias, I made a reservation for Accommodation: 5242302Reservation number: HA-X6BY4YArrival: 08/19/2025Departure: 08/24/2025Nights: 5Guests: 2 adults, 1 childHost: Maria Filomena Fernandes MartinsOn March 3, 2025, the reservation was canceled, they said they refunded the amount, but so far I have not received anything. name: Stace Gordon
title: VRBO is basically a fraud
text: VRBO is basically a fraud - they don’t post negative reviews and don’t have any true customer service.  I was duped into renting a poor property because only positive reviews are posted.     I actually think it’s criminal level fraud.   You are renting a place sight unseen and have no recourse if the host is a party to the fraud.    I’ve filed a complaint with the AZ attorney general in my case but this is systemic fraud.   The reviews are meaninglessAvoid Arizona prop.  #3427087 at all costs!!Edit - This VRBO response just confirms their fraud.  They took weeks to explain why pricing info isn’t allowed in a review and then prohibited my review as not timely.    Their own guidelines do not prohibit pricing comments.   Their system is well orchestrated fraud.   DO NOT TRUST VRBO.

name: stuart
title: Vrbo could do better but clearly not that bothered
text: Booked a villa for extended family of 10 through Vrbo which was changed 3 days before departure. Substitute villa was unfinished (kitchen incomplete, work still being done on pool). We had to battle to get 3rd villa (which was lovely) but lost 1 day of holiday sorting out. Compensation offered amounted to $10/ person. Vrbo's attitude typically that of large/ faceless organisation i.e. hollow words ("we're so sorry"/ "We truly regret the inconvenience") coupled with paltry compensation. Problems arose through no fault of ours and Vrbo didn't do anywhere near enough when problem arose, when we were trying to sort it and then afterwards. Reading other reviews, this is consistent theme. BE WARNED ALL WHO ENTER WORLD OF VRBO....

name: Jennifer Kloihofer
title: Beware! Lying thieves run Vrbo
text: A word of caution to anyone planning a trip, don’t use Vrbo.I booked a place and cancelled it within the house cuz I found a better place on Airbnb and my full 100% Vrbo refund was missing $534.15!When I called them they tried to blame it on foreign currency exchange…. I cancelledthe booking within the hour! What kind of foreign currency exchange scam are you running Vrbo?And if that’s the case why do you say you give a 100% refund?Not 100% refund minus foreign currency exchange rates.Oh also, I was given no reference number for my incident or contact information for the department handling these types of issues for vrbo so I have no idea if or when someone will be contacting me about returning my stolen $534.15.I will NEVER use Vrbo again and strongly encourage anyone who does to always double check to make sure they received all of the refund they should have gotten if they have cancelled a reservation in the past!

name: Hillel Posner
title: Simple story, VRBO failed us
text: Simple story. We went to Mexico to see my dad one last time (he is very ill). 3 days before the trip our host had not responded to our request for location. We called VRBO, they said we had to wait until check in before they would do anything. The night before check on, at 1 am, VRBO cancelled the reservation. They said we could book on hotel, VRBO or Expedia, there were no places within the price margin they gave us on these platforms. We were stuck with no reasonable options. Just had to spend a ton of money. VRBO did nothing. So much for their guarantee. Didn't even offer to help find another place. We lost a lot of money and had a lot of stress. Would never use again.

name: Carrie Doyle
title: I’d honestly give zero stars if…
text: I’d honestly give zero stars if possible. We’ve had the most awful experience ever with VRBO!! We’ve been super hosts for over 5 years, had over a hundred positive reviews, and they just cancelled all of our listings without warning for no valid reason. We’ve spent over 20 hours solid on the phone getting hung up on, dropped calls, transferred, and every time being told they couldn’t help us. There’s one person in there entire company who can make decisions on our account and not once has he ever emailed us back or called  after 10 emails on our end and 8 phone calls. They say his department doesn’t have phones 🤔 and that he has no supervisor to talk to. I’ve asked if he’s a real person and not a bot and their only answer is that “he’s part of our team”!! It turns out there reasoning for cancelling our listings is because the mother of one of our already booked renters messaged us asking for room/bed layout and we used the words “contact” and “email” after she asked if her daughter could contact us with any more questions in regards to their upcoming travels. Her daughter originally booked me as her wedding photographer (that is my full time profession) and I recommended they also book our rental for her family. Naturally she already has my number and my email to communicate about her wedding. It appears that VRBO has ai generated tag words that if you use them in messaging you will get your listings disabled. I went to the extent of providing them the following documents to prove our case and they will not reinstate our listings at all and will not let us talk with anyone who can actually help us. I provided them…1. An original email inquiry for wedding photography from nearly a year ago.2. A copy of my photography contract with her.3. A copy of my photo business questionnaire where it lists the woman who messaged us on vrbo as her mother4. A copy of their booking of the property nearly a year prior to her mom messaging us about room/bed layout5. A copy of their receipt of down payment for lodging and photo booking from nearly a year prior to her message.6. And letters from both my bride and her mother stating they had no idea that having the mother of the bride message us on vrbo would be an issue and get us flagged for removal.Vrbo refuses to look at any of it, refuses to let us talk to Leon who apparently is the only person on earth who can make a decision on our account, and refuses to even acknowledge that they are not providing us any customer service help even though we’ve supported their business financially and been super hosts for over 5 years.They are truly the worst worst platform for hosts. Zero support, zero customer service, and zero professionalism. We’ve had nothing but a very positive experience on Airbnb and booking.com. Every time we have a question they are so helpful. Save yourself the time and headache and steer clear of vrbo. In our research they have numerous current lawsuits, fail to payout hosts, we’re recently under investigation with BBB, and are in financial trouble from poor management.Updated as a response to VRBO....As of 4/21/25 there has been no email response from the team responsible for our account with Leon being the team leader for our account. His original email to us was 02/27/25 of which we responded that same day with questions. He has not responded once to us in nearly 2 months. Customer support tells us to communicate with him about our case and he refuses to respond even once and refuses to provide us customer service.

name: Jeanne Ackles
title: Cannot get them to return our damage deposit. No means of communication except ai.
text: We have been back home from our holiday for 6 weeks and cannot get anyone to return our damage deposit. I have been trying to find a link for this company for communication in order to get our deposit back and are completely at a loss. We left our rental spotless and fully sanitized. So very angry!!

name: Manuel Rabelo
title: By far the worst app for hosts
text: By far the worst app for hosts! Their market maker is awful, they change pricing without telling you, and their fees are outrageous. Their customer service is the worst (if you can understand them), and customer support is extremely rude. If you cancel a reservation because their system failed, they charge you 10% and suspend your account. Stick with AirBnB for your hosting experience, they are by far better.

name: Karen Cracknell
title: The main problem with Vrbo is they do not communicaTE WITH EACH OTHER OR THE CUSTOMER PROPERLY EVERYTHING IS A STANDARD FORMAT.
text: The main problem I had with Vrbo was when you tried to get a refund not from the property that you may have cancelled but from Vrbo themselves for the service fee etc. It took me at least 6 weeks after numerous phone calls and emails which were always replied with ( we understand your frustration but are awaiting reply from owners of property. It was not the the owners I had a problem with it was vrbos side of things but they just kept blaming the owners and saying they had tried to contact the owners but they would not reply and when I spoke to said owners they had no knowledge of vrbo trying to contact them.At the end of the day it was not the part of the contract with the owners but a contract with vrbo.It was not untill I got my solicitor involved that things started to move very quickly and a satisfactory outcome was achieved.So Vrbo sort your refund procedure out because we can all do without the hassle when all we want is what vrbo originally promise when you have to cancell a villa.

name: Melissa Flowers
title: THE WORST APP AS A HOST
text: THE WORST APP AS A HOSTThe app is not user friendlyDoes not allow for a co hostThe customer service is HORRIBLEWe appreciate that many people do use it and want the business but at the expense of EXTREME STRESSthey do not have the option of ID verificationThere seems to be no care or concern for hosts or their propertyWE WILL DROP OUR PROPERTY

name: Chalet Kanimbla
title: Hosts, don’t waste your time with Stayz/VRBO!
text: Hosts, don’t waste your time with Stayz/VRBO!I used to be a loyal Stayz traveller, so naturally, I wanted to list my property with them when I became a host. My listing has now been live for over a year. In that time, I’ve received consistent weekly bookings on Airbnb, with over 50 reviews and an average rating of 4.96. On VRBO? Just two bookings in total.I pay a premium for a channel manager to keep my listings synchronized across platforms, so before cancelling, I reached out to VRBO support to check if there was an issue with my listing.Unfortunately, the support experience was incredibly frustrating. The agent I spoke with, Ella Mae B, wasted 30 minutes of my time and repeatedly directed me to check MarketMaker to assess demand. I explained clearly that there’s no demand issue—I’m getting plenty of bookings through Airbnb. My suspicion is that VRBO’s algorithm doesn’t rank your listing well until you’ve had at least three booking reviews, similar to what I experienced with Airbnb (which only took a few weeks to overcome).That said, it seems like a classic chicken-and-egg problem—or worse, that Stayz simply doesn’t work anymore, and support won’t acknowledge it.Ella Mae was unwilling to escalate the issue or provide any real help. After trying my best to make the platform work, I’ve decided to cancel my listing and will be recommending that other local hosts don’t waste their time either.

name: Stephen Willis
title: 24 hour emergency line is nothing of the sort. Weekend ruined.
text: Arrived to find only 2 of the 5 bedrooms were unlocked, and we had booked for 10 people. 24 hour emergency phone was nothing of the sort. Message service only, and no reply forcing most of our family to stay in a nearby hotel. Not sure what they would do with a significant emergency, and family celebration weekend ruined.

name: Martin Mosebury Smith
title: A very strange booking platform
text: A very strange booking platform. Minimal information available despite an AI assistant. Enquiry to the host not functional. Having made a booking and confirmed by bank card received a message "Your request was declined". Are we booking accommodation for an offered service or not?

name: Vicente Garcés

OF COURSE vrbo didnt do nothing about it and their emails are “ we cant do nothing about it”. Well you MUST do something about it as you are the platform that brings guest.
