text: I had a deeply frustrating and disappointing experience with Priceline that disrupted a major life event and left me stranded with my family in the middle of the night.I booked a prepaid, non-refundable car rental through Priceline (Confirmation #: 780-975-535-16) for pickup at Atlanta Airport on May 3rd at 1:00 AM, ahead of my graduation from Georgia Tech. I was traveling with my wife and two kids and needed to be at the ceremony early in the morning.Despite having a confirmed reservation, no car was available upon arrival. I contacted Priceline support, and they assured me the reservation would be canceled, that a refund would be issued, and that expenses for Lyft/Uber and the inconvenience would be reimbursed. We were stranded at the airport and had to book a hotel and use Lyft—all at my own expense.After waiting 36 hours, I returned to the airport and booked a new reservation, but the rental company mistakenly applied the pickup to the original reservation. Priceline then denied the refund, claiming the original reservation was used, even though I had no vehicle for 36 hours.To make matters worse, Priceline has refused to issue a meaningful refund, despite the fact that I had no car for a significant portion of the reservation. Every time I call, I'm told that the best they can offer is a 10% coupon for a future booking which is completely unacceptable given the circumstances. This doesn’t even begin to address the inconvenience, added expenses, or the disruption caused on a milestone day for my family.This was not my fault, yet I’ve been left with the burden of extra costs, lost time, and poor service—with no accountability from Priceline. The handling of this situation was misleading, inconsistent, and completely unfair. I expected better from a major travel service.I do not recommend using Priceline for car rentals—if anything goes wrong, you're on your own.

text: A month after booking a package trip and just one day before flying out, I still hadn't received any information. I tried accessing Priceline by entering my email and phone number, but it claimed I had no trips. When I called customer service, the AI immediately detected my upcoming trip, so it makes no sense that I couldn't access it on their website. The customer service agent claimed I entered my email incorrectly because it included "+priceline." They couldn't understand that "+priceline" creates a temporary email that forwards everything to my main email, allowing me to sort it and see if they sold my information. I use this method for every website, hundreds of times, without any issues. I don't know if the problem was on Priceline's side or Gmail's, but the main issue is that they can't correct more than three characters in an email. As a result, I had to rely on a random agent typing out my information in an email and sending it to me through customer service, rather than receiving the links and information directly from Priceline.

I contacted Priceline to discuss a full refund.  The agent was great!  She was knowledgeable and courteous.  She told me that Priceline would request a refund from AIr France and to call them back in 10 days.  I did so and spoke with Daphne, a supervisor at Priceline.  While she didn't have the answer yet, she stated she would contact Air France to authorize the refund. She asked for my phone number to return the call.  I received a call back from Daphne at Priceline within a few hours with the very good news that a full refund would be issued.  She stated it would be 7-10 business days for it to be received in my account.  I received the full amount of the refund yesterday (about 5 days)!  Kudos to Priceline and its staff for their service...I really appreciate it!

text: recently reserved a hotel for my son’s soccer tournament and was explicitly shown that I could cancel until July 30. Since we hadn’t received the tournament schedule yet, I wasn’t sure we would need the first night, so the cancellation policy was important. While booking, the website froze and refreshed, saying the reservation time was no longer available. Despite this, my bank was charged, and the hotel confirmed a reservation existed.However, I received no confirmation email or booking number, and the hotel confirmed that no email was tied to the reservation, meaning I had no way to manage or cancel the booking. Because it was booked through Priceline and I had no reservation number, the hotel couldn’t help me further.To make matters worse, Priceline has no way to look up a reservation without a booking number, and their automated phone system kept hanging up on me. When I finally reached a real person, they told me the reservation was nonrefundable unless I could provide a screenshot of the cancellation policy shown before booking, which, of course, I don’t have.They’re now charging me the full amount (nearly $900) whether or not I stay, even though the site showed a free cancellation window when I booked.Priceline’s system is broken and sets customers up to fail. There is zero accountability when something goes wrong. Don’t risk booking through them, especially for time-sensitive or expensive travel. I’ll be warning others on every forum and everywhere I can.

title: BIG SCAM! NEVER AGAIN!!
text: I booked a rental car on Priceline.com. The name of the car rental agency they assigned me was AMERICA CAR RENTAL on 5124 W Cypress St, Tampa. Fl 33607, (also known as) SONIC ENTERPRISES LLC (aka) CAR RENTAL CONSOLIDATED.  Priceline charged me $108.00 for 6 days for a mid-sized car which I thought was a great deal.  I arrive at Tampa Intl Airport and I had to take an elevator to the ground level, go outside and call AMERICA CAR RENTAL  to send a shuttle to pick me up and take me to their rental agency.  I get there and I am like 3rd in line.  I hear the woman at the counter complaining because they did not take her auto insurance which required her to purchase THEIR insurance. Then the guy in front of me was yelling and complaining because they wanted to charge him an extra $500.00 for auto insurance. He walked out.  I said to myself, "what am I in for?"  Sure enough I get to the counter after waiting in line for at least an hour only to be told they don't accept my auto insurance (Amica),  plus I had to pay a $500.00 security deposit, plus I had to purchase the toll package. They said if I refused the toll package then they had to charge me an extra $25.00 for not purchasing it.  What started as $108.00 for 6 days ended up to be a $294.00 bill.  After at least an hour and a half later I finally was able to get my rental car.  The only good thing I can say is although the car had a huge dent , I liked the ride and had no problems with the car.  Also the drop-off experience was seamless.   I received a survey from AMERICA CAR RENTAL. The survey had no link to click on and some words in the survey were misspelled.  Something else to note is  there are multiple companies in this agency.  My advice is to contact your car rental agency to make sure they take your insurance and there are no other hidden fees.  Very unprofessional.  Next time I will rent my car directly through Enterprise or another reputable company.  I will never go through Priceline again or rent a car through Sonic or America Car Rental.

title: Warning to Priceline Users – This is a SCAM and Priceline is Enabling It
text: I rented a car through Priceline in April 2025, opting to use my own insurance coverage as I always do. The pickup was at Economy Car Rental, 3356 Elmbank Rd, Mississauga, ON L4V 1A6 — and the experience was an absolute nightmare from start to finish.First, the counter associate was extremely unprofessional and dismissive. Then they hit me with a mysterious, bogus fee, claiming it’s mandatory even when using your own insurance. It’s not an insurance fee — it’s just a money grab. When I asked, they told me “Priceline should’ve disclosed it.” But I read through the entire Priceline itinerary and disclosure — and there is ZERO mention of this ridiculous charge.I spent over two weeks and more than $100 on my cell phone bill trying to get someone at Priceline to help. I called multiple times, spoke to multiple agents, even asked to speak to a manager. I begged them to at least issue a letter so I could dispute the charge with my credit card company — and they refused. I was left stranded with no support, no resolution, and no accountability.I urge Priceline to start vetting the companies you promote. A quick glance at the reviews for Economy Car Rental at that location shows over 100 one-star reviews — filled with frustrated, disgusted, and scammed customers just like me. This company uses bait-and-switch tactics, lures customers in with low prices, and then slaps on fraudulent fees at pickup, knowing you have no other choice.The fact that Priceline continues to list them despite this mountain of negative feedback tells me everything I need to know: Priceline doesn’t care about its customers. If this is how you operate — by giving shady businesses a platform — then I will never be using Priceline again, and I’ll be warning everyone I know to do the same.Shame on Economy Car Rental for running a scam, and shame on Priceline for turning a blind eye.

text: Dear Priceline Customer Service,As a Priceline VIP and long-time Expedia Elite member, I never imagined I would be compelled to write a letter of such deep dissatisfaction. But after what I endured during my February 14–17 car rental reservation (Trip #741-208-965-16, Confirmation: NUPES7), I feel obligated to not only express my outrage but also warn future customers of this vendor and the shortcomings of your platform.Let me be absolutely clear: I was treated with utter disregard by your rental partner, Flexway. And despite raising this issue promptly—on February 14 and 15—I am still waiting, over three months later (as of April 30), for any meaningful resolution or accountability from Priceline. If this is how your VIP customers are treated, I can only imagine what everyday users go through.Here’s what happened:Attempted Cancellation at Pickup:Upon arrival at the rental location, Flexway tried to cancel my reservation without explanation. No professionalism. No courtesy. Just confusion, stress, and delay. Only after protracted discussions was I begrudgingly handed a vehicle—not the one I booked, and certainly not one that met my needs.Filthy, Unsafe, and Unsuitable Vehicle:The car was in unacceptable condition—dirty, unkempt, and potentially unsafe due to worn tire tread. I had to take the vehicle to a car wash immediately, costing me time, money, and the start of my important trip.I am attaching:A car wash receiptVideos and photos of the car before and after, found here: Photo/Video EvidenceFalse Advertising and Mismatch of Booking Details:I reserved a 7-seater suitable for transporting VIP guests—what I received was not fit for purpose. The back row was cramped and inappropriate for adults, forcing my guests to arrange alternate transportation. The embarrassment this caused during a first meeting with investors is beyond words.Mileage Restrictions on an “Unlimited Mileage” Rental:The car came with a 200 km/day limit—completely unacceptable given I explicitly selected a vehicle with unlimited mileage. This felt like a bait-and-switch tactic that misrepresents what Priceline advertises.Refused Early Return Credit:I returned the car the same night—less than 6 hours after pickup. The Flexway staff acknowledged the return but refused to process it, insisting on billing the full 4-day rental until February 17. This means I paid for a vehicle that was unused and sitting outside their office. It’s exploitative, and frankly, dishonest.Why This Review MattersThis was not just a bad experience—it was a breach of trust. Priceline, by enabling vendors like Flexway who misrepresent services, treat customers poorly, and ignore accountability, you're complicit in damaging your own brand and user trust. If your team doesn't act on repeated customer complaints, then your VIP program means absolutely nothing.Let me be perfectly clear: I will never use Priceline again. And I strongly advise others—especially professionals and international travelers—to think twice before trusting your platform. This experience was humiliating, inconvenient, and completely preventable.I am requesting a full refund for this trip and a formal response addressing why this case has remained unresolved since February. title: Terrible Experience – Lost My Money with Priceline, United Airlines, and Xcover Insurance
text: I booked a flight through Priceline with United Airlines, and before completing the purchase, I was prompted to add travel insurance to protect my money in case I needed to cancel or change the trip. I paid for the ticket with the insurance included, trusting that I would be covered in case of emergencies.Later, I encountered an unexpected emergency and needed to change my flight date. I contacted Priceline, and they told me they couldn’t help because it was a United Airlines ticket, and I needed to contact the airline directly. When I spoke to United Airlines, they said my ticket was a basic economy fare and couldn’t be changed. I explained that I had purchased insurance, and they told me to contact the insurance company.I reached out to Xcover (the insurance provider), and they directed me to submit a claim online. I provided hospital documents and appointment letters and completed the claim process. The very next day, I was shocked to receive an email saying my claim was denied with no detailed explanation.I followed up by calling Priceline again. The customer service agent was very rude and unhelpful. She eventually transferred me to David, the supervisor, who bluntly told me that “your policy doesn’t cover this situation.” No empathy. No effort to resolve anything. Just a cold response and a complete loss of my money.This experience was deeply frustrating, and I feel scammed. I strongly warn others NOT to book through Priceline or purchase Xcover insurance. Their customer service is horrible, the insurance is misleading, and your money is not safe. You will be left alone with no help when something goes wrong.

name: James Bowen
title: This was the worst retail experience I…
text: This was the worst retail experience I have had in my 61 years in life. I booked a trip for my son and I to go to Puerto Rico for my son's birthday. My son is Autistic and non-verbal and when traveling in an airport requires a wheelchair. Long long story short, Priceline gave us an itinerary with the wrong hotel contact information. Our Delta Airlines flight had the wrong gate number on it (which I don't think was Priceline's fault) so we missed that flight. I booked a flight for the next day with JetBlue. That flight was delayed several times over a 9 hour period (again, not  Priceline's fault). During this period, I tried to call the Hilton Hotel that was on our itinerary. It was the wrong phone number. Each time I tried and couldn't get through (the phone number had 3 options and no matter which one you chose, you got a voicemail or were simply disconnected) immediately after each attempt to reach the hotel, I also called Priceline who called THE SAME NUMBER, and just apologized saying they can't get through either. I just wanted to call the hotel and let them know that we were still coming there so I would be sure to have a hotel room when we arrived. Finally after two days, we ended up leaving the airport and had to go to the hospital emergency room because my son was engaging in "self-injury-behavior" as he gets frustrated when forced to wait in one spot for hours. Just prior to leaving the airport, I called Priceline to ask what they were going to do. That representative "googled" the hotel and got a different phone number. We called the hotel on a 3 way call and the hotel clerk stated, "that is not a valid confirmation number, we do not have a reservation for these travelers and our hotel is SOLD OUT, so even if they arrive we can't give them a room". Apparently that was the Hilton Condado, but we were supposed to be staying at the Hilton GARDEN INN Condado, both hotels in Puerto Rico but obviously two different hotels. Priceline had called, and placed on my itinerary the WRONG hotel contact information. The Priceline representative assured me that I would receive a full refund. That did NOT happen. Priceline for months refused to refund even a penny. Someone at Priceline changed my method of payment from credit card (which IS how I paid for this trip) to cash. I was informed of this from a JetBlue representative when I tried to request a refund directly from JetBlue who has a strict NO CASH refunds policy. After I made that request from JetBlue and was denied the refund. Someone at Priceline again went into the JetBlue reservations system and changed the method of payment from cash back to credit card and the credit went back to Priceline. Priceline told me that the Hilton Hotel was refusing to issue a refund because I was a "no show". That also was not true. When I contacted the Hilton Garden Inn Condado directly, the desk clerk informed me that they only amount that Priceline was charged was a $227.25 "one night cancellation fee". I had paid for 8 nights, so Priceline got those funds too. The rental car I rented for 9 days had no phone contact number on the itinerary. I got a $131 refund from that car agency. At one point over the hundreds of hours on the phone with Priceline, on a RECORDED phone call, a Priceline representative told me that he could credit the entire vacation package back to my credit card if I paid WITH A DIFFERENT CREDIT CARD a cancellation fee. I told him that I thought that was wrong but to resolve that issue I would pay the cancellation fee. I asked how much that fee would be and he told me $2000.00 is the cancellation fee. I gave him a good piece of my mind in that call. That was extortion at its finest. In my opinion there is certainly some sort of corruption going on at Priceline. I contacted the FTC (Federal Trade Commission), the BBB (Better Business Bureau) but still no refunds from Priceline. It wasn't until I called Boston's Channel 7 News at their "Solveit7" office that suddenly Priceline started to respond to my inquiries and no longer was sending me their generic "No Refunds" emails. I was originally charged $5353.11 for this trip and so far, thanks to "Solveit7" I have received a little over $4000 in refunds. Interestingly, and in support of my belief that their is some sort of fraud going on at Priceline, all of the refunds went back to my credit card EXCEPT the refund for the JetBlue refunds that I paid on my credit card but someone at Priceline changed the method of payment to cash, Priceline 3 weeks ago said they sent me a check for that refund. Still not received, but nonetheless interesting that they didn't want to issue that refund to the card. BUYER BEWARE!

title: PRICELINE deserve a 0 for deception
text: PRICELINE deserve a 0 for deception, misrepresentation, false advertising and bait and switch.Having used Priceline before, I would never have thought my second booking could go so wrong.I normally write reviews on completion of a trip or service, however this situation has prompted me to look at Priceline’s reviews and on seeing a clear pattern of deceptive behaviour and poor customer service, I’m compelled to write a review 2 days into our trip.All inclusive boutique Hotel in Cancun booked and paid for upfront in March.Booking options included all inclusive pay now and all inclusive pay on arrival.  I opted for the all inclusive buy now due to the lower cost.Booking was confirmed and immediately I noticed ‘free breakfast’ so I contact Priceline via chat and the AI advised indeed booking is all inclusive. Not trusting the AI I emailed customer service. The email bounces, so I call and again am assured booking is all inclusive. Fast forward a week before booking, I emailed the hotel about special services due to trip being an anniversary and my gut told me to ask if they had reservation as all inclusive. Lo and behold they say no breakfast only. I contact the chat again and as clear as day it says my name, the hotel and that the booking is all inclusive, again I call Priceline and the same is confirmed so I relay this back to the hotel.On arrival the hotel again says booking is breakfast only. I’ve come prepared with copy of the chat stating my name, date of booking, hotel name and confirmation of all inclusive. Reception turns the PC monitor around and says well Expedia has only paid for breakfast and board and the amount was 50% lower than what I had paid Priceline. I understand many parties are involved now and commissions are paid etc, but it seems bizarre that the hotel would only receive 50% of what I paid to purchase the package. To make matters worse, the hotel said they had two bookings on the system for me one for all inclusive which was pay on arrival and the other which was breakfast only and paid by Expedia, but still required local taxes to be paid before they could complete check-in.Alarm bells are now ringing. I’m embarrassed, frustrated and tired after a 20 hour journey.It’s 9:30pm local time by the time we check-in and we are hungry.  We are charged an additional cost for our meal.I try calling Priceline 3 times, each time automated system offers a callback, but guess what no callback.I’m now restless and irritable and can’t sleep. I call again at 4am the next morning and finally get to speak with an agent. Like other reviews I’m passed around after they acknowledge my booking is indeed all inclusive. A supervisor escalates and says I will be called back with a resolution and that they would validate with the hotel. 12 hours later, we’ve only had breakfast and not received a callback. The hotel has heard nothing from Priceline or Expedia, so I call back again (at this point I should mention I’m purchasing roaming credit to contact Priceline). title: Misleading Booking, Zero Accountability, No Emergency Protocol
text: I booked a stay at Angsana Velavaru In-Ocean Villas through Priceline, advertised and confirmed as All-Inclusive. However, the reservation I received via Booking.com showed Half Board. I raised the issue immediately and provided written proof of the original offer and legally binding contract provided by Priceline themselves confirming the booking package. That was seven days ago. Despite repeated attempts to resolve it, nothing has been done.I’ve spent over ten hours calling Priceline, out of which four hours on international roaming to US and other six hours from UK to US, only to be passed between departments, hung up on, or redirected to Booking.com — who confirmed that the only contact they received from Priceline was to request a quote for an upgrade, for me to pay extra, not to fix the error.Every time I called, I was told by so-called “supervisors” that there is no protocol in place for this kind of issue, as “it has never happened before.” I was also told that escalated emergencies have no timeline for resolution, yet in the same breath, I was assured this would be handled within 24 hours as a priority.It has now been seven days.I am a few hours away from check-in, and still have no confirmation that the package I paid for will be honoured. The resort has confirmed that an upgrade to all-inclusive would cost over $2,000 — a cost I was never meant to incur.This situation has been beyond stressful and entirely avoidable. Priceline failed to deliver the service they advertised, ignored clear evidence, and offered no real support. Their “emergency escalation” process is nothing more than a stalling tactic.Avoid Priceline at all costs, especially for international or high-value bookings. If anything goes wrong, you are on your own.

name: Hayward Turner
title: Frustrating Experience
text: Frustrating Experience – Website Design Flaw Cost Me Time and MoneyHayward jrI had an extremely disappointing experience booking a flight through Priceline due to a flaw in their website’s name input fields. The site provides four separate columns: First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, and Suffix. Naturally, I placed my suffix in the “Suffix” field as intended. However, once the information auto-populated, the suffix was incorrectly placed after my middle name, causing my ticket to be issued with a misspelled and misaligned name.I only realized the issue when I logged into Emirates directly to check my flight details — something Priceline did not flag. Because of this system flaw, I was told I had to pay $30 for a name correction, even though the error was caused by Priceline’s poor form design. To make matters worse, the agent informed me that if the name correction wasn’t accepted, I’d have to cancel and rebook the flight, costing an additional $120. They mentioned I might be able to request that $120 back through an escalation, but there was no guarantee.After spending 5-6 hours on the phone with multiple Priceline representatives, I’m left frustrated, financially impacted, and extremely dissatisfied. This experience has been unnecessarily stressful and costly for a mistake that should have been prevented by better website design and clearer guidance.Priceline needs to fix the gap in their system regarding suffixes — travelers should not have to pay for their technical shortcomings. I expected better.

I thought at the very least the refund would be straightforward, given that Way.com could not deliver the service I paid for.But instead, what followed was an endless, frustrating back-and-forth with their support team. The dismissive tone and refusal to take accountability made the experience even worse.At this point, I’ve lost money, time, and patience—and I’ve made it clear I will never use Way.com again. text: I will never use Way again.  I've used them several times previously with overnight parking lot reservations and such and had no issues.  But the one time I had an issue, they were completely unhelpful.  I don't blame them necessarily for the bad experience at their contracted parking lot company, but I very much blame them for (1) being completely unable and/or unwilling to remedy the issue (a non-running pickup shuttle) and (2) suppression of negative reviews on their site.After my poor experience with one of the parking garages advertised on their site (Express LAX Long Term Airport Parking) I still pinned most of the blame on the parking garage and not Way, despite Way offering nothing in the way of real assistance.  That said, I was confused as to how a garage with a sterling 4.6/5 rating from nearly 600 ratings and 60 reviews somehow left me and those waiting on a shuttle with me with the completely opposite experience.  I thought maybe we were just very unlucky considering no one in the reviews made mention of the shuttle or non-responsive staff being a problem.  Even if my situation was a weird, poorly timed one-off, I felt that other travelers should be made aware and attempted to leave a negative review of the parking garage on the Way.com site.  The post was pending review and I got a bit suspicious.  Sure enough, the review didn't post after a few days.  I thought, well maybe technical difficulties...and tried again a couple of times to leave the same review.  Again, the review never posted.  So then I checked Google, and as I begin to suspect, the parking garage had a very subpar rating (2.3/5) with many recent reports of the same exact experience that I had.  It became obvious to me that Way was intentionally suppressing negative reviews (and perhaps even adding fake positive reviews).  I have no other potential explanations of the disparity between the positive reviews on the partner site and the many negative reviews on the independent site.What is really unfortunate about this violation of business-consumer trust is that in my opinion it is unnecessary--there are *many* other parking garages in the area on their platform.  If one garage had a poor rating, I would simply take my business to a different facility on the same platform.  This breech of trust and violation of what I consider to be good business ethics is unforgivable and I will never use the site again, and I will discourage anyone that I know from utilizing the service as well.

text: I have been using globalairportparking.com for many years as I travel (fly) nearly every week. They never showed up after quite some time... upon call back, the hotel employee said that they thought we were an airplane crew, so the shuttle van never showed up.  They said we could wait 45 minutes or call an Uber.  So 30.00 and an Uber drive later, finally got into our car on the hotel property.Upon calling GlobalAirportParking's phone number to tell them about this incident, they initially said that they would "investigate," and then said that they have to call the hotel to verify and go through a process.  I learned that they did call the hotel, but the employee that made the error already left for the day and they asked us for the name of the person we spoke to that made the error.  Are you kidding me?  How would I know or remember that for a shuttle ride?  Why would I ask this person's name during the phone call and why would it matter?  Now I know better.I had to send a string of emails and go back and forth to finally receive notification that they would reimburse us only 25% of our total cost of parking, which was only 17.87, which was whopping $4.27!  We were out the 17.87 AND the 30.00 for the Uber... when I told them that wasn't fair, they offered 15.00 in "Way Bucks" which is basically credit toward a future parking reservation.It's not the money, it's the principle of it of course! So I'd like to share this bad review to the public to make sure you get the person's name who made the mistake, write multiple emails and phone calls to this company (over 2 hours into this so far) to only gain more frustration and grief.Tessa was the customer service person who I dealt with via numerous emails, but maybe she is not allowed to refund money, but nonetheless, they could have done a much better job.Buyer Beware... normally good, but not this time!

Each customer service rep I spoke to was harder to understand than the last and they kept making things unnecessarily complicated and did not treat me with any sort of understanding. They just kept repeating the same unhelpful things and did not provide any sort of solution and after weeks of trying to remain calm and giving everyone the benefit of the doubt, I realized no one would listen to me unless I got MAD. I had to relive the stress of that day and repeat the same story over and over again to multiple people because I kept getting passed along. title: Way.com Nightmare
text: On Aug 2/24, aiming to Park my car for 10 days before catching a cruise to Alaska, I appeared at the hotel below to park at this doomed reservation I had made on July15/24 through Way reservation at a MC charge of $128.51CDN:Confirmation No. # OGI46482721Extended Stay America Southcenter SEA Airport Parking15635 W Valley Hwy, Tukwila, Washington, 98188.On arrival, I was informed in a very aggressive manner by the hotel that we were the third client today who presented at their hotel checkin misled by way.com which "appeared to be overbooking their hotel for car parking".  I was told to "find some other place to park".There was a 30 minute taxi required to get to Pier 66 in Seattle from the parking site and although I had arrived before noon I was now faced with having to research on my iPhone where I could Park my car for 10 days before the window for checking in on my cruiseship 1 to 1:30 PM closed.  Because of your company overbooking me, I had to find only what Parking was available that day and the cost of that was $220.40USD/$315CDN at the DoubleTree by  Hilton near Seattle Airport. (See invoice emailed to you Aug2/24-18740 International BLVD-Park and Fly) This was enormously stressful to search for, drive to for confirmation and hope the alternative site could accomodate us, with the potential outcome missing the $10,500.00 NCL cruiseship that we believed we had carefully planned for! This was a nightmare situation which we dealt with at a cost 250% greater than promised by Way.com. I cannot think of any other solution than your company stepping up and at the very least refunding the difference in cost, which does not even accomodate the stress and time spent finding and  securing an alternative parking site. You have refunded 130.79 CDN on Aug 2/24. I therefore request, at the minimum, financial compensation for the balance of my parking cost = $315CDN -130.79CDN = $184.21CDN. I remind you I have previously forwarded to you the invoice from DoubleTree.From Way.com:We understand your frustration and the inconvenience you experienced. We have investigated the situation and confirmed that we have a contract with Extended Stay America and did not overbook their parking. While we cannot refund costs not paid directly to us, we are committed to resolving this issue. We have already issued a refund of $130.79 CDN and would like to offer additional support to help mitigate the stress caused. Please contact our customer service team to discuss how we can further assist you in this matter.=================================I contacted Way.com Customer Service as recommended. Here is more evidence of the lack of organization and duplicitous advice from this company:"Hi Chris Mahony,Thank you for your response,Upon reviewing the refund mentioned in the feedback, it is confirmed that the amount of CAN $130.79 is equal to $91.85 is already refundedAs stated in the feedback, we cannot issue a refund for an amount that has not been paid to us".So much for "contact our customer service team to discuss how we can further assist you in this matter".My experience tells me that this company acts gratuitously, is unjust and unwilling to take responsibility and is disorganized in its partner relationships. I would advise everyone to avoid usingWay.com. Otherwise, use at your own risk and make sure if you do to phone to confirm with the hotel or partner that the process for booking is trustworthy or better yet, bypass this co. and make the reservation directly.

This is the second time their app let me down and the last.  I prepaid for parking at a lot.  I have the Way app so I didn't print out my reservation (shame on me) I got to the lot and pulled up their app. I clicked on the order on the home screen and scanned the QR code.  It came back and said invalid.  I checked and the one the app pulled up was for a future reservation not the current one, a bug but not the end of the world.  I now have two cars behind me, waiting on me. A couple more clicks in the app and I find the current reservation.  I click the current reservation and instead of giving me the QR code it says, “add your credit card number so we can link it to your account and save you more money.”  There is no way to skip this screen to get to the QR code.  I exit the app and go back in.  I now have 3 cars waiting on me.  I go into the reservation and again it wants me to put in my credit card info.  Mind you, this is not a verification of any kind, it's simply so Way can sell you more stuff.  By this time, I'm at the parking lot, I have 3 cars waiting on me.  I don't have time to pull out my credit card and type it into their app so I can get to the QR code, that I already paid for.  So, I just hit the button on the kiosk to give me a parking slip and go in. I contacted Way customer support and told them the situation.  Ways response was Sorry, but our refund policy doesn’t allow us to refund you.  You must cancel the reservation before your reservation date to get a refund.  I explained to them, I had intended on using the reservation, I tried to use it, but their app blocked me from getting to it.  That I had no way of canceling prior to the reservation since I was at the kiosk at the lot when the Way app failed me.  They responded with the same response.  I tried two more times after this to explain my case.  They just kept hiding behind their refund policy.  Also beware that while making a reservation there is a check box for their Saphire+ subscription.  If you don’t uncheck it every time you make a reservation it starts charging you a monthly subscription fee

name: customer
title: Terrible ... reviews bogus, attendant lies, agent unhelpful
text: Made reservation thru Way.com with BMI parking Orlando.  When I arrived there were a fourteen people with suitcases waiting for a shuttle.  My handicapped wife and I joined the group after checking in.  Twenty minutes later, and with more people now waiting, a shuttle arrived.  The driver got out and left.  No replacement driver.  Twenty more minutes and an attendant comes out as if he would be driving.  People loaded their own suitcases and then got on board, us included.  No driver.  Just heat.  People started getting out.  The attendant said he would get a ticket if he drove, and that a driver was coming.  Twenty minutes later, no driver.  People now started getting Uber and, like me, asked for our keys and money back.  We had to get to our flights.  My car was right by the office where I had parked it to check in.  It hadn’t been parked.  The BMI attendant said that I could process my refund through Way.com.  This all meant, for a handicapped couple, frantically going to another garage and trying to get to our flight.Did I mention the mounds of trash adjacent to the waiting area?I asked Way.com for a credit of Waybucks and was told, that because I had checked in, despite no shuttle as advertised, despite my car not having been parked, despite the distress, they would not refund me.  When I pointed out the shuttle advertised by them was non-functioning for us, they said the shuttle was complimentary and read the fine print.This is a terrible reply.  They have not made just a dissatisfied customer but an enemy.  Spoiling the start of our vacation and not making a simple, miniscule $20 something refund.  Just realize that if you use Way.com, and you end up screwed by the deal they sold, you will get doubly screwed by them.

name: Terry Conner
title: If you drive a full size pickup (ours…
text: If you drive a full size pickup (ours is a 2016 Ford F-150) plan to be RIPPED OFF!  On March 30 I made a reservation for One Switch MIA Parking for the period December 1 thru December 8 at the way.com website.  The description and license plate number of my vehicle was required to make the reservation.  My credit card was charged $46.66 that day by way.com. On November 29 I booked a reservation for my son’s 2014 GMC Sierra for the same time period again through way.com.  The description and license number was again required. The charge that day to my credit card was $45.84.  When we arrived on December 1 at One Switch MIA Parking to check in we were advised that we would each have to pay double because our trucks would take up 2 parking spaces.  I asked why we weren’t charged correctly when we booked the reservation since we had to give the model numbers at that time and One Switch said that was way.com’s problem, not theirs.  I asked that both trucks be parked side by side which would only take 3 spaces.  That was not possible.  So One Switch charged my credit card $90.00.    What a $@ way to start a vacation.  They have you over a barrel because they know you can’t find other parking and get to the airport on time to make your flight.  Also if you don’t check a certain box on way.com you are automatically enrolled in something that automatically charges your credit card $1.95 a month. Stay away from these CROOKS.

name: Carmen G
title: Not transparent
text: I was making a reservation online and their website shows 3 steps for checkout, although the second step already says checkout. However, I selected dates and price and was waiting for a detailed summary of my order when without summarizing the charges it completely checked me out just when I was reading that the lot had no shuttle to airport.  So when I thought I could still cancel the reservation, I had already been charged a total price which was higher than initially quoted because it included fees and taxes. So I bought a reservation without any idea of what the total charges were going to be. When I tried to cancel the reservation, I get this box that I have to accept reward points instead of a cash refund. I thought that these points would be used when I made the right reservation, but there was no mention of how to use rewards again just taking me to checkout.Given my prior experience, I decided that there was no way I would click on the checkout button. Their terms explicitly indicate that cancellations are fully refundable before the start day of the reservation. I had to search website for terms because they are not easily displayed. So the only reason I’m giving a 3 star is because the customer service person said she would credit my card back the charge. We’ll see if this happens.A couple of years ago, I used way to make an airport parking reservation just like this time. I found, then, a website that was easy to navigate with a clear statement that the reservations could be canceled. Now everything seems hidden including the automatic subscription you get at a fee, when you make a reservation. This subscription program is not clearly explained, and with not getting a summary of charges before making the reservation, I didn’t even know about this subscription being also charged. Perhaps if they were more upfront with all their terms and requirements as they were a couple of years ago, they wouldn’t be losing customers like myself. But they are not being transparent making me wonder if someone else bought this app. It is definitely not the same.

title: Way.com Long Term Parking SCAM!
text: I paid for LAX Long Term Parking 11-10-23 thru Way.com as my plans changed last minute and I  needed immediate LAX Airport parking within half an hour of signing up and paying. Their reviews raved how responsive they were in obtaining parking within 15 minutes of signing up which saved multiple reviewers from missing their flights.My experience was far from what was stated.  I ordered and paid for parking at 3:14pm for 4:30pm parking lot entry to make my 7:17pm flight.  I received the Confirmation email forthe parking lot location the next day 11-11-23. I was already out of the country!  When I requested a refund I waited on the phone for 1 hour 37 minutes for Daniel to answer my call. He said he needed to confirm with the parking lot records that I had not entered and parked. I  also needed to forward the PAID receipt for alternate Parking on 11-10-23 because of their untimely confirmation the next day.  I am still waiting for my refund.  I do not recommend this company. Their reviews are BOGUS!  I submitted a claim to my credit card company for reimbursement and did receive an immediate Conditional Credit in full. Way.com has yet to respond OR REFUND MY $197.00 after more than 30 days.UPDATE:  1-12-2024  Still waiting for my refund through Way.com / AirportsParking.com... Good thing my credit card company is persuing the refund for me.I finally received the following correspondence from the Dispute Department, Amy on 12-30-23:We are so sorry for your overall experience and delay in getting this resolved for you.So we do not further delay a resolution for you, by any chance would you be willing to drop the dispute with your bank, so we can have access to your funds?After 2 months, this is the response I receive!Good thing my credit card company is handling the issue and had immediately credited my card in full.....I do not recommend this company.  Be well.  Happy travels!

name: Mr. Byrd
title: Don't fall for their bait-and-switch…
text: Don't fall for their bait-and-switch scam! They overbooked and abruptly changed my parking destination less than 1 hour before my arrival time!They also dared to claim it was a "free upgrade," when in fact it was a downgrade to a less secure parking lot that was about 30% cheaper if you booked directly!Worst of all, this parking lot (ARB parking) they sent me to was notorious for damaging vehicles, which they did to mine, leaving a dent on the front passenger side.Aside from their bait-and-switch tactics, both the app and the mobile website are buggy and do not allow me to log in. They don't send you an email confirmation of your original booking, so be sure to take a screenshot or download a copy of it from the main website. Otherwise, when they abruptly change your reservation to an inferior option, you won't have proof to dispute it - and they will ask you for proof even if they know very well that they are at fault.Their customer service was horrible. They had no intention to help despite the many problems I encountered. So, I was forced to dispute this with my credit card and report the problems to BBB for any hope of action.Ultimately, you should steer clear of this company. They will only cause you headaches.

I ultimately ended up booking parking with a different company alltogether.  2 days later, I saw a charge on my credit card statement from Way.Com. Furthermore, I never received a confirmation email telling me that I have a new reservation, alerting me to this charge.  I believe they broke the law here, by charging my credit card without having my authorization.  I also believe this is systemic for this company, and they probably do this to many customers, as it may be a part of how their business model is designed.   Very shady.  I will never use Way.Com again, and I warn anybody and everybody to stay away, as businesses like this need to be dissolved.

name: Wendell Ricketts
title: In a few words: Never, Ever Use Way.com
text: We reserved SeaTac airport parking via Way.com at the South Tukwila, Washington, Days Inn. We arrived on June 29th approximately two and a half hours before a 6:55pm international flight on which we were booked. (I would note that Days Inn is owned and operated by Wyndham Hotels & Resorts.)We parked and were assured by the Days Inn desk clerk that the airport shuttle would return within 20 minutes at most. I wasn’t happy with this delay, but, at that point, enough time remained before our flight that we had leeway.Once that time had passed, I asked again when the shuttle would arrive. The answer was vague, and I asked the desk clerk to call the driver to find out his location. The desk clerk did so and assured us that the shuttle was “fifteen minutes away.”That time also passed, at which point we began to be concerned about missing our flight. This time the desk clerk supposedly again radioed the driver (he went into a back room to do so, so I don’t know whether he actually called) and was told that he was at the Sea-Tac Airport South Motel 6 and would arrive within 8 minutes. (In fact, according to Google Maps, the travel time between the Sea-Tac Airport South Motel 6 and the South Tukwila Days Inn is exactly 8 minutes.)When the shuttle still did not arrive, I asked again, and this time the clerk said there had been an accident outside the airport, which had delayed the driver. I knew this was a lie because, if the driver had been at the Sea-Tac Airport South Motel 6 as reported, he was already more than three miles beyond the airport.At that point I asked the clerk whether he could provide a taxi voucher so we could call a taxi. No, he could not. I asked whether Days Inn would cover the cost of a Lyft. No, it would not. He had no other solutions and became very snotty. “We share the shuttle with Motel 6, and I can’t do anything about it.”We called a Lyft, which arrived at 5:37pm and dropped us at the airport at 5:49pm, one hour and six minutes before—I repeat—an international flight. That fare was $27.65.When we returned from our trip on 10 July 2023, I called the shuttle via the Ways.com app (which actually directs the user to the phone of the Days Inn in South Tukwila) and was told that no shuttles would be available between the airport and the Days Inn that evening. We were once again forced to call a Lyft, and that fare was $26.66.The total of both Lyft rides was $54.31. When we booked with Way.com, we paid $142.32 (on June 27th) via credit card. That fee was for parking and GUARANTEED AIRPORT SHUTTLE to and from SeaTac Airport. We did not receive that service and, in fact, suffered stress and aggravation, on both ends of our trip, because of Days Inn’s and Way.com’s failure to honor its contract with us.After weeks of trying to resolve this charge, Way.com responded by saying, in essence, "Read your contract. We're not responsible for airport shuttle service."That's utter nonsense. Way.com's rates are LOWER when there is no shuttle service, which means they are increasing the price when shuttle service is included. That means they are charging you for it.And ALL of that means they should resolve bad service like this.

title: False Advertising. No Price Match/Beating
text: I used to love to book all of my airport parking with Way.com but recently It ent to book parking at my local airport park n fly hotel and the rate was double what it usually is. The response just sort of said that their prices were based on availability and time of year and that I wouldn’t find a better deal, but that has nothing to do with price matching the price that I found in another website, as this is something that they said that they did. I can actually still book at the competitor’s site for half the price of way.com. I’m extremely disappointed because way.com was my preferred place to book airport parking but I won’t be using their services anymore. Beware their false claims of price matching/beating.UPDATE (7/21): After reading the response I received from Way.com to my initial review, it is clear that this company does not listen to customers and their feedback nor do they care. I understand that pricing changes all the time and that there are policies and whatever, this review and experience has nothing to do with changes in price on the way.com site it has to do with the advertisement on the parking lot that I wanted to book stating that way.com would beat any price lower than their currently advertised price by 25%. When I contacted them because I found a price lower than their most current advertised price ( at the time) they simply did not respond. I followed up, and they did not respond again. Not until a full 11 days after I came home from my trip did I get a response that simply said that they had the lowest advertised price around for that parking lot… well you didn’t when I was booking and I have already parked and picked up my car and no longer need your services. I was able to find a website that charged me less than HALF of the amount that Way.com wanted to charge for this parking lot for the time that I needed it and instead of sticking to their policy of beating competitor’s pricing, they ignored me and then denied their price having been higher in the first place. OneStopParking did a much better job with this parking experience and I will no longer be using way.com for my parking needs, I suggest you don’t either. Who knows how they will try to screw their loyal customers next.

title: Prepaid parking…voucher refused.
text: I purchased 5 days of prepaid parking from Way.com.  On my return day, June 18, 2023, I arrived early and went to get my car.  My Way.com voucher was not honored.  After multiple calls to Way.com and an extended hold, I finally spoke to a live person.  After an additional time on hold, they advised that because I was leaving the parking facility 25 mins early, my way.com voucher was being rejected.  I was advised to pay the full parking facility prices and submit my receipt "for a refund."  I did so and after several days of inaction, I checked my credit card online.  Not only was there no refund, of either the original amount or the full facility amount I was forced to pay, I saw that Way.com had actually made duplicate charges to my card for the same facility and the same period!When I filed a dispute with my credit card for the second charge, Way.com then advised that I would need to drop my dispute in order for them to reverse the charge.  I called my credit card and withdrew the dispute so Way.com could proceed with the refund.  I advised Way.com the day the dispute was dropped.I then received follow up emails from Way.com advising that I still needed to drop the dispute and I advised them that I had already done so.  Well, I have now received an email from Way.com saying I must provide to them PROOF that I dropped the dispute in order for them to proceed.Never have I ever experienced this kind of run around from any service provider.  I have disputed credit card charges in the past and they were resolved by the merchant directly with the card company. The merchant reverses the charge and the dispute is resolved.  I have never had to cancel a dispute for it to be resolved.I have now been charged $125 by Way.com for services it did not provide in addition to the charges I had to pay to the parking facility in order to get my car out.......because I arrived 25 minutes early.Way.com is an unreliable service provider with atrocious customer services that will give you the run around and not work to resolve any issues with the goods and services it may or may not provide.I would caution against purchasing any goods or services from Way.com and if you choose to do so, buyer beware.  Don't expect any kind of satisfactory customer service from this company.

text: I was considering using this website to make a parking reservation. I did not complete my transaction. I did not receive any confirmation emails or texts. I did not receive any receipt or record of completing the transaction. They said that they have a strict policy that refunds cannot be given for cancellations less than twenty four hours before check in for the reservation. I did not have an opportunity to cancel because I was not aware I had been billed. They have failed to deliver a refund. At best this is a result of them having a shoddy purchasing interface; at worst it is an intentionally slimy method of securing more business that banks on people not wanting to make a fuss over losing $50. If it was the former I would expect a refund and would consider giving them further business in the future. The fact that they haven't makes me think its the latter and I will never do business with them in the future and strongly advise that nobody else does either.You will notice a reply from way.com below indicating that they would like for me to contact their customer service (assuming they do not take it down at some point). I did. Their customer service was terrible. name: Lucinda Lawson
title: Site at SeaTac was dark and no one…
text: Site at SeaTac was dark and no one around. I called and they won’t refund anything. I’ll never use way.com again.

name: Abe
title: Scam artists
text: Was near the airport looking for a 7 day parking location, made a reservation and then found out it was too far for me so I Immediately tried canceling online it didn't allow me to, so I called WAY and the rep told me I can't cancel, so in the end I never parked there but was charged for 7 days instead for them allowing me to cancel within 5 mins of making the reservation or at a minimum charge only one day? Why 7???Beware! They take advantage of their customers.I'm going to dispute this charge on my CC and I encourage all who had this issue to do the same, maybe they will learn to be honest and not steal our hard earned money.

name: Laura Marsh
title: If I could give zero stars I would
text: If I could give zero stars I would.  This was the first time using this service and I was confused with how the booking app worked.  Instead of booking for the correct nights, I booked two reservations for the same night.  I will admit, this was my mistake.  I was traveling, enjoying my vacation with my son and did not think to check the reservation until our return day.  I called Ways to see how I could pay for the days I still needed and was told they could not help me.  When I tried to explain my situation, I was told how stupid I was because their app could not possibly make a mistake.  Because if the aggressive nature of the representative, I asked to speak to a supervisor.  This individual was even worse and left me in tears by the end of the call.  Please do not book with these people who do not have a soul and only care for profits.

name: jeanne takahashi
title: Deceptive cancelation policy
text: The company advertised easy cancelation but In reality they will only refund you in "way bucks" that can only be used by paying to join there service. The price is only average and the advertising is deceptive stay away!

name: Stephen Montgomery
title: Horrible customer service
text: After talking with a supervisor, I received the needed supportPrior to talking to supervisor this was my review:Horrible customer service. I was double charged due to a website issue (blank page after submitting, no obvious confirmation and then reloading of the site). I made reservation about 10 mins prior to check in. Tried chatting with customer service but site wasn’t working with the chat. Finally found their phone number 2 minutes after check in and they wouldn’t cancel the duplicate reservation because it was past check in. They told me to email them. Tried that multiple times and just got no’s and that $34 of way’s money is more important than doing the right thing.

name: Devon Johnson
title: Check the reviews
text: Check the reviews, you'll see a common thread to this - found parking for $10, but was charged $38.  Not what I signed up for, incredibly dishonest service.

name: David Alvarez
title: Recommended by a friend
text: Recommended by a friend. Purchased 2 parking passes showed up parking lot was full. Attendant told me to go around so shuttle can get out. Went around and more cars out in the middle of the street with heavy traffic. Attendant then asked me to park outside of lot  in the grass between fence and street grass area that was very bumpy not for a luxury car. Attendant then said if you don’t want park there , to call cancel get a refund. Way wants me to provide a receipt for other parking used. I did and still no refund. Unprofessional at every step of the way. Would not recommend parking lot or way.com to anyone. I would rather pay more and have no hassles. Specially at an airport parking when time is limited and don’t want miss flight.

name: Larry G
title: Do not use, they don't guarantee reservations!
text: I made a reservation two months in advance for seven days and when I arrived at the parking lot (MCO) the lot entrance was closed off. I went to the desk and was told the lot was full.I went to the only lot available that cost $100 more than I had paid WAY. Com.After contacting way.com all I got was my $40 refund.This is what I was told, "Way is an online marketplace and does not work in these places directly and any information we have is provided directly by the parking.Way cannot be held responsible for any services, not rendered. I would request you to please check our terms and conditions for more information regarding additional concerns. "Had I known this I would not have used them and neither should anyone else!

name: Valerie
title: Your taking a chance parking is available!!
text: I reserved a spot for an international flight, and no parking was available the morning of my flight. I called, and they had no options. I had to frantically find a spot in a city I knew nothing about and paid more than double for parking. And they won't reimburse for out of pocket costs. Beware and have your own backup plan!

name: Jan
title: Sheraton Pittsburgh Airport 51 minute wait
text: I've used way.com a few times with no problems, but this time, the Sheraton Pittsburgh Airport Hotel made us wait over 50 minutes for a shuttle and neither the hotel not way.com feel like this is an issue. "Please understand that shuttle services are complementary to all bookings and not charged to the customer and that the charge paid by the customer is for the parking which you have utilized" is all I got from either. They don't seem to understand that without a sensible shuttle service, parking would not be booked.Details: We arrived at PIT on 12/19 a little late but I had all my luggage and was ready for pickup at 10:21 PM when I called the hotel the first time and was told that the shuttle would take 20 to 25 minutes. I tried to call the hotel again at 10:49 when every shuttle but ours had arrived but nobody picked up the phone. I called again at 10:53 and was told that it would take another 20 to 25 minutes for the shuttle to arrive. At that point I started arguing with the hotel personnel that this delay is not acceptable, they should have a different shuttle pick us up if theirs isn’t available and that I’d need compensation for the delay. They lady said that she’d talk to her manager the next day and let me know. I have not heard back from the hotel. The shuttle finally arrived at 11:12 - 51 minutes after my first call. During this time, we saw pretty much every other shuttle pass us at least twice including “Globe” that sometimes takes customers to below hotel, but this time did not get a call to do so (we asked).Quick update on the response from way.com below: It says to “Please feel free to contact our support team at (408)-598-3338 for further assistance on this matter.” I did and the assistance was zero – just exactly what they had said before. This once again proves how little way.com cares about their customers’ time.

name: David Francois
title: SERVICE IS HORRIBLE
text: SERVICE IS HORRIBLE!No customer service available.There is no shuttle available  even though they mention one at the website.They won't reimburse your money even if you decide to cancel a service.STAY AWAY OF WAY.COMTHEY ARE A BUNCH OF THIEVES !!BEWARE! DO NOT USE WAY!

name: Keenan Melvin
title: scam
text: scam. I booked parking on their website, arrived at the parking lot only to be told they have no relationship with way.com.

name: Michael Pierce
title: Worst travel and parking aggregator…
text: Worst travel and parking aggregator ever. Seemed like a scam from the beginning. Booked Airport parking in Oakland and never sent me an address for the parking space, an email for receipt or parking instructions, and then, after our entire flight and trip got canceled because of the Southwest meltdown around Christmas 2022, charged us for a full week even though we only parked at our space for four hours (paid for 6 days) and the local parking company--who was awesome and gave great customer service--resold and booked our space within hours of us sadly slumping back to retrieve our car. WORST customer service ever!! They incurred ZERO cost and traded their $15-$20 margin for robbing my family of $120. We booked a $500 for a week rental car (and 3 other pre-paid activities) that were "un-refundable" and ALL refunded us instantly because of the once in a lifetime flight cancellation Southwest situation. Talked to the manager. No empathy. No brand foresight. Just rigid, inflexible, dickishness.

name: Beverly West
title: The parking & transport to Orlando MCO…
text: The parking & transport to Orlando MCO was seemless. The return was not good.  Chose this parking because it picked up on the Delta B terminal but when I called they said 15 minutes.  Ok that is acceptable.  30 minutes no show then they said they would pick up at A terminal only. No way with all this luggage!  Another company took us & 3 other groups to A terminal & waited there another 30 minutes.  Very poor communication 😕.  The reason we booked was because of long term parking & available to pick-up at B Terminal in Orlando! I would not use this service again due to lack of communication. Good app, poor service.

name: Paulpa 'Mchale
title: Terrible place
text: I arrived at 7653 narcoosee rd. Orlando Florida at 1:00 am , the staff was very unorganized and rude, after waiting over an hour with no car in sight I kept asking them when I would be able to get my car, and the staff kept “no English “ after they spoke perfect English previously, I finally got my car at 2:50 am (one hour and 50 minutes later) I will never park there again!!!

name: Rich Silverman
title: Egregious Cancellation Policy
text: Terrible customer service and cancellation policy. I pre-paid for five nights of parking near LAX for $100. The issues started when I arrived at the garage and couldn’t access the QR code to enter the facility because of technical issues with the app. After pulling aside and calling away customer service, I was finally able to park. When I got to the airport, my flight was ultimately delayed 8 hours, which meant I would miss my connecting flight by about 7.5 hours. The airline could not offer me a viable alternative and I wound up being forced to cancel my entire vacation on the spot. Three hours later I returned to the garage to get my car. I contacted Way for a refund and they told me it wasn’t possible because my flight was delayed and not cancelled, despite being unable to get to my final destination. I am now out $100 to park for three hours and the trip I have been planning for a year is ruined. Thanks, Way. I will never use them again.Update: after leaving negative reviews and tweeting them, I got a partial credit to my account. I would’ve preferred a refund to my credit card but at least it’s something.

name: xtwo f104
title: Fake rates and impossible to get a refund from them
text: They sell you parking spots by publishing lower rates and then once you get to the parking garage they either simply refuse to honor the parking code or ask you for more money to park. Also their refund process is almost impossible to deal with.

name: John Bruestle
title: I arrived at the La Quinta Inn in Costa…
text: I arrived at the La Quinta Inn in Costa Mesa and the person at the front desk told my wife there was no airport parking there.I did not feel safe leaving my vehicle somewhere where staff don't know what is going on. I called to get a refund and both the customer service person and manager were like robots just repeating that they can't issue a refund because the hotel desk person did not turn us away.Park your car somewhere where the employees know what's going on.

name: Lyle Johnson
title: BMI Parking at Orlando? I Think NOT.
text: I reserved a space at BMI parking, offsite at Orlando, FL, for 6:00 am.  At 5:30 am, I pulled into the lot. VERY poorly lit, completely jammed with people trying to check in their cars. I opted to go to economy parking. I called the number on my reservation which kept going to voicemail. I called the company that owned the lot, who told me I needed to talk to WAY.com. I called them a few minutes after 6:00. This person is paid to say no. You can't get them to see logic. He told me that since it was after 6:00, they would charge me the full amount of the charge for the three weeks I was gone. I told him I had tried to call long before 6:00 am but the number I had only went to the lot. He said the number to Way.com was there, but I still cannot find it. He became very rude and sarcastic and I had to hang up on him, which is all he was trying to do.I have since found out that even if I had gotten a refund, it would have been credit for future parking only.It makes me sad that places like this exist. Why is it so important for them to screw the customer when all they want is a refund for a service that was not used.UPDATED REVIEW: I received an automated reply from way.com. It is pretty much the same garbage as all of the rest of the replies. This is the part that I love the most…” While Way does not own or operate any of the locations on our website, we always want to make sure you are getting the best service possible. As a third-party booking company, we rely on our partner locations to inform us of any changes to their service and we apologize that this did not happen in this instance.”Parking at BMI Orlando would probably be fine if they did not have way.com as their parent company. You never deal with BMI except when you drop off your car or ride a shuttle. Booking and complaints are all handled through way.com, and it is way.com who will not refund your money under any circumstances.Buyer beware. You WILL GET what you pay for.

name: Pawel Stefanski
title: Their parking functionality is terrible
text: They hide behind other front-ends (findparking.com, etc) and do not provide effective customer support in case of problems. In my case - I was sold a parking spot 9+ miles away from the airport w/o any means of getting from there to the airport. How's that for a "service"??? On top of that their mobile app lacks a feature to easily & quickly cancel a parking reservation.  Their "customer service" blabs about being sorry, apologizing, etc. but effectively does NOTHING to resolve the issue (edited: see their response below... "they apologize". But did they refund even the parking charges, not to mention the extra costs of last minute airport parking? No.) Never again.Pro forma:  the essence of the online "Find Parking" service at an airport like DCA is, quite obviously, to offer a reasonable alternative to the airport parking.  In case where such parking is miles away from the airport (like in my case 8+ miles), it’s natural to assume that some form of transportation to the airport will be provided AS INTEGRAL PART of the service (& included in price of it).  Otherwise the whole endeavor would make no sense - why pay more for a less convenient parking, or get the parking only to be miles away from the airport w/o any means of getting to it?  That’s WHY I reason that Way.com have not fulfilled the customer service expectations - by accepting a parking request for 5:30 am without providing a shuttle to the airport at substantially the same time.

name: Jason He
title: Worst experience. No confirmation number sent. No refund.
text: Worst experience.Reserved San Jose airport parking at double tree hotel but never received any confirmation number. The hotel didn't allow me to park since there was no confirmation number. I had no time to call them and wait in line and ended up parking in economy lot. Called them 1 day later and asked for refund. They said no. Need to dispute via my credit card.

name: Jillian Lalli
title: Fraudulently charged. I was charged 2 times for my initial…
text: I was charged 2 times for my initial transaction.  I was told that there would be no refund due to the fact I didn't see it it immediately.  Then when I went to get my car I had to pay a 3rd time. Again my fault because I didn't want to fight about it in 20 degree weather at midnight. I put in a fraud dispute with my credit card company and will be lodging a complaint with the BBB.

name: Alex
title: This is a scam
text: This is a scam, plain and simple.  They charge a needless fee on top of whatever you'll actually pay for parking directly to the lot.They also require that you install their app but don't say that until you try and actually enter the parking lot so you have no ability to refuse.  Then when you install the app - SURPRISE! there's no way to retrieve your reservation so you need to make a new one!  Want a refund on your original reservation?  Tough, their support email goes into a void - better just report the transaction with your credit card company.If this app has any use it's to look up parking spots and rates - but then contact the lot directly and never give these grifters a dime.(And of course they reply with some boilerplate legal that has literally nothing to do with my complaints!)

name: Branko Mladenov
title: Problem with online reservations because of internal server error
text: I tried to do online reservation for parking but I got message "INTERNAL SERVER ERROR". I tried it again but with the same result: "INTERNAL SERVER ERROR". After that I received  2 approved reservations via email!? They charged me twice for the same date and same vehicle. It took me a day to get a response from them to cancel one of the reservations. But they did not refund me the full amount they charged me =$26,66. They refunded only $25.12 When I asked for the full amount they said it depended on the exchange rate so they had no obligation to refund the full amount. I am very disappointed that because of their Internal Server Error I have been charge twice. I lost a day in communication with them and they did not refund the amount they took from my account. Will never work with them again.

name: Cafes
title: Paid $$ for nothing!  No refund. No credit.
text: I paid for parking at an airport location.  When I went to the door to let them know that I was parking for 14 days, they had no record of that service.  They were going to charge me again.  I was nearly late for my flight out of the country.  I contacted WAY.com and they did not issue a refund.  They said they would give me a credit but that never happened either.  DO NOT BOOK WITH WAY.COM!

name: Ray
title: No Refunds for Parking Full
text: Pre-paid for a parking spot near the airport for a total of 4 days, but spot was unavailable when we arrived.  After we couldn't wait any longer, had to finally abort and rush to find another lot.  Refund was denied due to "contacting after the check-in date".  Went back and forth with support but got the same response.  Total waste of time and money down the drain.  Lesson learned and we will never use again.  I hope this doesn't happen to anyone else.  Good luck.

name: AnnBeth Giddings
title: AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE
text: My name is Elizabeth.  I booked parking on cheapairportparking.com for the Hilton Miami parking lot but received no confirmation. Luckily I screen shot the success payment received screenshot.  Drove to the location.  The parking facility did not recognize the website or the screenshot.  After 30 minutes verifying with hotel and parking garage, they thought it was fraud.  Paid cash, parked and dashed to airport.  During the conversation with my bank to cancel card, it was uncovered that Way was the vendor.  Researched the contact number and called Way while at the airport. After over 21 minutes talking with the rep and another 7 mins with a manager, my $58 was not refunded.  No credit was given for future parking.  AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE! BEWARE! So I paid for parking twice!

name: Jennie Huynh
title: This website is a total scam. Report them to FTC and BBB!!
text: I booked an airport parking through way.com at the Rodeway Inn airport parking lot. However when I reach the place I was turned away because the parking is completely full. The manager told me that they repeatedly asked Way to close down the listing but it didn’t  happened and they ended up turning many people away on that day. After I was refused service, I had to ask my friend to park at their place because I couldn’t find any other alternative parking lot due to time constraints (my flight was within 30 mins). When I contacted Way, they first told me that they need the business to confirm that I was indeed turned away on that day but they couldn’t call the business and there were no complaints at all from that day. But I later learned that the parking lot received many phone calls that people are in my exact situation. After many email, Way learned that I didn’t park at an alternative parking lot, and they used the excuse that I can only get my refund if I can provide alternate parking receipt, even if the manager at the parking lot confirm that I didn’t park there. I have submitted a charge dispute and also report this business to the federal trade commission and also Better Business Bureau

BEWARE STAY AWAY THEY ARE A SCAM I will call amex and delete their app. Funny I never use prkg apps only the parking lot directly. title: This company is a total scam
text: This company is a total scam.  All the reviews for their parking lot companies are clearly fake.  None of the poor reviews I've submitted have been posted.  One of their parking lot companies scammed me and I ended up out over $900 for parking that I pre-booked and paid $305.  When I contacted Way they told me that it wasn't their problem and didn't respond when I asked about the fake reviews.

name: Jerry
title: I wish I hadn't used way.com
text: I used way.com(i.e. never refund) once and had a bad experience along with many other recent reviewers. The shuttle service wasn't running at the hotel that was advertised to offer free parking, so we then had to pay to uber to the airport, causing us to almost miss our flight. After getting home I reached out to way for a refund, and was sent they're policy statement off of they're webpage that you need a magnifying glass to read that states they're not responsible for the shuttles. That's fine, but shuttle service was main reason I went ahead and booked through them, otherwise I would have used a different service. And the hotel manager said she would authorize a refund when contacted by way. Plus, way advertises the free shuttle, but didn't honor it. So I tried to avoid online complaining, but after reading all the recent reviews, it looks like they DO NOT REFUND any money. I have better things to do than waste my time haggling over $50, but this company was in the wrong. Next they'll probably reply with a happy message apologizing about my experience and give a number to contact that will just waste more time. Choose a better company for parking arrangements.
