name: Rai Simonson
title: Bait and Switch
text: I experienced a bait and switch with Way.com and the parking facility. The website says “fee for oversized vehicle,” but the website doesn’t describe what an oversized vehicle is. I arrived to park my small sized pickup truck and was told at the last minute it would be way more expensive because they charge more for “oversized” vehicles. My vehicle is not oversized and easily fits in normal sized parking spaces. I declined and asked for a refund. The garage told me to contact the website. I contacted the way.com and asked for a refund and was told that because the parking garage created a ticket for my parking stay that I was no longer eligible for a refund. This is a classic dishonest bait and switch. Do NOT purchase parking through this website unless you like the kind of deceptive business practices I have described.

name: Selena B
title: Beware of their extra sales taxes and unscrupulous practices
text: Used "way.com" to reserve airport parking. I was able to select the start and end dates and times. Completed all the other pertinent information including credit card details then the website asked for the vehicle's license plate number and the screen froze. I was unable to continue so I selected the back button on my phone. This brought me to a new reservation. I started again and this happened a total of 4 times. The system never provided a confirmation number so there was no way for a user to know any of the previous reservations were succesful. So I had inadvertently made a total of 5 reservations.When I tried to use the webaite cancel the duplicate 4 reservations the system only showed "Way Bucks" credits for 2 of the 5 reservations and no refund. This all took place between 12:00am and 12:50am 11/27/22.  So I sent them an email at 1:03am to cancel the 4 duplicate reservations. Only to receive a reply that the 3 reservations created for 11/27/22 12:45 - 3:34am could not be refunded because cancelations are required to be made prior to the start of the reservations. This would NOT be physically possible based on the time the reservations were made.When I called both the customer service rep and manager said no refunds could be made. Manager told a bold face lie, telling me that my payments had already been sent to the parking lot company. However, my bank shows that all transactions are still pending.To add insult to injury they are also charging almost twice the amount for our state's sales tax. When I asked how/why I was told it might be a problem with their website.They have unscrupulous business practices that defraud and financial damage their customers

text: I had a fully reserved parking booked through WAY.com. I had a flight early morning on Saturday. When I reached the parking, I was denied a spot because they were full. Looks like this company is a total scam!!PS: Just before writing this review, I got a pop-up from Trustpilot saying that there are many fake reviews reported for this company. And I totally believe that. Just sort the reviews by 'Most Recent' and you will hardly see any positive reviews in the last 2 months. That's the reality of this company.

name: Robert
title: Fraudulent Change Fee When Airline Changes Schedule
text: JetBlue changed the flight schedule for our departure flight from Jacksonville to New York to meet our international connection.  JetBlue and Royal Air Maroc both notified me of the change directly and did not mention a need to re-issue the ticket.  I received an e-mail from AirTkt.com asking me to confirm the time change for the flight, to which I responded.  AirTkt then charged me $25 per ticket to "reissue" the confirmed tickets. The ticket was issued as a through ticket on Royal Air Maroc ticket stock, and JetBlue was perfectly prepared to honor the original ticket without re-issue.  In other words, AirTkt baited me into authorizing an unnecessary re-issue with their e-mail stating that "If you will not reply to the email you may miss your flight."  The email did not mention a fee involved with confirming that I was aware that the airline had changed the flight time.   Finally, AirTkt completed the fraud by claiming that they needed to re-issue the tickets, but no actual re-issue was done.  The ticket numbers remain exactly the same as when first issued in December.  So, AirTkt charged me for something that not only was not "required", but no service was actually provided for the payment extracted.  UPDATE:  AirTkt kept responding to my e-mail with boilerplate pablum about their policies and nonsense word salads.  This morning  I was informed that they would be "making an exception" and refunding my $50.  So, to prospective buyers, I say that you can, in fact, get a good deal on business class tickets from AirTkt, but remember that you are dealing with a consolidator, not a regular travel agency.  Read and understand what you are buying.  Buy separate travel insurance from a third party to cover the price of your non-refundable, non-changeable tickets in the event of an emergency cancellation.  Realize that until you check in for your flight the airline can do nothing with your ticket, except maybe give you seat assignments.  After you check in, the reverse is true.  AirTkt is completely out of the picture.  BUT, as this episode has demonstrated, AirTkt is a sleazy outfit that will try to game you for unearned fees on the back end.  There are other reliable consolidators out there:  Buy from one of them.  If you buy a ticket from AirTkt, my advice is to follow up on the airline's web site to ensure that the airline has the reservation and then never communicate with AirTkt again about that reservation.  Caveat Emptor, and travel on.

name: Deepak Seth
title: Misleading Pricing and Poor Customer Support – Disappointed
text: I booked through SmartFares for the first time after finding it via Google. The fare was shown in euros (€580), and there was no mention that the charge would be processed in US dollars. After payment, I received an email showing a $688 charge—higher than expected due to currency conversion. I accepted it reluctantly but was already concerned by the lack of pricing transparency. Later I noted €623 was already reserved on my credit card for this booking.The next issue was even more frustrating: I was told the booking wasn’t confirmed yet, only reserved, and I’d get confirmation later. If nothing came within 48 hours, I was advised to call a number—which turned out to be unresponsive. Other numbers didn’t work either. The email address on their site bounced back. Only the US-based number connected, where I was told to wait until the office opened. I also sent out a message via chatbot. Finally I reached a representative who told me the booking had failed due to one flight segment being unconfirmed. He offered a confirmation if I would pay another $20 and informed that he has already discounted the higher price by applying a coupon.At that point, I requested a cancellation which was done in the system while I received a message to urgently call back due to an issue with my booking. Finally spoke to someone very responsible, who confirmed the cancellation, assured me a refund would be issued, and emailed the confirmation.While one or two agents were helpful, the overall experience was poor—misleading pricing, broken contact details, and delayed or missing communication. It took a lot of effort to get basic support. I was left feeling misled and frustrated, and I won’t be using SmartFares again.

text: I am facing a medical emergency and have obtained a letter from my doctor stating that I am unfit to fly. Instead, I was informed that if I did not provide a new flight date immediately, the flight would be marked as a no-show, leaving me liable to pay additional fees.I explained that I could not afford to pay for a new flight at this time due to the costs I have already incurred for medical care. name: Lauren Bickley
title: Avoid SmartFares at All Costs: A Nightmare Experience
text: I am writing to express my immense disappointment and frustration regarding my recent experience with SmartFares. On September 1st, I purchased domestic return airfares for my husband and myself. While the initial quote was provided in AUD, I was shocked to discover that upon deduction, I was charged in USD, resulting in an overcharge of $329.88. Attempting to address this issue, I diligently reached out to your customer service, flight change, and support telephone lines—none of which ever answered. I then sent numerous Emails to all the addresses I found attached to my flight itinerary including billings department, customer support, and one for schedule changing - all met unanswered for weeks.Growing concerned, I submitted a claim to block my credit card transaction and initiate an investigation through my bank. Despite being informed that the investigation would take longer than expected, I finally received a voicemail from the billings department at SmartFares, assuring me the matter would be resolved. After 2 more attempts to make contact, my refund was received in my bank.However, the nightmare didn't end there. I had booked the 6.40 pm return flight where I would arrive home before 10pm. Any later and I would be arriving home at midnight. Although it was a premium price to fly 6ish, I am pregnant and knew I needed to pay that price for comfort. Shortly after my refund was issued, I received an email stating a schedule change, pushing my departure to 8.50 pm. To add insult to injury, there was a 6.10 pm flight available, a mere 30 minutes earlier than my original booking. Despite my 16 attempts to rectify this through SmartFares, I was met with incompetence and lack of responsiveness. Each time, I was promised a resolution from the schedule change department that never materialised.Upon reaching out to Virgin Australia directly, I learned that SmartFares can grant authorization for the airline to take authority of the account and make the simple change. Despite my plea to Mack within the scheduling department, I have received no reply or further assistance. My numerous attempts to contact SmartFares were met with the same templated responses, advising I was placed on a few different 8ish timed flights and frustrating dead ends.This experience has been beyond disappointing. Having traveled extensively my whole life (Including the international role I worked in until covid arrived where I would fly a minimum of 4 times a week for over five years), I have never encountered such abysmal customer service. The lack of communication, the run-around, and the utter disregard for my wellbeing or concerns have been nothing short of distressing. It is inconceivable that a company can treat its customers this way and still operate.To anyone considering booking with SmartFares, I implore you: Avoid this company at all costs. The time, energy, and distress endured in dealing with their woeful customer service are not worth it. You will not seek a resolution. Choose any other travel centre or book directly with the airline for your peace of mind.

name: Bruce Richardson
title: Predatory 3rd party Priceline.com service
text: The 3rd party service, GuestReservations.com I am told by an IHG hotel is owned by priceline.com.  This said, Priceline.com customer service has no record of reservations made on this site.  The site's predatory practices should have you blocking guest reservations.com along with priceline.com sites because as the following example will show, they are clearly a sleazy and predatory organization.  Now let me explain why.  After using them twice, I made a 3rd reservation in 3 weeks on guestreservations.com that needed adjusting.  The hotel told me that they were locked out of the reservation and that any changes had to be done by the third party. I waited for over 1.5 hours on hold with guestreservations.com, listening to the most annoying music loop followed by a repeating message telling me that my call would be answered in the order that it was received.  I finally hung up, understanding that they were never going to answer the call. The hotel advised that since they were locked out they had no choice but to recreate the reservation and that I would need to get hold of guestreservations.com at some point soon to cancel the incorrect upcoming reservation flat.  They advise that upon receiving my request that the 3rd party should contact the hotel to verify and then should process the cancellation flat.  I finally got a hold of the website's customer disservice dept the following day, speaking to somebody clearly located in India.  She advised that their policies allowed no option other than to process a cancellation retaining roughly 80% of what was paid.  She was immovable on this subject, continuously repeating the position.  I then explained what my policy would be... To never use their service again and to educate others in advance to avoid being taken advantage of in a similar fashion.  She didn't care.  I told her to feel free to diary my information and check back in one month, 6 months and a year to confirm what their lack of customer service has cost them.    Ironically, I found their pricing is also higher than what I have been offered by the hotel the last few times that I have compared rates for curiosity's sake.  Anyone that chooses to still use them, has been warned and does so at their own peril. I hope this helps save others from being taken advantage of in a similar way.  Best of luck!

text: *** Update*"**What a comical response below. They don't give you a reservation or confirmation number. I'll be taking further action to have this company investigated.They literally spoofed the ACTUAL hotels website I booked with (I almost always book direct) AND even charged it to the name of the hotel on my credit card. I booked a suite. I got here and had a "mini suite" booked in my name with a $300+ price difference. We realized on check in that was NOT our room and when they gave us the check-in paperwork, the price whoever booked this paid was over $300 cheaper than what I was charged. They added a fake phone number, email, and address to my reservation. The room was booked with a MasterCard that wasn't even mine. We refused to sign our name (since that's clearly a card that doesn't below to us). They don't send booking confirmations and if you call their customer service it says to "contact the hotel directly". FRAUD. Will be looking into reporting to law enforcement.

title: This is a scam - cancelled my stay and refused my refund
text: Update: Guest reservations replies to my post here and again tells me to email them. But I already have, to the same email they provide multiple times. Twice before hanging up, I asked them NOT to cancel my booking as I needed the hotel reservation - unless the refund was confirmed.Shortly after hanging up, promising me they would follow up. Then I promptly received an email confirming my hotel reservation was cancelled. Then after my numerous email exchanges, still no refund.You cancel my hotel reservation then refuse to refund?I was forced to make a separate booking with the hotel.The last time they would email me back, they said their 3rd party booking partner had received full payment but refused the refund request. But the hotel confirmed with the said 3rd party directly, who confirmed by email that they never received any funds.Guest reservations stipulated that I must get an email from the hotel with name and title of the hotel employee, stating they will agree to the refund. But they cannot write me such an email because #1. their mysterious 3rd party agent never received the funds, and #2. the hotel itself never received the funds (which would be paid to them by the 3rd party agent).I had to pay AGAIN to make the same hotel booking directly on the hotel's website. The hotel kindly provided me with their correspondence with the said 3rd party agent. I sent all this plus my correspondence with the hotel to Guest Reservations as asked.But when I sent all this, all communications stopped. They're not even pretending to entertain the refund request now?Since it seems from the reviews that "some" people do get their refunds, can someone at Guest Reservations help me with a refund? Not sending me to another generic email with no response.

text: Be really careful when buying through the website.It IS LEGIT. name: Kaat V.R.
title: Warning: Misleading and Possibly Fraudulent Booking Platform
text: Due to an error in the booking system of Guest Reservations, our hotel reservation was confirmed twice within a span of two minutes. It is technically impossible to complete two separate bookings in such a short timeframe. Despite this clear glitch, Guest Reservations refused to refund the duplicated charge, stating that by completing the booking, we agreed to their terms — even though the second confirmation was triggered by the platform itself, not by us.Moreover, this platform is highly misleading. It gives the impression that you're booking directly through the hotel’s official website (in our case, UNA Hotels), only to find out later that you’ve unknowingly used a third-party platform.To make matters worse, at the end of the booking process, an additional fee of nearly €500 was charged — and to be clear, this is not a city tax. No transparent explanation was given for this charge.We are currently exploring legal action and wish to use this review as a warning to both potential travelers and hotels. From our experience, this platform engages in practices that are deceptive and highly questionable, if not outright fraudulent.Avoid Guest Reservations at all costs.24.04.2025 - Addendum following the response from Guest Services to my review:We would like to point out that we already informed your company more than a week ago of the issue via the email address you mentioned below. name: frances Firmin
title: Maybe not a scam but a very deceitful business model
text: I thought I was booking with Ritz Carlton Santiago from the look and feel of the website which came up on google.  I missed the small  logo from this business network operation in the top right corner so did not realise I was dealing with an aggregator.  The price of the room was was very reasonable so I proceeded.  The money was deducted from my account straight away. The receipt and confirmation showed a large uplift for fees and taxes but I had paid by card.  The charge on my card statement showed payment to *Hotel Ritz Carlton*.   I arrived at hotel and as previously advised would happen I was asked for credit card, I thought this was for incidentals although the charge was high but I thought it would be reversed on check out. On check out the hotel charged the full amount for the stay, I still thought the transaction would be reversed. After I left the hotel I realised that there was no reversal of the charge.  I contacted Ritz Carlton who said the booking had not been prepaid.   After some considerable difficulty I managed to contact guestreservations.com who "handed" off my complaint to Priceline.   A check on line shows that my booking was made through the guestreservations.com, fulfilled by getaroom.com, confirmed by hotelvalues.com and my complaint is now being managed by pps.priceline.com.  I am currently out of pocket by UK £930 for a booking which I paid at the hotel despite having already paid this organisation  believing it was at very least acting for and on behalf of Ritz Carlton when taking the booking.   This is an appalling way of doing business.  Priceline have twice asked for proof I made the payment at the hotel which I have provided and now have passed on my complaint to "escalations"at Priceline but there has been no response.  I have contacted "legal!" at Guestreservations but they have not replied either.   I want my money back it should be a simple operation for whomever made the hotel reservation to confirm they did not pay for the reservation and to refund my money to me.   There is another issue in that the original charge included an element of "taxes", if guestreservations has not paid the funds to the hotel then they have not made the necessary tax submission so they must be in breach of tax laws and regulation.

title: "Guest Reservations" is a SCAM! Stay away!!!
text: Guest reservations is a scam. On 2/24/2025 I made a 2 nights reservation at a hotel oversees through "guest rereservations.com". The night was $154.25. After using my credit card and paying for the 2 nights, the total charge showed as $435.98 that included $127.45 as Tax Recovery Charges $ Service Fees. I immediately received a confirmation email, but this time from "confirmations" @ "hotelvalues.com" . The email stated that my reservation has been prepaid and is fully guaranteed. To my surprise when I arrived to the hotel on 3/23/2025, the date of checking in, there was no trace what so ever of my booking at the hotel. None of the reference number, the confirmation number, nor my first and or last name showed any made reservations what so ever. I had to book another room and pay again to stay in the hotel. After returning to the US I contacted the help and support phone number to get a refund. They asked me to direct my request through an email with all evidence, which I did immediately. I include the checkout email from the hotel and the new invoice. Except this time I was given the email address of  "customercare" @ "pps.priceline.com". After a few days of back and forth emails, they informed me that they will not issue any refunds. And thus, I lost $435.98 to this scam.Be careful and stay away from these online services. They will show you how good of a deal you are making and try to rush you into making the payment. The case I created with price line is case #CN06109840. My booking reference is #R5470458243.Nabil M.

title: Avoid GuestReservations.com at all costs!
text: This website is a complete rip-off. I was charged even after I cancelled the transaction before final confirmation—just after entering my card details. Good luck trying to get in touch with a real person or get a refund. I wasted hours trying to resolve the issue and am still chasing my money back.Do yourself a favor: DO NOT use GuestReservations.com. name: Wendy Knight
title: I regret the day I booked through Guest…
text: I regret the day I booked through Guest Resrvations. I was looking at a hotel room for 3 nights for a total price of  £385 in a Travelodge hotel. I was looking to see if I could get anything cheaper decided I couldn’t so went back to Travelodge. A window popped  with a special deal of £304. When I went onto the payment page a clock was ticking saying I only had 10 minutes to get this deal. The price wasn’t on the payment page so I clicked back to check that £304 was correct. It said it was non refundable but at £304 it was a bargain so I went for it. Once I clicked pay, the price of £912 came up! I immediately contacted the company but they stuck with their non refundable line saying they would just refund 20% as a good will gesture.I have ended up paying over £700 for a room in a cheap hotel. I believe they know what they are doing when they put that window up with the clock ticking. They know that there is no way that anyone would think the amount they quote as a special deal would be for one night only. How can it be. Special deal when it is so much more than what you would pay direct to the hotel.

name: Emily Franklin
title: I made an IHG hotel reservation through…
text: I made an IHG hotel reservation through a third party who call themselves “Guest Reservations” for dates 6/26 - 6/30. When I booked, I chose the ‘pre-pay’ option because it was slightly lower cost. I did not realize, nor did they make it clear until after booking, that it was 'nonrefundable'. Additionally, Guest Reservations clearly intend to deceive customers by appearing to be the hotel website, which is what I thought when I booked.Fast forward a couple months and my travel plans changed. The email confirmation said to call x number if I need to make any modifications. But when I called and explained that I will only be staying for two nights instead of the original four, they told me that they cannot make any modifications and that my only option was to cancel my reservation WITHOUT a refund, and then rebook with the correct dates. What?? They told me there was nothing else they could do for me, and that I’d have to reach out to the hotel to change my reservation and to get a refund because Guest reservations had “already sent the money to the hotel” - that is a QUOTE from the person I spoke to.I called IHG, and the person I spoke to was was able to resolve the issue, so I thought at first, by calling Guest Reservations and asking them to cancel my original reservation and refund me the full amount. They agreed to do this (according to the IHG person I was speaking to). IHG rebooked me for the correct dates. in the meantime, 6/28–6/30.The issue is that Guest Reservations never actually cancelled my original reservation, nor did they refund me the $1600+ that was promised. When I called IHG they told me Guest Reservations is the only one who can refund me the money. So Guest Reservations lied to me, saying the hotel would have to refund me. Then they lied to IHG, saying they would cancel and refund me.This is a terrible business model and they make their money by deceiving customers, and then lying to them when any changes are needed.

name: A. R.
title: WARNING!!! - ATTENZIONE!!!
text: On 11/03/25 I booked a room  for the night between 11 and 12 March 2025 at  Hotel Isa in Rome through their website, the appearance of which led me to believe that it was the Hotel Isa's website.At the time of payment, which should have amounted 320.98 euros, I was charged an additional fee of 124.75 euros that was not declared during the booking process and was not due.I sent a written complaint asking to be refunded as soon as possible, otherwise I will turn to the judicial authorities to protect my rights.In data 11/03/25 ho prenotato una camera per la notte tra l'11 e il 12 marzo 2025 presso l'Hotel Isa di Roma tramite il sito web di Guest Reservations, il cui aspetto mi ha portato a credere che fosse il sito web dell'Hotel Isa.Al momento del pagamento, il cui totale ammontava ad euro 320,98, mi è stata addebitata una commissione aggiuntiva di 124,75 euro che non era stata dichiarata in fase di prenotazione e che non era dovuta.Ho inviato un reclamo scritto chiedendo di essere rimborsata il prima possibile, ove non venisse effettuato ho intenzione di rivolgermi all'autorità giudiziaria per tutelare i miei diritti.

name: Alexandre Oliveira
title: Awful
text: I made a reservatoon at Porto City Hotel. The amount raised from 52 to 83 due to taxes(!). Tried cancelling the transaction, but it was not.possible. I tried to.contact but there is no email available. The contact form needs a reservation number, but the email received from Giest Resrrvations didnt have one!Very disapponted

name: Brih Ngh
title: Horrible Customer Service - False advertising
text: Unfortunately made a booking through the platform which advertised breakfast, wifi and shuttle. When the confirmation received, shuttle was not included amongst other things.Stayed on the line for customer service for over 2 hours, and called multiple times, only to be able to be assisted by the Sales team who do not have the tools to view or change any bookings.Strongly advise to stay away, save yourself the hassle and book directly with hotel or other reputable platforms.

name: Sarah
title: Fraud
text: Booking on the website indicated was not the final invoice. It was tripled by the time I paid.For Example, on the Website, for the duration of my stay it stated £222 (3 nights). And when I clicked on Book Now, the next page was to enter my details and submit. Next thing I get is a confirmation email for £661.85.This was nowhere indicated on the website at time of booking. When I called customer service, they said that the increase of cost was due to taxes, and they broke down multiple taxes that I was being charged for which was not indicated or mentioned on their websites. This is false advertisement and misleading and should not be allowed to do this.Update: I have reached out to Guest Reservations as per their response to my review, and have had no response. Thus making me think they are scammers.I have since then reported my incident to the crimes unit and this company has been flagged up as fraudulent.My case is now under investigation.I have yet to hear from GuestReservations.comI have fallen victim of a fraud. Please be aware of that and they should not be trusted.If you are also a victim please raise this to stop this company from inflicting their schemes on anyone else. They must be stopped.

name: Anna Kinsella
title: Guest Reservation Site
text: I booked a 2 night stay in a Radisson Hotel in Ireland. They charged me an extra €125 for taxes and services. I tried to cancel but was told it was non refundable. BEWARE! I will never use this site again.

name: Greta
title: Almost 50% of taxes & service fee
text: I e-mail them asking for the taxes and service fees (which is hidden), they didn’t reply as of now. I read about the bad review about them and now i’m not advising anyone to use this website! Never again

name: Brian
title: FRAUDULENT - SCAM
text: STAY AWAY!!!! They are not affiliated with Hilton as their website suggests. Hilton Conrad actually told me that they have received numerous fraudulent claims for other members who booked through them. After cancelling and them refunding my trip which made them appear legitimate at first, they charged me again the same day under another false company (Priceline.ccs.com.) I only learned this after having to call the number provided next to the charge on my credit card.  They continually will charge your credit card if you do not notice and send pings (per the Discover agent) to see if your card is still active and will repeatedly charge hoping you do not notice.

name: Richard  W
title: DISHONEST   DESPICABLE AND DUPLICITOUS  BEWARE
text: DISHONEST:    This company clearly pays Google to get its advert placed at the top of the listing when searching for hotelname + reservations.   The website name then begins with hotelname.guestreservations.com which is a deliberate and dishonest trick intended to fool customers into thinking that they were accessing the hotels own guest reservation website.The prices are then significantly higher than the hotel's own website or via one of the major reputable booking chains.     Dishonest,  despicable and duplicitous in my opinion.

name: Alex Sanders
title: Classic scam!!!
text: This is a classic scam of a company.if you see them - run away!Otherwise you risk of paying 50-100% more than what you saw on the reservation page for your accommodation.It is a absolutely astonishing that no consumer protection agency is dealing with these scammers.They trick you with the deign of a page to make you believe you are at the hotel’s own reservation page - beware you’re not!You see price per night - that looks reasonable or attractive and you never see the total sum to be charged or those junk fees they add up before you click the pay button - once you click pay - all of a sudden you realize that you’ve been charged a total sum that is significantly more than the price per night that you saw on the reservation page.Upon booking, I did not receive the booking number or invoice - all of this is designed so that it makes it difficult for you to realize what has happened and why were you charged so much.When you try to call them - it is difficult to bypass the automated messaging system - but once you manage to speak with the real person - they put you on hold, pretending to be “checking your reservation” and keep you on hold for more than 30min - they do that deliberately so that you just give up.I spent an hour on the phone from two attempts with their “customer service” - they just repeat the same script - and the operators there know they are working for a company that tricks people paying junk fees on top of actual hotel room cost.Look it up on YouTube and google - massive number of people complaining about how they operate.From outside looks like a legit company - but it’s all to trick you - don’t fall for it.Remember - NEVER EVER book with them!

name: coordinator
title: They are not a scam
text: They are not a scam. I made a transaction with them and requested a refund on the same day. I received the full refund within two days.I made the refund because I got a good offer from Make my Trip.

name: James Kelly
title: I am a regular user of Travelodge web…
text: I am a regular user of Travelodge web site and yesterday I booked a 3 night stay on their site with a saver rate of€321.00.When I checked my email to make sure booking was confirmed I found that this company had accessed the booking system of Travelodge and confirmed my booking at a cost of nearly €500 which is way above what the 3 night stay was advertised at by Travelodge. I request that Guest  Reservations .com refunds me either the difference or the full amount now.  This to me is not a great experience and I am not at all happy with the way Guest Experience.com carryout their business. I will be discussing this with both my bank and Travelodge in the morning. One other point they asked me to quote my booking number in all correspondence but never furnished me with one.James Kelly

name: Dee

name: sherry diez

title: This company is a scam: STAY AWAY AT ALL COST
text: This company is a scam: the advertised prize is not what is withdrawn, and the money was drawn without the mandatory code+text confirmation.I spend an hour waiting for their 'customer service' without ever reaching a person who could help, despite "free cancellation" policy.I never received an email confirmation so I only know my reservation number because I took a screenshot of the confirmation page.I have written my bank to try and stop the money transfer, this is a fraud.

text: No email, no response, no confirmation.Need a room but now no idea.

name: Kate
title: Room rate was €125. Charges €195
text: Room rate was €125. Charge me €195. Didn’t send me a confirmation email or booking reference. Phone line on website is automated and required itinerary number  this to get through to an agent. Eventually I got through to someone in the sales team who found my booking and provided me with the itinerary number. And said there were €60 euro in charges that covered ‘free breakfast’ and parking that I did not book. And hotel fees. A complete scam. Nowhere in booking journey were any of these fees highlighted.

name: Jürgen Wente
title: A website to ribb you off
text: I tried to book a Hotel in Berlin for two nights. However the websites functions in way that a better price offer  changes the terms without mqking you aware of the changes, in my case the dates were changed (1 day backward ) and the cancellation police altered. Instead of of notifying me of this changes a popp up Windows told me: book now, just 1 room left at this price.When I received the booking confirmation with the wrong dates I cancelled immidietely within Minutes and requested a booking for the correct date.  Of course this was refused, neither refund or rebooking.Conclusion: a website to ribb you off

name: Paul de Ronde
title: Very bad experience
text: Very bad experience. Booked a room and was subsequently asked to share my credit card details, which I did. Then found out the room wasn't booked and got a two sentence message informing me that the place was fully booked without any compassion, let alone a solution.

name: Julie
title: Unresponsive, unhelpful and deceitful company which steals your money
text: This is a deceitful and unhelpful company.Firstly their web address deceitfully appears to be a direct link to the hotel itself - it wasn't. Secondly the price they first quote is not the full price - I noticed  when my credit card sought verification on their app I that they had added an extra £102.40, so I declined the transaction, however it still went ahead anyway.Thirdly I tried immediately contacting them about this twice through your website and was twice told I would get a response within 24 hours – no responses ever came.Finally when I contacted the hotel today they told me that the room had been booked through Booking.com - which I did not use. However the hotel had sent a message to say that the hotel was closed that week but they had booked me into another and was I OK with that. I never received this message because it went to Booking.com and Guest reservations did not forward it to me. So not only was I not getting what I had booked,  but it also would have led me to arrive at completely the wrong location.Unresponsive, unhelpful and deceitful company which steals your money.

name: Michael Lynch
title: Tried to book a room in Berwick upon Tweed. The real price via Guest Reservations was three times that quoted
text: Tried to book a hotel room in Berwick upon Tweed for three nights. The initial quote was £188. Half hidden at the end of the booking page the price was £563. Thought it a mistake, so phoned the number, thinking I would get through directly to the hotel. Instead, got an American voice. Claimed there were no rooms vacant for my dates. Offered a room in hotel 'virtually next door', at £581. I declined. But I then found a room on a different website which offered a vacant room in the original hotel I wanted for £255. This company is a scam. I don't know why this hotel is signed up with this dishonest company.

name: K. R.
title: it’s a trap / scam with the lousiest after sale
text: Wanted to book 1 night in Amsterdam and by accident booked two nights. When calling twice within the 30 minutes after booking, to get customer service to set this right, the sales clerks instead tried to book me another night, instead of being proactive / understandable.Both nights were not refundable and the customer service doesn’t exist at all, as you get transferred to a tape. They are using a dirty trick of pushing people in to book in a certain time span, with a low price offered on their website (which was very similar to the one of the hotel where I wanted to book). Eventually they charged double/ night on what they offered in the time span. Additionally we need to pay an extra fee when upon arriving at the hotel. This company is ‘how conveniently’ not on Google, as the ratings would be as awful as this one. Horrible company and a true scam!

name: MM
title: DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY
text: DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY! Was looking to book a hotel reservation in London and the price looked good. Pressed to pay and realised that the price was almost double (written in small print at the bottom of the page) quickly closed the page but was charged anyway. DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY!

name: Victoria Gay
title: DO NOT USE
text: The correct date for the booking was entered. The date was changed during the booking process to today’s date. Guest reservation refused to correct the date and the hotel Meon Valley Marriott Hotel would not help. They have stolen our money. DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY

name: Patricia Henry
title: Guest Reservations took THOUSANDS of dollars
text: I mistakenly believed i was on the hotel site. Their website is intentionally deceptive- then i was charged $1600 A NIGHT for a standard room at a Hyatt hotel. The full price is not reflected until it’s too late and they included a thousand dollars in fees. FOUR THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED DOLLARS for two nights in  standard Hyatt……and to top off they only booked me one night at the hotel. (I spoke directly with Hyatt and have the confirmation) It’s absolutely mind boggling. They continue to give me a customer service run around. And the customer service email comes from an @priceline.com email, so Priceline is involved and participating in this unethical practice. So I’m out THOUSANDS of dollars because of this deceptive unethical and downright evil company. I was told today there was ‘no need to keep calling them’   NO NEED??? They charged me two months mortgage for a Hyatt hotel room in Florida. The Ritz Carlton with a meal plan  is cheaper.

text: Very disappointing experience - this website seems intentionally deceptive. Recently booked for a hotel in Vanuatu and the price displayed on GuestResevrations.com was about what we were expecting to pay for the 2 nights accommodation. It was only after clicking to confirm the payment that in the fine print we saw the total to be charged which was twice as much! The displayed price was actually "per night" but that was not shown anywhere except in small font below all the payment information. Intentionally deceptive. It was too late to cancel the transaction. Never again.

name: Anonymous
title: From bad to worse
text: This has gone from bad to worse.I cancelled my reservation on line and received an on-line confirmation that the reservation had been cancelled. However, it is two weeks later and the hotel has still not received confirmation of the cancellation.I tried to call Guest Reservations and if you do not say you want to make a new reservation then you get get put onto Customer Service. I spent 1.5 hours in the afternoon on hold and they never answered at which point I gave up. I called again and said I wanted to make a new reservation and was immediately put through (!) After explaining the situation I was transferred back to Customer Service and back on hold. I did this twice but the last step is always being transferred back to being on hold despite promises that someone would help. I tried asking to be put through to a supervisor and was told I would be, but guess where I was transferred to: Customer Service again !!!!And just to rub salt in the wound I recently received an email responding to my initial review asking me to call - guess what? Yes, Customer Service - aaaaaargh!This is a terrible company to deal with - I strongly advise if you are reading this PLEASE do not use this company - always book directly with the hotel or with a site you are familiar with such as expedia, booking.com etc. My advice from experience is to avoid Guest Reservations if you want to preserve your sanity and the contents of your wallet.

name: Dawid
title: I strongly recommend avoiding…
text: I strongly recommend avoiding GuestReservations.com and ReservationsStays.com. These websites mislead customers into believing they are booking directly with hotels when that is not the case. They use hotel names in their URLs and run Google Ads designed to resemble official hotel websites.Not only do they impose excessive booking fees, but they also create confusion for guests who think they are dealing directly with the hotel. Many frustrated customers end up contacting hotels for refunds, only to discover that their bookings were made through a third party with unfair policies.Such deceptive practices undermine trust in the hospitality industry. To avoid unnecessary fees and booking headaches, always book directly with the hotel or through reputable travel platforms.

name: The Talbot Collection
title: I strongly advise travelers to avoid…
text: I strongly advise travelers to avoid using GuestReservations.com and ReservationsStays.com. These websites mislead guests by using hotel names in their URLs, making people think they are booking directly with the hotel when they are not.Not only do they charge massive booking fees, but they also offer no real customer support when issues arise. Many frustrated guests have come to our hotel believing they booked directly with us, only to realize they overpaid significantly through these third-party sites. This leads to confusion, disappointment, and refund requests that we, as hotels, are not responsible for.These deceptive practices are damaging to both guests and hotels. If you're booking a hotel, always check that you're on the official hotel website to avoid unnecessary fees and frustration.#Misleading #AvoidThisSite #GuestExperience #BookDirect

text: ***UPDATE (reply to GuestReservations)***The customer service was contacted the next day with no help provided, info below.Booking Ref. # 4652054425Booking Confirmation # R5481062666Case Reference Number: #CN05976182Customer Service person - Divine A.Be very careful with GuestReservations.com, better do not use! name: Beverly Fuller
title: Terrible experience - absolute fraud!
text: I am devastated! I just got charged for a booking I didn't even make! I got quoted an amount of EUR 159.20 and went to process the credit card payment. I don't know what to do because I cannot get hold of Guest Reservations telephonically and they just shut me down in the email.

name: Happy Gallano
title: This COMPANY is a scam
text: This COMPANY is a scam. Please be careful. I actually thought I was making a reservation directly through the hotel. I called the hotel to make changes to my reservation only to find out that guest reservation is a third party company. I called  their 866 number and the agent said they are Priceline company. Agent  Jovie won't allow me to change the date of my reservation but willing to cancel my original reservation yet won't guarantee a refund. Fortunately I got a hold of the hotel manager and got my reservation fix.

name: Jurgen O
title: No Customer Support
text: Giving us a valid number to call Support would be a great start! But I guess they don't want all their deceived customers calling to complain, so make it impossible.This is the worst travel company I have ever had to deal with. The actual costs were considerably higher than what's advertised on their site and they pretend to be what they're not (read the fine print!). Bookings are non-refundable. But my real complaint is about their lack of Customer Service.Multiple attempts to call the number they provided for Customer Service / Help / Support (both local numbers and a range of different USA numbers) all sent me to the same call centre. Regardless of the options I selected, the choices always came down to: place a new booking, or go into a loop of listening to messages telling you to call your hotel directly. No other contact information, no interest in actually serving their customers.How sad that their parent company, Booking Holdings, states it gets "The Right Results. The Right Way", and that all its affiliates and suppliers pride themselves on Absolute Integrity.Stay well away from this company. They do not understand the meaning of integrity.----UPDATE: 11 MarchThank you to the Guest Reservations team for following up on my complaint and refunding my booking. While the initial experience was not good, and I would have valued being able to speak to an actual person, your responsiveness is highly appreciated.

name: Bertram Pereira
title: This company is a scam
text: On the 18th of November, 2024 I googled "High Wycombe Hilton" and clicked on one of the first results expecting it to be the official Hilton site, I reserved a room for the 18th of December to 27th of December, 2024. A few minutes after booking after I got the booking confirmation (booking number 98171798 and getaroom booking R5277865375) I called on their helpline to try and cancel. They told me that the booking was non-refundable and cannot be changed or canceled, I informed them that I had looked and can see the exact same room listed on the hilton official site at not only a lower rate, but also 100% refundable if canceled before December 12th. The customer support rep suggested that I make another booking for the refundable room and they would try and talk to their Hilton rep (Tobais I believe) and if Hilton approves, they would cancel my original booking and I could keep the cheaper and refundable one, If Hilton doesn't agree to a cancelation, I could cancel the fully refundable one. They asked for my credit card information again and booked another room (Booking #93218550 and getaroom booking R5277913129).. The very next morning I got a notification from my credit card app that my card was charged $2500 for a Nikon camera and I had to reach out to Nikon to have that reversed. On further correspondence with their support I was repeatedly told that my original booking which was non-refundable was canceled and since it was non-refundable, I had to forfeit the amount and only had the newer booking (93218550) active so I had no option. I reached out to hilton support and was informed that both bookings were active and I managed to get the newer booking canceled, however, Hilton informed me that since this was booked from a 3rd party, they will not be able to issue a refund. I filed a dispute with my credit card company and the next day got an email from priceline (getaroom) stating that a refund has been issued (I am yet to see the refund hit my account)After more than 3 months of fighting and trying to get a refund I had to file a dispute with my credit card company - The company has still not issued me a refund, but given all the evidence I shared with my credit card company, they issued me a creditthis is a horrible company - BEWARE

name: Nicole Reinhardt
title: Stay far away from this website.
text: Stay far away from this website.They do not provide *ANY* flexibility.  I wanted to change from one room style to another - same hotel, same dates, same guests.  They charged me a $900 (!!) cancellation fee and refused to reinstate.  Horrible.  Horrible company.

name: Neela Cleary
title: **Scam alert**
text: They charged me an extortionate “service fee” ($850) on top of the advertised room rate. This excessive fee was unexpected — if you read the other reviews here, you’ll see that many people have been similarly misled by their website.2 days later, I reached out to the hotel directly, and they confirmed they have absolutely no record of the reservation. When I queried this with Guest Reservations, they made the absurd claim that the hotel may not see the reservation in their system until a few days before check-in (almost 3 months from now!!!)Guest Reservations are advising me to cancel my reservation (even though it doesn’t exist outside of their own records) presumably so that they can hang on to the money pursuant to their “no refunds”policy. Total scam. Avoid them at all costs.

name: Gudrun
title: Terrible experience
text: Terrible experience. The site looks like you get to the site of the hotel (name of the hotel you seek in front of the name of this company), but that's not the case. They charge a quite unexpected exorbitant extra fee, which you do not see before your creditcard is charged. In my case, the hotel (one night) cost ca 179 Euros, and the unexpected extra was ca 90 (!!) Euros. This was - according to the company - a 'tax recovery' and 'service fee', including i.a. 'cleaning fees' or 'resort fees'... I have asked to get back this extra fee but have not heard a word.Update: after complaining I got half the fee back. However, I do not change my rating, since it should not be necessary to post a negative review before getting some of the extreme rate back. Moreover, the reason they gave for the fee, is false: They said they have to pay the hotel for i.a. cleaning. This is not true: The hotel had never heard of this company....

name: Judith Orzechowski
title: SCAM/FRAUD - Avoid!!! Settled with FTC in 2017 for fraud and has not stopped
text: Made a reservation for 4 nights in a London  hotel costing a total of 1572. The site added unexplained additional charges of 1150. Making the total bill over 2700. A cancellation fee of 1900 was added to this. None of these charges were explained prior to paying with the credit card - see below for similar experiences. Buyer beware. Expensive mistake!The site appears first on the search engines and looks like the hotel webpage - do check that it is in fact the hotel's website where you are booking.Upon further investigation I called the hotel and they told me that the booking have been done through Booking.com! Not even directly with the hotel.Whilst the hotel and Booking.com were willing to provide a full refund on the booking, Guest Reservations would only allow the refund if I paid the 1,900 cancellation fee. In other words they would take 1,900 from me even though they would not be out of pocket! This of course was not an option as I would still have to pay for the hotel on top of the cancellation fee. Whilst the hotel and Booking.com tried to do the right thing, GUESTRESERVATIONS.COM will ensure that there is no escape.Don’t be fooled, called 6 times to have the issue resolved to no avail.The site has responded below and provided their customer 'care' email address supposedly to try to resolve the issue. Let's see if they actually do the right thing...For the time being AVOID like the plague.Checked the site for fraud and lo and behold they have had to settle with the FTC in 2017 - I wish I had checked sooner. I hope this review helps others to avoid my faith. I may have lost my money but I don't want others to unwittingly fall into the same trap.

name: DH
title: Practicing borderline thievery and…
text: Practicing borderline thievery and abusing trust through booking process and site design, in a most likely wanted way.It starts with paid referencing and a lading page mimicking the legit hotel page like: www NameOfTheHotel/Guest reservations/….so it looks like you are on the Booking page of the given hotel, just that it may "not be phone optimized”Showing daily rates at the decision process then not until the validation process. Where you see changed rates + outrageous added feesI booked a single Room showing 98 CHF/nightand saw 200/Night in USD!!! + more than 156 USD agency fees once you press validation it was too late to cancel.the paiement perception stayed pending for what seems to be all or almost all retraction period.Booking confirmation comes from a different named group called hotelvalues dot com a site known for similar practices.Customer service showing a USA phone number regardless of your location.I can’t believe such site is still allowed.  will most likely flag this to consumer groups and ask to register a fraud with authorities.

name: Lisette
title: Bad bad bad.

title: No way to contact this company. Please use email below
text: This company is a scam avoid at all costs. Their call line disconnects and they don't have a customer service centre. We tried to book a hotel through them, we wanted one night, they added a second night and charged us. We couldn't contact anyone to change it and when we canceled, they still charged us. Literally every email we tried bounced back, every phone number we called disconnected us. DO NOT USE!!Edit: I have contacted Guest Services using the email supplied and providing all requested info. If there is any satisfaction I will update.Update: I did receive a full refund. It took months, but they came through. changing my review however because of the difficulties in contacting them, it will remain low.

name: Tara McAuliffe
title: Do not book through Guest Reservations
text: Do not book through Guest Reservations. If you do read through the policies very carefully, NO cancellation policy and they charge you the full amount the minute you book the rooms! I do not like to book through 3rd parties. I thought I was booking directly through Hilton, the “guest reservations” website did a great job posing as Hilton. When I received the email confirmation, the email was from Guest Reservation, not Hilton. I realized it was a 3rd party and canceled within a second. They fully charged my card ($700) and refused to refund and still booked my room. When you call them they are not helpful, and say they cannot refund, and will not reactivate the room charge (even when the hotel says the room is still active and booked in my name). I was out $700 and they had my CC information. I called five times to dispute and to try to work with their customer service. They were zero help and all I heard was “no”. They kept asking the name of the Hilton rep I spoke to who said my room was still active. It felt scamming to me. Thankfully Hilton called them directly for me.Update 3/6/25: received my refund, but it was directly through Hilton NOT Guest Services. Hilton must have paid this agency and Hilton refunded me the full amount. I’m a Hilton honors member and I booked the room directly through Hilton. I’m assuming this is why.Reply back to Guest Service: I already contacted you, thanks for replying to this. Your company still refused to refund the charge of $700 after I canceled for one second. You fully charged my card. Hilton refunded my money thankfully. There’s no need to reach out to your support, I tried multiple times and you all were terrible to me.

name: customer
title: Dishonest Crooks
text: It’s kind of pointless writing this review as most people won’t have a clue they are using guest reservations.com and will think they are on a hotels own website. name: Vincent Loubser
title: guestreservations.com
text: I went onto Google to try and make a booking at the Victoria and Alfred Hotel in Cape Town. One of the first sites to appear was guestreservations.com. I looked at the options and compared the prices and their prices were quite good, so I made a booking. The price that I chose was R6281.00 and this was about R500 cheaper than any other website.Then I was directed to the next page where you have to fill in all your personal details and your bank details. And then you pay. This is where I got an smssaying that I just paid R9 482.12 This was a shock to me and when I had a better look at the page it had a summary in small print on the right where taxes and fees were added. This made my booking over R2000 more than any other website.Maybe I should have concentrated better to see this summary first, but you don't expect the price that you chose to change when you pay. I travela lot and this has never happened to me before. It is not right to not included the full price from the beginning, not at the end. False advertising.I tried to click on links like "Contact us" or "Manage your Booking", but all links appear as "403 Forbidden". This is where red flags come up immediately. Not happy!!! I want to cancel.28 February 2025I sent an email to guestreservations.com and they did reply and told me that they would refund me a part of the booked amount. I appreciate this and I will add one more star to my review.I will have to wait and see how ling it takes to get the refund, but at least they came back to me within a day.

text: I recently made a hotel room booking with this company, Guest Reservations. It seemed like a good rate, and I did not notice the additional 85% extra on the bill for booking fees. name: The Fenstermachers
title: Fraudulent and Unethical
text: Fraudulent and UnethicalGuestReservations.com uses paid search ads to trick people into thinking they're booking with a site like Expedia or Priceline when, in fact, they have no official relationship with any of the hotels they claim to represent and you wouldn't know that without scanning for the disclaimers. The charge more than the hotels do on their own sites and they are 100% unwilling to accept cancelation for any reason, at any time. We clicked on their ad by mistake and thought we were booking a room at a specific hotel we were looking for in one city and they booked us in a hotel by the same name in another city. We called immediately to ask for a cancellation due to an error—made in the midst of trying to book last-minute travel for a family emergency—and they refused, telling us we should have read that they have a no refund policy and should not expect them to provide one, even under these circumstances. Plus, there is NO WAY they have 5-star reviews from all their customers like they claim in their own promotions and on their own site.

name: Lisa Marie DeSanto
title: DO NOT BOOK THROUGH THIS DECEPTIVE COMPANY
text: DO NOT BOOK THROUGH THIS COMPANY! I was charged $639 for a reservation for one night at the Madison Beach Hotel - a Hilton property in Connecticut. Due to an extenuating circumstance I needed to cancel this reservation, with the intention of rebooking after my crisis had passed. I thought I booked this reservation directly through the Madison Beach Hotel -- whose site clearly stated I had a 14 day window to cancel, prior to check in -- only to find that "Guest Reservations" was a third party site when I received a confirmation of cancellation stating it was non-refundable. The Better Business Bureau features 22 PAGES of complaints from people who all said they thought they were on actual hotel sites - because Guest Reservations sets their site up to make users believe that they are dealing directly with the hotel/property they're interested in booking with. I cancelled 3.5 weeks before the check in date. I made multiple attempts to contact Guest Reservations and spent hours trying to get help. I finally got through to a rep who offered to reach out to the hotel (due to the extenuating circumstances) and get approval for a refund. She said she received approval and I'd see a refund in 3-5 days. It never came. When I called back they told me they didn't have a record of the conversation and would not honor the promise of a refund unless I called the Madison Hotel and got their permission. When I called the Madison the reservation number I was given wasn't even attached to my name or party! They HAD no reservation for me. And I'm still getting charged. I'm an experienced traveller and I STILL got tricked by this deceptive business. They are a scam and should be shut down. Hilton (the Madison Beach Hotel's parent company) wanted to help but they couldn't find a reservation TO give permission to cancel. The people at Guest Reservations heard my crisis story and are still refusing to do the right thing. The insult on top of the suffering due to the crisis has been awful. I can't believe how heartless they are. Their website is cleverly deceptive, tricking people into thinking they are on the hotel site they are booking with.

name: Joost
title: Non-transparent pricing and non-GDPR conform data processing
text: When trying to book a hotel room over this site the following happened: on the first page of the search results, the different rooms are shown with prices. E.g. one room for 271€, price clearly marked in big letters, well visible.When clicking "Book Now" on this to continue booking, a page appears where you are to enter your personal data. I did so, but before entering the credit card data, I checked what I entered and noticed that in the small box to the right of the page, where the booking details are mentionned, the price changed: from 271€ to 377,89€ (apparently the 271€ is the price without taxes). In my opinion, this is done by purpose to mislead people to think the room is cheaper than it actually is.Then, since the room was just too expensive, I stopped the process an closed the window, believing that the data would be deleted anyway, since ther was a banner saying that my reservation process would block the room only for 10minutes.And then, the spamming started: a few hours later I got a mail reminding me of the unfinished reservation. I ignored it, and this morning I got the next mail. So this site is not only swindling about real prices but it's also processing data that it has no right to do so according to EU GDPR: since the reservation was not finished and only blocked for 10 minutes, they should have deleted my data. Furthermore, I never gave them the right to send me any mails concerning whatever promotional stuff.To conclude, I would not trust this site neither on the prices they display, neither to give them any sensitive payment information.

title: Update after Customer Care
text: After the distressing experience below, I contacted the customer care team as instructed and they have issued a refund.I wish i didn't have to jump through so many hoops to get there though, this should have been sorted when i contacted them over the phone.Still kudos for actually listening and getting it sorted in the end.=======================================ALWAYS DOUBLE CHECK THE WEBSITE YOU'RE USING TO BOOK TRAVEL/HOTELS EVEN IF IT LOOKS LEGITIMATE!These guys are true con artists in a digital age.Booking #R5416273985I am UK based and I booked a hotel in Munich using what i thought was the hotels website directly - I quickly realised i had booked the wrong room/dates as soon as i pressed 'OK' - so almost immediately got in contact with the hotel to say i had made a mistake and to cancel the booking so I could re-book - it was then the hotel told me the reservation was done via a booking agency and I needed to contact them... I checked my confirmation email and only then realised I had used a company named 'guest reservations' and that the cost was significantly more than I thought I had paid thanks to the now infamous "Tax Recovery Charges & Service Fees" that had been added at some point- these fees were the same cost as a night in the hotel room!!!This company is based in the USA and i called them (costing me who knows much in phone charges) and explained that I had just booked the wrong date and needed to cancel so I could re-book - the lady on the phone was somehwat sympathetic but told me in no uncertain terms that I could not get a full refund, the hotel had no power to cancel it on my behalf either, and if I were to cancel the booking this would cost me 90% of what I had paid (£600!) - absolutley scandalous.I feel like such an idiot for falling for their underhanded tactic of disguising their website and search results to look like the legitimate hotel one and for missing the 'hidden fees' but it's at least somewhat comforting to see i'm not the only one who's been duped.Have now had to raise a dispute with my credit card provider to try and recover costs, insane.as another reviewer has stated; Under the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (CPRs), businesses in the UK are required to provide transparent pricing information. Failing to disclose significant fees until after a customer has entered their payment details may constitute a misleading commercial practice. Furthermore, this lack of transparency contravenes the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which requires that terms and conditions, including pricing, be fair and clearly presented to consumers before a transaction is completed.This "business" certainly fails almost all of that criteria.what a distressing situation. Avoid these charlatans like the plague.

This site shows hotel rate but hides the tax recovery charges and services fee - I initially booked a two-room stay for a total rate of £298, only to discover after entering my payment details that an additional £174 in taxes and service fees had been applied. This was not clearly communicated on your website during the booking process.Under the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (CPRs), businesses in the UK are required to provide transparent pricing information. Failing to disclose significant fees until after a customer has entered their payment details may constitute a misleading commercial practice. Furthermore, this lack of transparency contravenes the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which requires that terms and conditions, including pricing, be fair and clearly presented to consumers before a transaction is completed.This situation has caused me significant distress, both emotionally and financially. A surcharge of £174, representing a 58% increase on the original booking amount, is excessive and unreasonable. Had I been aware of these additional costs upfront, I would not have proceeded with the booking.I kindly request the following actions:1.	A full refund of the £174 in hidden fees.2.	A detailed explanation of why these charges were not transparently disclosed during the booking process.3.	Assurance that your pricing practices will be reviewed to prevent this issue from affecting other customers in the future.Please treat this as a formal complaint under your complaints procedure. I expect a response within 14 days. Should this matter remain unresolved, I may escalate it to the relevant consumer protection authorities or pursue other appropriate actions.Update - customer care team responded and as gesture refunded fees which was good but definitely need clearer labelling of fees.

title: Scam company
text: Guest Reservations is by far the worst experience I've had booking a hotel, and I feel obligated to warn others before they fall for the same trap.1. Only after confirming did I realize I had been redirected to a third-party site, which added a host of unexpected issues.2. Outrageous Hidden Fees: After booking, I discovered that they’d tacked on extra charges totaling over 60% of the room cost! There’s no transparency, and by the time you see the final amount, it’s too late to cancel without heavy penalties. They’re clearly banking on you just accepting the extra cost to avoid the hassle of dealing with them.3. False Promises of Amenities: Breakfast was supposed to be included, yet when we arrived at the hotel, we were informed it wasn’t. Guest Reservations had apparently promised it without coordinating with the hotel, so we were left high and dry and had to pay for meals separately.4. Ridiculous Check-In and Check-Out Times: The booking stated check-in was at 5 pm and checkout at 10 am—what hotel has less than 17 hours for guests? They’re effectively giving you half a day and then charging for a full one. It felt incredibly unfair and dishonest.5. Frustrating Customer Service: I spent over an hour on the phone trying to cancel or get the extra charges waived, and every time I asked to speak to a manager, they’d offer another tiny discount. It started feeling like a negotiation with scammers more than customer service. The “discount” capped at 20%, which barely covered half of the added fees. I finally gave up after an exhausting back-and-forth that got nowhere.6. Breach of Privacy: Just hours after booking, I received a call from another company offering hotel packages. This has never happened with any other booking I’ve done online, which makes me think they sold my information. This is an unbelievable invasion of privacy and makes me extremely wary of how they handle personal data.Overall, Guest Reservations is nothing but a trap with shady practices, hidden fees, and a complete disregard for customer satisfaction. Avoid them at all costs and book directly with the hotel to spare yourself the frustration and financial hit. One star is generous for the experience I endured.

text: For upcoming 10/15 knee surgery, I made hotel reservations on 10/10 with Tapestry By Hilton The VERVE Boston Natick, Massachusetts online direct or so I thought. When I called the hotel on 10/11 to cancel the reservations, I was told it was a third party booking and had to connect them directly.  I looked at the credit card activity which showed the hotel name; upon further investigation, the email came from Guest Reservations; they use the hotel name on the credit card activity so that it looks like I was booking direct.  When I called the telephone number listed on the email, the “customer service” representative stated the cancellation policy but I mentioned the circumstances as well as the booking was done LESS THAN 24 HOURS from when it was booked.  He said he would request a one-time courtesy cancellation to waive the penalties associated with my hotel booking. I submitted copy of the original doctor's letter about surgery cancellation due to shortage of IV fluids.The hotel partner, Guest Reservations, denied the request due to cancellation policy (subject to a $238.71 USD change or cancellation fee) and they didn’t care at all about the unforeseen circumstances (Hurricane Milton and IV fluid shortage) which definitely would be grounds for waiver.   Good customer Service means truly reviewing all factors for the waiver and if legitimate, should approved not negated those factors by just stating the cancellation policy; neither the doctor, hospital, nor I had foreseen the nature of Hurricane Milton and its effect on transporting hospital supplies (IV fluids) to hospitals for needed surgeries.Per Chantal Reynolds of Guest Reservations Customer Care, I resubmitted on 11/4 my request, for the third time, a refund of the $238.71 cancellation fee due to national IV shortage.Upon further review of my detailed explanation for the cancelled hotel stay, Guest Reservations Customer Care did expedite the cancellation fee refund on 11/7; and did go a long way in paving good rapport, compassion; understanding and acknowledging the legitimate factors by approving the waiver. name: karen wright
title: THIS SITE IS CRUEL , doesn’t care about kids
text: THIS PLACE IS A SCAM . Do not book a room from these evil , heartless people . I tried so hard to get my money back OR just accept the fact that I was over charged and just use the  room at the extorted, extravagant, overpriced fee that the actual hotel didn’t even know where it came from. I’m talking $143. How can a business begrudge a mother and her daughter $143 back? Or just say OK we will let you use the room for your 143 that you already got taken out of your bank account? Please be careful if you cancel. They will take your money anyways and you will have to make a brand new reservation and pay again !! I just don’t know how this is allowable in this day and age. I have read reviews of this company on other sites and they say the same story. That you call back immediately to cancel and they will not let you , it is a scam. Stay away from these people, especially if you are on a limited budget and have children. I have been on the phone for over 3 hours with customer service people . I reserved a room at the Andirondack Lodge for just one night - The Guest Service site offered a rate of $98.00. I had my daughter make her first reservation and she felt so special,I confirmed it and then it rose to $143.28! I said to my poor daughter , “What did you do ?” Thinking it was her fault. She had chosen the wrong lodge location as well! I called and canceled immediately , explaining the situation with my daughter. They said they would have a specialist look at it and it would be up to their hotel partners . I called the hotel directly and they had never heard of Guest Services. Then they took the money out of my bank , I called again . Three days later - now it’s being handled by another specialist.  I have the feeling it’s going to be canceled and I will be left with no reservation and out the money . How can this be legal ? The site should at least let people reinstate the reservation once they realize they have been scammed . So sad - my daughter cried - I can’t afford $268.00 for a $98.09 hotel room . It’s not fair. I am praying they refund my money, or at least let me eat crow and stay in the hotel for a price that I didn’t agree on . When I mentioned canceling the cancellation, the lady said , you will have to make an entirely new reservation and it may be at a higher rate !! Can this be legal ?!??

name: Damn
title: I am giving 2 stars because I got a…
text: I am giving 2 stars because I got a full refund quickly 👏👏I thought I was in the authentic Hotel’s website when I booked my $183 a night room.A receipt and confirmation were sent to my email and I was happy and ignored it.I saved the email for check in day, and reference for dates.I have a coworker who happens to be traveling to the same destination a few days ahead of us.He asked me what they charge.I said it’s not too bad, under $200 and well worth it, but that I’d let him know.I pulled it up and The email said guest reservations and shows a picture of the hotel, and stated that the credit card charge would read blah blah blah AND it INCLUDED the name of the real Hotel.So I still thought this was the actual hotel. Then I saw the charges were $443 for  ONE night.It had a breakdown of fees with a higher charge than I’d thought ,and an‘other fees’ line I’d never seen before,This Hotel has never gouged me before, and I was in disbelief and disappointed with paying that.I told myself, well there is a concert, maybe they do this to people now for event dates.Coincidentally I get a flyer in the mail  offering me a free stay for 2 nights offer, available for the month I had already booked.I called the Hotel and asked if I could change to the free offer from my paid booking.They said sure let’s take care of that.Then they came back and said they couldn’t help since I booked through a 3rd party.I was in disbelief and argued that I booked through your website.Then I asked the name of the 3rd party and can’t even remember what it was even called.I told him I did not use that company, and thanked him for the info.I’d never heard of this rando place and asked him if he had, and he said yes.So then I asked if they had any available rooms left for my dates,and they did.I booked with the hotel then and there on that phone call.Now I was seriously doubting I’d see a dime back of my money or be able to cancel.When I studied the email better it had a cancellation option, I selected  it, confirmed yes I want to cancel, and it actually worked!A full refund was on my card within like 4 days.So 2 stars for giving me the money back that you almost scammed me for.I’m sure many people will NOT notice what they paid or even check the charges.Just like me.They’ll assume the Hotel they like, is now ripping people off(if they bother to look)because they won’t notice it’s a different company’s email.Guest reservations is so vague and no one would doubt a reservation with that title that displayed the Hotel info in the booking.If the Hotel Clerk hadn’t told me the rando name that he had, I’d have never put two and two together.I started googling and saw others who claimed they booked off the real Business site.Many others have fallen for the same cloney scam that I had.Thanks Guest reservations or whatever other aliases you use, for my refund !!!
