name: Amit Sinha
title: Guest Reservations are liars and cheats.
text: Guest Reservations have a misleading and fraudulent mobile website wherein the (exorbitant service) charges are listed below the button to complete payment. Luckily, I had my 2-factor authentication on and I received a code to confirm the transaction. In the meanwhile, I got a chance to view the fees being charged and I decided against entering the authentication code. To my surprise, this company still went ahead and completed the booking.I got in touch within a few hours with their customer care and spoke about how they charged us an exorbitant fees. They happily agreed to send $50 as a goodwill gesture, knowing fully well that they are fleecing customers anyways. I asked them regarding the details of the charges. They said they charge cleaning fees, resort fees and other fees on behalf of hotels in addition to taxes. I contacted the hotel directly. They said they had no such charges. I went back to them with the hotel’s reply, and this time around they gave a lengthy reply making no sense and substance.I have reached out to my bank and disputed this transaction saying that I never intended to make the transaction in the first place. This company is a liar and a cheat of the highest order. I would like you to refund all the money, as I have made a separate booking with the hotel directly. Never ever use this website. They lie, they cheat and they steal.

name: Herma D
title: This website is a scam
text: Update: I sent an email as requested by Chantal, but (two weeks later) still no reply :(This website is a scam! They had good prices on their website (and it looked like it was the website of the hostel itself), so I booked it with in my mind to cancel the booking I already made by another agency. Only when I confirmed I saw that they charge $60(!) for taxes and services for 2 nights in a dorm room (while other sites don't). So I sent an email to costumer care and I got no reply. Than I contacted the hostel itself and they immediately cancelled this booking, while keeping the booking from the other site.However, I never got a confirmation email from GuestReservation, they already charged my creditcard (while the hostel itself advises to pay cash). So now this agency has the money without needing to pay the hostel. After 3 emails to customer care (that should be available 24/7) with no answer I decided to write this review.

name: R. Branan

name: DEBBIE PIDDINGTON
title: Beware of this company
text: Beware of this company. I thought I was booking directly thru the hotel (which was my intention) as a Sydney number came up under the hotel name. I even told the lady when I rang that I knew the price I could get it for on line (thru booking.com) and was hoping by booking directly thru the hotel I would be getting it at a better deal.. she quickly came back with the price of $181.82 + taxes & expenses .. I then asked for a full price including taxes and expenses and she came back with a new price of $265,50.. which was still better than booking.com's $309.00.. I then asked her if this was Australian dollars and she said "yes mam".I proceeded with payment .. and after the call I looked at my visa charges and she had charged me in US dollars, so $410.04 was charged to my visa.. over $140 Australian more than quoted.I rang them straight back & told them they needed to replay the conversation I had with the sales person as I asked her twice if it was Aus dollars.. they then had the nerve to offer me 3% refund? When I said that was not acceptable they then offered me 10% .. (mind you that was also only on the original quoted price of $265.50 not the $410.04 I paid)...I said no I wanted the full $144.54 they deceitfully took from me.They said their team would look into it and someone would review the original call & "email" me back?. BUT they couldnt tell me when that would be.If they do get back to me and refund the full difference they over charged me by charging me in US dollars rather than Aus dollars as I was lead to believe I was being charged in.. then I will update this review.

name: Joost van Daelen

name: Jodie Watts

name: Justin Freeman

name: David Philipona

name: Richard Bridge
title: Avoid at all costs, a scam masquerading as a travel agent
text: As so many others have posted here, this is basically a scam masquerading as a travel agent. name: Alix Rowe

name: Ian in lancs
title: Avoid Guest Reservations !!!
text: I googled a hotel in Newcastle UK the top result was the hotels name with guest reservations.com following it. Which I did not realize was a stand alone company. The room rate for 2 nights was shown as £229. The next screen had a 10 minute countdown timer to suggest I had to enter all my details within the time limit to get this rate. The confirm details button was on purpose positioned above the section showing the full price which had changed. Under the pressure of the timer and not thinking to scroll past the confirmation button I was then charged £457.11 !!.   I only saw the price when I checked my credit card. Thinking I had booked direct with the hotel I called and was told the rooms were booked via expedia at a cost of £271.  Trying to contact Guest reservation.com on a Saturday proved useless instead the automated line bounced me around and in frustration I said I wanted to cancel as I could not get an option to talk to someone.  Turns out my booking was non refundable.   I used the contact page to send 2 emails, received no answer and finally I managed to call and was told the policy was clear, the reservation is non refundable and they could not reinstate a booking after a cancellation. So £457 gone and no room either.. Absolute robbery from the way the website used the hotels name to the way the price was displayed, and the pressure selling tactic and hiding the full price below the confirmation button.    Three days after posting this review I was contacted and a full refund was given. Thank you Guest reservation.

title: Note 100% NON-REFUNDABLE policy before booking
text: I needed to book a hotel room and typed in the specific hotel that I wanted to stay at.  I clicked on the first site that popped up, holidayinnaiken.guestreservations.com, thinking that was the hotel's site (based on the fact that I typed in a specific hotel and this address includes that specific name of the hotel including the location).I booked a room for $146.00 (for a one night stay), which ended up actually costing $213.46 after the additional charges and fees that I wasn't aware of until booking.I ended up needing to cancel the reservation, which was the first time I realized that this was booked through a third party and that the reservation was non-refundable.  I canceled 6 days after booking for a reservation that was 4 months away (so not a last minute or delayed cancellation).As soon as I canceled and realized the reservation was non-refundable I called the number provided (within minutes of canceling).  I asked if the reservation could at least be reinstated since there was a non-refundable policy and was told no.  So, $213.46 later I was not allowed a refund or reinstatement and am just out of that money with nothing but frustration to show for it.It should not be legal for a third party to have a web address so similar to that of the hotel without having to put very conspicuous language on the site making it clear this is a third party. text: A common theme on these reviews are the hidden fees that appear once you've booked according to the price you see compared to what appears on the booking confirmation..... This one is no different.I booked 2 x nights in London and thought I'd get a decent hotel at the price shown at £282.04.  Despite me checking I could see no extra costs as you sometimes see, so imaging my surprise to see the booking confirmation of £449.00.These were £166.96 charges for "tax recovery charges and service fees", although there was no mention of these when I booked.One other thing to note is that by some strange coincidence these hidden extra charges were to the exact penny to round it up to a whole pound sterling!I'm sure some faceless homeworker will come out and reply to this about them being very transparent with extra costs etc and that they're clearly shown..... They're not no matter how much they falsely claim they are.  I spent a hour looking at them and two other chain hotel websites and these hidden fees were mentioned nowhere.  I'm sure I'd have noticed £166 of extra costs.A truly poor organisation who let people book and hope they don't see the extra fees until they arrive and pay..... I look forward to their pointless automated reply.I had a reply and it was as I fully expected (American English spelling) and just some automated reply, or at least that's what it read as.  I booked it through you and not the hotel and fully aware that you're not affiliated with the hotel, so thanks for the patronisation (no 'z').  I booked it through you and had the confirmation from you with your then hidden fees showing..... hence why I cancelled it immediately.  These hidden fees are not clearly shown at all so try not to claim they are as there's no way I'd book a hotel for two nights with such inflated high cost extra fees.

text: The website and the billing process is intentionally designed to steal money from honest customers. The arrows on the “Complete Reservation“ button would typically mean that clicking the button would bring up another webpage to allow the customer to actually complete the reservation, including reviewing final costs. Instead, clicking the button triggers the automatic payment. This is in direct conflict with the payment terms shown directly above the button. They put the cost, including the fees, below the yellow button, and you wouldn’t notice this if you didn’t scroll all the way down. The website is clever and in most cases legal, but it is absolutely intended to get customers to make unintended purchases, with no opportunity for refunds. The billing terms and payment process is fraudulent and illegal. It says “my credit card will be charged upon submitting a reservation request”. It’s impossible to submit this request without completing the reservation. When I pointed that out to these scammers, I got a full refund. If by chance you decide to cancel a reservation, this company keeps 100% of the cost. Not just their fee, but the room cost as well. What legitimate company would do this? In my case, they were going to keep $421 and provide no service whatsoever. Do not use this foreign company whatsoever. title: We stayed at the DoubleTree by Hilton…
text: We stayed at the DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston North Shore for three nights while attending my brother’s wedding in Danvers. We were very impressed by the hotel’s amenities, service, and location. The hotel is conveniently located near the highway, making it easy to access Salem, Boston, and other attractions. The hotel also offers complimentary parking, which is a great bonus.The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful, from the front desk to the housekeeping. They greeted us with warm chocolate chip cookies upon arrival and made sure we had everything we needed throughout our stay. They also accommodated our special requests, such as early check-in and late check-out, without any hassle. They even surprised us with a complimentary bottle of champagne and a card to congratulate my brother on his wedding.The rooms were spacious, clean, and comfortable, with modern amenities such as 32-inch HDTVs, free WiFi, and large work desks. The beds were very cozy and we slept well every night. The bathrooms were also well-stocked with toiletries and towels. We especially liked the view of the golf course from our window.The hotel has a lot to offer for entertainment and relaxation. We enjoyed the indoor pool and spa at the Atlantis Sports Club, which was connected to the hotel. The pool was large and heated, and the spa offered a variety of treatments and massages. We also had a blast at the Water Park of New England, which was also connected to the hotel. The water park had slides, rides, and games for all ages. It was a great way to have fun with the family.The hotel also has a restaurant, a lounge, and a coffee shop on site. We had breakfast at the TradeWinds Restaurant every morning, which offered a buffet and an à la carte menu. The food was delicious and fresh, with plenty of options to choose from. We also had lunch and dinner at the TradeWinds Lounge & Bar, which served New England-inspired dishes and drinks. The service was fast and friendly, and the portions were generous. We also grabbed some coffee and snacks at the Starbucks in the lobby, which was very convenient.We had a wonderful time at the DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston North Shore and we highly recommend it to anyone looking for a quality hotel in Danvers. The hotel exceeded our expectations in every way and made our trip memorable. Thank you to all the staff for making us feel welcome and pampered. We will definitely be back!

title: So that's the story.
text: So that's the story.I booked a room for one night through the website. Let's leave aside the fact that the price indicated next to the room did not include all the "extras" of taxes and conversion fees from local currency to the dollar, and the final price jumped by 400 NIS.In the details of the type of room I booked, it was specifically stated that there is a balcony in the room. After placing the order, I called the hotel that the order was indeed accepted and that I was getting a room with a balcony. The hotel told me that the type of room I booked only has two rooms with a balcony and they are already booked for the date I chose, and that if I want to make changes to the booking, to call the company I booked from.From this point began a long and exhausting saga. I went through close to five agents, and to each one I had to detail each time what the story was. They repeat and recite the cancellation policy, and that I cannot cancel without paying full price for the room. I explained to them repeatedly that the room I booked was not the room I was actually getting, but there was no one to talk to. Everyone recites the same words. I felt like I was talking to bots and not to humans. Everyone apologized and everyone was very kind, but no one really helped me.In the end they asked me for proof that the details shown on the website indicate that there is a balcony for the type of room I requested. I need to send proof, when at any given moment they can connect to the website and see. But of course the onus of proof is on me, but every format I sent was not accepted in their system.In the penultimate conversation, which lasted 43 minutes, I asked the agent to transfer me to a responsible manager. She told me he couldn't take calls. But after a few minutes she came back to me and offered me a 10% discount, but I have to cancel the order and order again. I asked her what's the point, because if I cancel I pay full price, so what does the 10% discount give me? She had no answer for that. After a few minutes she came back to me with a 15% discount, and a few minutes after that with a 20% discount. I explained to her that I was requesting a cancellation without charge, and then she hung up.I called again. The agent who answered me, suddenly miraculously managed to open the proof I sent, and agreed to forward my request to a partner or whatever, together with the proof that the information published on the website was wrong, and said they would get back to me.I wonder if they will come back or if I will have to spend two more hours today on the phone with your blunt agents. shame!=============So in the end I got a regular room without a balcony, even though on your website you advertise that the type of room I chose is with a balcony.But beyond that, I think your whole behavior is one big fraud.The price published on the website was published in local currency, which is NIS, and the price for the room plus breakfast was supposed to be 950 NIS. However, after confirming the order, I noticed that you added a tax of $93.21 to the price, which is an increase of 357.9 NIS, so that the amount I was charged for in total was 1333.89 NIS.When I arrived at the hotel I was surprised to find out that I had to pay another 132 NIS which is 18% VAT!Needless to say, this really pissed me off, because if the additional taxes you owe does not include the VAT, then what does it include?In short, instead of paying 950 NIS, as I originally intended to pay, I ended up paying 1,465 NIS.About one night!!!! When in fact I stayed at the hotel for less than 24 hours! for a standard room!!!! There is no justification for paying such a price.I see it as a scam.As far as I'm concerned, I will never order from you again, this was the worst vacation experience I've ever had.And please spare me your automatic "we're sorry for your negative experience" response.

name: Sharon Gardner
title: Golf Clubs Arrived Perfectly--Our Suitcase, Not So Much
text: We recently used Ship Sticks to transport two hard cases of golf clubs and one hard suitcase. The overall process—from ordering to pickup—was straightforward and user-friendly. We appreciated receiving our shipment ahead of the quoted delivery time, which was a pleasant surprise.Our golf clubs arrived in the same condition they were shipped, reflecting careful handling on that end. However, the suitcase did not fare as well. Upon arrival, it was clear that it had been tossed around during transit, and unfortunately, the pull-up handle was broken beyond repair. The handle no longer closes, making it unsuitable for airline travel. Additionally, removing the damaged handle leaves exposed metal edges that could pose a risk.While we’re pleased with the speed and convenience of Ship Sticks, the handling of our suitcase was disappointing. We recognize that shipping large items carries some inherent risks, but we hoped for more consistent care across all shipped pieces.For those considering Ship Sticks, we recommend it for golf clubs and other sturdy, protective cases but advise caution when shipping standard luggage.

title: Ship sticks saved my bucket list trip
text: Ship sticks saved my bucket list trip. I was a first time SS user. I had the clubs shipped to a hotel on the Friday I was scheduled to arrive. Well when I arrived, my clubs were "out for delivery" so I figured they would be there in a couple hours. About 5pm, a hotel employee came and said FedEx tried to deliver but didn't have my room number, but didn't think to leave them at the lobby. FedEx said they probably wouldn't be able to get them to me until Monday. I had 3 rounds of prepaid golf scheduled and no clubs, shoes, weather clothing,etc. I was going to have to rent clubs and purchase jackets. No matter how much I pleaded with FedEx to bring them Saturday or I offered to pick them up. I was checking out of my hotel early Monday and wouldn't even be there anymore if they were delivered. I was beside myself, me and 7 friends had planned this trip for over a year. I texted SS. I don't even know the person's name that was at the other end, but after a couple texts, I felt pretty confident I would have them next day. I woke up the next morning and before 8am I had an update that they called the station where they were and it wasn't open yet. 30 minutes later,an update said the clubs were picked up by a third party and on the way to me. I received them with time to spare before the first tee time of my epic trip.Though none of this was Ship Sticks fault, the person on the other end of the text messages corrected a major dumb error by FedEx and saved my bucket list trip. I am beyond grateful.

One day we had asked 4 times for an umbrella, and then we finally realized we were not going to receive one that day.  There were plenty available, but our requests to the pool concierge were continually ignored - he was not overly busy, but he seemed to only want to have conversations with his favorite guests and I suppose we were not in that group.  The next day there was a different pool concierge, and she was very attentive to our needs. Cesar, the pool bartender, was beyond fabulous!  He always made my mango margaritas quickly and super delicious! We absolutely loved our butlers - they always greeted us when we went out to the elevators, and they managed to obtain dinner reservations for us every night when the application said there were no tables available - we loved that!  We were so sad to leave paradise, but we will definitely be back next year!!

But what happened? Zero response from the Headout team. No one picked up, no chat support, no assistance whatsoever.As if that wasn’t enough, my second booking for KL Tower Sky Terrace was also a disaster. It rained in the evening, and visitors were not allowed on the Sky Terrace for safety reasons. Again, the KL Tower official politely asked me to speak to the agent to amend the ticket for the indoor Observatory deck. And again — no response from Headout.Both bookings were ruined, my money and time wasted, and the entire experience soured — all because Headout’s team is unreachable, unaccountable, and completely unprofessional.Avoid Headout at all costs if you value your time, money, and travel plans.They’re happy to take your money but disappear when there’s a problem.

title: Visiting teamLab Phenomena Abu Dhabi…
text: Visiting teamLab Phenomena Abu Dhabi was like going into a living, breathing artwork. The installations responded to my presence—lights shifted, sounds echoed, and spaces transformed as I moved through them. In one room, a massive black sphere floated mid-air, gently drifting when touched before returning to its original position. Another space featured glowing orbs that lit up and chimed upon contact, creating a symphony of light and sound.The architecture itself felt organic, with flowing forms that blurred the lines between walls and ceilings. Each room offered a new sensory experience, from interactive digital butterflies to immersive light sculptures. The entire journey was both surreal and grounding, inviting introspection and wonder.It's more than an art exhibit; it's an exploration of perception and interaction. Whether you're an art enthusiast or simply curious, teamLab Phenomena offers a unique experience that lingers long after you leave.

title: Avoid at all costs
text: Avoid at all costs — misleading, overpriced, and completely ruined our Eiffel Tower experience.I booked a "hosted entry" tour to the Eiffel Tower through Headout via paristickets.com, paying €262 for 2 adults and 2 kids. The website explicitly states: “Meet your host at the designated point, get escorted through queues, and let your host line up to validate your tickets on your behalf. Then, head to the elevators and enjoy access to the 2nd floor or summit, as you explore each floor at leisure.”None of this happened:We were not escorted through queues — we stood in line for 2.5 hours, with two young children.The host did not line up on our behalf — we waited the entire time just like everyone else.We did not explore at leisure — the host gave a full guided commentary, which I had deliberately chosen to avoid.Summit access was closed, and we’ve received no meaningful compensation for this.What’s worse, the entire experience ruined our expectations and impression of visiting the Eiffel Tower. The kids were exhausted and just wanted to sit on the ground — the moment was completely lost.In the end, we got what the Eiffel Tower sells for €58, but paid nearly five times more. I requested a refund of the difference between the official tariff and what we paid — they refunded just €32, which is frankly an insult. This service is deceptive, overpriced, and shows zero respect for customers.Book through the official Eiffel Tower website — or, if online booking isn’t available, just go and stand in the line yourself.And the truth is: you end up standing in the same line anyway — whether you have a host or not. It’s just much cheaper without them. You’re basically paying extra for nothing.

title: My visit to Dolmabahçe Palace and Hagia…
text: My visit to Dolmabahçe Palace and Hagia Sophia was truly unforgettable. Dolmabahçe took my breath away—the palace is incredibly grand, with crystal chandeliers, marble staircases, and beautiful European-inspired decor. It was fascinating to walk through the same halls the Ottoman sultans once did. Hagia Sophia was just as powerful, with its unique blend of Christian and Islamic history—seeing ancient mosaics alongside Islamic calligraphy was deeply moving.However, I do have a few comments. First, while the ticket included “skip the line” access, it didn’t cover security checks, which still took time. It would be much more efficient to have a fast-track lane for that, especially for people who book online.Second, I feel the price is getting too high. Hagia Sophia used to be free, and now it's quite expensive for tourists. I believe such historically and spiritually significant places should be more accessible, like the Blue Mosque, which still offers free entrance. These are treasures meant to be shared and appreciated by everyone, not just those who can afford it.Still, the experience was rich in history and beauty, and I’m grateful I got to see it. Just hoping for a few improvements in pricing and entry logistics.

title: Misleading, disorganized, and a complete waste of time
text: I booked the “Guided Tour of the Eiffel Tower with Summit Access” through Headout, and it turned out to be one of the most disappointing experiences I’ve had with any tour company.First of all, the group was advertised as a “small group between 10 to 20 people.” In reality, we were 34 people crammed together, making it impossible to hear or follow the guide. This was false advertising — plain and simple.Second, the listing implied that summit tickets were pre-booked. They weren’t. We were made to wait in the public line just like everyone else. Our guide didn’t have any tickets and had to buy them at the booth while we waited. By the time they got around to it, summit access was sold out. So we paid for a summit tour and only got to the second floor.Even Eiffel Tower staff acknowledged that Headout tours are known for showing up without tickets, leaving customers stranded in long lines and missing what they paid for.Time promoted was 20:30, but only got in at 21:32. Had we known the truth, we would have just bought official tickets directly from the Eiffel Tower for a fraction of the price and without wasting a good part of our evening standing around. we paid 70€ pr. person - and it cost 23,5€ at eiffeltower.This experience was misleading, frustrating, and a complete letdown. It also directly violates Headout’s own Terms of Use, which promise accurate and reliable service descriptions.I’ve requested a full refund — and suprice - no reply from them. They only send 21€ back pr. personHeadout is not trustworthy. Save yourself the hassle and book directly through official sources.

text: Honestly, this was one of the best days we’ve had in Dubai.We started with Miracle Garden, and it felt like we walked into a fairy tale. Flowers everywhere — heart tunnels, castles, even a full plane covered in flowers. Super peaceful, super romantic. We just strolled around, took a ton of pictures, and enjoyed the vibes. Go around golden hour — it hits different with the sunset.After that, we headed to Global Village — complete switch in energy, but just as amazing. It’s like traveling the whole world in one spot. Every country has its own section with food, clothes, souvenirs, and shows. We ate from like four different countries, watched some live performances, and walked around till late. It’s colorful, loud, and just a vibe.If you’re in Dubai and have one full day to enjoy, do Miracle Garden during the day, Global Village at night — you won’t regret it.

Never using Headout again.PS: I actually paid 140 EUR for 97.55 worth of tickets. The ticket I received had the original prices on them (e.g. 19.85 instead of 28). Further to that they don't offer children tickets (6 to 18) even though the palace do offer such tickets. And to top it, they raise prices for the peak periods. After a lengthy dispute and me several times asking them to bridge the 28 I paid to the 19.85 on the ticket, they offered me a refund of the difference. So raising my feedback to 2 stars, but tourists beware!

text: We spent two full days at the Kennedy Space Center, and honestly, it still wasn’t enough — this place is incredible! Sitting down with someone who’s actually been to space was surreal. He shared amazing stories, insights, and answered our questions with so much warmth and passion. We so wish we could’ve taken a photo with him — that’s the only thing that would’ve made it even more memorable!There’s so much to explore — from the Space Shuttle Atlantis exhibit to the Apollo/Saturn V Center and the exciting simulations. Everything was well-organized, interactive, and perfect for all ages.If you're even remotely interested in space, this is a place you absolutely have to visit. Two days gave us time to really take it all in, and we’d go back again in a heartbeat!

title: I made a reservation with HEADOUT for a VIP experience and got the Economy treatment
text: I made a reservation with HEADOUT for a VIP package for my son and I at the Kennedy Space Centre. What I ended up getting was a regular general admission for 2 people. The reservation was made directly with HEADOUT and they charged my credit card USD $445 for the VIP experience (which they promote on their website). Unfortunately, something went completely amiss between HEADOUT and their representative Gray Line Tours with regards to my VIP reservation. Prior to the day of the VIP experience, I received a text message from Gray Line Tours advising to be at the stated pick up point (ICON Park) 15 minutes prior to the departure time of 8:00 am. We arrived at ICON Park at 7:45 am. Upon arrival we noticed a small airport type shuttle bus and asked the driver if he was providing the transport to the Kennedy Space Centre, he responded that a bus would be arriving at 8:00 am and to remain where we were. The bus did arrive and we boarded along with about a dozen other passengers. Enroute to the KSC a guide on the bus elaborated about all the wonderful things we could see and do during the visit. At the conclusion of his speech, he proceeded to hand out admission tickets. Long story short, when we arrived at the KSC and got off the bus, I asked the tour guide if this was supposed to be the VIP experience and he responded that we listed were on his passenger pick up list as being general admission passengers, when I explained that I had paid for the VIP experience for two (2) people, his response was "speak with the company that you purchased the tickets through, there's nothing i can do for you". I have since inquired with the company (HEADOUT), sent messages (including directly to the co-CEO Varun Khona) and received two responses - generally weeks apart and from different HEADOUT support staff. The co-CEO Mr Khona must have been far too busy to take any interest in quickly resolving my issue. In the end - which is where I now appear to be, as no one is responding to my follow up messages, I was offered a $110 credit towards a future HEADOUT experience, to which I completely declined as I do not intend to travel where HEADOUT may have other experiences, and in addition I was also offered a 10% reduction on a future experience, again I declined. What I have asked for is a REFUND to my credit card for the difference between what I paid ($445) and the value of the general admission ticket which amounted to $150 for two people, that difference being USD $295. Each time I raise this this request I receive a statement from HEADOUT Support stating "Regrettably, as the tour's scheduled timing was not adhered to, we are unable to process a refund for this reservation. We appreciate your understanding in this matter". Or another statement "Our local operators maintain a strict no-cancellation and reschedule policy for this experience that prevents us from doing so". Instead of owning up to an error and resolving the problem, I get completely irresponsible statements that no sense whatsoever. And each time I question the response (to better understand what is meant), the email thread goes dead. All in all, I suggest anyone contemplating using HEADOUT for a VIP experience at the Kennedy Space Centre, rethink it, and find another tour operator that will stand behind what they sell and, if something does go wrong they make it right. HEADOUT gladly takes your money and unfortunately when something does go wrong, you are on your own after that. AVOID this company.

I read some bad reviews of hosts that had not turned up or tickets that weren't usable so I was very anxious before the trip as the trip was booked to achieve my 8 year olds dream of going up the tower. However for anyone who is experiencing similar feelings after booking - it turned out really good. The person arrived at the meeting place with the tickets on time and then the host arrived shortly after. He was very engaging and made the walk to the Tower very interesting. He guided us through security and up to the second floor in the lift - any waiting was minimal though I have no idea if he did actually get us through any faster than normal etickets or not. Any waiting we did have was made more interesting by the host. As mentioned, not sure it was worth the extra money, however it wasn't a disaster and it meant there was no moments of stress once the host had arrived. As an autistic adult it would have been overwhelming to arrive at the Tower and try to figure out where to go at each stage though it is absolutely doable and we would have managed. Basically - it was good though unnecessarily expensive.

text: We were recently in Barcelona and took the Metro to Park Guell.  After an extremely long and steep climb, we arrived at a gate to be met with the sign 'Sold Out'.  I immediately went online and found that there was a guided tour with this company still available, starting in 20 minutes.  I quickly signed up and paid 69 euros for the 2 of us. Went back to the gate and were told that the tour left from a different gate.  Vague directions were given.  We hurried along and received a text from Headout confirming our booking.  I texted back that we were lost, having no idea where this gate was.  A phone call followed where I explained what had happened and asked for directions to the gate.  I was told that all the necessary information was in the booking confirmation and I should just use my GPS.  I said I was already doing that but it wasn't being cooperative (which happened a lot in Barcelona).  No help was offered and we were told the tour wouldn't wait if we were late.  We hurried along and finally found the correct gate but it was now just over 10 minutes past the tour time.  I texted that we had arrived and the response was 'Too late'.  I asked if we could join the next tour or get a refund.  The response was 'No and no'.  Just that! We were devastated and could not believe that we had been treated so badly.  The only good thing was that this gate was near a bus stop that took us back into central Barcelona.  Two very tired and hot 70 year old women returned to town 69 euros poorer and having been deprived a visit to Park Guell which was to have been the highlight of our visit.  Our holiday was over the next day so no chance to return.  After receiving such rude and unhelpful treatment from the person at Headout that we spoke to, I will never use this company again.

name: Natalia
title: Never use them
text: I’d like to share my experience of visiting Windsor Castle in London with tickets from HeadoutPros:- [ ] A bit discounted price- [ ] Buying tickets online vs offlineCons:- [ ] Terrible customer service- [ ] Company doesn’t care a  bit of customersSummary: take care and never use themThe whole story.We visited London for 2 nights and used Headout to book tickets to Windsor Castle. By a stupid mistake we booked it not for 4/17 but for 4/18 when we were leaving.The problem was only found when we arrived to the Castle - it’s about 1.5 hours from London - and tried to enter the Castle.We were told that it could be easily fixed if we purchased the tickets in the official site; in our case we can try to call to Headout to fix that.We tried during more than an hour. 4 times we waited, waited, waited while Headout “served other customers” and then were just disconnected.Until my wife tried to call, I tried to use Headout’s chat. IMO - and I’m a QA assurance Engineer - it is designed so bad, so un-intuitively, it’s almost impossible to use. 5 times I had to re-enter my name, email address, type my question, and then receive a request to restart chat. It was a nightmare. Finally I got through and received the answer that in my case none changes are allowed.At that time my wife could finally got to a live representative and heard: the best I can do is to give you a discount if you purchase something from us in the next year.Let me repeat, we were nor asking to change for a missing date/time, just to change from next day to current day. It could be done easily if Headout cared just a little bit about customers.We won’t accept that “discount” and we’re ashamed of such USA company. Never again will buy anything from them.Please share to your friends

name: Wouter
title: Tickets enterance Sint-Pieters church
text: Booked tickets for Saint Pieters church enterance and Dome visit by stairs in Rome :- In the end the tickets were valid and real, although I had my doubts of it being just a scam.- Hugely overpriced : enterance to the basilic is free and dome access is 10 euro/pp + 5 euro/pp for audioguide, I paid 48 euro which means 18 euro to much for 2 persons.- Needed to contact Headout 6 times by mail and chat to get the tickets. They keep you waiting with nothing if you don't chase for your tickets yourself. Chasing by escalation trough chat and email.- First you get nothing "tickets in process", after 3 emails/chat you get a PDF that still not contain actual tickets, additional 3 email/chats you get a QR code for the enterance.- "Tickets available day before experience", "tickets within 4 hours", "tickets 24 hours before visit"... you get the same answer but none of this is true... Unless you push for it. Please don't trust any timing they tell you!- You never speak to an actual person at the location, always a service-center located somewhere around the world. The emails contain errors in writing, there is never a phone number or specific email mentioned, so not possible to actually reach somebody.End result : afraid of being a full scam I'm happy I received tickets in the end but hugely overpriced and you need to push them 10+ times to get something... confronting them with their own lies... otherwise you end up with nothing, except the loss of your money...

title: Lesson learned
text: We recently visited Seville and as one of the main activities we booked a tour through Headout for the alcazar and cathedral tour two weeks in advance. We received a confirmation of the booking, Headout took the payment, we downloaded the app and our booking was showing confirmed status( even on the agreed day of the tour), we received updates/reminders  from Headout of our upcoming tour ( up to the day before), we received email tickets that looked valid (with qr codes).  We met the tour operator in Seville on the day who informed they had not received the booking - on contacting Headout they had sent a later email (which had gone into my spam) saying they in fact did not have a ticket. On the day it was not possible to buy tickets as they were sold out.  Lesson learnt here in spite of all the above suggesting you may have a ticket, maybe you don’t - in my view this is an Untrustworthy service - also they made no attempt to refund until my complaint ( on the day of the tour) to which they apologised and offered a ticket a week later. They offered additional Headout vouchers :) - We had the opportunity to book this trip via our hotel which in future I’ll be doing.

text: Had a truly awful experience today with the Valet Parking at the Southampton Cruise Terminal after returning from a cruise with P&O.The issue, in fairness, lies with the subcontractor that Global Parking Services use here - a company called Southampton Valet Ltd who are completely useless.So, after leaving our cruise we went to the short stay car park at 10:00 to collect our vehicle only to find literally dozens of very agitated clients of GPS / SVL waiting for their cars.Some of these people had booked an 8:00 pick up and were still waiting at 10:00.To say tempered were fraying is an understatement, Hampshire Police had to attend to try to sort out the situation.Eventually a few cars arrived for collection and the on site reps offered to take some of us to the car park to collect our vehicles in person.So, SVL took us to the WestQuays Multi Storey Car Park handed over car keys and told us where our cars were parked - or at least on which level of this huge 15 storey car park they were on - in my case level 7.Only, my car wasn’t on level 7 - there then followed a 2 hour search for my vehicle (involving calls to the security office to check their ANPR system and the kind assistance of a security guard) before I eventually found it on level 2C.When I drove back to the Cruise Terminal to collect my wife and our luggage about a third of the people I had seen 2 hours previously were still waiting, including a few of the 8:00 bookings.It my absence the victims of SVL had been chatting to Port Staff who confirmed the company wasn’t registered or licensed for meet and greet parking and were known to be extremely dodgy.They actually operate a scam - SVL park your vehicle in  a multi storey for a weekly charge of £35. It seems that this isn’t authorised by the multi-storey operators who were outraged when I called their security office.So, GPS charge their clients £130 for a weeks parking, subcontract to SVL who then improperly dump your car in a non secure multi-storey that costs them £35 and a healthy profit is made by all.I suspect that SVL are entirely aware that they shouldn’t use the multi-storey and probably move the cars around during the week to make it less likely that their activities are less likely to be noticed by the multi-storey operators. This would perhaps explain why my vehicle was 5 floors away from where SVL said it was located.So SVL are rogue operators but Global Parking Service's have, in my humble opinion, been utterly negligent in engaging the services of a cowboy operation and have failed in their duty of care to their clients.

After my weeklong trip I returned (at 12:30 AM) to find that the catalytic converter on my car had been cut out and stolen!  Obviously, even though entry is monitored, the lot itself is not and criminals take advantage of the lack of security.  In contrast, at a dedicated lot, there is a 24/7 attendant, lighting throughout and pick-up vans are constantly roaming the lot for pick-ups and drop offs, all of which discourage criminal activity.  To add insult to injury, when I attempted to exit, the card reader said I owed $200 since my time "had expired" even though I already paid Global up front and scanned the provided QR code upon entry.  I had to go back to the front desk to explain my situation to exit the lot.  (Did I mention this was after a flight from the west coast and after midnight??) Needless to say, I was already seriously pissed off that my car was vandalized and then had to waste time UN-F***ing an admin screw-up.  This dismal level of service is emblematic of the saying that "You get what you pay for".  THIS SERVICE ABSOLUTELY SUCKS AND I DO NOT RECOMMEND USING IT.  DON'T BE AN IDIOT--USE A REAL LOT DEDICATED TO PHL TRAVELERS!

After he was done yelling at me and arguing with me, he finally asked me where I was and told me that I needed to go to the 7th level... where I found a more helpful gentleman who helped me with my bags and showed me where to park and gave me a slip of paper with a bar code to use when exiting so my card would not be charged for the parking. I appreciate that the shuttle was included in the price.Upon returning, I was fortunate to take the first shuttle back from the cruise port. The driver told me to use the elevator to get to where my car was parked. The elevator filled up so I decided to wait and take the next one. I pushed the button and waited but no elevator came -- I don't know what happened to all the people who got on, but... it never came back, so I walked with my luggage up to the next level and found my car. As I was leaving the garage, the gates were up and the scanner was not functioning so I don't know if I will be charged twice for parking. I hope not! As I exited the building, I was blocked by a taxi unloading passengers and their luggage. One of the passengers knocked on the window of the shuttle which was also just leaving. She said that her group had waited over an hour for the shuttle but nobody came, so they took a taxi. She was instructed that they could take the elevator up to level 7 and find their car... she tried to summon the elevator, but stated that it was broken. I left. I hope they got some help. Good points? My car was still there, safe and sound. I was lucky my experience with the shuttle was good. Bad points? Whoever answered the phone was rude, nasty, argumentative and told me that I should follow directions, instead of helping me. Whoever runs this company should give this guy some lessons in customer service, and empathy for little old ladies on disability from effects of chemo and radiation treatments for breast cancer. Whoever runs this company should install signage on the front of the parking garage so people know that this is the right parking garage. Whoever owns this company should install signage at the entrance scanner and gate to tell people that Premier Cruise Parking is located on LEVEL 7. Whoever owns this company should hire a customer service person to be at the entrance gate to welcome customers and help them get in the gate and find the location on Level 7. Whoever owns this company should have a customer service person at the cruise port to make sure returning customers are in the right place to catch the shuttle and to make sure the shuttles are running frequently so nobody has to wait over an hour for the shuttle and finally get their own taxi... COMMUNICATION is lacking at this company. It is so important and so EASY to do if you just put yourself in the shoes of your customers and make sure you are meeting their needs. But, seriously, either get that guy on the phone some serious customer service and communications training, or fire him. He's making your whole operation look like it's run by socio-phobic psychopaths!!!!!

My recommendation is that you have either a print out of your receipt or have it on your phone to show proof of payment.  That’s what I did when the Manager showed up to look at this. That said, I’m still monitoring my Credit Card account to make sure there are no further charges to it.Other than this “attempt” to over charge us, we’ve had no problem with Global Airport Parking. title: Disappointing Experience with Outdoorsy…
text: Disappointing Experience with Outdoorsy and PayPal Payment Option.I rented an RV van through Outdoorsy for a holiday trip and decided to use the 0% interest payment option through PayPal, allowing me to pay off the rental in four installments. To set it up, I linked my credit card to my PayPal account, expecting a smooth transaction. However, I was unexpectedly charged interest on my credit card.When I contacted Outdoorsy for assistance, I received no support. They simply directed me to PayPal, stating they received the payment from PayPal and that the issue was not theirs to resolve. They also mentioned that other customers had experienced the same issue with this payment offer. If that's the case, why is Outdoorsy still offering a payment option with these known issues?While I understand that PayPal may be at fault, Outdoorsy is the one offering this payment option on their platform. As such, they should have taken more responsibility in resolving the problem. Instead, they passed me off to PayPal, leaving me frustrated and without any resolution.Additionally, Outdoorsy should have made it clear on their platform that customers choosing this payment option must first be approved by PayPal. When I selected the payment plan, the process appeared seamless. But when I called PayPal, they asked if I had received an approval email. I had received an email authorizing the payment to Outdoorsy, Inc., but it turns out this was not the approval email they meant.It’s incredibly disappointing that Outdoorsy, a company that provides services to customers, showed no interest in addressing my concerns once they had received their payment. The lack of customer service and accountability is unacceptable. I will not be using Outdoorsy again and strongly advise others to be cautious when selecting payment options on their platform.

name: Cam Bogan
title: For Outdoorsy C-Suite
text: First of all, full transparency, I have never booked through Outdoorsy. What I have done is researched the internet universe to find an affordable place to live for a bit less than a year, because I am temporarily homeless. I specifically included the term "long-term" in the Google Search along with "RV rentals" and Outdoorsy came up close to the top and stated there on the Results page, "So unless you're looking for a 6 month rental..." , so I decided to see what was available on your site. I used your filter to choose my price range (by the way, you really need to add a Sort option to list RV's from least to most/most to least expensive option, because without it, you're wasting your customer's most important and non-renewable resource, their time) and realized that there was no option for long-term rentals with a reasonable monthly charge option. And thanks to the lack of Sort option for price-grouping, I had to look through 50+ options that were in my area. Since listings are ALL by the night and most for over $100 a night, that would make my legitimately long-term need of a 7 month rental (specifically 11/1-05/31), at $100 a night, $22K. The people that have the kind of money that make this amount seem reasonable, would likely just buy an RV, that way they can use it then put it on here for their entertainment subscription fund. I'm not asking you to stop being a predatory American company, I'm just asking you to be more honest and direct with your offerings. And, if you're already missing me before I sign off, don't despair, I will be doing another one of these reviews  for your unbelievably manipulative process by which you require customers to run around in figurative circles to close their Outdoorsy account. Toodles!

name: Chris Kutensky
title: I have been a long time host and renter, with Outdoorsy and others
text: I have been a long time renter and host, for 8yrs with Outdoorsy, as I recall. I'm my experience, they have a fantastic website and process. At days end, they are middle men. I felt that they handled CV19 when business was ten fold, smoothly when they were likely under staffed and many inexperienced renters, we're on the road renting RVs because airplanes were shutdown. I host in CO, a tourist state and if I had 20 Airstreams, I could have rented them all, easily. I can only imagine how hard Outdoorsy and other RV vendors worked to try to keep millions of units and millions of personalities Happy! It's a law of averages, and you'll always have some negatives, but as you can see it's 5% and when I was a kid, 95% was an A+.  Having rented and hosted for years I've learned any negative review is just like anything, it's based on personality and expectations, unless there is a blatant neglect of communication. Otherwise, personality plays a role, and I'm just as guilty of having too high expectations and no different than a dating website, every profile has a certain effort to market, whether price point, or allowing Pets when other do not.So, I say, always look at the big picture and the % of positive stars as some people post negatively based on emotion, or one-sided points of views, for example, host or renter. I recommend you consider the RVs age first, as age has wear/tear, and match that age to the competitive cost. Photos are great on sewing the design and general unit, but it doesn't show parts and like an aged car, truck, computer, what have you, age plays a role. Personally, I am thankful for Outdoors, introducing me to some fantastic, renters and I truly enjoy RVs and love being a Host, seeing renters come home after their journey and family vacation, all relaxed and happy. You can see the stress that has left their shoulders from PickUp to DropOff. BUT that said, there will always be certain personalities that you just can't live up to their expectations, and as a Host, you just tell them, text me, call me, let me know how I can help. We will handle any issues that comes up, if any, work with RV repair vendors, pay them, and upon drop off, if determined it wasn't Wear/Tear, we have deposits to reimburse us, but we just want you to enjoy, and so does Outdoors. It's a vacation, time to relax and enjoy and avoid making Mountains out of MoleHills as they say, as it's all comes out in the wash.  And over many years, I have issues as both renter and host, always minor but even issues with Brand New trucks or Rvs, it can happen, so keep comms open, that's what I recommend. No one wants a bad vacation for anyone, and that certainly not why Outdoorsy and Hosts option this industry. I saw this as I've had 1 or 2 personalities who tend, finding to complain whether RV, other industries / business they get involved in, they just tend to demand and it's just characteristic, no matter who the vendor may be. In today's world, it's hard to connect with this persona as they communicate one-way, and talk at you, instead of with you. I've seen very very few, but it's exaggeration and characteristic of the submitter, but to submit 1 star, even start to a middleman vendor, seems more emotional, than offering readers the positives. Why blame Outdoorsy unless the entire vacation was unruly managed start to finish, canceled or destroyed, at their direct blame. I just think emotions are not good reviews. With a great of Tv experience, I know some folks get upset about small things where others accept that "life happens". Wear and tear exists when you rent units over 5yrs, it's part of Rv life, there are tons of forums you should look into, per model you wish to rent, as that can help too.  Life is short, enjoy your vacation and just know that the older the "rental unit" it's more likely to have some small glitch occur, and don't try to fix or work on a Hosts Rv, without working with them, as I've seen people break things trying to Google How To, so let your Host handle it. And if an RV repairman need to get involved, hand it off to Host, they need to know who's working on their unit, and they know their Rv best, or either way, let them pay direct, hand it off to them, so you can go back to enjoying your time with family, friends or your journey.Two way communication is the answer. As long as there is two-way communication, there is no issue that can't be resolved. And no need to blame Outdoorsy or other vendors in general, your our Guest(s). Just work together and you will be in the 95%, I say, from my years in Rv works. Hope this helps!

name: Modoka
title: I was a Host on Outdoorsy
text: I was a Host on Outdoorsy.The hosting process just to get started was aggravating to begin with.  It's like no-one was serious about helping me get started.  You had to send them the same documents multiple times and they just kept passing you to the next customer service representative. The customer service was crap... After 2 or 3 weeks of trying to get set up, I was finally able to.  Skip to my first and only renter..  After their trip, they returned the camper late, and I understand things happen.  However, the Toilet/Tank was full and clogged first off.  I had to pay for the state park to let me empty it.  Next I noticed on the outside of the travel trailer there was duct tape across the arms and the main beam of the awning, Stretching the entire length.   Last, one of my slide outs were stuck in and and wouldn't go back out.  Mind you I emailed outdoorsy the photos plus receipts and I had to hire a mobile RV Mechanic to make the slide out work again.  They did a review and said they can't use the customers deposit for the damages.  (EXCUSE ME!) I understood that's what a deposit is for.  So that if something breaks that the deposit will help pay for the damages.. HUH, I guess not.  Either way Ive emailed back and forth with the piece of crap company and gotten nowhere.  They refuse to take the money out of the customers deposit and not pay me back for the mobile mechanic or the waste fee.  To me it's just the point of it all.  I do not recommend anyone using outdoorsy for your RV rental hosting needs.  BEWARE!!!

name: kerriecameron
title: At a loss for our holidays because customer service did nothing to help us
text: After booking an RV we tried contacting the host to set up arrangements.  The host wasn't responding. I emailed host once 3 weeks and a second time one week before reaching out to customer support for help.Customer supports response was that they give hosts 24-48 hours to respond because "we understand life can throw your routine off".  I replied with our timeline of trying to contact the host and asked that they help us reach the host. I haven't heard anything back from customer support after this.I emailed multiple times and I called multiple times. No one would answer the call, and once I was on hold for 30 minutes (no exaggeration) to only be disconnected after a recording told me no one was available to take my call.I reached out on social media with my situation and got a response to call or email customer support for assistance... really?!  That response just added more to my frustration.I had to cancel my reservation one week before our holidays because of the unresponsive host and lack of support from the folks at outdoorsy.  Thankfully the amount was deposited back into my account.Now aside from this frustrating experience with outdoorsy and their host, I am $80 out of pocket for the "service fee" that wasn't refunded... Really?!  What service did I pay for??  A whole lot of wasted time on my end for trying to get service, I should charge outdoorsy for my time, not the other way around.But the worst part of all this is my family and I have been looking forward to this, our annual holiday that we work very hard to afford and now we don't know what we're going to do.  We have a campground  booked with nothing to bring with us. So to quote your customer service I guess "life can throw your routine off" but replace "life" with "outdoorsy".From this experience, my take away is outdoorsy doesn't care. At no point did anyone on your end try to resolve this matter.  You have profited off my service fee and my family is now at a loss on what we will do.  An appropriate action on your part would have been to 1) Respond to our concerns first and foremost 2) Try to resolve our concerns by helping us contact the host 3) If the host remained unresponsive, find another solution if possible.  Would there have been another rental you could have helped us manage? We even would have paid more for a bigger camper if necessary.  But unfortunately none of that happened.No one wins from this experience! Outdoorsy, sure you made money from my service fee, but you had to refund $800 and our holidays are one week away and we don't know what we're going to do.Outdoorsy if you do care about the people you are providing services to and making a profit off of, you still have time to make this right for me and my family. I have little hope, but at this time I have little options.

name: Justin Pintler

name: Zach Klimko
title: Giant red flags
text: Giant red flags. We rented a trailer that had a completely dead battery, and we were given no idea by the owner.We provided Outdoorsy time stamped photos of the battery going dead within 45 minutes, even after hours of running a generator to charge it. We lost all our food overnight, we had no heat. We had an incessant beep that kept our dog and family up, and the only way to stop it was by running the generator at all times, which clearly isn't an option in the middle of the night.After weeks of internal review outdoorsy sent us a photo of their terms of service with yellow highlighting on the line saying "failing to use the vehicle in compliance with all instructions and warnings provided by us and hosts." Not sure how we could have better used a dead battery that was not disclosed. We did buy additional propane as the owner did disclose that he didn't even check if they were filled. And we weren't given a key.Hideous experience and clearly Outdoorsy is going to back their owners over the customers. Buyer beware.

name: May L.
title: RENTER BEWARE
text: Since Outdoorsy refuses to post my negative review on their site I will post it here.Backstory -Outdoorsy provides a 14 day window to provide a review. I was about to post my review on their site at 11pm on the 14th day and it said I was no longer able to post as they operate in central time and it was already 1am the next day so I missed their window by 1 hour.I was then asked if the review was positive as they could manually post a positive review for me but not a negative one.Can someone please explain how this is a fair policy that they can manually post a positive review but not a negative one? It’s screams scam all over and fake positive reviews.Here is my review of my RV rental experience:RENTER BEWAREAs first time RV renters, we were extremely disappointed with our stay and the treatment of our group. We had to depart a day earlier than expected and had called the host to let them know. I asked what we needed to do before leaving and he said just make sure to turn everything off and close the door. They never mentioned anything about cleaning the RV before we left, nor was it mentioned to us when we checked-in. Later that evening, we received a message saying we had left the RV in a ‘state’ and that there were stains on the cushions and blinds and they were charging us $775 for excess cleaning and to replace the items that were supposedly stained.We were honestly shocked by this message and offered our apologies and even to come back and clean the RV due to the misunderstanding of what the prep fee covers as we were under the impression it covered the cleaning (it literally states on Outdoorsy that the fee is to cover professional cleaning and required maintenance checks).We were told that they were unavailable and had already cleaned half the RV. We explained that we were under the impression the prep fee covered the cleaning but then the host began to scold me telling me they had left cleaning supplies and that I was making excuses as to why it wasn’t cleaned.They did not care at all that it was a misunderstanding and that if we had known we were supposed to clean it, we would have done so.We feel taken advantage of as first time RV renters as there is no way it would cost them $200 of time to clean the RV, $431.15 to replace the dinette cushion with a tiny yogurt drink stain or $144.45 to replace the blinds that we had supposedly stained.Hopefully this review can help the next person renting so they do not get scammed like we did. Make sure you read the paperwork before you sign it and do not be too trusting of hosts. Also make sure to take photos and document before and after as we forgot to take photos before we left and therefore had no evidence of our own to dispute their claim.

name: Sad Camper
title: Same day cancellation by owner
text: Our host/owner cancelled at the last minute on the day of the rental.  He was very nice and apologetic, but that did not help our camping trip.  He had a known medical condition that he did not make accommodations for.I give the company two stars, rather than one because we did get all of our money back, from Outdoorsy, and the company did make an effort to find another camper, but due to the last minute notice, the few available did not fit our needs.

name: Kelly Martin
title: We rented an RV June 2022
text: We rented an RV June 2022. The person we rented the RV from was great. However, the awning fell off during our travels. We had purchased an insurance policy and paid the thousand dollar deductible. Then outdoorst proceeded to essentially harass my car insurance company for additional damages for which they paid out an additional $3000. We're not even sure how the awning fell off but we were considered responsible. My insurance company said that there was a clause in the rental agreement stating that although the insurance was purchased through outdoorsy, they had the right to pursue further damages from the car insurance. I would never use this company again. it was an awful experience.

name: Gord Nuttall
title: Average SaaS company
text: Better roadside assistance needed.  I feel they only care about bookings, a typical SaaS.  And how they get away with taking 40% is beyond me. They charge the renter and host both around 20% per booking.  Way to high imho.  Should be more like 15% like airbnb and VRBO.  That's a finder's fee, not 40%.  Competitors are the same.  It must be the insurance companies.

name: Christoph Mischke

text: There is an international transaction fee of 3% of all payments, although I paid in Canadian dollars. Will never rent there again.

name: Graham
title: Probably won't be trying Outdoorsy again
text: I have used Turo to rent cars on vacations and thought Outdoorsy would be similar.  I submitted my "application" to rent a very attractive van, using the Outdoorsy website, selecting from the calendar for available days.  I also sent a supporting message to the owner, giving some information about me and my wife.  I did notice that many of the postings by other owners and this one had no bio: "Host bio coming soon! **** is committed to providing great stays for guests." I received a message from the owner saying that our requested dates were taken and the van was being used by the owners family.  I let them know that the online calendar still indicated availability.  They have still not updated that.  I am sure there are other options but I just could not be bothered struggling with the back and forth.  Will use a commercial business next time.  Similar pricing.

name: scott
title: Great times
text: I would leave no stars but that is not an option. Our trip went great trailer was wonderful everything went smoothly

In the beginning i had a few people who misrepresented their situation. I cancelled with them and i was given to understand it was my fault and i could face a penelty. It has been a good experience all the way around with these renters.I have one issue about issuing a refund to one guest that outdoorsy has not resolved.

name: Anita

text: Booking an RV through Outdoorsy was straightforward, but our trip was plagued with issues that led us to request a refund. Despite numerous calls, I’m always told, 'We will contact you in 48 hours,' but no one ever follows up. This level of service is unacceptable. Save yourself the hassle and book elsewhere!

name: Joseph  Cooper
title: The camper was at the site and set up…
text: The camper was at the site and set up when we arrived and that's about as good as it gets. Tanks were not emptied the unit was filthy, curtains missing, smoke detector was removed, refrigerator and freezer had food items, cabinets were full of stuff, mattress with big stains, bad smell from tanks not emptied and no keys to lock the unit and that's not all. They put us in contact with the owner of the unit and all he could say was Im sorry and he will see that we get a refund. They say how sorry they are but do nothing to correct the situation. They need to inspect the campers they are renting out some how, like have to owner send pics day of delivery or something. I could go on but they won't care.

name: Ryan VanSickle
title: I’ve hosted my RV for 2-years on the…
text: I’ve hosted my RV for 2-years on the Outdoorsy Platform and finally removed myself completely this week. The service/support, App Issues and overall inadequate screening processes are not worth the effort.To use one example - Outdoorsy “verifies” drivers and renters through a “proprietary process” which it states gives you the piece of mind that a driver is legally able to drive a motor vehicle. One renter ended up causing damage while driving my RV and at the end of the trip the Outdoorsy Team went to file a claim and found he hadn’t had auto insurance in more than 2-years and his driver’s license had been revoked by the state. The claim/repair took several more weeks to be approved and has still yet to be resolved as they worked through how to appropriately handle the situation. I wouldn’t trust someone who shows up to take your vehicle from the App; there are great, honest renters out there but Outdoorsy’s policies don’t allow you to differentiate.*9/11/24 Update: I’ve been contacted internally by the Outdoorsy Team but can share that there still hasn’t been any progress on my Claim Status. The uninsured driver who damaged my vehicle submitted fake Insurance Information and Outdoorsy is “waiting to hear from them” before they proceed. I’ve left a handful of messages with Progressive to no avail. Be ready for a multi-month repair if you have any damage done to your RV.

name: Kimia Malekzadeh

name: Tracy Federwitz
title: This business is fraudulent
text: This business is fraudulent - stay away!  I have been repeatedly charged on multiple occasions by this company without any warning or explanation.  It started well - I rented a camper and they held a $500 security deposit on top of the rental costs.  We returned the camper without any issues.  They released the security deposit.  Then, a month later, they reauthorized the $500 charge without any explanation or warning, even though my rental had long been over.  Then a month after that, Outdoorsy charged my account AGAIN for $341, without any warning or explanation.  My rental had then been over for two months - they are total frauds.  DO NOT WORK WITH OUTDOORSY, as a renter OR host!!!

name: Lynn Van Eaton
title: Look elsewhere
text: As a host with Outdoorsy I’ve found several inconveniences doing business through this company. Navigating their website/app seems convoluted and illogical. I have to click through too many other menu options to get to my calendar to update my availability. The app only allows you to upload up to 5 photos for the pre- and post-trip inspections and also requires printed inspections which take up a lot of time. The company is pretty paper-heavy. Hosts are required to print out the 28-page rental terms & conditions in addition to roughly a dozen pages of pre-arrival checklists, walk-throughs, booking documents, and post-trip inspection FOR EVERY GUEST. These things should all be available through the app but that’s not an option at this point. The company takes 25% of each booking payout, which is the most I’ve seen among the 5+ RV rental platforms I’ve researched. Plus they charge the host a cancellation fee of $50-$100 (after the 2nd cancellation within 6mos) even if the host has to cancel as a result of a renter doing damage to the RV or if a guest bails but doesn’t officially cancel. Why should the company, who suffers no inconvenience, get a cancellation fee? I’m giving them two stars instead of one for the fact that they seem to have a large pool of guests & hosts to connect. However if you’re looking to rent out your RV I’d look elsewhere.

name: Nahomy Atias
title: Stay away from this app
text: Stay away from this app! I booked a trailer and the host confirmed, after that she asked for more money saying the app didn't calculate the delivery, which I call BS, because I did paid 250$ as a delivery fee, since she accepted that means I'm subject to HER cancellation policy, and she won't cancel. Customer service is completely useless. I had to file a fraud case with my credit card to get my money back!

name: Cesarino Battistel
title: Double billed for security deposit (see update)

name: Stephanie Peoples
title: JUST STAY AWAY FROM OUTDOORSY-READ THE REVIEWS AND THE FINE PRINT
text: JUST STAY AWAY FROM OUTDOORSY!Today is 7/29/24 and I am still dealing with a bogus scam claim from 7/4/24, 25 days later!  I have spent several hours over many many days trying to communicate with Outdoorsy and I deeply regret using them.We are experienced campers.  We decided to rent an RV this time to make things easy (ha!).  We paid about $400 (in addition to rental, insurance, and Outdoorsy fees) to have it delivered and set up. During our rental over the 4th of July, the power cord + surge protector failed...resulting in a smoking, melted plug.  We were left with no power, no A/C, and we are in Texas in the middle of Summer. To our surprise, the the owner filed a damage claim against us which resulted in many headaches and countless hours of wasted time-with no real help from Outdoorsy. In fact, whenever I called, I could only speak with someone in the PHILIPPINES-never the same person, and never a last name.  Sometimes someone would respond via email, but would not be available by phone.  There was always a promise to escalate, but no follow-through.We had actually purchased the stationary insurance (also called excess insurance), which we learned that they defer to YOUR PERSONAL AUTO POLICY FIRST.  When I went back, I eventually found this in the fine print, but had to click through several pages and links to get to-essentially a rabbit hole. After the owner was told by our insurance company that this was not a qualified claim (and subsequently denied), he then pursued it with the Outdoorsy stationary policy-which was also denied. He told our insurance company that he would pursue it through the security deposit. They then emailed to ask us to approve a charge of $400-to pay for their faulty equipment-even after 2 denials stating that we were not responsible for their equipment failing. We declined. We cannot get anyone at Outdoorsy to help us with this, though we have reached out via phone and email multiple times. Today we learned that Outdoorsy has charged our card for ANOTHER $750-the original amount of our deposit.After another call and another request to escalate-they are telling us that they have released it.  I have yet to confirm that with my CC company, but will need to make sure that all future attempts to charge us will be denied.A side note of the stationary/excess policy-they also add an additional charge for roadside assistance-which you should not need if you are not towing the vehicle.  In fact, the policy becomes null and void if you move the camper for any reason on a stationary policy.We would never even think of trusting Outdoorsy again-it's really just a platform, taking a cut, and cheaply outsourcing their customer service.There is no protection and no one to call who can do anything to help.

name: Wanderlust AV
title: I've rented my vehicles via Outdoorsy…
text: I've rented my vehicles via Outdoorsy for three years now.  On a recent rental, one of my clients had a minor issue with their rental.  We discussed and decided a small refund would be best suited to resolve the situation.  Outdoorsy instructs you to call them if you would like to refund your client for something other than a cancellation.  When I called I was told that Outdoorsy would keep their 25% cut of the refund.  That's right, Outdoorsy keeps their 25% "host service fee" on the amount of money you REFUND as the host.Outdoorsy is not much of a service but provides a great disservice to both the renter, to whom they charge exorbitant fees and force the sale of often redundant insurance products but also the owner, from whom they take a 25% cut, even when the owner didn't ultimately keep those funds.I would love to see another business disrupt Outdoorsy and provide a quality, peer to peer, platform for rentals.  Most renters already have adequate auto insurance that covers their rental. Most owners need little more than a platform/market on which to rent their rigs and a payment processing service that allows for security deposits to be held appropriately.   What nobody needs is Outdoorsy in the middle of it all, bilking all parties for every penny they can.Follow up to Outdoorsy's response- yes, that's correct, you are keeping 25% of money the owner does not keep.  There is no confusion here nor is anyone implying that an additional fee is charged.Folks, this is why Outdoorsy releases 100% of your payout after handoff; it ensures they are keeping 25% of that money no matter what happens during or after the rental.  No other platform keeps their fee, particular a 25% one, on money you don't actually net.  In this case I wanted to refund my renter $750.  Trouble is, Outdoorsy only paid me $562.50.  I can't refund money I never received and Outdoorsy refuses to return their $187.50 cut of those funds that, again, are not in my bank account, to the renter.  They refuse to explain what they are keeping that $187.50 for and I don't know a soul who could rationalize why that money wouldn't be refunded to the renter.I can't post images here but would love to share a breakdown of a trip with the public to shed light on the exorbitant fees Outdoorsy hits both renter and owner with.  It's classic gig economy corporate shenanigans where a real service/platform is provided but everyone gets ripped off in the process of utilizing it.The fact that they want a 25% cut of money you don't get paid really says it all though.
