name: Brad
title: I rented a travel trailer that stated…
text: I rented a travel trailer that stated was "brand spanking new" that had too much to list here wrong with it. Broken awning, bathroom vent, etc. Through observation, video, and photos this was not new or even close. But what really turned things was me being alerted by someone at an intersection in the midst of returning vehicle that one of the tires was making a "bad sound". My wife and I rolled down windows and could definitely hear what she was saying. Tried to see if I could determine the cause. Thought it might be one tire that looked like missing something. At that time, I messaged owner rep to say something was wrong and asked if I should stop or continue to return. Was told camper had always had an issue with a tire and that I should be fine. A few miles later the tread on the tire separated causing a massive blowout and damage to the undercarriage. Was told in this process that there was no visible evidence of outside damage and tire appeared to be faulty. Also, through this process was told that tires were new by owner (worded in such a fashion as if to release her of any liability because this doesn't happen to new tires, while failing to recognize this is where they happen the most). Was also told that there had been a blowout on the same tire 2 months prior. Was told that is why "I" have insurance and within hours my $500 deductible was taken. I disputed the deductible because I am to be given a safe and reliable vehicle to rent. Was not provided a safe and reliable vehicle, and then when something on the camper failed, the expectation was of me to fix it or pay for it. This would be the final response from my dispute...Hi Bradley,After an investigation and careful consideration of the evidence provided by both parties, we have decided in your favor.We believe you should be refunded $250 from the security deposit claimed. While we uncovered that the tires were over 5 years old already, we believe you should shoulder $250 since the damage was incurred during your rental.And here is my response and reason for 1 star....Think I will consult with someone on this. Aside from a contradiction within your response which has to leave someone lying by stating they were outdated tires when I had multiple people state tires were new (with one very important individual stating they were new and faulty), it is the holding the renter accountable due to the actions of an owner that finds this resolution appalling to me.If what you state in your resolution is correct, then the lack of action by an owner to provide safe and reliable tires has taken place. If what the owner and her handyman stated (and documented) is correct in stating the tires were newly purchased, it was they who purchased and installed an inferior product and not myself. Had I punctured a tire, went to purchase a new tire on my own, the tire then exploded causing damage, I would most certainly be singing a different tune. But your resolution seems to state that I must pay 250 dollars because someone provided me with an unsafe and unreliable vehicle for rent. It's hard for me to not think of a thousand scenarios at play here that would represent the same type of conclusion. Such as, what if an owner has an engine failing?  Was repaired with substandard or improper parts that result in complete engine failure while on the next rental. Would the responsibility of the renter be to replace the engine? If so, then there are no protections from the owner's doing whatever they want, with WHATEVER they want, because of no consequence. And I have a significant issue with this because the initial response from the owner of my rental was just that. And I quote, "that's why you have insurance".As far as I'm concerned, the first and foremost priority from the owner is to provide a safe and reliable vehicle for rental. The fact this did not happen should instantly render any contract null and void and prohibited anyone from obtaining my deposit. I seem to believe most people would agree with me. And what adds insult to injury is that you have a host who is falsely advertising a vehicle that is not as it is portrayed.What also bothers me greatly is the fact that I reached out to the owner's representative prior to any damage occurring to state there was an issue. Specifically asked him whether to continue or not. Only to be told they have always had an issue with a tire and I should continue.I will say basically the same thing I said to the owner. This is absolutely about principle. I do not believe I should pay 500/250/or even 5 dollars. The responsibility of repairs needed due to faulty parts and equipment provided by an owner should not rest on the renter in any shape or form but that of the owner.

name: Nigel Bell
title: Abandoned by Outdoorsy
text: I hired a RV through Outdoorsy through August 2023 (20 nights). They sub-let to another company in the days/week before commencement - being told the campervan I booked (5 months earlier) was no longer available. A 'similar' vehicle was available when I arrived (same price, same conditions).  Wrong.No stealth camping as few curtains (!), no pillows (!), limited stove or utensils (!), no outdoor seating or  cover (!).  Not what I expected or paid for ....But worse was the developing problems with the two-year old automatic vehicle (a Mercedes van!).From Day 1 it had problems - wrong gear, shuddering forward, over-revving - which was increasingly dangerous when driving on US freeways at half the set speed.  Stop-start - stop - shudder - stop - start - stop altogether - so multiple calls to the intermediary company, then Outdoorsy.Outdoorsy provides intermittent phone calls/call-backs during the afternoon, leading to a request to drive (!) to the nearest specialist repair workshop (30 miles away).  Tried on back-roads .. but same problems and the vehicle again died half way, leaving me at the edge of the road in 108F degree heat in the middle of no-where ... for 15 hours /overnight!Many Outdoorsy phone calls - no action - before next morning the tow vehicle was sent to the previous (wrong) address!Eventually, towed away to the repair shop.  Long wait before they diagnosed the problem.  Meantime, Outdoorsy told me I was one my own - they wouldn't supply an alternative vehicle.  I was expected to start all over again with a new hire (whilst marooned in the middle of nowhere!)."Not good enough, we have a paid contract" I said - and let me speak to the manager.  It took a week before a manager sent an email back, asking about my problem !!!!And fortunately for me, the dealer found and fixed the 'drive' cables/electronics that had been chewed through by 'varmints' prior to my hire.  So after two delayed days of hassle I was able to continue.LESSONS:Outdoorsy would not meet their contractual conditions when it got hard....they made their vehicle replacement problems mine ...Outdoorsy is better at PR and marketing than delivering ...Outdoorsy subsequently made it very difficult to get a refund for the lost two days of travel ...Don't believe their promotional spin .. my experience says you're on you're own if there's a vehicle replacement problem.

name: Umar Chouhdry
title: Beware of Outdoorsy's Misleading…
text: Beware of Outdoorsy's Misleading Cancellation Policy and Poor Customer ServiceI recently had an incredibly disappointing experience with Outdoorsy, a company that seemed promising for RV rentals. My ordeal began when I booked a van for a trip in June, well in advance. Realizing the costs were too steep for my budget 10 days later, I decided to cancel, expecting a reasonable refund considering the trip was nearly 5 months (June 2024) away. To my shock, I discovered that Outdoorsy had a hidden trap in their cancellation policy, costing me over $1000 in cancellation fees, for a service I never utilized.The van owner, under the guise of convenience, persuaded me to switch from Turo to Outdoorsy, which I suspect was a maneuver to exploit Outdoorsy's cancellation policy for his financial gain. Outdoorsy's policy, which mercilessly penalizes customers for cancellations made outside a narrow 48-hour window post-booking, is both unfair and predatory, especially when cancellations are made well in advance of the booking date.Their defense? A rigid adherence to a policy that favors hosts at the expense of customers, trapping hard-earned money with no service provided. The fact that this trip was months away and the rushed booking process facilitated by the van owner makes this policy even more egregious.Outdoorsy's lack of transparency and customer empathy has left me feeling cheated and disillusioned. Their policies do not protect the interests of the customer but serve to enrich themselves and their hosts at our expense. I caution anyone considering using Outdoorsy for their RV rental needs to think twice. You may find yourself, like me, out of pocket for services you never received, entangled in a web of unfair policies designed to profit from your change of plans.Final Rating: 1/5 StarsAvoid Outdoorsy if you value your money and seek a fair, customer-centric rental experience. There are other platforms out there that respect and protect their customers' interests far better.

name: Laurie Aaron-Chodoronek
title: Our family of 6 got scammed by Outdoorsy!!
text: Our family of 6 is planning a 10 day road trip this summer and wanted one vehicle comfortable for us all. I found the perfect vehicle on Outdoorsy, absolutely stunning! We were all so excited. The booking was glitchy and instead of charging a deposit with the reservation I was charged the full $1,300 for the trip that doesn't start for 5 months! I contacted customer service, they fixed it and charged me $757 in Feb. for a Jul. trip, balance later. I never received a confirmation from the vehicle owner, just from Outdoorsy. A few weeks later my daughter inquired about vehicle features and found out the vehicle was sold a year and a half ago and the owner can't get Outdoorsy to remove it. I contacted customer service to cancel and refund all my money. I was told they won't refund my money unless the vehicle owner verifies my claim. Now the vehicle owner has become unresponsive too. If you try to cancel the reservation on Outdoorsy they keep a service charge of $145. It's a total mess and Outdoorsy accepts no responsibility in validating a reservation, or vehicle availability or promptly refunding my money. For a finish, I'm now disputing the charge with my credit card company under fraud protection. Outdoorsy took my money, won't refund it, for a vehicle that isn't available. These people are scammers! Watch out!

name: christie
title: Avoid at all costs!!
text: Edited to add that following my review outdoorsy have finally sent us on the 'invoices' from the owner which is a screen grab from Amazon and a shopping cart for another website! The owner hasn't even ordered the parts they've charged us for and outdoorsy have still taken the money from us!Steer clear!! We visited LA and hired an RV through outdoorsy for ten nights to see some sights and enjoy a family holiday.On delivery of the RV the owners told us they'd been up all night trying to fix the slide out after the family that rented it and finished with it the night before our trip has broken it and we need to be extra careful with it as it was not fully fixed, handed us a screwdriver and sent us on our way. Should have run a mile then!First night we struggled with the slide out and the over cab bunk wouldn't work, asked owners for help and they said they'd work it out and let us know the morning after!! So 3 beds down and no where for the kids to sleep we finally found a you tube video on how to over ride the system and bring the beds down.Long story short we had several issues with the slide out and the owners advise was to not use it, but since we'd rented the RV as a family of 6 we needed the slide out working in order to have enough space to sleep. Ended up having to stay in one place so that the owners who were exceptionally rude and aggressive over the phone could come meet us to try fix the issue, they managed a quick fix but told us we'd only be able to perform one more slide action and so we couldn't visit anywhere else in it and had to drive in one from San Fran to LA. During one of our drives an awning over one slide out actually came loose and on advice from the owners my husband and sons had to climb up on to the roof of the RV to remove it!! We stayed in touch with outdoorsy via email during the trip so that they were aware of the issues we were having and they continually reassured us that they would help us claim compensation on return to the UK.The owners also advised us that the TVs in the RV didn't work without dvds (despite advertising that it had an outdoors TV entertainment system and two indoors) so we never used the TVs.When we delivered the RV back to the owner she herself didn't turn up and instead sent her husband who rushed us out saying he was late for a school play (they chose the collection time) he wouldn't do a walk round but verbally confirmed happy with the RV and zoomed off within five minutes of us arriving back.On return to the UK they've claimed $1300 of our deposit and have only started 'TV and slide out topper' as the reason. We've asked them to confirm what was wrong and what they mean by that but got the response 'tv and slide out topper'We've gone through outdoorsy internal review and they took over a month to decide that they don't know who's at fault and cannot provide us with evidence or proof of even a basic description of what they've claimed the money for as they say the money was taken by the host and not outdoorsy (shows as outdoorsy on our statement)They do not want to know. I'm not sure how money can be taken without any proof as to what for or why.Were assuming the slide out topper means the awning they actually told us to remove and was also missing from the other side of the RV so I'm certain somewhere another family have been charged for that and it's never been fitted or replaced.I've warned outdoorsy that this owner needs removing from the platform but as long as it's making them money they don't seem to care.Do not book with this company please save yourself the hassle. A month on from our holiday we're still chasing our money back.When the initial claim was made on our deposit outdoorsy told us it was just a hold whilst the internal investigation was ongoing and that it wouldn't actually be taken but a few days later it left our account.Dishonest, unreliable and unhelpful.

name: Aaron
title: Beware
text: From the very beginning the people we were dealing with were less than up front about various maintenance issues.  They knew exactly how many miles we were traveling and that we were using the unit to move our 97 year old mother, who had just had a stroke.Basically there were several things that would fail, cause further damage and even perhaps cause injury that we had to fix.  When we returned the unit the owners claimed there was damage from a slide out unit that, to our knowledge, was working when we dropped the unit off.  We just walked away from the $1500 deposit and then, after dragging things on for a month they want more money.  I billed them for the work we had to perform and hope they just leave it at that.The impression I got from the process is that leaving things that will cause further damage is a strategy to have an excuse to grab the deposit from unsuspecting renters.  At this point it feels like they are trying to pick us up by our feet to shake all the change out of our pockets. We have already paid thousands of dollars and the maintenance of the vehicle should not be our problem.Just beware, I can't speak about all the owners, but these seem to want to take advantage of us.  The extra insurance we purchased has proven unresponsive and the Outdoorsy customer support is offering to try to bring resolution, so will see if this can end any time this year...Update: The interior damage insurance we purchased did come through, but it took quite a while.  To their credit Outdoorsy did give us a token credit to express good will and acknowledge our inconvenience with the issues we experienced.  Maybe through the process the owners, who are young, will learn about maintaining their equipment.Just beware, don't make assumptions and ask questions about the condition of the equipment.  According to the Outdoorsy policy, if the owners disclose a problem and you accept the rental, you become responsible for the problem and any further damage it may cause while in your possession.  If you experience issues with the equipment that require attention, if the owners are not cooperative, you are stuck on the side of the road and may be financially responsible for getting repairs done.

title: Watch your reviews and communicate quickly if there is an error.
text: UPDATE:  As can happen with technology - a problem can arise that was unintended and that appears to be what happened to me.  For that reason, I am amending my comments because while the system is flawed - the customer service team responded professionally, acknowledged a system flaw, and confirmed that it shouldn't have happened - which is GREAT.  Mistakes happen, and that is understandable. I feel confident that my issue was a glitch and for that reason, and the great communication with Outoorsey, I am revising my star rating from 1 to 4.  PRIOR REVIEW:  I saw an "automated review" on my account today that said, "Faith Lucchesi canceled reservation two days before our trip. Automated review."  While true in part, the guest initiated the cancellation, and to be kind, I AGREED TO REFUND ALL FEES that would have been due because of the cancellation policy. By agreeing to assist a renter, Outdoorsy's automated system told all other renters that I canceled someone's trip without the added fact that I did it at their request and agreed to refund all monies despite the cancellation policy. When I saw the review, many months after the harm was done, I called to discuss the matter, and the review was removed, but the damage was done. I was seriously misportrayed by the platform for more than six months, without my knowledge -and it was THEIR automatic response to the situation that published the review. NOT the guest, not me as host. And it was a lie as stated. The corporate decision to punish hosts who help guests is a shockingly myopic business decision and others should know this when reading reviews or considering becoming a host.

text: Update:After reaching out to more than twelve individuals from Outdoorsy Support and the Resolution department, who made promises to assist but unfortunately did not take any action to help, after exchanging almost THIRTY emails over the past month and engaging in nearly ten phone calls, I decided to share my experience through a one-star review below.Interestingly, once I posted this review, a transformation occurred. The Outdoorsy Customer Experience team stood out as the most professional and responsive unit within Outdoorsy, a stark contrast to my previous encounters. I appreciate their commitment to addressing my concerns and swiftly investigating the situation.With this positive development, I'm revising my review from one star to a five-star rating. This shift reflects the effectiveness and dedication of the Outdoorsy Customer Experience team. Thank you so much for your prompt attention and resolution.For the Manager Escalation: 4892316For the Resolutions team: 4881847The need for an enhanced level of customer service is evident, particularly in the case of the Resolutions Specialist. I encountered an issue with my trailer, which had been returned in a damaged state by the renter from Calgary. Regrettably, the renter from Calgary proceeded to present fabricated photos to the Resolutions Specialist falsely depicting a different deteriorated trailer with mold infestation. These images were inaccurately portrayed as my own trailer, despite clear disparities such as mold-free panels and a dissimilar fridge model in my brand new trailer.Upon bringing this discrepancy to the Resolutions Specialist attention, she acknowledged the erroneous nature of the photos and our conversation seemed to be progressing positively. However, the situation took an unfortunate turn when the renter from Calgary, in an unjust act, left a one-star review for my trailer. This review lamented the presence of rust and mold, while including the aforementioned misleading images on the Outdoorsy website. I took the initiative to kindly request that the Resolutions Specialist consider the removal of this unjust review, given its foundation in false imagery. Regrettably, the Resolutions Specialist declined my request, offering no explanation for her decision.Common sense would dictate that a review based on falsified photographs should be promptly removed. Yet, the Resolutions Specialist approach proved to be contrary to this principle. I have expended way over seventy hours hours grappling with this predicament, yet resolution has evaded me. This situation underscores the need for caution among trailer owners considering posting their listings on the Outdoorsy platform, as the potential for vexation and inconvenience looms large. The absence of logical decision-making due to inadequate training on the part of Resolutions Specialists compounds this concern.In an effort to escalate the matter, I sought the contact information of the Resolutions Specialist's supervisor over two weeks ago. Regrettably, this information has yet to be provided, even as I pen this review. My numerous interactions with Outdoorsy Support yielded no results, as they indicated their inability to intervene in a matter that the Resolutions Specialist is responsible for. Despite my request for a managerial intervention, no such communication has been initiated on their part.In summation, the experience has illuminated the necessity for a more proficient customer service approach. The situation highlights the urgency for Outdoorsy to address the shortcomings in their resolution processes and impart practical training to their staff. This will ensure that clients are not subjected to undue stress and dissatisfaction. For those considering listing their trailers on the platform, cautious contemplation is advised, as the existing system may engender frustration. The pursuit of a reasonable solution remains ongoing for over the month now, with the hope that Outdoorsy will demonstrate a greater commitment to customer satisfaction in the future.

text: You may not get paid!!!Unfortunately Outdoorsy has not lived up to the potential we thought they would when we researched companies to list our RV through. We have had numerous encounters where we were not taken care of as hosts.Our most recent experience involves not being paid for a rental that went out over three weeks ago. I have contacted support six times in various forms of communication, chat, email, and phone. Every single time I contact support they tell me they are going to take care of the issue and will follow up with me in 24 hours. The last time I called I asked to speak to a supervisor as I am done. I was told that they could take my information and that a supervisor would contact me within 24 hours because apparently, I have nothing better to do than sit around and wait for them to contact me yet again.Here's the situation. A renter requested to add a pet the day they were picking up our RV for their rental. I approved their request and added the pet fee through the app. Keep in mind the renter requested this addition through the app and was well aware of the additional charge. Now Outdoorsy is telling me that is what is holding up our payout because the renter has to AGAIN approve the request. I'm baffled by this process as it seems extremely inefficient.So here we are three weeks later and still no payment for our rental. I have even requested that they drop the pet fee and just pay me out of the original payment. Nope. They continue to give me the run around with no results.The last encounter we had with them was due to damage done to our trailer. They denied an insurance claim because it was not a collision. So I'm not really sure why they require renters to pay for insurance when it does absolutely nothing for them. Then Outdoorsy suggested that we as the owner reach out to the renter to see if he would be willing to pay almost $1,000 out of pocket for repairs. Absolutely no support from Outdoorsy. Isn't that why they get paid to be the middleman? Apparently not. Thankfully the renter was willing to work with us otherwise we would have been out almost $1,000 for a rental that only made us $330. But it gets better. The renter was happy to pay us through a different form of payment outside of Outdoorsy so we wouldn't incur charges. Well, Outdoorsy does a great job at monitoring your communication with renters and told us that we were not allowed to do that. That we HAVE to run the payment through them. Ok, fine. I asked the representative on the phone how the processing fee would be handled since we were only charging the renter for parts. She told me that we would not have a processing fee. Guess what? Yeah, there was a processing fee of $30. So now instead of breaking even on parts we were in the hole.At this point, I'm not even 100% sure why Outdoorsy takes such a big cut of the payments because there is zero support for owners. My next step if I don't get a resolution is to file a complaint with BBB. Oh, and we will be removing our rental from Outdoorsy. Not worth it unless you have hours of time to take care of your renters, clean your rental, and fight with Outdoorsy to get paid.

title: Many shortfalls, but much potential to excel.
text: Outdoorsy takes an unreasonable percentage of the rental cost, given the amount and quality of service they provide. Their website does not provide sufficient information to the host from tentative guests, such as number of people, whether or not there are pets, etc., despite guests providing that information on the website to facilitate their search. I always have to ask to determine whether or not to apply pet fees, and to ensure I have sufficient linen/commodities for my guests. Customer support staff are always friendly, patient and quick to respond. They ensure all your questions have been addressed before ending a call/chat session. Customer support staff are not fully aware of the coverages of the policy and provide inaccurate information on what is and is not covered by the insurance policy. Outdoorsy insurance policies do not cover blowouts, leaving owners/hosts liable for blowout related damages directly associated with rentals. I disagree with this, as blowouts are one of the most common damages experienced in transit and damages occurring during the rental ought be covered by the rental and deposit funds ought be subject to those damages. The claims process moves slowly. I had a claim covered by the policy that took just shy of three months to be reimbursed for parts and labor for repairs, despite having all necessary documentation provided to them within 3 weeks of the incident. They initially attempted to pay me $300 less than what was owed and I had to go back and forth with the claims team to get the matter rectified. The staff is friendly and cooperative, but difficult to talk to the same person each time, forcing me to explain the situation to a new person each time I call in. I will be leaving the platform and utilizing an alternate service provider for my rentals. I wish them luck and hope my review provides some insight that helps them improve their services in a way that allows them to succeed and grow as a business.In summary, Outdoorsy has much potential to improve and become a quality source for hosts and guests to find one another, but currently lacks much in website quality, claims coverage, claims efficiency and claims accuracy.

title: WARNING to all potential customers of…
text: WARNING to all potential customers of Outdoorsy!My experience with Outdoorsy was initially smooth. We rented an RV and had an enjoyable trip. However, our experience turned sour after returning the RV. We did a thorough walkthrough with the owner, and everything seemed fine. The owner even asked us to leave them a review, which we gladly did—a wonderful and appreciative one.But then, Outdoorsy hit us with an unexpected $600 charge for supposed damages! We were taken aback, as nothing was wrong during our rental. We disputed the charges and went through a back-and-forth email battle with Outdoorsy. Eventually, we managed to get only half of the money back (keep in mind that they take an extra $1000 deposit for future damages).The most frustrating part is that we contacted Outdoorsy to remove the glowing review we left for the RV owner, as it no longer reflected our experience. Outdoorsy, unfortunately, refused to remove the review. This means that our positive review is still misleading other potential renters who deserve to know the truth.Outdoorsy's review process is deceiving and flawed, enabling hosts to exploit the system. This was not the first time we've felt that a host abused this system. It leaves us questioning the fairness and reliability of the reviews on their platform.As a caution to others:Outdoorsy requires a $1000 deposit for damages, so be prepared for that.Take detailed pictures before and after your rental to protect yourself from false claims.Do not write a review until you get your full deposit back, as you won't be able to edit or remove it afterward.It is simply unjust and not ethical to refuse someone the right to edit or remove their review, especially when the circumstances have changed. Numerous other review platforms allow such modifications, so it is surprising that Outdoorsy does not offer this basic courtesy.I strongly advise future customers to be cautious when dealing with Outdoorsy. Their deposit and review system needs a serious overhaul to ensure fairness for all parties involved. It's not right for customers to feel cheated and misled by misleading reviews and unfounded damage claims.⚠️⚠️⚠️ Don't let yourself fall victim to Outdoorsy's flawed practices! ⚠️⚠️⚠️

title: Promising Concept with Room for Improvement: A Review of Outdoorsy
text: The concept behind Outdoorsy is fantastic, but there is room for improvement in their system. I have encountered some challenges while using the app, particularly during the checkout process. Uploading pictures for departures has been quite frustrating, as it takes a long time, and if you accidentally close out of the app, there is no way to get back in and complete the process. It would be beneficial if the app allowed users to load pictures at the end or provided a backup option to email them, ensuring a smoother checkout experience.Additionally, implementing a step-by-step guide for the checkout process could be helpful. This would assist users in ensuring they complete all the necessary steps correctly and avoid any potential issues.On top of that, I've noticed that there is room for improvement in the site's marketing. It seems like there aren't as many people inquiring about rentals as one would expect. Enhancing their marketing efforts could attract more potential renters and increase the platform's overall success.In conclusion, while I love the idea of Outdoorsy, some improvements in their app's functionality and checkout process, along with a stronger marketing strategy, could make the platform even better. Addressing these aspects would enhance user experience and potentially attract more customers to this fantastic concept.

title: It is OK. Not the best, not the worst.
text: I think the website and invoicing options are clumsy. It is not as good as it should be for the percentage that is taken from the rentals.  For example, I should be able to create Add Ons that are only charged upon return if the renter does not abide by the rules and it should be easier to refund clients without having to call Outdoorsy. Also, it is difficult to track money via Outdoorsy.  There are substantial delays in getting money from rentals, and if you do refund a customer it doesn't create a separate line transaction for easy tracking.  I don't want to be an accountant.  I want to rent vehicles.   But, I do like that Outdoorsy handles a lot of the other headacheds and also is tied to Roamly to provide insurance.  All in all, i don't think it is a terrible platform, but certainly has a lot of room for improvement for the money they take from each rental.

text: Before using BravoFly for the first time I read many negative reviews here to see where people had experienced issues. There is a soft up sell going on at all times, which I decided to ignore, picking the zero cost option at each step .. looking at the total cost clearly displayed on the right of my laptop screen as I did so.Once nice touch by BravoFly, they asked if any assistance will be needed *before* payment is made, I just had surgery so I opted for WCTG.BEWARE people who can/do not read, at the very last step I was again offered the 'opportunity' to upgrade to some flex plan, the wording is honest but tricky. If in doubt click the button that is NOT encouraged, just like always, for decades !-/I entered the CC info clicked PAY, verified using my bank app that the TOTAL AMOUNT was indeed the amount I expected .. how can anyone get this wrong ? Back from bank app to BravoFly payment confirmed and I was reminded I needed to wait up to 24 hours [maybe more because of assistance request] while BF agents worked feverishly on my behalf as I slept.Went to bed .. woke up .. got up [mofg ouch *!* surgery] .. checked email account I had given to BF .. yes all good, flight booking complete, logged into BF account with the email address I had given and checked everything looked ok, got the Airlines booking code from BF website.Logged into my previously registered Airline account which uses a different email address [cute] enter the BF supplied code and .. voila .. there is my booking along with the assistance request.I did update my contact details on Airlines system as the phone number got muddled [the country code was merged into the local number].Any changes to the flight booking must be made via BF, I can add secondary services via Airlines' site if I wish.What can I say, post Covid I stuck to booking directly with the airlines, this time I thought I'd be adventurous. BF saved me over 20% which is enough to matter IMHO.So far BravoFly are worth 4*s .. only magicians get more. If things go South, rather then East, I will update here.

name: Ali Sadek
title: SCAMMERS: Avoid Bravofly!
text: Misleading Policies and Terrible Customer Service.I had an incredibly frustrating and disappointing experience with Bravofly regarding a refund for my roundtrip flight from Australia to Costa Rica. I purchased their Full Flex service, which supposedly guaranteed a 90% refund for cancellations. Unfortunately, this service turned out to be a scam hidden behind convoluted fine-print terms and overcomplicated policies.Misleading Full Flex Policies:I received an email from Bravofly on May 5, 2024, confirming that my Full Flex insurance was active. However, Bravofly later claimed this email was sent in error, despite the terms stating:“The Voucher is valid for 12 months from the date the customer is notified of its details.”This means the service became active on May 5, regardless of an earlier refund. Bravofly refused to honor this, stating that a technical error absolves them of accountability.Poor Communication and Lack of Accountability:It took more than six months of emails to finally receive a response from someone with a name, rather than generic replies from their "Customer Care" team. Their responses consistently failed to address the core issues or provide any meaningful resolution.They ignored their responsibility for misleading communication, instead blaming me for not “confirming” whether the service was still active. Why should customers need to verify the validity of an email sent by the company itself?Nonexistent Escalation Process:Their representatives repeatedly refused to escalate my complaint. I was told the resolution would not change, even though their internal error directly caused my financial loss.Fine-Print Policies:Bravofly’s Full Flex service includes hidden restrictions, such as:Cancellations must be made before the outbound flight.Refunds do not apply to one leg of a booking.These terms were buried in the fine print and were not clearly communicated during the booking process. Instead, Bravofly relied on technicalities to avoid honoring their advertised services.Outcome:I was only refunded $120 for a $4,000+ ticket, which is insulting and unacceptable. Bravofly’s lack of accountability, refusal to escalate, and reliance on technical errors to deny claims make them a company I cannot recommend to anyone.Final Thoughts:Avoid Bravofly at all costs. Their Full Flex policy is a scam designed to mislead customers, and their customer service is one of the worst I have ever experienced. They do not answer calls, provide no clear escalation paths, and fail to resolve legitimate claims. If you value transparency and professionalism, book with another provider.

text: A Two-Year Struggle for a Refund;Booking id: 1893426462Date of booking: 14th dec 2021Ryan air flight: FR4769PNR: T8ZHHSReturn flight : VY1265 PNR: QIW6KNI am writing this review to share my deeply frustrating experience with Bravofly, which has been nothing short of a nightmare. Over two years ago, I booked a flight through Bravofly that was subsequently canceled. Despite their initial assurances that I would receive a refund, I am still waiting.From the onset, communication with Bravofly has been abysmal. After my flight was canceled, I immediately contacted their customer service to inquire about my refund. Each time, I was met with vague responses and empty promises that the refund was being processed. I was assured multiple times that my case was being prioritized, but these claims have proven to be hollow.The company's lack of transparency and accountability is staggering. For over two years, I have been caught in a frustrating loop of automated emails and unhelpful customer service agents. Every interaction feels like starting from scratch, with no one able to provide a clear status update or a concrete timeline for when I might receive my refund.Bravofly’s handling of this situation has caused me significant stress and inconvenience. Not only did I lose the money spent on the tickets, but I also had to deal with the added financial strain of rebooking flights through another provider at the last minute. The customer service experience has been frustrating, with long wait times and representatives who seem either unwilling or unable to assist effectively.It's clear that Bravofly’s systems and processes for handling cancellations and refunds are severely lacking. A two-year wait for a refund is completely unacceptable and speaks volumes about their disregard for customers.To anyone considering booking with Bravofly, I urge you to think twice. My experience has been an ordeal that I wouldn't wish upon anyone. The promise of affordable travel quickly becomes irrelevant when you are left fighting for a refund for years, with no end in sight. The distress and inconvenience caused are beyond measure while my senior parents wait for me in Brazil to finally see me after more ages apart. That's what I paid thousands of dollars for? @Bravofly went silent when I most needed them.#TravelNightmare #BravoflyNeglectsClientsDetails on the flight issues: I was checked in for the two first flights when I checked in the Airnz flight on the 26th Nov 2023, so all I needed by the time I landed in Auckland was to print my boarding pass to Chile (Qantas flight operated by Latam, hence why I could not access a boarding pass from my phone) and then my GRU flight boarding pass. My AirNZ flight from Palmerston North to Auckland landed with a 5 minute delay. I ran from the domestic terminal to the International terminal and talked to a Qantas staff lady. She told me I needed to print the boarding pass with Latam, not Qantas. I quickly went to Latam counter, nobody was there. I found an Auckland Airport information staff and they helped me find a Latam lady that was not even on the counter anymore. She rudely dismissed me saying that I missed the check in as it was closed 5 min ago and did not care about the fact that I was already checked in the system so she just needed to print my boarding pass. She told me she could not to anything else for me and directed me to bag services so I could retrieve my bag. She told me she could not do anything for me. I called both Qantas and Latam, both told me they could not book a new flight for me because the travel agency was responsible for the bad itinerary. I talked to Airnz staff at the airport, they dismissed me as they said the delay of my flight landing 5 minutes later was not a delay and that they had no part to play in the connection to Santiago. Latam bag service lady told me my bag was nowhere to be found. After 4 hours, an airnz lady found my bag. Bravofly online system chat was dismissive at first, then less dismissive afterwards but completely vague about booking my new flight.

title: I would strongly advise reading this complaint before making any booking with this company.
text: I purchased a full flexifare ticket over a year ago and had the unfortunate experience of having to cancel and rebook. A totally deceptive policy. Still I had to use the credit voucher because they would not refund the whole purchase to my card. I booked another flight using the credit voucher and the balance of another $1700 charged to exactly the same card that I originally used for the first purchase. The ticket was for a girl that was displaced by the Ukraine war, and when she arrived at the airport in Warsaw, she found that the ticket had been cancelled by Bravofly. Bravofly did not even pay me the courtesy of informing me that they had cancelled the ticket, I only found out when the passenger found that when she arrived at the airport the ticket booking had been cancelled by Bravofly. I contacted Bravofly from Australia, to find that they then claimed that their system had picked up a possible fraudulent payment, which was from the exact same card I used the first time. They refused to assist this poor girl stuck at the airport in Warsaw, stating that the only way to solve the issue was to buy another ticket at full price by using my card again - there was no way they would assist at all. Just heartless money hungry, unethical liars and cheats. I had to firstly pay for a hotel for 3 days for 690 Euros, so that she could fly out on a different day using a different ticketing agent. It took 8 months to get the refund for the extra payment from my card and another credit voucher for the previous one. They changed their story about the cancellation claiming that it was not a suspected credit card fraud, instead they then claimed that the reason that they cancelled the ticket was because they said that I had initiated a dispute over the transaction, which was a complete lie. They told me that they would not refund the card portion nor offer another credit voucher to replace the first one until I supplied written p[roof that the dispute was withdrawn or cancelled. If you know banks, they were not going to supply any documentation like this simply because I did not open a dispute in the first place, so they could not help by lying in writing saying that i had closed the non existent dispute. The only way out of this ridiculous situation was to then open a dispute and close the dispute, therefore the bank could then say the dispute was closed. This took 6 weeks for the bank to send the documentation stating that the dispute was closed. So apparently I received a valid voucher, which I just tried to use 2 weeks ago (nearly a year and 4 months since the original booking - Bravofly had kept the $5000 I had paid in total for the 2 tickets) unfortunately after multiple attempts using 4 different credit cards and also the alternative PayPal payment option, I kept getting an error on the payment page, rendering this credit voucher completely useless. My due date of departure is now only 48 hours away and countless hours and chat messages later including a 2.5 hour international call to their call center in UK, has resulted in me still being unable to book a flight using this voucher. Their very useless customer service of course refused to take responsibility for the payment gateway failure even though I used multiple cards from 2 different banks and also the Paypal option. Instead they of course divert the responsibility to my bank. I called my bank and found that no transaction had been declined for any reason by the bank, none of the transaction attempts were even logged, which means that my bank was never contacted to request payment. The fact that payment by Paypal resulted in the same payment failure indicated that it was not a bank problem and that it must have been a payment gateway problem or a Bravofly issue with me trying to use the credit voucher. essentially, Bravofly seem to be trying to keep the entire $5000. I WOULD STRONGLY ADVISE EVERYBODY TO NOT USE THIS UNETHICAL COMPANY THAT USES DECEPTIVE AND  DISHONEST BUSINESS PRACTICES. I T IS SIMPLY NOT WORTH THE FEW DOLLARS YOU THINK YOU ARE SAVING BY BOOKING WITH THEM.

title: I booked a flight through Bravofly
text: I booked a flight through Bravofly, not realising it was a third party. My flight was with Lion Air. Three weeks later I received an email from both Bravofly and Lion Air saying it had been cancelled. Three days later an email from Bravofly said that the only alternative offered by the airline was a refund but it could take 2 months.I booked another flight. With Jetstar.Two weeks later I was offered an alternative flight for the cancelled flight by Lion Air. I emailed and declined. Said I wanted a refund. They said they could only work with Bravofly. I contacted Bravofly they said they were seeking a refund.I continued to receive emails about the alternative flight indicating I had been booked. I tried several more times with both parties to resolve it.I was told the refund would take 2 months. When that came and went. I reached out to Bravofly. All I received is a copy and paste response that they are seeking a refund.I ended up raising a dispute on the transaction with the bank.After another 6 weeks the bank substantiated my claim and I received my money back through Visa.The bank will need evidence. Go to the chat function on Bravofly and ask for evidence that they are seeking a refund. None will be given. Eventually the chat will time out and an option to send you a copy of your interaction will appear. Use it as evidence that you have sought a refund.Once you have your money back, immediately cancel your card. Bravofly has since illegally re-debited my card and I have now needed to redispute it through the bank.I received my money back through Visa a second time. But have since cancelled my card to be safeCustomer service with Bravofly was terrible. They promised that if I withdraw the dispute and provide them evidence they would refund me. When I said that was blackmail and that if I was entitled to one they were legally obliged to provided it. They declined to allow me to speak to a manger.To be clear on how Bravofly operates and why its hard to get your money back.  They take your money then pay for the flights on their card. So you have no control of the transaction between the airline and yourself. They don't care if the flight is cancelled or if you get on the flight as they don't provide a service. Book directly with an airline that way you are protected under your country's consumer protection laws.

title: Terrible system, terrible service
text: If everything works perfectly, then Bravofly is probably ok to use. Just gotta hope everything goes perfectly...In my case, I booked a round trip international flight. Just one, but the amount of headache it caused made it seem like I had booked 10 or 15. If the flight gets cancelled, they send you an email to inform you. No phone call, just one single email. Oh, and they give you one alternative to either say yes or no to. If you dont like it, they will get back to you in a few days with another email, to which you can either say yes or no to. Oh, and the link expires after 48 hours, so you better be quick about it. Oh, and sometimes the links just dont work, even when you are quick enough. I probably called them close to 10 times, which, among the companies that do still have phone support, is probably one of the toughest to reach. They only have a UK based phone line, so if you're outside of the UK, you better have a way to call internationally. Then, you'll need your booking ID in order to pass the automated prompts, and after that you'll have to carefully maneuver the maze of prompts they give you in order to actually speak to someone, otherwise it'll just hang up on you and you have to start all over. When I said I had called 10 times, I wasn't including the times I had to try again, by the way.Anyway, for months on end I was bombarded by "your flight was cancelled" and "alternative flight proposal" emails. Finally I managed to get one that I liked. Well, come time for my return flight, it appears that my fight no longer exists. But all the cancellation emails I had received were for my outgoing flight. Hmm... Well, guess what? After thoroughly reviewing all 20+ emails I have received from them about cancellations alone, hidden among them was another one that said a fight had been cancelled. The emails are also very light on details, and so the only way I would have known is by looking at the place where it says 'which city to which city.' It wont refer to them as outgoing / returning, 1st or 2nd, etc, or provide the date or number of the flight. Thankfully, the staff at United air was super helpful (this was in Japan btw) and was able to put me on a similar flight within a few minutes for no extra charge, after I had just showed up at the airport for a flight that didn't exist. Having been on a flight or two in the past, all I can say is that I wouldn't expect it to have gone that smoothly anywhere else. I was very nearly left stranded at the airport with no assistance from "Bravofly" whatsoever, or refund for that matter. If not for the good grace of Japanese customer service, I'm sure I would still be trying to work this all out days later. Probably a few hundred more phone calls to Bravofly later as well.

title: Wish there was a way to give a MINUS…
text: Wish there was a way to give a MINUS STAR!!On June 9th, 2022, we booked our flight with Bravofly for a trip from Richmond Virginia to Port of Spain Trinidad. JetBlue would take us to Fort Lauderdale and then to Port of Spain on October 24th. This one-way trip was 694.81 USD for 4 passengers.On June 29th we received an email from Bravofly advising us of a minor change to our flight which was by no means minor as there was a cancellation of the flight from Fort Lauderdale to Port of Spain. So that our destination was completely ignored. Also to our great annoyance they confirmed this change without our consent – “We have already confirmed the changes with the airline on your behalf so you do not need to do anything.”After 27 emails and three phone calls we were advised that we had three choices, two of which would be travel vouchers which would mean having to use this scam of a travel company and the last choice was cash refund. This company is so fraudulent that the choice of the travel voucher was made to look as if that was your only choice at the bottom of the screen there was “Other options” to click on to see all three choices.On Aug 20th we got a cash refund of 563.88 USD.This is by far the worst customer service we have ever received which ended up ultimately costing us 130.93 USD. We had to also book our own alternative flights from Virginia to Port of Spain. Bravofly was never able to even offer alternative viable options. We even realized that JetBlue eventually had options to go to New York and then to Port of Spain but we never even offered that. In researching we have discovered we had no recourse once we chose to book our flight through a travel agency. However, we are spreading the word by all social media means so as to prevent further persons from being suckered by BravoFly. If JetBlue has refunded the full amount to Bravofly, they have then kept the 130.93USD in an entirely unethical manner.We acknowledge we should have done our research on Bravofly before using them. But that does not mean they should be allowed to continue  scamming their customers.We also filed a complaint on airconsumer.dot.gov escomplaint ConsumerForm.cfm and we encourage others to use this means perhaps you may get some redress. But it is my great hope that Bravofly will either change their business practices or be put out of business.

name: Laura Stransky
title: Fabulous Trip!
text: Overall, my husband and I had a wonderful time on our trip to London and Paris.  The tour was advertised as 3 nights in London and 3 nights in Paris.  Shortly before our trip began, they changed our flight to London to a later flight so we basically lost a day there.  Two and a half days in London was not enough time.  We were able to do all of the tours scheduled for London, but we would've liked to have more time exploring the city.  I also would've liked if airport transfers were included in the tour.  On our flight to London we were seated in the very last row (57!) of the plane right between the two restrooms on the plane so it was hard to get any sleep with people going back and forth to use the restrooms.   I had trouble getting a time for one of the tours as it wasn't on my travel documents I received from Great Value.  Luckily there was someone in the office in the US when I called them from Paris! They were able to email me my "final" documents with the times for the tours, but that should've all been done BEFORE we left the US! Train from London to Paris was nice.  We were disappointed to find our hotel in Paris was a good 30 minutes from the city center.  It took us 55 minutes one afternoon to return to our hotel because the traffic is so bad there.  We would've preferred a hotel right in the city center so we could just walk out and go to the attractions in the city.  Instead, we had to pay for an Uber every day to get into the city.  The hotel was very nice, almost looked new, but we wish it was in a different area.  We didn't feel comfortable walking around at night, at all.  Again, overall it was a fabulous trip, but I would never choose the hotels we stayed in.

text: Italy is, of course, beautiful and ITA Airways was incredible.  The location of the hotels were not so great. Best Western in Venice was right across the train station and made sense. The itinerary could use some help and needs to be more thought out from a tourist stand point. title: Horrible London Hotel Booking
text: As part of our London/Paris trip, GVV booked us into the Zedwell Underground Tottenham Road hotel in London.  This hotel was absolutely the worst hotel experience our group has ever had when traveling.  Rooms are four/five levels below ground floor, with no windows, no pictures on the walls, no closet and no space to accommodate luggage, no hair dryers, no nightstands or lamps, no chairs or desk, no TV or telephone, no safe, refrigerator, no carpeting.The "bed" was a basically a mattress on the floor with filthy bedding.The room was not serviced our entire stay with the exception of two clean bath towels each day (no washcloths or hand towels). We had to specially request that they replenish the toilet paper.Because there were no hair dryers or clothes irons in the room, we were forced to go up to another floor to use communal hair dryers and irons in a "beauty/ironing room".The bathroom had a shower that left water all over the bathroom floor and an extremely tiny sink. No tissues or other amenities that one might expect in a four star hotel. The shower wall was moldy and unclean with hair on the walls. One morning we had no water. The plumbing was extremely noisy with various sounds during the night. Although this hotel boasted that the rooms were soundproof, noise from the subway trains were heard constantly throughout the night.But perhaps the most concerning issue to my party was the feeling that our safety and health were at risk by staying in this facility. The subterranean floors including the reception area in this hotel all reeked of sewage and stale air. In the event of a fire, there would be no way to escape. One of our party became ill during our stay and had to have EMS from the NHS come to evaluate her and transport her to the hospital. The EMS stated that the air in the hotel was very unhealthy due to no circulation and that it would be impossible to evacuate a patient by stretcher if necessary. Fortunately, the ill member of our party was able to walk out. It is possible that the unhealthy conditions in the hotel contributed to her illness. Three of the remaining members of our party ended up with severe head colds.GVV refused to compensate us in any way for this disgusting hotel.  Our travel voucher said that our stay included an “English breakfast” but the hotel had no food services.  GVV did refund us $10 per day per person for the missing breakfasts, but this amount is quite laughable to think that one could eat breakfast in London for $10 (7£).  GVV insisted that the hotel delivered on their online description.  Only if one considered a “curated playlist” to be constant subway train noises and “soothing scents” to be reeking sewage.Because of this horrible hotel experience, I cannot be comfortable ever using GVV again for travel and will definitely warn my friends from using them.  Their failure to offer us any compensation for this bad experience shows that they do not “Value” their customers, only their bottom line.In response to your response:It would still behoove your company’s reputation to offer monetary compensation for our unsatisfactory experience.  And I DO NOT mean in the form of a future travel credit, which is no more than you offer for all of your customers in the form of a $100 off pp travel voucher on any future trip.  I believe one of my co-travelers suggested that a $100 refund pp would be appropriate and acceptable to us.  But I guess you would rather receive a one star rating for your customer service.

text: Great Value Vacations did it again! Another beautiful destination that was easily adapted to our personal travel needs and interests.Our trip to Budapest, Vienna and Prague (Central Europe) was filled with storytelling, historical drama, delicious local and international cuisine, architectural wonders, arts and culture that seamlessly blends old-world charm with modernity. You really feel transported back in time when you walk the streets and enter buildings that have been standing for centuries, each one telling the stories of the people and events that shape the unique identity of each city. What was previously unknown to us was how much of a shared history this region has, yet how uniquely different the impact and significance on each one - such a treasure! We believe travel presents an immense opportunity to learn and expand one's worldview. Great Value Vacations does an awesome job of making that possible. Whether it's fully escorted packages with planned activities, self-drive options, or last-minute, budget deals that you personalize, they make it interesting and affordable and easy.We have reviewed many other "budget" travel websites purportedly offering "the best packages and affordable destinations" only to be disappointed with the options. Then, we find ourselves returning to GVV and booking an amazing vacation. Travel smart - use Great Value Vacations. We're already exploring our next destination! title: Additional hidden costs
text: One thing that wasn't very clear was that we were only given vouchers to stay at category one hotels or B&Bs and there was only one that I was able to find in the whole country in the area that we were going that was a category one. So we ended up paying an additional $360 to be able to stay in the places we stayed. Also the insurance that I paid 10% of the trip cost was really a rip off. And looking at it more closely you would have to cancel 30 days in advance to have received any ability to utilize the trip cost for a future trip. It didn't cover any other problems that might occur or if you would've gotten sick right before the trip you were out of luck.I did appreciate the email reminders to run off my vouchers and those sorts of things. We have done other trips with great value and if I was going to do it again I would do one where they took care of booking the hotels for us. also since it is an economy flight you have to pay for your seats and it was an additional $140 each person on the way there and $111 each person on the way back so when you add all of that additional cost on it is really more expensive than presented.

name: Patricia Date
title: Mismatched Expectations on an Otherwise Nice Trip
text: Overall, the trip was pleasant and we enjoyed many aspects of the experience. The itinerary was well-planned in terms of the sights and locations visited, and we appreciated the efforts of the guide throughout the journey.That said, I believe the value of the trip was a bit misaligned with the expectations set during booking. There was significantly more walking involved than described in the trip materials, which would have been helpful to know in advance for planning purposes.Additionally, one of the buses we traveled on had a very strong mold and musty odor. It was a very unhealthy situation for all of the passengers on board, especially those with allergies or respiratory issues. While our guide did their best to arrange for a new bus, the bus company would not accommodate the request, which made that leg of the journey uncomfortable and concerning from a health standpoint.As for the accommodations, I would personally rate the hotels closer to three stars rather than the advertised four. One particular hotel had a nice main building that was featured in the promotional photos. However, the room we were assigned was in a separate, much older structure behind the main hotel—resembling more of a garage or storage space than a guest room. It was small, very aged, and not at all reflective of the quality shown online. This was disappointing and felt misleading.In summary, while the trip itself had enjoyable moments, a few adjustments in transparency around hotel quality, physical activity levels, and transportation conditions would greatly improve the overall experience and perceived value.

name: Douglas Frick
title: Don't Make Assumptions: Aggressive Itinerary, Questionable Logistics.
text: Overall I had a good experience, but I'd recommend any customer considering travel carefully reads all documents, and reviews and tests the schedule and questions the logistic before booking. I was surprised how aggressive the itinerary was, and there was one location that logistically made no sense.I accepted an invitation to book the same itinerary that my brother's family recently purchased. The booking experience was simple and the information provided did prove thorough and accurate. But were a couple disconnects from my previous experience and expectations that I'd advise other customers to carefully consider, especially if you aren't used to travel packages like this:  1) Seat Certainty: since the airline seat assignments are not confirmed until shortly before actual travel, I had to pursue my own additional coordination and significant cost with the airlines to be able to select seats to ensure I'd have a seat with my travel companion. Ultimately, that was wasted effort and cost, because the overnight/overseas flight was only half full, so there was plenty of flexibility within the cabin on the flight, but at booking you will not have an opportunity to select/secure your seat or upgrade without the extra coordination and additional cost.  2) Travel Insurance Limitations: I opted to purchased travel insurance, but did not carefully read the policy. I had assumed I could cancel and claim against the insurance up until departure, but that was not the case. Unfortunately, my fiancé did have a medical emergency the week of the trip and we were uncertain if she would be up for the travel, but upon closer review of the policy, I realized cancellations would have needed to be made 72 hours before departure, so ultimately the insurance did not provide the flexibility I would have expected for the cost, and in the future, I would not opt in to that service. This may all be very standard, I just assumed the coverage would be more flexible than it actually was. 3) Very Aggressive Itinerary: we covered a lot of ground between cities and I underestimated the amount of time we would be driving- on average 3 hours a day-which left little additional time to explore at destinations. But, I could have paid closer attention to the package details to have been better informed. The hotels were all clean an comfortable but they were not necessarily close to the day's activities which created a lot of seemingly unnecessary travel time and backtracking. For example, the hotel for night 2 was 90 minutes past the next morning's activity, which meant an hour an a half of backtracking to make that activity and the same duration back; so that hotel just made no sense. The extra travel time eliminated any chance for exploring the locale, and the hotel itself was the least special of all lodging; so that location for two nights was totally absurd and the low point of the trip. The other surprise was that my room overlooked a cemetery, not the scenic lagoon which seemed to be the draw. I was able to change rooms for a reasonable upgrade fee. If I could have edited that stay out of this itinerary and stayed closer to the next day's activities, my review would be higher. So overall a good, but not great experience. I would book with this company again, but I would pay closer attention to details.

name: Kate F.
title: Dublin was great, but GVV was challenging
text: Our visit to Ireland was ultimately great, and the hotel was better than expected (plus a great location between airport and downtown Dublin). Also, the customer service is extremely frustrating until you get to the final booking agent - they're terrific. But the people prior aren't very helpful or pleasant. And know that the flights are booked somewhat separately, so that process is quite clunky.If you do choose to book w/GVV, buy the insurance. That saved us when we had to rebook for another date. That allows you to switch packages if needed, although not travel companions.I do not recommend the Scotland B&B package - that was our original trip, and it requires you to do hours of work to book the B&B's yourself. I thought it would be fun, but the booking site (separate from GVV) is very antiquated and time consuming. Plus, almost all decent/nearby B&Bs require an upcharge to the package cost.Overall, our trip was good, so if you book a straightforward package, you may be okay. text: The company was able to troubleshoot when an air traffic control strike disrupted our trip. Unfortunately our flight home was scheduled with not enough layover time so missed our connection home to Boston but airline put us up for the night. Accomodations were fantastic. Transfers were appropriate. Would recommend to others to make their plans through them.

name: Jake George
title: Top Notch
text: Great Value Vacation is a very accurate name for this company. I highly recommend them and do often recommend them to friends and acquaintances who are considering vacations.

name: Kathryn
title: Great trip and package!
text: Very happy with our trip. We had a number of questions prior and some couldn't be answered, so there was a bit of back and forth between GVV and Cosmos. The representatives at GVV were great but didn't have all the answers. All good

name: Christine Nedeau
title: A Curated Trip for an economical price!
text: First time travelling with GVV.As soon as we purchased our trip, we received detailed itinerary and so much information to make the trip our own.The price for airfare, accommodations and rental car CAN’T be beat! (Rome/Tuscany trip) And they include tours without extra charge. The hotels/villa were charming and service was great. We upgraded our car for extra room for 4 (extra cost) as we drove all over Tuscany. Our return flight from Florence was delayed which caused us to miss all our connections to Munich and the US. The airlines took care of transportation, overnight stay in Munich, food and everything was coordinated so easily for us. I worried that getting an economical trip would mean low-end accommodations and less attentive services, but I was wrong. The whole experience felt very curated for our group!We are already planning our next trip through Great Value Vacations, and I CANT WAIT!

name: Robb  Polo
title: Paris
text: Paris, France city break. Awesome 3 night getaway for an outstanding price. 4.75 out of 5 stars. Great Value vacations is my go to for affordable travel to amazing destinations.

name: Brenda OConnor
title: The deal was too good to turn down
text: The deal was too good to turn down and worth every penny

name: ReverseCynthia O'Toole
title: Our trip went off without a hitch
text: Our trip went off without a hitch. Our hotel in Dublin, the Crockett Park was very nice and accommodating. Our rental car was exactly as ordered. The extra tour we added in Dublin was worth it We were pleased with the B n'B accommodations we selected along the way. Seeing Ireland by car is the best way to go.

name: Bridgette
title: Amazing trip especially for the price
text: Amazing trip especially for the price! The Towers hotel was 4 stars I just do not recommend eating there. Food was terrible there! But obviously food was amazing everywhere else. They had an ant problem too at towers hotel, but honestly so beautiful for the view directly looking at Mt. Vesuvius and location (visited Capri, Positano, sorrento square etc). So Can’t say I wouldn’t stay there again! Amazing trip! Can’t wait to book another.

name: Nicole R.
title: Great vacation package
text: Great vacation package. We had a great time visiting 3 different locations in Norway.  The guide we had was very informative and the split between guided activities and free time was perfect.

name: Rose Mary Camren
title: Bed and breakfast options are good…
text: The bed and breakfast options are very good. The only Very Bad Experience we had was in Scotland at The Eskbank, Dalkaith. Rude and his lack of safety in the bathroom caused a fall which greatly restriced my movement ability the last 4 days of our vacation. Otherwise was pretty great.

We could have easily skipped the very mediocre lunch for more time at the falls and eaten at Niagara on the Lake.

title: I just finished booking my Europe…

Super professional, kind, she was patient and went the extra mile for me and my friend. Thank you Gabriel. Can't wait for my vacation in Europe!!!

name: Regina Vittore
title: First time vacation package experience
text: I was a little nervous as this was the first vacation package I ever purchased.  Everything was incredibly well planned and every hotel was expecting us.  The flight was really easy, the rental car was really easy to pick up, and it was the perfect amount of activities: not too overwhelming.  Only one activity was booked on a specific date, allowing us a lot of control over our daily plan.  I was very impressed and will absolutely use this service again.

name: Kim
title: The hotel location was amazing
text: The hotel location was amazing,  they were very accommodating and breakfast was amazing. The bus stop was so convenient to the hotel and the tours and tour buses were great. Iceland air was terrible- just nickel  and dime you. Make sure you upgrade to more leg room.Make sure you print all your documents before you leave.  That came in handy.  Overall great vacation and some incredible  memories:)

name: Allen William DeCarlo
title: I took my mom to Ireland
text: I took my mom to Ireland, and the trip went incredibly smoothly. Great Value Vacations will be used again in the future.

name: Diane D
title: Great Value Vacations is far from a Great Value!
text: Don’t use this agency unless you want to pay WAY MORE than what it would be if you just went directly to the hotel/airline/car rental agency and booked it yourself.  Our friends booked the exact same thing as our trip through Great Value and paid $600.00 LESS than we did!  Great value is NOT a great value and everything is non-refundable.  At least when you book yourself, you can usually cancel some aspects of a trip up until a certain date.  Not so with this agency.  So disappointing!  Never again!  I will book everything myself and do the research.To reply to Great Value’s reply below, I would have cancelled the whole thing with you if I could have.  The fact that you “allowed me” to cancel the car, yes you did and I consider that VERY lucky because the girl I dealt with told me they would do it for me this “one time” for this “one” aspect of the trip and that’s it!  As for knowing if I am comparing apples for apples, our friends went with us at the exact same time.  Same flight.  Same hotel.  We travelled together and they booked their trip a week after I booked mine and asked me the details of our trip and booked their exact same apples for apples trip.   I don’t normally write bad reviews.  But I had to tell people about this one because $600 more is a total rip off!  Furthermore, if you are going to pay that much more to use the agency, one would think they would provide as many details as possible about the trip you booked such as with said airline you should book any bags in advance because the day of your trip the pricing doubles.  I will say that we enjoyed our trip immensely.  The hotel was a little dated but good and the airline was stripped down to where they  charge for water but we knew that from doing research after booking.  Everyone was very nice at the hotel and the airline.  It simply wasn’t a good value is my only complaint.  I even went as far as to look up the flight and hotel on my own after I booked through Great Value and it was in fact much cheaper online.  So the extra cost goes to the agency at a hefty price tag.

name: Mel B.
title: Amazing vacation to Ireland!
text: Amazing vacation to Ireland! Everything went smoothly from our flights, to the car rental, to the hotels! We couldn’t have had a better time! Can’t wait to plan our next trip!

name: Ray  Attig
title: Mostly a good experience
text: Mostly a good experience.  The hotels were very nice.  Our main concerns were that some of the hotels were hard to find , mostly because sometimes addresses in Ireland can be hard to find.  Also even thouth the hotels were not that far apart, it seemed like we were a bit hurried to get from one to another because we did stop alot to explore.

name: Natalie I.
title: Everything went so smoothly
text: Everything went so smoothly, from picking up the rental car to checking into the hotels. The rooms were nice and we had a wonderful time in Ireland! I will definitely be using this company again!

name: sherry lynn linn
title: Our trip to Ireland was amazing!!!
text: Our trip to Ireland was amazing! From the car, the flight and five hotels and no issues. Most of the hotels even let us check in early. The bus day trip thru the “.Ring of Kerry” was really nice and our driver John was excellent. He told us about the history and gave us plenty of time to stop and explore many areas. Can’t wait to book another adventure soon!

name: Nancy Todd
title: Excellent coordination with 3 cities

name: Holly
title: We wish there was more communication…

Our group just went with the flow and I didn't read each one to know that the Guinness tour needed to be booked weeks in advance so we didn't get to do that. Also there some cash only places that would have been nice to know to be prepared.Otherwise we loved our hotels and the people were so kind to us.

name: Mike R
title: Trip had too many unexpected fees due during vacation.
text: I enjoyed the trip - a Croatia coast road trip.  I did not appreciate that City Taxes were not included in the GVV pricing.  Even more bothersome than the City Taxes was the $131 Car Rental fee for returning the car to a different Airport than we picked it up from.  The GVV itinerary was built around the fact we would not be returning the car to the same airport it was picked up from.  This fee should have been "baked in" to the GVV travel costs.  For us to have to pay this "on top of" the cost of the aggregated vacation package was ridiculous.  I also looked that the hotel rates for the rooms GVV booked for us...based on that information I don't see GVV as a value any longer.

name: Enma Leticia Bonilla Sanchez
title: Hotels were good
text: Hotels were good!  I was not crazy about Leonardo's in Vienne, but Buda pest and Phage  were well appreciated.  Roma Hotel has been remodel recently and the staff takes their time to help with tour booking and guidance.  The other hotels are more modern and they just asked for me to go on line.  Which is no bad.  It is the way to tavel now, but front desk in Roma are very helpful

name: Jenny
title: No regrets!
text: The company was great to work with.  The price was excellent.  The hotels were good, not great.  For what we paid for the trip, we got a good deal.  I wish the hotels were more centrally located, but I have zero regrets about booking this vacation!

name: Lynn MARIE GARRON
title: All transfers and tours were on time

name: Donna G
title: Land of Fire and Ice

My husband and I rate this as one of the best vacations ever.  I bragged so much when I got home that now my family members want to go.  I will be using GVV again!

title: I loved the experience and it was…
text: I loved the experience and it was great. However, the Ibis Alessia Montparnasse did not have hot water for 3 of the nights we were there. I was forced to open the windows which didn’t feel safe to do because I had a 5 year old in the room with me.  The rooms were also not spacious.

title: Ireland for 10 nights, 845 miles of adventure
text: We did 10 nights in Ireland.  It was great!  Driving in Ireland was an adventure.  The hotels were very nice and their locations were perfect for us. Some hotels were right in town and others were outside the city. We did all the included experiences but we had time to enjoy and explore the countryside as well. I'm so glad we took 10 nights!  We drove 845 miles in a beautifukl new hybrid Toyota.  Highly recommend for minimally structured adventure.
