text: There were aspects that I enjoyed and some that didn't create a positive experience.1. Hotels- I knew the hotels would be 3 star rated hotels but I don't know the criteria for the rating equivalency in the US compared to Italy. In some cases I would say they were 2 star hotels. Walls were dirty, bugs in room and on bed, bathrooms and windows were broken and in one location the hotel was in an area with run down buildings, graffiti, etc. I wasn't sure how a school tour was booked in this neighborhood and then we had to walk at night through it. The food wasnt really good at some of the hotels and we had dinner and breakfast there sometimes.  Some were better than others. I persinally think we were booked in hotels far from our destinations to save money but the quality wasn't good. On the positive side, the customer service was good from the front desk staff and they were friendly.2. Flights, the tour requires you to arrive 3 hours early which is excessive. If you need any special accommodations that require special seating or upgrades, forget about it. Ef doesn't care. They really leave you in a bind and say they can't help you. They won't take your request in advance and they won't adjust after. They say the contract doesn't allow, however the airlines, repeatedly said they were lying and they were the only ones who can make the adjustments to a group booking. They don't confirm the flights until 1 month prior which doesn't leave alot of time to manage the reservation on your own. They didn't care about my accommodation and told me that I would be released from the group booking 24 to 48 hours prior to departure to make changes on my own. That never happened and the airline told me that wasn't a thing and apologized for my experience with EF tour and said they are the only ones that could help me. I will add Lufthansa is not flexible to change a group booking directly with them and require that thr tour agent does it unless they release you from the group but EF would not release me.EF will accept advance room request for an upgraded price but don't do the same for flights. I will never tour with them again3. My child had fun with his friends but the days were so packed it took away from the enjoyment for them. The kids wanted the ability to have true free time. Everything was restricted. In some cases they got free time but only in a designated area. Free time or days didn't allow for you to stay at hotel or offer options. Everyone had to go to a specific space and have so called free time. It didn't feel like free time to them. In some cases you got free time before seeing the area so you didn't know how to spend your free time. I think it would be better to offer free time in between tours. Have the ability to stop along the way. Maybe the EF guide creates space for that.4. Website, they offer a checklist on their site. It would be helpful if it you complete a task to show completed.5. Bus, our first bus was old and had a wood rooftop. There were termites flying in it. Yes, termites.6. Food, the food was not good in most of the places. Someone told us this was known. They know the restaurants don't have good food. So why keep that relationship. One place fed us slop. It was disgusting. Most kids didn't eat and ended up going to McDonalds. One restaurant the worker yelled at our guide and was rude. Why continue to do business with them.We went to one that served us braised beef and green beans. That was the best in Florence.But in general, EF needs better restaurant partners. We are still paying for meals and they should be quality.Besides that, the tour Guide was great. No complaints with her. We all loved her.I appreciate the experience and some of the great places that we got to see and meeting new people but EF in terms of customer service and the quality of the hotels and restaurants were not great.

title: I had a great experience with my…

The hotel in Rome was located 20 minutes away from the Historical Rome. That was not the issue, the issue was that the hotel had a few hiccups when it came to the bathrooms and towels services. The shower was malfunctioning and caused an overflow of water to the actual bathroom's floor. Something similar happened in the hotel in Florence, but having the prior experience in Rome, the issue was taken care rather quickly.Overall, As stated before, we had a great experience. I believe that as a first timer taking a big group [39 travelers] abroad, made me become more diligent and thoughtful and not always believe that everything it is so far "perfect" before departing. With the latter, I meant that as a group leader, I will make sure that what I requested, will be granted or not, but at least make sure that I will know clearly that the excursions or places of visiting that we planned ahead of time,  are good to go and not been surprise in situ if any excursion is cancelled.

name: Mary Kay Felton
title: Disappointing Trip With Planning Flaws
text: Tour guides were difficult to hear in busy locations. There were no audiovox or other type of headsets to help hear the guides.  The tour seemed to be weighted toward the quantity of sites rather than the quality of the visit at each site.  Not enough time was allocated to adequately visit sites.  Ok for students who just wanted to hang out on a foreign trip with friends, socialize, take a quick look at the sites, and do some souvenir shopping. Disappointing for students who were looking for more of a cultural and historical experience i.e., more time spent in castles, cathedrals, museums, historic and cultural sites, less time in souvenir shops and shop brands that exist in the US.  Hotels should have been chosen more carefully.  One hotel was supposed to be a multi night stay but the rooms and bedding were so dirty the group got relocated to another hotel for the remaining nights (but not until they had to spend one night in the dirty hotel).

name: Wendy Bethoney
title: Spain & Portugal
text: My student reports that the tour guides were great, but there was not enough variation in the types of sites visited.  The biggest compliant was that the food was underwhelming and without much variety. This is disappointing as food is such a large part of a cultural experience. Not having direct flights and having long layovers is something that should be changed. There are multiple carriers with direct flights, so there is no reason for this. Overall, my student had a good time with friends, sharing new experiences, but there is room for improvement.

title: It was a wonderful trip that my son and I greatly enjoyed!
text: Our week-long trip to Madrid and Paris was packed with a wide variety of experiences, and we truly made the most of every moment! The local guides who joined us for site-specific tours were also fantastic—engaging, fun, and full of insight.Combining groups brought a few logistical challenges, particularly around differing expectations for timeliness. title: Almost everything was great, but flights
text: Almost everything was great, but the flights were so terrible I am considering not using EF again. Our tour guide was wonderful, the hotels were fine. The local tours were top-notch. So all good.But the flights were horrible.  On the way TO Italy, we left Portland, ME at 6:15 AM and arrived in Italy 38 hours later. Every other time I have flown with EF we have taken an evening flight out of Boston, which works fine. This time our flight was at 10AM from Boston which meant we had to miss a day of school. Our superintendent was upset and it makes him less likely to support trips in the future. We then flew from Boston to Montreal then had an EIGHT HOUR layover in the Montreal airport. Then flew to Italy. It was terrible.But the worst part was the return flight. When I booked the trip I was VERY clear with our rep from EF that our group had to land in Boston prior to 9PM on whichever night we landed because there is no bus back to Maine after 10:30. I said it repeatedly and clearly.  But our flight landed at 11:59PM.  I was very upset and spoke to the head person for our trip, Catie Groves, who explained that we can never ask for a TIME for flights, we can only give a day's parameter, not time. IT would have been very helpful if the first tour planner I spoke to had told me that. She had assured me that we could land before 9PM.So, once we landed, since there was no public transportation to Maine, we chaperones had to rent cars and drive the students to Maine--a somewhat dangerous drive after a 15 hour flight.I do not understand why it is impossible to request anything of the flight planners from EF. And I am upset that I was not told that my "land by 9PM" request was impossible to fill. If I had been told that we would have considered other options.I hate to put so much negativity in a review when most of the trip was excellent. title: I would rated our recent tour to Italy…a three out of five
text: I would rated our recent tour to Italy 3 out of 5 stars.What I appreciated most was the breathtaking scenery and educational depth of the itinerary. The weather was beautiful, and the views—mountains, rolling landscapes, and expansive blue skies—were absolutely picturesque. Each city showcased impressive architecture, rich in detail and historical significance. The remnants of the Etruscan civilization, in particular, were deeply inspiring. It’s unfortunate that the legacy of the Etruscans—as well as the profound influence of other melanated peoples such as the Berbers and the Moors—is often overlooked in mainstream narratives. These civilizations contributed significantly to the cultural, architectural, and scientific foundations of the Mediterranean world. The Moors, for example, preserved and advanced knowledge in mathematics, astronomy, and architecture, much of which later influenced the European Renaissance. Their contributions, along with those of the Etruscans and Berbers, can still be seen in the design, infrastructure, and urban planning of many Italian cities that are now major tourist destinationsIt’s unfortunate that these foundational contributions by melanated civilizations are rarely acknowledged, despite their lasting influence on Italian culture and infrastructure.I must also express my disappointment with the lack of hospitality we encountered. As a group made up predominantly of melanated students, we were often met with dismissive or cold behavior from locals. This left us feeling unwelcome in a country whose rich cultural heritage is, in many ways, built upon the contributions of people who look like us. That contradiction was difficult to ignore and certainly impacted our overall experience.Italy has so much to offer in terms of history and beauty, but true appreciation of its legacy must come with an acknowledgment of all the cultures that helped build it—and a hospitality that reflects that shared heritage.

title: Once in a lifetime experience
text: My son went to Peru with his classmates to perform a service learning project in the Vilcabamba region of the Andes mountains. EF Tours created a safe and robust trip experience for the teens, allowing them to experience much more than just the tourist attractions.  Everything - from airfare to meals, from hotels to last minute flight changes - was handled with attention to detail and care.  The trip consisted of many tours and experiences that immersed the kids in the culture of the Peruvians, in ways that were utterly unique and educational.  From experiencing pottery making, to playing soccer in the local park with young Peruvian kids, to salsa dance lessons, the tour guides were fantastic and went out of their way to let the kids LIVE in Peru for a short while.  The experience curated by EF Tours allowed ample time for exploration and reflection, and the teachers were well supported through the entire journey by the administrative staff and the local tour guides.While there were a number of travel issues on the return trip home, EF Tours did the best they could with delayed and cancelled flights, rerouting connections, and trying to get the kids home as safely and quickly as possible.  My one criticism is around the use of American Airlines - when flights had issues, it seemed they only worked with AA.  If they had worked with other airlines to get the kids home, I would have been more impressed. What should have been about 27 hours of travel ended up taking over 50 (yes fifty!) hours.  Some parents secured direct flight for their children from Lima to Newark instead of finishing their trip with their class, but we couldnt afford to do that.  My son flew from Lima to Miami to Chicago to Philly instead, and this meant we had to drive to Philadelphia to get him at 1 am.  While I understand the difficulty of rescheduling 28 people onto other flights, it seems that EF was only working with American Airlines.  I certainly could be wrong, but if direct flights from Lima to Newark were available, we certainly didn't hear about them.All of that said, when I asked my son if he would do it all again, even if he had to endure the horrible return trip the same way, he said "Absolutely - it was STILL worth every second of the horrible return trip. It was the experience of a lifetime and I am so glad I was able to go."

Two Boston TC's completed our tour group and were a huge bonus to us -- making our tour more meaningful by adding their EF expertise and genuine, positive spirit.Our group flagged one hotel, apparently a new addition to this particular EF Tour, as one for the company to revisit as we believe it is not up-to-par with EF standards. name: Alexandra Robalino
title: Italy Trip (Venice, Florence, Cinque Terre) Trip Review!
text: Our overall experience with EF Educational Tours was great, and our students truly enjoyed their trip to Italy. The itinerary was well-organized, and our tour director was knowledgeable, engaging, and did a fantastic job keeping the group informed and energized throughout the journey.However, there are a few areas where EF could make improvements. The air travel logistics were quite time-consuming, particularly the long bus transfers between the airports and hotels. Ideally, the drive from the airport to accommodations should not exceed two hours to ensure students are rested and ready to enjoy their trip.Additionally, the food provided at hotels could be improved in both quality and quantity, especially considering the nutritional needs of active teenagers. More generous portions and a greater variety of fresh, local food would significantly enhance the experience.Lastly, selecting hotels located in towns with access to local restaurants and supermarkets would offer students more flexibility and cultural immersion during their free time.Overall, it was a memorable and educational trip, and with a few adjustments, future experiences could be even better.

title: Pretty good!
text: Overall, my son LOVED his time in Italy with EF. The tour guide was “awesome” and the bus driver was “super fun.” He loved Italy and can’t wait to go back and explore more - he’s VERY glad that he joined this tour. Three stars (he said 3.5 but not an option here) are because of the hotels, food, and flights.Hotels: The hotels were not in great locations, and one was so dirty (trash and unidentified substances) they had to change rooms and STILL had to clean the bathroom themselves - this made him very unsettled and nervous about their arrangements and safety.Food: He also said the food was terrible (unless they were on their own and could fend for themselves) and was disappointed with the quality; he felt it could have been amazing given they were in Italy and food is an important part of experiencing a culture.Flights: Our hometown is not near a major airport, so it’s understandable flights will be tricky. However, on the way there they had an eight hour layover, and on the way back the flight was too late (on time, not delayed) to make the last bus home and the group leaders had to rent cars and drive in the middle of the night (despite having told EF they needed to be back by a certain time to make the bus).One last thing as a parent: Because their group was smaller they were paired with another school group from a different part of the country - awesome idea, friends were made! We knew about this ahead of time and there were no issues. However, upon return, we learned there was an additional small group (sounds like family) that also joined, and were there for “vacation and were drinking and complaining the whole time.” This was NOT told to us ahead of time, and we were not pleased to learn about the behavior on an educational trip with minors.He had an amazing teacher (and her husband) from his school that led this tour, and that made this a five star trip for him! Again he really did have “the best time ever” and without those two to help coordinate and offer guidance (and have fun!) it would not have been as much of a success. As a parent I wanted to leave an honest review to set expectations and help EF learn from his experience.Thanks so much!

The hotel in Florence was far away from anything, and while they claimed to have a gym and pool, the gym was closed and the pool required a reservation and 25 euro fee. Our flight in was late enough that the first day was essentially a waste. That said, it was overall a great experience for the kids — would do again.

title: This company doesn't care about students.
text: This company doesn't care about the students safety, they only care about the Tour Leader that signs the contract with them!  Our Tour Leader left of district on her own accord and would not give up her Tour Leader roll.  The superintendent and our activities director tried several times to get EF Tours to replace her and EF refused.  Our non district tour leader then removed our school staff as chaperones and replaced them with her friends, and EF allowed her total control to do that.  So I'm essentially sending my child to Japan with someone that no longer works for my district and her buddies!  We've voiced our fears and frustrations and EF Tours has told us they will do nothing to change this situation, they are 100% behind the Tour Leader.  So no, they don't care at all about students!  It's all about the money!

name: Corinne
title: Take the plunge! It is worth it!
text: I am glad that our family took the plunge and let our daughter go on an EF Tour to Spain (April 2025). I can't say enough thing about the chaperones that went with her but the tour guide provided by EF Tours was incredible. EF Tours set up great stopping points and things for the kids to do, the hotels they stayed out were secure and comfortable after their long days exploring. It was the week before Easter so all of the ceremonies were going on in different towns and I love that she got to experience this. I love that she got to try new foods, experiences, a chance to learn a different language and a view on things. While there was one down fall, this I can not blame on EF Tours directly but a group they were traveling (EF Tours as well) were not the most well behaved causing some issues the last night or two. Thankfully those individuals did not ruin the trip and they were able to make the best of it. I would absolutely use EF Tours in the future for my other kids if they so choose.

title: Eastern European EF Tour Review
text: Overall, our tour was great. I attribute much of that to our AMAZING tour director, Izabela, whose energy, knowledge and humor made our experience so much better. EF Educational Tours also seems to have great relationships across region of Eastern Europe because our local guides were also exceptional.I do believe, however, that their hotel partnerships could be improved. Three of our four hotels were acceptable but one was downright awful. Also, even with the three okay hotels, the locations were not ideal at all.Also, the included meals were hit and miss. Some were excellent but some were terrible. Admittedly, this was a high school tour so the restaurants probably didn't feel the need to go out of their way. However, I think they could do a better job overall.The tour bus was comfortable, clean and easy to see the countryside which is good because you do spend a lot of time on it traveling between destinations.I would recommend EF Tours because they do provide a great educational experience but be prepared for less than ideal food and accommodations.

name: Chrissy Lodovico
title: Saw A LOT in a Short Amount of Time!
text: I was able to enjoy this trip with my son since I am a teacher at the school too.  It was a fabulous time!  Very busy!  A lot of walking and busy days-we were non-stop, which is what you want to be when you only have a limited amount of time and so much to see.  My group were 18 year old boys so I was worried they would be hungry, but they were not! There were plenty of opportunities to eat, great breakfasts provided by the hotels, during free time, kids could grab a bite and check out the city themselves within a walking distance radius, which they LOVED.  Being with a tour group was great because we were able to bypass a lot of the lines when we were visiting places like the Louvre and Colosseum.  All in all it was a great trip, but you have to go into it realizing that there were going to be some hang ups like weather, or traffic, and just go with the flow.  That's part of the fun of travel!

name: J. W.
title: Tight schedule, but you see a lot!
text: The tour guide was very knowledgeable and pleasant. The guides for the excursions were a huge benefit as well. The schedule was too tight. Having to rush takes away from the experience and is very stressful. This is especially true for day 1, after flying overnight going right out into the tour is a lot. Many of us did not enjoy fragonard out of sheer exhaustion, and it has potential to be a very enjoyable tour. There was not enough free time. We ended up opting out of an all day excursion we had pre-paid for so that we could have some free time to explore.Most of the meals were ok with the exception of days 1 and 2. Day 1, the fondue, was good but felt like appetizers. After a full night of travel and a full day of walking this was not enough protein and vegetable. Day 2, vegetarian couscous, is not a meal for a large group. A few people enjoyed it, but most of the group ended up buying food or cooking in the room after we returned to the hotel.

title: Excellent tour of Central Europe!
text: The travel process was very smooth (I was on the trip along with my daughter), including the information leading up to the trip. The hotels were as expected…nothing extravagant but completely fine for a school trip. The app was very helpful and easy to navigate and customer service was knowledgeable, attentive and helpful on the few occasions I needed to speak with them. The trip program was well thought-out and maximized the amount of places we visited and learned about. The local guides were excellent, especially Daniela in Berlin. They were all very knowledgeable and informative. I do wish we had had more time to spend at Auschwitz and Birkenau…those two tours felt rushed and didn’t provide enough time for reflection and processing what we were seeing and hearing. Felt like a bit of a missed opportunity given the importance and gravity of these locations. Our main tour guide (Izabela) was just fantastic! She was super friendly, organized and knowledgeable. Having Izabela as our guide made the trip the absolute best it could be. Can’t say enough great things about her!!Overall the meals were good and did a good job of letting us sample local cuisine…the only meal that was sub-par was our first night in Prague. Would recommend changing that one up :) Overall this was an excellent trip and we had a fabulous time!

With good communication with group leaders, this disappointing experience could be avoided. Talk to group leaders before cancelling someone, please.

name: M.Santiago
title: Unforgettable Trip to Greece with Excellent Guides!
text: I had an amazing time in Greece with my daughter and her school! We visited so many beautiful and fascinating places — museums, historical churches, ancient ruins — and heard the most incredible stories and history along the way. Our guides were absolutely wonderful — friendly, caring, and always making sure we knew what was coming up next and how to be best prepared.If I had one small suggestion, it would be to offer a little more opportunity to experience authentic Greek cuisine. A lot of the included meals were understandably geared toward kids with picky appetites. During our free time, adults sometimes had to choose between exploring more or sitting down for a full local meal, since time in each area was a little limited. Tip for future travelers: Ask your guide early on for suggestions about the best times and places to enjoy a real sit-down meal — they know all the good spots and can help you make the most of your schedule!Overall, it was an unforgettable trip filled with amazing memories. So grateful we got to experience it!

name: Kelly Chen
title: Amazing cultural and educational experience in Japan
text: Our EF tour to Japan was an unforgettable and enriching experience that met all expectations, especially in terms of cultural immersion and educational value. The itinerary was thoughtfully designed to balance iconic sightseeing with authentic local experiences, giving our group a deep appreciation for Japan's rich history, traditions, and modern life. The balance between structured learning and free exploration allowed students to build their independence and practice critical thinking, while still feeling supported. text: While there were great parts to this experience, overall we didn’t feel it was worth the expense.On the positive side, the itinerary was excellent. The Buffalo mozzarella farm, the pizza and fettuccine making, and the gladiator activity were all really memorable and fun.A few of the critical things that did not meet our expectations:1. Instead of a direct flight, the connecting flight was exceedingly inefficient and took an entire day on both ends of the trip, which was both exhausting and frustrating. For the expense of this trip, we would expect a direct flight should be feasible with such advance notice.2. The food: Despite the fact that we filled out a form in advance with dietary restrictions, they were largely forgotten or ignored. Many of the trip attendees were vegetarian, but we were served ham and beef. In addition, the food in general was only fair. We were in Italy, one of the most noted places worldwide for food, but the included meals were disappointing and also lacked options. In such a large group it is unacceptable to expect every person to want the same meal.3. The hotels weren’t nice. The provided breakfasts were not good at all and the hotel itself provided only the most basic accommodations without any common areas, pool, gym, or anything for the kids to do.4. This was an educational tour, yet we got sadly little education. The “Whispers” in which we were to listen to the tour guides weren’t very good, making it hard to hear. The headphones were worse quality than those provided on airplanes. Plus the guide would explain things to the group, but with such a large group most people could not see what they were talking about, so it was too hard to follow along. Between the heavy accents and poor quality headphones, we picked up maybe 30% of what we were told, and that was trying really hard. We noticed many of the kids just lost interest or gave up out and played on their phones.5. Overall, the trip was far more expensive than it should have been with such poor flights, hotels, and food. We could have done the same trip for a direct flight, half the cost, and better food/lodging. The high price made expectations too high and therefore felt bad throughout the trip when the value fell short.

text: I am writing to caution parents and educators about using EF Tours for student travel. One leg of the journey included over 24 hours spent on a ferry and bus to get from Greece to Italy, a detail that was never properly disclosed ahead of time.The experience in Italy was no better. Students spent only one day in Florence, with no tours or structured activities scheduled for that day, except for a trip to a leather market. In Rome, the hotel EF booked was extremely concerning as it was located in a questionable area, and the rooms had no locks on the doors, raising serious safety concerns.Thankfully, overall, the local guides were good. He is definitely a great leader.  He made sure we were early to everything in case of heavy traffic, accidents or bus breakdown.  In being early, we were able to view other things not on our agenda.  My only criticisms would probably be always having a set item for dinners.  Not everyone likes certain foods like fish.  I also don’t eat vegan, so offering more than one set meal would be better.  Also, maybe switch up the paid dinners once in a while for a paid lunch and let us choose a dinner some time with a free time dinner time.  Other than this, this was my second consecutive year doing an EF Tour and as long as the folks I know keep doing one annually, I will continue to go.

title: We used EF tours for a family trip to…
text: We used EF tours for a family trip to Italy and Sicily over spring break recently (3/29/25 to 4/8/25).  We went with a group from our son's local high school.  Our tour guide (Guilia) and driver (Mikel) were fantastic.  The local tour guides were great as well.  We learned a lot.  Thankfully, the weather was great.  Our lodging and breakfasts and dinners were part of our package and already paid for.  When we had the opportunity (usually lunch) to choose our own food, it was much better.  Prior to the trip, we heard a lot of good things about the food in Italy, but unfortunately, most of our experience with food was not really good.  We stayed at 4 different hotels during our trip, and assume that the bedding in Europe/Italy is not a priority since all locations had very, very firm and uncomfortable beds.   Our first hotel was too close to the airport and highway, so very noisy especially since we had to open our windows because the hotel would not allow you to adjust your own room's thermostat even though there was one on the wall.  We actually enjoyed the island of Sicily more than the mainland of Italy.  Our experience on the ferry going from Naples to Palermo was terrible.  I would never do it again.  The ferry coming back from Sicily to Italy (30 min) was great, and we would do that again.  If we had to do this over again, we would take the 30 minute ferry to Sicily, drive the bus to Palermo, do everything we did in Sicily but skip the 1/2 day to Syracuse and devote more time to Pompeii (only had less than half a day).  We'd also spend more time in Amalfi, which for us was probably the highlight of the trip, especially the lemon farm experience.

title: Absolutely Unforgettable Experience!
text: This was truly a trip of a lifetime! From start to finish, EF Tours delivered an unforgettable adventure through Japan's iconic Golden Route. Our tour guides, Haruka and Baba, were phenomenal—so knowledgeable, full of energy, and incredibly engaging. They brought history to life, shared personal insights, and made every moment fun and meaningful.Highlights? So many! I was completely captivated by the Osaka temples and the peaceful beauty of the Nara shrines. Experiencing Japan's historical customs firsthand was deeply enriching. One of the most magical moments was visiting the small village near Mount Fuji—it felt like stepping into a postcard. And the Ice Caves? Absolutely breathtaking!We also enjoyed a cozy and authentic Sumo Hot Pot dinner, and the Open Fish Market in Tokyo was a culinary dream. The food throughout the trip was a feast for the senses—fresh, flavorful, and adventurous. Tokyo itself blew me away: immaculately clean, incredibly quiet for such a massive city, and the transit system was like something from the future—efficient, easy to navigate, and spotless.We even got a fun glimpse into modern Japanese culture with some colorful cosplay sightings that added a fun and vibrant touch to the experience.EF Tours nailed it. This tour was the perfect blend of tradition, culture, nature, and urban excitement. Highly recommend to anyone looking to explore Japan in a deep, authentic, and exciting way. Thank you, EF, Haruka, and Baba—you made this journey truly unforgettable!

name: Sara Glynn
title: Our tour guide
text: Our tour guide, Endika, was fabulous! 5 stars out of 5 stars for him. He shared a wealth of information, was so engaging with the kids, was very accommodating and kind. You can tell he’s passionate about his job and loves what he does- bringing culture and experiences to the children on the trip.I was fortunate to go on the trip with my son so I experienced everything firsthand. Our group leader was Stacy Vocasek and she was fantastic as well. She came from the Act School in CT. My son goes to the QMC middle college, which is a partnering school so we had no experiences with her prior to this however she was so inclusive and kind and also a wealth of information and helpful before and during the trip in so many ways.My only feedback or constructive criticism was the change of itinerary at the last minute. We were looking forward to the bike tour at Menserrat and the other group from other schools in New York decided they didn’t want to do that. We weren’t told it was going to drop from the itinerary until we were at the first day. I guess we are being reimbursed for it? The kicker was the other group then decided to do their own bike tour at a different location in Barcelona. Our kids in our immediate group were disappointed. I do feel that Endika was great in this scenario though and gave us some other local activity options our group could do. I feel like he was put into a few different challenges from the other groups not being collaborative or flexible and given that, he did an excellent job maneuvering and trying to make sure everyone was happy in the end. I can’t give him enough praises. I feel like the other groups weren’t as cooperative and challenged him a lot- even including dining options. I think he did a great job organizing restaurants so there was variety as well as some culture and the other groups did do takeout a few nights. Our kids in our group were open to just about anything and i think he appreciated that. I’d definitely recommend EF to other students and parents I know. My son already said if we went on another EF tour we should request Endika :-)

title: Wouldn’t Travel EF again
text: My son and I recently traveled to Greece with a school group, then chose to continue on to Italy without the group. I was very disappointed with their “Extend Your Tour” policy. While it’s marketed as a flexible option for travelers who want to explore more independently before or after the tour, the actual process is overly restrictive and lacks the transparency and customization one might expect.The main issues I encountered were the limited flight options and lack of communication about available alternatives. Despite requesting specific dates well in advance, I was offered only a narrow selection of itineraries, many of which were inconvenient or didn’t align with my the rest of our travel group. We were forced to fly a day later than the rest of our school group. Additionally, any changes or preferences came with steep fees or were simply not accommodated.I understand EF needs to work within airline constraints and group booking systems, but clearer expectations and more traveler-friendly flexibility would go a long way. Delta Airlines were happy to change my flight without any fee, EF Tours just had to give them the okay. However, they would not approve the change without a stiff fee along with threatening to cancel our flight home if we changed any leg of our flight. For anyone seriously considering extending their trip, I recommend planning your own post-tour travel separately rather than relying on EF’s option—it’s simply not worth the hassle. Or if I could redo I would have skipped all of EF tours and did the planning myself.EF Tours policy unfortunately falls short  as far as working with their customers or even listening to their concerns.

text: For my third trip, I took students and their parents on an EF Tour, choosing the "Experience Japan" option. It was amazing to cross the International Date Line, lose a day on the way to Japan, and then replay a day on the way home. We visited Okaka, Kyoto, Kanazawa, and Tokyo. My tour participants truly loved every minute of it. The experiences on this tour included participating in a traditional tea ceremony, a Zen meditation, and gilding our own pair of chopsticks.Aside from our first hotel and a glitch with our later arrival, our accommodations were stellar, and the breakfasts and dinners provided were mainly delicious. Kiki, our tour guide, worked hard to accommodate allergies and food plans for our groups.Our experiences at the sites on our itinerary were good. Japan is experiencing over-tourism in many places, so we encountered crowds at temples and shrines we visited, as well as at popular areas like Shibuya in Tokyo. These sites are popular for a reason.In most places, we had free time to walk around, snack, and shop - all of which were popular in our group.My group had such a great time that they are interested in taking the tour to Italy I've selected for next year.Japan - and EF - are 10/10 for responsiveness, helpfulness, and follow-up. They are the best bang for your buck, offering travelers a great visit without the headaches of planning and paying for all the individual parts of a self-planned trip. I am planning to return with my husband after this wonderful trip!

name: Michelle Pines
title: The EF Tour to Athens, Greece
text: The EF Tour process was seamless! Everything was laid out, time lines provided, to do lists were great. They provided free tour backpacks, even adjusted the tour itinerary due to a pending strike, so the kids wouldn't miss anything previously promised as part of the tour! They're fantastic to work with!

name: Browning
title: Our tour guide was phenomenal
text: Our tour guide was phenomenal!  The dinners were not good.  I'm not sure if this was because they thought they were catering to students ( who can be picky) but, when I have toured Italy in the past, the food was always a highlight.  The accommodations were fine.  It was nice for our group to be the only.ones at the villa the first couple nights so that we could bond before continuing on the rest of our tour.

name: Maritza Ortiz
title: Everything from day 1 was great
text: Everything from day 1 was great! The app is very easy and keep you on track of all the to do and date lines. Payments are very easy and flexible.My student had an amazing time,lots of memories and very educational.

name: Rebecca Yates
title: I had a wonderful experience on our…trip to French Riviera and the Alps!
text: I hada wonderful experience on our trip.  Our tour guide Lydia was so organized, helpful, kind, enthusiastic  and smart!  You could tell she loved her job!We had zero problems and she was such a professional.Our school sponsor did an amazing job as well. She was organized, patient and wise.Great memories were made!

name: Ashley Zomalt
title: Money well spent
text: This experience was so seamless with my child. Anything I worried or had concerns about was already thought of and planned for. My child said they loved their experience and for someone who is introverted, I loved that my child felt safe and free to be themself. It was an overall great trip!

name: Crystal O
title: A very memorable London experience.
text: Our experience with EF tours was very positive overall.  Logistics for day 1 were off a bit, resulting in no lunch for the group as we went from the airport to our first excursion so I would build in extra time on day one to ensure the guests have lunch.  I would also ensure that each restaurant has alternative options.  Although allergies and dietary restrictions were asked upfront, there are other things that guests prefer or not prefer to eat.  A good practice may be to have 2 options to pick from prior to the trip.  Our guide was great!  Very accommodating and knowledgeable about London and things to do there.  The kids and adults had a wonderful time learning and exploring on a daily basis!  So many new memories made!

title: Life experience, great, but……..
text: The experience was great. Showing the kids the culture, differences in the past and present of Peru. The tour guides were very good.Unfortunately, things did not play per advertised?We were told the kids would have breakfast and dinner included, and they would have to take care of their lunches. The two accompany flip-flopped it were most of the dinners had to be covered, which were quite a bit more expensive being that they took them to a specific location that was a buffet that had US prices?  I travel quite a bit and I know how this ploy works. They tend to get a commission for taking a bus full of  people to certain restaurants. If this would’ve been explained to us, we would’ve made sure the kids had sufficient funds for a $20-$25 buffet.The tour company also ran out of the bottled water. The result was they boiled water, but everyone got sick vomiting, and diarrhea.Another concern was their return flight was canceled due to weather. This of course is out of the hands of the tour group, but they ended up taking them back to the hotel. They stayed the previous night versus booking a hotel in Lima, which was a two hour bus ride each direction?For the amount that was paid, I feel that this tour under performed.My hope is the experience will overcomeThe frustrations they had.

name: Maria
title: Beware of EF Tours
text: Beware of EF Tours – Misleading, Overpriced, and Poorly ManagedMy experience with EF Tours has been incredibly frustrating and disappointing. They are essentially running a fraudulent operation masked as an educational travel service. Canceling a trip with them is nearly impossible – it took me five days, multiple phone calls, and long waits of over 20 minutes each time, just to try to speak to someone. Their callback system is a joke – it doesn’t work, and you’ll never hear back.They refuse to offer refunds, even when tickets haven’t been issued yet, and no hotel details are confirmed. That alone should be a red flag. They advertise an educational experience, but the learning aspect is minimal at best. On my Japan tour, we were given a mere 40 minutes to visit temples, but then spent an entire afternoon in a shopping district. Want to actually explore culture, history, or architecture? That’s on your own dime – taxi rides and extra entries aren’t covered.They also don’t cover lunch, so you’re constantly paying out-of-pocket. The cost of the trip is inflated not because of quality, but because chaperones go for free, and you and your kids are footing the bill. The accommodations are cheap, and it’s clear the trip could easily be done for half the price on your own with far better value.Even worse – if you're over 18 and encounter an issue, you're on your own. I had a ticket issue and was left stranded by the guide. I called the emergency number and was put on hold for 20 minutes with no answer. Tried the callback feature again – nothing. There is no support, even in urgent situations.EF Tours markets itself as a student travel company, but the reality is a logistical nightmare with poor customer service, misleading marketing, and questionable ethics. If you're considering traveling with them – don’t. You can plan a more enriching, affordable, and reliable trip on your own.

name: Amy

text: My child loved the experience and we were all wildly impressed with how much EF fit into their time abroad.  The downsides related to travel time (wildly long layover on the way to London) and having to wait for another school to land, go through customs, etc. It seemed like they tried to cut costs by combining trips and taking less-than-ideal flight options, which you don't learn about until very close to the departure date. name: Lisa Michalczuk- Vollmar
title: Adventure of a lifetime
text: Over spring break, I had the opportunity to lead a 9-day educational tour to Costa Rica with my students through EF Tours—and it was truly an unforgettable experience. Our itinerary took us through a range of incredible locations including Arenal, Monteverde, Jaco, San José, Sarchí, and the Central Pacific Coast.From kayaking on Lake Arenal and ziplining through the cloud forest, to hiking to the base of the Arenal Volcano and exploring the biodiversity of Manuel Antonio National Park, every day was packed with hands-on learning and adventure. We also enjoyed a crocodile cruise, a night tour of the rainforest, and one of the most meaningful parts of the trip—a cultural exchange with a local high school, which gave students a real taste of Costa Rican life and education.EF Tours handled everything with outstanding organization. As a group leader, I felt supported the entire way and never had to stress about logistics like hotels, meals, or transportation. Our tour director was knowledgeable, friendly, and great with the students—keeping everything on track while making it fun and educational.My students came away with new perspectives, lasting memories, and a deep appreciation for Costa Rica’s culture and environment. They couldn’t stop talking about the trip, and many said it was the best experience they’ve ever had. I wholeheartedly agree.I would highly recommend this tour to any educator looking to combine learning with adventure in one of the most beautiful and ecologically rich countries in the world.

title: My 13 year old son had a fantastic tour…
text: My 13 year old son had a fantastic tour in Greece over spring break. He saw so much, experienced so much in just a week. He gained independence from family but was surrounded by people his age and several adult chaperones (one a trusted teacher from back home). His favorite place was Poseidon's Temple.

name: CJ
title: Top notch tour guides
text: Top notch tour guides, they were all very lovely. Even though the bus broke down on us, because of a popped tire, the situation was resolved very quickly. There are some things I disliked. I didn’t like being treated like a child, on the bus. I can understand not wanting kids to eat or drink anything sticky on the bus, but to be a grown woman and having to throw out my ice cream and coffee was not something I can agree with. The kids making a mess should not mean adults are punished too. It’s the only thing I would say I very much disliked considering we were on the bus for many hours at a time. Also, to not be able to use the bathroom on the bus was ridiculous as well. Bladders are not always controllable, especially when we are hydrating to withstand the amount of walking we are doing. That is very bad for a persons health. Aside from that, I enjoyed the sites, the people, and the overall experience. I now know of places I would like to revisit and have more time to explore. There was so much to see and not enough time to see it. I love the educational aspect of the whole experience. Learning history out of a textbook was not for me, learning history by exploring where it took place is a whole new world. I loved it. I will absolutely be taking more tours with EF and I will highly recommend it to others.

name: Nicole
title: My daughter had a WONDERFUL time in Greece!
text: My daughter had a WONDERFUL time in Greece. She adored her EF Tours guide and said the local tour guides were great. All the experiences were amazing!The only reasons why I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 is from a couple of planning issues. First, the itineraries for Day 1 and Day 2 were combined on Day 1 because Day 2 was Greek's Independence Day so many places were going to be closed. I didn't understand why that wasn't taken into consideration when planning this trip months in advance.  Second, I would have liked if the group was seated together on the airplane. The group was NEAR each other but on all flights, my daughter sat by complete strangers. Luckily nothing bad happened but those are long flights and you don't know why kind of person is sitting next to your child for that flight. I would have been much happier if five rows of three could have been blocked out for their group to be able to sit by each other.

He learned so much through hands-on experiences and had nothing but great things to say about his tour guide, Roberto, who was both knowledgeable and friendly. A huge thank you to the teachers who made this trip possible—we truly appreciate your efforts! We’ll definitely consider EF Educational Tours for future travel opportunities.

title: Fantastic trip minus the layovers taking up 2 days
text: The activities on the trip were great. Food was great at each spot. Our tour director was very knowledgeable and fun to be around. We had one stop where the food was very plain and basic. Biggest complaint was the time we spent in airports. On the trip to the country we had a 7 hour layover and didn’t arrive to our hotel in Costa Rica until 10:30 at night, so one complete day was wasted in travel. On the way home we left the hotel at 10:00 am and arrived home around 1 am. Once again layovers killed a day. Advertised as a 8 day excursion but 2 were spent waiting in airports while other groups had more time in the country with more direct flights. We flew out of a main hub, but maybe more direct flights weren’t available? Not sure but that was a downer. Other than that we had a great experience and would do it again.

name: Desiree Lester
title: Great experience!
text: We had a great time in Paris, London and Normandy! Our favorite was Versailles and Paris. Overall our leader was great and accommodating and did a great job. The only reason for the negative star review was the food. We had the exact same dish the first two nights in a row and the entire trip consisted of potatoes. While I have no issue with beef and potatoes the same meal repeated on at least 4 nights was awful. We don’t mind the dish but it would have been nice to switch it up especially being in Paris and London and really not experiencing their cuisine. Also the breakfast included is the hotel breakfast(the best food we had actually!). Lunch sometimes doesn’t happen either with the packed schedule or we are given 30 minutes to find something quick and eat which can be difficult with both not knowing the area and the area being extremely packed with people. Also, be prepared for a packed schedule, there is a lot packed into a small amount of time and you will be going the entire day from the time you step out to the time you get back to the hotel. The downtime is the ride to each destination. Be prepared that drink during your day is not supplied and it can be difficult to find something to drink while out so make sure you check if water bottles are able to be brought with you so you can have something to refill for your trip. But overall a great experience and we would do it again!

name: Daniel Fink
title: Five stars easily except:
text: The trip itself was amazing.  My family of five enjoyed seeing new places, experiencing new cultures, and interacting with new people.  When looking back on our trip, the one thing that we absolutely could have skipped was EF's tour guide.Our tour guide was a combative, arrogant, dismissive, misogynistic nightmare. Our tour would have been far better, 5 stars easily,  had we not been assigned this person.He made us feel like we were on his vacation and he was doing us a favor.  Any time anyone would question his decisions (where to eat lunch when the tourists were paying), it would be met with negativity and arrogance.  Any question posed to him was seen as an insult.One of the most egregious things that he didn't do was his job.  When confronted with food allergies, he behaved as if it was an impossible inconvenience and how dare anyone expect him to follow the guidelines EF set forth. Apparently, making a restaurant aware of allergies in advance was a task far too difficult for him. When mentioning a food aversion, he took it upon himself to berate this person over the bus's microphone.My daughter badly twisted her ankle, and our guide acted like she had a paper cut.  I was literally carrying her, and his response was that we could get a bandage in the morning. We passed multiple pharmacies, and not once did he ask if we needed to stop.When we returned to the states, we discovered that she actually had a bone chip from this injury!  Our guide's response was to ignore her, even though I was practically carrying her, and never once to inquire about how she was doing.  Knowing that she had this injury, he continued to make her walk long distances and complained that we were too slow.  The additional guide on the first two legs of our trip, who was being trained,  was far more professional and considerate, getting her the medical attention that she required once we reached the hotel and frequently checking on her.  Our EF guide thought it was more important to distribute post cards that get ice for a twelve year old child.Our guide not only used the bus's microphone to air every thought that he had, he also used it to shame tour guests, whether it was to go to the bathroom, have a food aversion, or lost their passport.  We can understand that these things are sometimes difficult to deal with, but it is part of his job.He was also very vocal regarding his hate for one of our destinations.  There were people on the tour that had never been to this destination, were excited about the experience,  and he spent quite some time disparaging it.  After our visit to this destination, he was dismissive and rude to the tourists because they spoke up in favor of not only the destination, but the people as well.  It was incredibly unprofessional, and quite frankly, embarrassing.It appeared that our guide did not care what his job was, nor was he interested in doing it.There was nothing about our experience that he improved.  Instead, he actively made every moment that we were forced to spend with him insufferable.Our guide was hands down, the worst part of this experience.If this is the representative of the companies' values and policies, then this is not a company I want to associate with.  Our tour guide was the only bad experience and memory that we have from this trip.  Everything else was amazing, but it's not work a week with their tour guides.

name: Crystal F
title: Fun, educational, but may be difficult for those with physical limitations.
text: Our trip to Italy and Greece was very good. I loved visiting many of the historical and cultural sites such as the Vatican, the Acropolis, the Temple of Apollo, and the city of Knossos, home of the ancient Minoans in Heraklion on Crete. The students and I had fun walking around the shops and restaurants and trying many flavors of gelato and sampling other delicious foods.Our tour guide, Francesco, was great! Our bus drivers, especially Donato, were also very good.One recommendation I would make to travelers is to go to cities like Rome and Athens in off season times because even in March when my tour group went, many places in the big cities were crowded.One warning I would give to future travelers who would like to see the lovely countries of Italy, Greece, and Crete is to consider how physically capable you or your child is of walking in demanding terrain. Most streets and paths in these places are made of cobblestones and other types of rock that are not often level or very stable. Most of the historical and cultural sites as well as buildings in general are at the top of hills, on the sides of mountains, or elevated in some way. There are many, many steps, especially on the island of Capri, which makes travelling by foot difficult.Furthermore, all the hotels we stayed at had multiple floors and at least a few did not have elevators for guest use.All of this is to say that if you have any physical conditions that might limit walking, especially up and down hills, (I have arthritis and one of our group leaders has asthma) then please consider carefully if you or your child is ready for a trip like this as there seemed to be few to no options for extra assistance, although the group leader and I were able to ride up to the top of the Acropolis by elevator. Unfortunately, that elevator broke down on the way back down, and so we ended up stuck in the elevator for about 2.5 hours--not a highlight of the trip, but we were okay.

title: Overall the trip was a great success
text: Overall the trip was a great success. The students had a great time and were immersed in so much culture every day.  We did spend a lot of time in the bus. The dinners were hit and miss. I feel like it would work better to refine the agenda to have more authentic dinner experiences. Overall the dinner at the B&B Dinner of curry and rice was sparse and without option. The first dinner in Paris was rushed and under par for atmosphere. The lodging was okay. The initial night in Anchorage was not ready for us and we spent over an hour at the counter figuring it all out. I had to purchase an additional room to make it all work. I think that the London hotel could be a higher quality.  The other hotels were great. For food, the first couple of days were great. The breakfast at the B&B was good the first day but slammed the second and many of the kids didn't get much to eat. There wasn't a whole lot of time to sit with our team as a group and talk about the trip or our experiences. Being lumped in with two other groups created a mixed environment that made me question supervision and management for student of another group who were quite talkative and rambunctious throughout the entire tour. I think the tips for the bus driver and city guides should be included in the overall price tag of each tour and managed by the tour guide through EF. The main tour guide's tip should be structured as a deposit and given out based on an end rating of the experience. Changing currency through nations and trying to square the tips away on the journey created a lot of unnecessary labor.   I think our particular tour guide was outstanding. text: I think the experience as a whole was fantastic, my daughter was able to see several countries within the 9-day trip, and had a lot of tour-guided experiences that would've been hard to coordinate in such a short time span otherwise. The only issue I can think of was that my daughter missed out on a couple of the optional experiences that most of the group ended up going through while on the trip with her group. I don't remember seeing these experiences during the sign up process, I did sign up for the one or two that were available, but apparently there were a couple others that people were able to sign up for that I never saw, so she missed out. I went back and looked in our account, and I saw no mention of those optional experiences in the EFTours account, but most of the other students on the trip had them added and there was no way to have her pay on the day of, it apparently had to be paid for ahead of time. The process may have been missed by me somehow (though I really don't know how), but either way, it seems like everything should be bundled in together so nobody in the group ends up being left out. title: First and last time with book EF tours
text: My son went to Iceland with his classmates on EF tours. There were 14 students. We didn't receive the flight info until a few weeks before the trip, and they had the worst flights booked. They had economy, and we had to pay for a checked bag, they also didn't receive food service for a 7 hour flight to Iceland from the US. The kids had layovers going to Iceland and coming back they had a layover in a different state, slept at a hotel near the airport and got a 6:30am flight the next day. They didn't land until 10pm the night before, and they were coming back from Iceland to the US so they "lost" 4 hours. EF didn't take into effect that they had to check a bag so we had to pay for a checked luggage on the flight home, as that wasn't enough. We paid almost 6k for the trip, and it didn't include lunch. Waste of 6k for a trip of a lifetime turned nightmare with flights and hotels. Never Again

text: I am writing as a parent of an 18-year-old who just completed an EF trip to Berlin, Krakow, and Prague.From what I heard, the guides were very good, and the content of the tour was often excellent. No complaints there.At the same time, the schedule seemed hectic, undermining the experience of learning and enjoying. Far too much movement in a very short time. Why the rush to cram so much in?Also, I take issue with the Auschwitz/Birkenau tour. EF allocated only three hours to visit this venue, followed by a side trip to a nearby salt mine unrelated to the Holocaust.The juxtaposition of the two sites was, at best, tone-deaf, and at worst, insulting to the memory of those slain by the Nazis.Concentration camps shouldn't be bundled together with unrelated tourist activities, as if they were just another site to check off on a list.

name: Rebecca N
title: The beginning of the trip was extremely stressful.
text: The beginning of the trip was extremely stressful and very chaotic due to our Tour Director Fatima. She was extremely unorganized and had poor time management skills. It started with her being late to receive our group at the airport. She did not interact or speak on sites we were going to be visiting. When we arrived in Rottenburg the Hotel was lovely. Once we gathered with our Tour Director she gave very brief and scripted information on the site we were visiting. We were extremely late to our 2nd and 3rd dinner, to the point the restaurants were going to turn us away. The 3rd nights dinner we were so late the owner was extremely rude and the food was not edible. Our children walked with the head chaperone and Tour Director to a local pizza place so they could have dinner. Our Tour Director was asked to stay and walk back to the hotel with our group and her response was "I am exhausted and can not" then she left the group to walk back to the hotel without her. While on the tour bus and going to sites on our itinerary she was putting on her makeup, taking selfies and posting on Instagram. Our Tour Director did not interact or speak to us about the sites we were going to or if she did they again were just scripted facts. Fatima was asked multiple times by the adults about different scenery and areas and most of the time she had no answer and once she googled it she did not share it with the students. The biggest concern I have is for the safety of the students. We were running late (Fatima had the group stop for Gelato) and the group was separated because she was walking so fast. I asked Fatima twice to slow down and her response "they need to walk faster" Fatima continued with 5 students from our group and I waited as I saw how far behind our group was to make sure no one went the wrong direction. Well the first group of students arrived and were going to walk in the wrong direction away from our tour bus. I waited for all to get to my location and pointed them in the correct direction of the tour bus. The Chaperones were at the rear of the group to ensure no one was left behind. Our Tour Director did not care if anyone was left behind. I felt this was extremely reckless and unsafe for our students. She was not prepared for any sites we went to and last minute getting maps and even then she never got enough for the whole group. I feel she was extremely unprofessional and lacks the people skills to do a tour. Our Tour Director was replaced for the last 2 days by Dejanna and she was a total game changer. She was WONDERFUL! She interacted with our group, gave great detail about the sites we were going to and spoke to us about history of the countries. Dejanna was very knowledgeable and she made the tour bus rides fun and interesting and was constantly pointing out beautiful scenery and again giving facts. Dejanna although she was not with us in the beginning she still talked about a lot of places we had been and about local history and culture. Her time management was complete opposite of our original Tour Director. We were able to meet our itinerary schedule and had longer than 50 minutes to explore and eat. There were 2 occasions our group was waiting on Fatima: #1 she was shopping for jewelry. #2 She was eating (buffet dinner). I feel that for the most part Fatima was treating this as her vacation time and not a job. There were things we were not able to see due to her poor communication and lack of time management. Our tour bus driver was agitated by her tardiness as there are driver rules to follow and Fatima did not appear to care. I can give further detail if you you request. The hotels were nice, our bus driver was great. The hotel breakfasts were very good and the dinners were lacking as far as options for all. I am thankful EF stepped up and replaced our Tour Director(wish it had been done sooner) with Dejanna. I honestly can not say enough great things about Dejanna. I feel like I learned more in the 2 days with Dejanna then I did the whole time with Fatima. text: I’ve had the unique experience of traveling abroad with student groups nine times and this tour marked my fourth with EF as a Group Leader. Live Fado and Flamenco performances didn’t just entertain—they told stories that brought history to life. Every day offered opportunities to connect with the music, arts, and languages of these incredible countries.The itinerary struck a perfect balance between education and adventure. Whether exploring breathtaking cathedrals, wandering through historic quarters, or marveling at dramatic coastlines and pristine beaches, students were constantly engaged and inspired. Our time in Costa del Sol felt like a dream—beautiful accommodations, relaxing surroundings, and a sense of security that made the experience even more enjoyable.Our Tour Director was simply outstanding—knowledgeable, passionate, and incredibly organized. He created an atmosphere where both students and chaperones felt supported and excited to learn. The local guides were equally phenomenal, sharing their expertise in a way that was accessible, fun, and memorable.EF’s commitment to safety, structure, and high-quality educational experiences continues to earn my full trust. I would absolutely recommend this itinerary to other Group Leaders—it’s a dynamic blend of cultural discovery, historical depth, and student-friendly adventure. I can’t wait to offer this same tour again to future travelers as it exceeded all expectations!

name: Kayleigh Darling
title: I used THS for 22 days after reaching…
text: I used Trusted House Sitters for 22 days after reaching out to a couple who referred me to the website as they were not able to sit for me. I believe this is the first ploy in marketing this website and that actually they were never really going to be available and just market this app.Upon submitting a listing I quickly received an application from a young girl, with AI looking photos, who got my name completely wrong and offered to sit my dogs, she had no reviews, lives in Maylasia apparently. THS claims people are verified but it seemed suspect to me and like a fake profile. This did not feel like a sensible or safe application to accept and I proceeded to invite a number of people to sit for me, all of which declined, or just didn’t reply at all.After 22 days and worrying about availability for summer holidays I decided THS wasn’t for me or worth the £139 (and that’s a basic membership with a discount apparently).I asked to have a partial refund given my short lived and negative experience, I was told this would be escalated to a manager and was informed within a few hours there would be no refund, none of the details I shared were taken into consideration and I was told this decision is final.I do not recommend, go for something else like Rover where you pay for sitters but there are a lot more reviews and at least you get replies more quickly from members because they’re being paid. I found 3 offers to accept for dog sitting within 3 hours.Rubbish customer service, rubbish experience.

name: Skyla

name: Amy Jeroloman
title: The Site Favors Sitters over Housesits & the messaging is misleading
text: I spend a lot of time making a profile and loading pictures for a housesit. There were two applicants which then makes me not eligible for a refund. One waiting nearly 2 weeks to say she couldn’t come since she didn’t have a car. The other took another sit just before we were to meet.Many of the sitters have profiles that aren’t actuate. Some don’t live in the state listed, others don’t want local sits or long sits. Some aren’t really available since their calendar’s aren’t up to date. Some are unreliable and don’t follow through since there isn’t any loyalty to the Pet Parent.I’ve also recently realized some sitters are using this site to promote their personal pet sitting business at an expensive rates. (Some are on Facebook.) They’ll use the reviews and background checks from this site to show they are ‘trusted’Lessons Learned: Basic plans are not eligible for a refund. If you get two applicants, you’re not eligible. The site favors sitters over housesits. Don’t believe the auto messages to sit back and wait for applications. Better look and make offers if you want to have a sitter through this site. I’ve had to hire a local person, not on this site, at twice the regular rates and also additional charges for each pet. Ouch.

name: Mrs Sarah Wood
title: In the end we had a good sitter but…
text: In the end we had a good sitter which worked well.However I had MANY refusals, a lot of whom said ‘would love to but not this time’. Also replies from sitters who were not available despite showing as free on website. This is frustrating. I also had  3 who said yes and then changed their minds. One who suddenly remembered that they didn’t have a car and couldn’t get to us!As with a previous review I could find no way to register that some sitters appeared to be time wasting.

name: Charlotte Stockwell
title: Peace of Mind
text: This would be the fourth time we have used Trusted Housesitters. Each time, we have been more than happy with the people who have come to take care of our animals and house.One of the stays was for 16 weeks, others have been shorter.The process for assessing who is best suited is efficient and we have been able to identify who we want to sit for us very quickly. Communication via the app is easy. All sitters have been great at sending us photos of the animals - especially the two cats who are very keen on sitting on laps.Once you have set up your listing, it's easy to update.We have had nothing but really delightful people come and stay - some local - some from overseas.Our last house sitters were with us for 6 weeks and took fabulous care of our rather elderly dog and two very old cats.I didn't fill out the info about our house on the app but have left a comprehensive file at home with all the appliance manuals and a separate debit card with a small amount of money on it for emergencies such as a plumber or electrician. No-one has ever taken advantage of that.The cost to join is reasonable and knowing that the sitters have access to online veterinary support if they need it also reassured us.We have recommended this site to many others.

Communication was great and I returned to a relaxed, happy and healthy kitten.A super exchange of accommodation for cat-care.The whole process and the app / support worked seamlessly.

name: Miranda Holman
title: I was recommended the site by a friend…
text: I was recommended the site by a friend who joined. We have thoroughly enjoyed our experience so far (have been on two sits so far with another one booked in August).The houses we have stayed in have been beautiful and we have been able to explore different parts of the UK.I would recommend reading the profiles thoroughly before you commit so you know what to expect and there is no surprises to either party.We have really enjoyed our house sits and spending time with our new furry friends. I would definitely recommend giving it a go.

name: Mrs Murphy
title: CRAZY GOOD PLATFORM
text: We have been house sitters for 7+years and helped approx 70 home owners enjoy their travels, knowing their cats, dogs, sheep, rats, cattle and more are being well looked after.  The site offers multiple opportunities to travel far and wide, it's up to us to secure the sit with confidence that it's a match.  There have been times the match wasn't quite right for example, home cleanliness, home owner attitude or not true reflection of care required, but l have to say it's a crazy good site! You meet some fabulous people who have become friends in our world and we spend time with wonderful animals in amazing lovely places. We don't want to commit to a dog or cat at home, so sharing is fabulous.  We want to travel because being retired and at home can mean job after job and l get bored and want to travel locally and overseas while l can! I love it that we can  help people and feel appreciated. Yes sometimes home owners cancel but as long as the reason is genuine; we had planned to go to Guernsey July 2025, but sadly their elderly labrador had to be put to sleep, so they cancelled and offered to pay for any travel costs we may have incurred... luckily we had not arranged travel yet, but how kind and thoughtful to offer if we had.  We ourselves have been on the verge of cancelling due to a medical diagnosis that required lots of scans, operation and follow up treatment, but thankfully our friends, who sometimes join us on a sit, came to our and the home owners rescue. Either side cancelling can be difficult, l think l would always recommend the home owner has a back up plan, just as we do if our travels across the other side of the world are cancelled. I think it's amazing that we have walked into people's homes, never met them, taken over all they love, shared their home and pets and then left! other times we have spent an evening with good food, wine and great company, having chatted away like we have known each other for years! There are so many stories you could tell, which have enriched our lives and our friends who sometimes join us. It's addictive!!

name: Corinne Matheson
title: My experience was ok
text: My experience was ok, not great, but that had nothing to do with Trusted House Sitters.  The web-site worked for me, and I was given e-mails to remind me when my house sitter was coming.  I had the sitter come a few days early while we were here as we live off grid and have horses, so there is a lot more to learn than just having cats and dogs.  We feel our sitter helped themselves to toilet paper rolls, food and gas (for the generator) since they live in a little car when not house sitting and they said they get food from the Food bank and get money from the Government to pay for things when not sitting.  This person was very charming and talkative and very helpful with writing us instructions to help future sitters using AI to write everything.  So very personable and charming, but I feel we were taken advantage of.

name: customer
title: Terrible Experience – No Support from TrustedHousesitters
text: We had a truly awful experience with TrustedHousesitters. Our sitter cancelled at the last minute right before our 3-week holiday, leaving us scrambling to find alternative arrangements. To make matters worse, the platform offered absolutely no support. Their chat service is unresponsive, there’s no phone number to call, and messages are routinely ignored.After many attempts, I finally got through to someone who promised reimbursement for the emergency pet care we had to arrange. That was over three weeks ago. I was told I’d receive the funds within 7–10 business days — still nothing. Since then, TrustedHousesitters has continued to ignore my messages.Even more frustrating is that the sitter who cancelled on us still has glowing 5-star reviews and continues to get bookings. The platform doesn't allow you to leave a review if the sit was cancelled — effectively silencing honest feedback and misleading future users.I urge anyone considering this service to think again. You're better off booking a reputable pet sitter directly and having peace of mind. I’m now pursuing a small claims case in the UK to recover my money, as this entire experience has felt like a scam.Update 11th May: Provided trustpilot my name and email so that they can pass on my details to trusted housesitters. In the meantime another day with me chasing these people up for my claim has passed. Heard the same thing today that they will chase this up with their claims team tomorrow  😂

name: Katherine P
title: Positives and negatives
text: I use the service for sitters to look after my cats on holiday  I have had some good experiences with sits that have gone well. However, I have also had confirmed sitters cancel twice after going through quite a bit of a discussion, at quite last minute. These were five star rated sitters. Maybe I have missed it, but when the sit is unconfirmed I could not see an option to leave a review, so these sitters can be leaving people in the lurch without there being any indication that this has happened.

name: Justine Song
title: GOING DOWNHILL
text: I've been using Trusted Housesitters for over 10 years and it has been a great way to communicate and connect with pet parents, as I am a caregiver. However, the site now seems to run on algorithms and show posts as "NEW" or "LOW APPLICATIONS" to entice you to click on them, only to find out they are old posts. So - newcomers, beware because the amount of sits does not necessarily match what's actually CURRENTLY AVAILABLE. It's a shame, but competition seems to have caught up here. I still use the site, but I am very aware and conscious of scams and re-posts. Do your due diligence if you're going to pay for this service.
