name: Sam (now abroad in UK/EU)
title: Have completed 5 sits thus far -- what a Phenomenal resource for "responsible" travelers!
text: I'm an American, now semi-retired (a digital nomad still providing services on occasion for clients back in the States), and TrustedHousesitters has delivered a delightful as well as invaluable re$ource for my initial travels here in the UK where I’ve just completed my 5th sit. I’ll be commencing my longest sit yet next week which will last an entire month; to date I’ve house/pet sat for 10.5 weeks collectively in recent months via this comprehensively designed site, and have been consistently impressed with all aspects of TrustedHousesitter’s program for volunteers.Prior to pursuing this path, I did a good deal of research and this site not only had impressive reviews over their decade-plus history, but their scope of offerings also looked to be the largest on-offer -- small wonder given how WELL they facilitate their matchmaking service between sitters and hosts globally. I opted for their premium membership and was especially reassured by their money-back guarantee re: landing a sit soon upon joining or a refund would be forthcoming. So that was probably the final assurance I needed in taking the plunge, and I’m Very thankful I did – the caliber of hosts/homes/locations on offer has been absolutely ideal for me, including given my love of historic properties.  Not only was I invited back for a return sit straightaway from a favorite host for a fave lil’ doggie, but their stately country manor was built in 1780, and is also situated in a gorgeous rural locale…just my cuppa!  : DTHS’s scope of offerings is truly staggering – and I’ll next be heading to Spain – and I especially appreciate how detailed each listing is. For example, I’m able to specifically filter results for properties with high-speed internet since that’s an essential for me. And other key amenities I look for are also readily referenced (or not) on each sit’s listing so sifting and sorting in determining a best fit opportunity is very easily accomplished. I also congratulate THS on their review policy, and while I haven’t needed to access it (thankfully!) it’s also invaluable to know that I can readily connect to a vet for advice as a component of my membership.I feel very “looked after” as a part of the THS community, including receiving very responsive support from customer service the couple of times I’ve reached out for minor assistance. Overall, I’ve had such a positive experience in fulfilling my sit commitments, and am grateful for the reviews (all 5-star!) I’ve received thus far -- which then facilitates obtaining subsequent sits, so I do feel rewarded for my diligence and care on my host’s behalf. Thank you, TrustedHousesitters…you’re deeply Appreciated by this solo traveler and I’ve frequently raved about your service to others, both in my travels here as well as to friends et al. back in the U.S. – this volunteering route is a key component in removing the majority of my housing-related expenses so it’s made this adventurous new chapter of life financially viable for me. And, as a Huge add-on bonus, it’s also concurrently equipped me to meet and interact with locals which has created a far richer travel experience for me too. I HIGHLY recommend this beautifully-managed resource as they’ve surely earned my 5-stars in return!

text: My last sitter was extremely good. I gave a 5* review! It’s what home owners want to see. However, I advise everyone, sitters and pet parents to do their homework and ask the right questions of the sitter or home owner in order to ensure you get the right match. Do this via the App before switching to other means of communicating. It’s all great unless there is a problem.  Having read reviews on THS it’s clear that customer services for people experiencing problems are terrible. It’s all Bot run and the replies to reviews are from a standard template. There appears to be no resolution even if premium membership. So beware!Be up front and clear about what irks you. I’ve had some miscommunication issues with sitters but I’ve learned from them. I offered a sitter some food from the freezer and he took it he could eat the lot!! Lesson leant!! As a pet parent I want to be generous to my sitter but I don’t want to be taken for a ride. I have had mostly positive experiences so far. My pet has been well cared for and that’s what counts. Please do provide at least the basics for your sitter. title: I love this platform...
text: I love this platform... it allows me to indulge my love of animals and love of travel for just a nominal annual fee. It builds trust and friendships across the miles and allows the building of a mutually beneficial arrangement.I have long used Air bnb for short breaks but always missed the company of animals. Now, unless I'm booking a family break (with our dog), I search TH instead.I've only ever been a sitter and am in awe of those who open their homes to others in this way.

name: Rebecca Talbott
title: Godsend for finding care for our kitty…
text: Godsend for finding care for our kitty cat!So far this app/website has been a godsend for finding caretakers for our kitty cat when we travel. It's allowed me to finally travel without feeling guilty about leaving my cat all alone.

name: Yvonne Herkemij
title: This app provides a 100% win-win
text: This app provides a 100% win-win for both pet/home owners as well as house/pet sitters.  It is clean as no money is exchanged. Love this concept and have had nothing but positive experiences.

name: Kathleen Doria
title: TH has connected us with terrific opportunities,
text: TH has connected us with some terrific pets, in interesting places, and with very decent and committed pet owners. We completed 5 sits in 2024 and we received 5 star reviews across the board. Our hosts received 5 stars 80% of the time, so you can see we are very happy with how TH connects us to satisfactory pet sitting opportunities.The disappointment or frustration is with the software. The software and app don’t always apply the filters, whether you are trying to limit which pets (dog, cat, farm animals, etc.), specific dates (suggested dates are out of range), or location (a better understanding of United States geography and/or commonly accepted names for regions, e.g. Texas Hill Country, Olympic Peninsula). Texas covers a large landmass and searching by city/town name is not always helpful. Searching the entire list of available sits in the state is burdensome.As a prospective sitter, I would also like to be able to see a host’s profile BEFORE submitting an application.I have referred friends to sign up as hosts only to learn that they have spent hours writing up instructions on pet care, To Do/Not Do lists, and interesting things to see/do in an area, never knowing that TH offers a Welcome Guide format. They do not, if ever, become familiar with the Welcome Guide (as a Host) until they have secured their first sitter.

name: Ben Bertoldi
title: DO NOT TRUST this company with your…
text: DO NOT TRUST this company with your beloved pets, house or money and pay for a membership it's a total scam. I signed up based on the terms advertised that a full refund would be available within 14 days of the 5th sit being declined. When I requested a refund within this timeline I was advised by the customer service representative on advice from their supervisor this was not possible. It looks as though the terms have changed or are no longer visible on the website and they are refusing to honour the terms of the membership agreement signed up for. Misleading, deceptive and I suspect fraudulent. Extremely disappointing. Sharing to help others not make the same mistake.

name: Madeline
title: Great Experience
text: I’m so glad I found this platform. Being part of this community has enriched our lives in so many ways, and we’re excited to continue exploring, learning, and sharing our adventures. :)

title: Love  the pets

Be respectful and kind and you will have such fun with your animal hostTPS is such a great idea and well set up.Take responsibility seriously

name: Lynn P.
title: Great idea from great company
text: Being a technophobe I did manage to master the form filling and find the process quite straightforward. We have nothing but praise for the Trusted Housesitters because the system works and you can find someone suitable to sit for your precious animals. Honesty is key to the process working

I recommend this site to anyone who would be looking to travel in this way. I couldn’t be happier with THS.

name: Phil
title: Two years ago my wife and I were both…a new lease of life

This is a great win-win for both sides.

name: Andres Enriquez
title: Never trust the person that they send to your home.
text: The last 2 sitters I had were something out of a horror movie.  "P" has 50+ great reviews and that is why I chose her for my 1 week sit while away in Madrid.  She showed up at noon....6 hours early and was irritated I wasn't home for her to start her sit.  Upon meeting, I wasn't happy with my choice as she was a bit off and wouldn't stop complaining about things...insisted I get Netflix for her entertainment and told me all her possessions were in storage and she uses their platform so she doesn't have to pay rent.  I basically had a homeless person in my home for a week.  "D" was my even worse nightmare as I came home from being away for 10 days in Vienna to feces and urine everywhere, $800 of Amazon deliveries missing and absolutely no updates or communication while I was gone.  When I texted, called and emailed asking where my packages were I got no response.  I escalated this through THS and it took 30 days to get a response since my complaint. They made a "note" on the sitters profile and told me that his defense was that my place was dirty.   "D" claims to have made "Tens of Thousands of Dollars" on Rover and other platforms yet he can't even walk my dog and left feces everywhere without even picking it up, that's why my place was dirty.   Finally...THS is uncooperative and won't give me "D's" last name or address so I can press charges with the police.  THS wants the police to call them directly for "D's" personal info.  In other words, the identity of the people you allow in your home is confidential, yet what do you really know about them?

name: Letitia Tappa
title: A great experience
text: I have been a member for going on 3 years now, and have had 4 sits, from 3 different sitters (one couple I used twice). For the cost of membership, you get a year's worth of vacation sits with your pet in your home. The sitters get a year of international home stays.For homeowners, there is a fairly lengthy process of creating a guide to your home and your area, but it's well worth it.We have not had any issues with anyone who sat for us. They have been retired people, tech workers wanting to relocate, and a young person looking at different areas to settle in our state.Everyone is vetted by the company and background checked, and ids verified. I realize that people can always slip through the cracks, so it's important to meet your sitter via skype, phone, or in person. (And they can vet you).It's a great idea, and so far it's working for me.

name: Zoe Byrd
title: Most gigs are win win, but Pay where Pay is due.
text: The Trusted Housesitters website is very professional and user friendly. They provide a very good service to both house / pet sitters and home / pet owners.Most of the trades are a win / win for both parties.However, because there are some gigs that require more care and work, those gigs should pay the pet sitter. For instance homes with more than 3 pets are good candidates to pay their pet sitter.A button could be added that the pet owner checks ON when they realize their situation deserves remuneration and they are willing to pay for services. They could indicate on a scale how much per day they are offering, or they could work that out off the site directly with the pet sitter.The pet sitters, maybe in the review process, can click a button ON to indicate that this gig should have been a paid gig.Thank you for your attention to this matter and for sending it up the Trusted Housesitters chain of command for serious consideration.

name: Veronika Pavlová
title: It is awesome
text: It is awesome, trustworthy app. I am very happy I am part of it. The app is works great and the options there, are endless.

name: Lee Kaiser
title: After my first two sits totalling five…
text: After my first two sits totalling five weeks I won't be renewing next year. I'm finding as a sitter that pet parents have unreasonable expectations to the point of abuse. Perhaps this is because I am choosing only long sits. More chance for things to go wrong on both ends. My very first sit I had a pet medical emergency and was sitting up all night with the dog cleaning up vomit and diahrrea inside the apartment. Then the electricity shorted out and I had workers coming and going and no lights. I contacted the owners immediately on both things. I am not saying these things shouldn't have happened (especially poor doggie) but I do take issue with the owners then having the gall to deduct stars for me being "unprepared" and bothering them. Not a bit of thanks. Shocking and depressing. The next sit also made me feel underappreciated and depressed. They also deducted stars because of when I arrived at the sit and complained their description was inaccurate and realized I would have to take taxis to grocery shop because it was so far away. Sitters with less than five stars don't find sits. What a waste of my time and effort and money since I'm paying for this abuse. I feel like TH is the only one benefiting and not putting in enough guardrails to prevent this kind of abuse. They need to do away with this star rating system and just allow comments. Most pet parents won't accept anyone with less than five stars even though the ratings are all subjective. Sitters aren't employees and yet pet parents see them that way when they accept these ratings as serious and accurate. It would be like having a job performance review based on what your fellow workers think of you rather than your boss.

name: Marlen Pando
title: 4/5 Love hate relationship
text: We are a DINK couple, so we try to travel during the off-season. During these instances we LOVE THS, there usually is a variety of trustworthy applicants to choose from who are happy to take care of a senior cat and a Samoyed. Usually a sit already makes up for the annual cost on the platform (if you were to compare it  to Rover or Wag).HOWEVER and here's the part we hate, during Christmas breaks it is a pain in the .... getting anyone. There is an oversupply of housesits available and the sitters we have had the past 3 years we have used the platform, were mediocre at best. We have experienced it all during those times, sitters ghosting you around Thanksgiving when they had already confirmed the Christmas sit, coming back to dirty sheets and dry cat puke on the floor, broken kitchen appliances, sitters who do not even bother reading the welcome guide and drown you with questions during your holidays... you name it.If you are like us and travel during off-season mainly, you'll probably have no issue finding amazing sitters. But if you are planning on using it during the big holidays... you might find it a bit more difficult to attract worthy sitters. Make sure you make available your dates in advance and pray, besides identity screening, I don't think there are many filters they can use to screen sitters. Always check their reviews!!!

name: SJM
title: Horrible insurance for pet sitters and home owners
text: This company must have been founded as a house sitters-only app and is now predominantly a free pet care app. The problem is they offer no insurance plan to speak of to protect sitters or homeowners.If a sitter gets bit by a dog with behavior issues on a sit, (and there are plenty) too bad, they offer no insurance and expect you to use your health insurance. If a pet gets sick or injured on a sit, too bad, they expect the owners of the pet to use their pet insurance. (But don't require that members have pet insurance.)The problem is that we live in a litigious society, and when people's homes and pets are at stake, emotions run high. There are MANY pet owners asking for care for pets that are practically on their death bed, and for pets with behavior issues not disclosed. Could you imagine being bit by a dog on a sit and then having to pay for medical care yourself? Could you imagine having a sickly pet die on your watch with a hysterical homeowner ready to blame someone for the death?I met a woman completely laxidazical about allowing her cat outside with nothing but an unlocked baby gate in her apartment stairway who then told me her last sitter lost her cat.THS has horrible customer service. I had a sit cancelled last minute and it took them FOUR days to respond. They kept the sit active on my profile so I could not find another.Their emergency line is for the birds. It will take someone six hours to call you back.THS WILL cover the replacement of something in the house that is broken during a sit if it costs more than $500. They will also cover if a dog bites a third party not involved in the sit.Their insurance is worse than Rover's and Rovers is very bad. If you are a sitter, you could pay for your own pet-sitting insurance, but many insurances won't cover third-party app sits. So you have no choice but to trust fall with some strange pet owners.They basically tell the sitter and pet owner to work out any differences independently, so no help there either. Any angry homeowner can claim the sitter stole something or leave them a terrible review, and guess who is more affected by the review? Is it the homeowner with the two million dollar home that people want to stay in, or is it the sitter who wants to travel and is looking for a nice place to stay in lieu of spending money on an Airbnb?  It's exploitative in that the sitter cannot really be honest in their reviews on cleanliness, etc., and must act grateful for the opportunity to stay in opulent homes, sometimes caring for multiple pets for no monetary compensation. I have arrived at homes that were disgustingly filthy with splatters all over the microwave, greasy fridge handles, rotten food in the fridge, layers of dust on all surfaces, crumbs and bugs on the floor. Disgusting. I have also arrived to TWO sits where large dogs have pooped and peed all over the place after only being alone for an hour or two and the accident issue was never disclosed.After paying over a hundred dollars for a membership, THS also does not insist that pet owners carry pet insurance, and doesn't seem to moderate the many, many members who ask for "local only" sitters. Well, this app markets itself as being a solution to Airbnb offering people a place to stay on their travels in exchange for pet sitting— not really the case with all the members asking for LOCAL ONLY people to take care of their multiple dogs and cats for free.Essentially Trusted House Sitters is a FREE PET SITTING APP that is ruining the paid pet sitter economy and has worse insurance than Rover. If you want a pet sitter, hire one. AND MAKE SURE THEY ARE INSURED for both of your sakes. This is just predatory gig economy stuff at work.How nice for THS to be collecting hundreds of dollars for each pet sitter and pet owner and then offering nothing in terms of customer service or insurance.NOPE!

name: Kathleen
title: Great when it works, horrible when it doesn't!
text: In October, I posted my listing for Christmas travel and received a few applications from sitters, speaking to each and confirming one 2 months in advance.  10 days before my travel, I confirmed with him that everything was fine and then 4 days before the Sit was to begin, I contacted him to confirm his estimated time of arrival at my home.  He however got angry, started to complain about how he was too busy to make travel arrangements, began to hint that he wanted me to pay for his travel because he did not have the money, then eventually said he would not come and I should find a kennel to put my dog in instead.   While TrustedHousesitters can not be liable for individual sitter's behavior, they were not able to do anything to assist me in this situation.  I had to spend my whole weekend, instead of packing and shopping as planned, trying to find another dogsitter.  I found one that I am very happy with locally (not using THS) who I will end up paying almost 500 dollars!  This is ok, but then why did I waste money on an annaul subscription to THS?? So, while I have had a few good experiences with TrustedHouseSitters, I have to say, they have no way of dealing with issues like this, which means they are not to be trusted at all.  Trusting means that we can count on someone in both good and bad situations, and while I do not fault them for the behavior of the sitter, this shows that their business model is flawed.  There should be a cancellation penalty for Sitters who cancel last minute, which is forwarded to the Homeowner to cover their unexpected expenses if another suitable sitter can not be found on the platform.  THIS would be trustworthy, but what happened in actuality, is NOT a trustworthy model.  Its really unfortunate because I loved the idea and had such good experiences with my first 2 sitters!  But, one can not rely on a company that has no way to handle problems when they arise.Update (based on their reply): TrustedHousesitters has taken zero responsibility for the absolute failure of their platform’s services. They made no effort whatsoever ever to help find a replacement sitter, they offered no monetary compensation although I paid for their service which failed.  Their customer service made a bunch of useless suggestions which wasted more time for many of their users. And then they laughably write a review response signed by “TeamTrusted”.  Apparently they need a better understanding of the definition of the word Trust.  I trusted their offering and paid an annual fee for their services.  And have learned through this experience that they unfortunately can not be trusted.  What a bummer.

text: We’ve been thrilled with our experiences with TrustedHousesitters! We’ve had the privilege of staying in beautiful homes and bonding with amazing animals, all while creating unforgettable memories as a family.The platform is easy to navigate, but there’s definitely room for improvement to make it even more user-friendly. Adding filters for beds, bedrooms, bathrooms, whether a car is available or needed, and whether the location is walkable or not would be extremely helpful. While many hosts provide some of this information in pictures or descriptions, it would be great to have these details searchable or clearly visible on their profile upfront. This would save sitters time and make it easier to find sits that match their specific needs.Overall, TrustedHousesitters has been a fantastic tool for fostering connections between sitters and homeowners. With a few updates to its search and listing features, it could become even more seamless and accommodating for all users. title: Trusted housesitters is effective enough
text: Trusted housesitters is effective at arranging a housesit. It works well and connects people effectively. The app is a bit clunky to load when messaging, I prefer to move to whatsapp or sms messaging.I'm a technical person so I have some ideas to improve: There are tiny details that are not prompted in the process that think would be fair enough to include for reasonable preparedness. eg The Welcome Pack document isnt required for hosts to provide, but as a sitter, you don't know if they have prepared one or not- if there isnt one prepared for you, you only find out after the sit is accepted, so you have to factor in more time to discuss the care details like medicines, routine times, walk duration / activity levels, pet aggression triggers. These important details are good to capture in a "welcome pack", it is unfortunate when its not provided for and you are left find out over the stay. It would be useful to have a little icon or something to indicate there is a welcome pack prepared before applying for sits.On the topic of Welcome pack, it would be cool if sitters could submit addition suggestions to the host's version of the welcome pack - or comments to each section for example... in case there are tweaks or ... different... experiences than those described in the document.There are other things I would like to see further refined, like getting sit information to include details like arrival times (eg morning, midday, afternoon, evening, or, even more specific!) to capture those important details up-front before applying (eg. for the case where someone has a flight to catch and they want to hand over keys in person, but as a sitter have a big distance to travel and its tough to get there in time to meet their exit time). These details are able to be discussed during the initial call, but is pertinent and reasonable information know before applying (when browsing & applying for sits) for logistics planning. If these details are displayed on a listed sit, it allows a sitter to discuss it fairly, having thought about it beforehand. It can be tricky (or surprising eg if you actually have to travel down a day earlier and add a day at the end) as you try to fit in after the application is made and everything else is arranged well.

title: TrustedHouseSitters will not help you, if you encounter a bad pet/house owner.
text: Warning to others - be very wary of TrustedHouseSitters as a company. We have found they can not be relied upon to act ethically or meet their obligations, if you are unfortunate enough to encounter a bad host who has lied on their listing & treated a sitter badly.TrustedHouseSitters agreed the host (house/pet owner) had broken guidelines, misled & caused harm.They repeatedly assured us of their support during extensive investigations into a bad host (who has misled, clearly lied, been libelous, had a dangerous & unhealthy home, had undeclared internal security cameras, and a pet with serious untreated conditions).TrustedhouseSitters assured us we were following correct procedure from day one (speaking to them from the sit, regarding the condition of the pet & house). They agreed with us the pet/house owner was in the wrong, and they assured us of their support.We put many weeks of work into providing extensive accounts and evidence.The pet owner continued to act entirely unreasonably, making clearly false, unsubstantiated & bizarre accusations (such as fabricating that there were arguments, that we had our family come to stay, and that we blackmailed them).In the end, TrustedhouseSitters only removed the Host (pet/house owner's listing), to protect themselves as a company & other members.For us as the sitters, they have done nothing to help at all, only adding to the harm done.Trusted House sitters have taken our money anyway, and made an unfortunate and harmful experience worse for us.  Our otherwise excellent profile & reviews are now damaged and cannot be used. Until that point we had enjoyed it and had great hosts, and having to leave THS by finding sits independently has changed the course of our lives.I recommend taking extreme caution with choice of pet/house owners, to find alternatives to TrustedhouseSitters, or to at least be aware of the harm that may be caused by the unreliability of this company.To THS:The pet owner has demonstrably misled with their listing details, and since THS advised to end the sit early, and the host agreed, they turned particularly vindictive & malicious, and have clearly lied and been libelous in a review (left in the last hours of the 2 week window) damaging our profile beyond use.The THS individual looking after our case is stubbornly refusing to remove it, with a 'process only' attitude from the individual working on our case, ignoring the wider perspective and circumstances of the case.Whilst Airbnb have a policy to almost never remove even ridiculous and highly unreasonable reviews. TrustedHouseSitters is not Airbnb.Read our case file. Be professional, act reasonably, use initiative - make decisions at your discretion to ensure the ethical course of action is taken.Consider all the facts of the case, be confident that you can defend your decision making, as the professional and right thing to do.Adding to what we have been though by making us do all this work, then not helping us at all, is simply wrong.Please - re-open the case and do the right thing.

name: Janine M
title: Sitters not valued enough
text: I have been a pet sitter for a year and has not been a great experience for me. I didn’t start too well, I was sitting a house and dog, when I arrived the owner was about to leave. The house was in such a mess, the owner had a party the night before and no time to tidy up. I felt I was commited and didn’t want to let anyone down and of course my thoughts were with the dog.My next sit was a 4 hours drive from where I live a beautiful house and adorable dog. The owners went abroad for 4 nights. I was sending pictures on our walks of their dog for reassurance. The one night I want to bed early, 9:30pm, the next day I saw that I had so many messages, about 6 missed calls. I obviously contacted them as soon as I woke up but did put a bit of a bad taste in my mouth that the owners were so neurotic. I did get a good review.My last sit, not by design as I will explain later, was for 3 weeks. Two cats and then I was given a photo gallery of around 60 plants with instructions for watering. I am not green fingered but I did my best looking after this plants. The water process took an hour at a time and twice a week. When the owners returned, they could see the cats were well looked after but apparently I had killed one of the plants. They then would not leave me a review, I had given 3 weeks of my life to look after the cats for no financial rewards but do expect a review as it helps secure other sits. THS said that there is a 2 week cut off for reviews so they could not do anything.I have tried to get sits after this experience but was very angry. I set up favourites on my account but whenever I get notifications they have already in reviewing mode. I have tried to resolve this with THS but nothing has come of it.I have not renewed my membership, I didn’t feel valued from the owners I house and pet sitted for. The process actually costs me money, I have to pay a subscription and travel to the house. Although it is rewarding to bond with the pets I do not think the owners give the sitters enough credit. Perhaps they feel they too have paid for a subscription and deserve a service.

name: Abdulkadir Tolola
title: to improve trustedhosuesitters
text: by Improve Matching Algorithms: Developing a more personalized and accurate matching system would help pet owners and sitters find the best fit based on location, pet type, experience level, and availability. This could reduce mismatches and improve user satisfaction.Encourage Transparent, Detailed Reviews: A two-way review system (where both sitters and pet owners can review each other) with an emphasis on specific feedback—such as cleanliness, pet care, and communication—could provide more transparency. Encouraging users to leave detailed, balanced reviews can help future users make better choices.Offer Additional Support and Mediation: In case of issues, having a dedicated support team available to mediate between sitters and pet owners can be reassuring. This could include 24/7 support or a hotline for emergencies.Provide Insurance Options: Offering optional insurance or enhancing existing policies to cover accidents, damages, or cancellations could protect both parties, building trust and helping users feel more secure.Develop Comprehensive Pet Care Resources: Providing sitters with resources and training materials on pet care, especially for popular or exotic pets, could improve the quality of care. Sitters could complete online certifications to increase their profile credibility and gain additional trust from pet owners.Expand Community Engagement: Creating forums or online groups where sitters and pet owners can share experiences, advice, and recommendations can foster a stronger community and increase user loyalty. TrustedHousesitters could also host virtual or in-person events to connect users.Enhance the Mobile Experience: Many users rely on mobile access, so optimizing the mobile app with features like instant messaging, video calls, and easy access to user profiles can make the platform more accessible and convenient.Provide Flexible Membership Plans: Offering tiered membership options based on service levels or frequency of use (e.g., for occasional or frequent travelers) could attract a wider range of users.Highlight Top Sitters with Verified Badges: Creating a “top sitters” feature where highly rated, experienced sitters receive special recognition on their profiles can help owners feel more comfortable when choosing sitters.By focusing on trust, safety, and user engagement, TrustedHousesitters can create a more dependable, community-focused platform that better serves the needs of both pet owners and sitters.

name: Devon
title: I do not like using THS at all
text: I do not like using THS at all. The expectations of care levels for pets, especially dogs, and for household chores, should be a paid gig for caregivers. This is not a good deal. Unless of course you have nothing required of you all day, like retired people, or you’re the pet owner. But even for vacationers, this is not a good deal, especially single/solo travelers, it could work for couples. Often you can’t leave the dogs for more than 4-6 hours which means your vacationing time of exploration is limited and often it’s much like a job. You’re required to wake up at certain times, feed/refill food/water 2-3x/day, you must walk some dogs up to 3 x a day for 45 minutes, you’re supposed to sweep the whole house, vacuum, get the mail daily, skim the pool of leaves, pick up dog poo every time (which can be a lot of poo all day), put it in the trash, make sure the trash and recycle goes out on the street for city pickup, I mean seriously, this is not vacation for free! And as a person who was studying my doctorate online full time, all these responsibilities were just over the top for me. I will not be using this service again unless I’m desperate. If you want dog care that provides all requirements for dog care, pay your caregivers/house sitters, especially since I paid $150 up front to use THS. I always used to get paid for both in the past. I will use Rover and get paid for my time with dogs. If this was actually just house sitting like the name says, it’d probably feel more like an equal exchange. I suggest you be a person who has a lot of energy and feels like their days are long. I definitely find it more worth it to pay for hotels/Airbnb.

text: One of my dogs has IMHA disease and for that reason cannot get vaccinated to prevent any chance of relapse. text: Majority of users constitute a certain entitled demographic of microaggresors that have perfected the facade of being friendly & accommodating but treat sitters as lesser than. If a home has consistent 5 stars for cleanliness, I will go in having high expectations. I had a bit of culture shock seeing how many people don't maintain their home. But also not so surprising for a group of people that normalize wearing shoes indoors.Also customer service seems like a headache, as voiced by many users. Congratulations for the B Corp Certification - I am now aware of the low standards that company has.The automated reply really shows the extent of their customer service.

title: Great Experience and Grateful for the Site
text: I have been using THS for a long time and I am very grateful for the opportunities it has provided me. It is a wonderful service when people use it as intended and understand its purpose, which I am not sure all truly do. The most important thing to know about this site, as with any other housesitting site, is that it is strictly a matching platform.They are not personally vouching for any of the sitters on the site, though their identities are verified, and US sitters have a background check. Anyone can join as a host.They really can't do much about some of the more common problems people will complain about, like a dirty home or cancellations on either end. I think they do their best to remove problem sitters and hosts and will investigate complaints, but at the end of the day, their role is limited. They are not party to any of the agreements made between the hosts and sitters.Both sitters and hosts need to do their best to vet each other, and take full responsibility for their decision to enter into these agreements.In the decade I have been sitting, my experience has been very positive and I believe this is the case for most people who use the site on both ends.But there is risk in everything, and it is important for people to understand what the site can and cannot do for them. I think it is important to read their terms and conditions, which spell it all out pretty clearly.

They said if the sitter turned up at our house even after cancelling the sit, they'd advise contacting the local police.In the end, the sit was cancelled by the sitter after a few hours of back and forth. title: Pros and cons
text: Don't be fooled by these faux polite responses from Trusted Housesitters below your reviews; TH is rife with double -standards,  and TH customer service  are the nastiest and the rudest people who ever drew breath. I'm not the only one who's experienced this.I ended my time on this website as Homeowner (HO) and sitter, with 47 perfect reviews over 4 years. Here's the truth:-It is actually illegal to go to another country to petsit even though there's no pay. It's considered work and you can get denied entry if found out.-You will meet some truly wonderful HOs and sitters if you are lucky. If your luck runs out, you'll realise that...-TH only cares for the HOs, who are allowed to do and say anything they want to the sitters. Do not expect support from TH if you run into difficulty.-TH consistently acts against their own terms of service, which carry no actual weight as TH lacks integrity.-HOs can cancel a sit spontaneously. Sitters can cancel after contacting and being sternly rebuked by Customer Service.-HOs  illegally have visual and audible surveillance of sitters without their knowledge, and this is allowed and supported by TH (regardless of how Terms of service reads).-HOs can and do impose exploitative and abusive demands during the sit and if a sitter refuses, and customer service will always support the sitter. HOs can be incredibly entitled.-HOs are actually allowed to charge you money to stay at their homes even though you're taking care of their pets. Read enough postings and you'll find HOs asking for money. Report this to TH and you'll see that this is accurate.-Sitters constantly and consistently overservice Homeowners and tolerate HO's abuses without reporting it to TH or in reviews.But don't take my word for it. Try them out, and see for yourself .  They're the equivalent of a free-for-all dating service with abhorrent business practices.One last thing: please do not ever let yourself be dependent on TH for sitters,  housing or support. When you come across a truly vile situation with sitters  HOs  or TH customer service, have money set aside for a sitter or a hotel, and be prepared to leave the company.All the best to you!

title: Win/Win for Everyone!
text: We’ve had one experience with TrustedHousesitters.com and it has been very positive. It does take a measure of trust and I was really nervous about it and probably wouldn’t have done it had it not been an emergency. We were going to be gone for five weeks and had a dog sitter lined up, who backed out at the last minute. No one else was available, and this was really our only option. But it turned out great, win-win for both us and the housesitter. We get a free, background checked house sitter and they get a free place to stay. The person we selected has been absolutely wonderful, so wonderful in fact we’ve asked her back for another short trip we’re taking in November.  I really appreciated being able to read profiles, invite people to apply, and interview over FaceTime so that we were comfortable with them and they were comfortable with us. We will definitely be looking for another house sitter from TrustedHousesitters.com in February for another long break.

I contacted support and had this corrected. I then checked my credit statement 2 days later and noticed another new "agent fee" for $10.39. name: Diane M. Leggio II
title: Our Honeymoon in St Lucia
text: We traveled & stayed from Nov 17 thru Nov 25, 2019.  We went to The Hideaway at the Royalton St Lucia.  This was our honeymoon.  It all started when I originally booked our honeymoon to Punta Cana back at the beginning of May of 2019 and then the news hit over and over again with all of the issues/deaths in Punta Cana.  Then the headache began!  Of course I then had no interest in going to Punta Cana for fear of our safety.  In hopes of not losing any deposits already made, I embarked on a very long journey to find an adequate substitute.  Adult only honeymoon by the beach with ocean view and luxury accommodations.  St Lucia’s Hideaway at Royalton was our only option that we wanted to consider after looking at every option on bookit .com and I mean every option which took me weeks to research & decide.  Then the next journey was even getting someone on the phone to see what my options were in cancelling Punta Cana and going to St Lucia.  Can’t tell you how many phone calls with hour wait times and then not being able to speak to an Airline agent who are only available during the week, didn't know that, and at one point they were so inundated with calls because EVERYONE wanted out of their Punta Cana trip, they finally had to add an automated message where you then had to go on their website and put in for an appointment for a phone call which then gave you a 3 hour window I believe it was.  So my phone call was on a Friday from like 2-5pm.  The Airline people  close at 5pm.  They called me at 4:45pm.  I finally got everything switched over to St Lucia, the trip was $1,000 more than the Punta Cana trip, my choice of course, then a $200 per person fee the Airline charges to change your flights.  Yikes!  Well it is what it is as I was no way going to Punta Cana.  Then as soon as we hung up, I saw my new itinerary which was incorrect!  UGH!  I was in tears.  The agent changed the dates of my trip which had us arriving 1 day later.  I had to go back on the website to make another appointment.  I was so upset thinking I will have to pay another airline fee for another change.  There was never any discussion of changing of my dates.  Luckily Corporate saw my appointment request with comments that they messed up on my dates so they called me the next day, Saturday and got that all fixed finally – this was June 21st!  Thank heaven!  I will say everyone I ever talked to was very nice!  By this time I am spent with getting this all changed/fixed for like the past 6 weeks and being in the middle of planning a wedding AND a honeymoon.  For the next four weeks, out of curiosity I priced out the same exact trip, and it kept coming up $1,000 cheaper.  So of course I am furious that Bookit.com took advantage of everyone changing their trips to get out of Punta Cana.  They absolutely would not do a price adjustment!  Lastly, luckily, I was on their website in October and noticed I had an alert that my flights changed.  They eliminated my connecting flight from Miami to Vegas that Monday so we had to spend the night in Miami and catch the 1st flight to Vegas Tuesday Morning.  So not only did I have to spend money on a hotel room for the night in Miami, but my husband and I also had to take an extra day off work, without pay, as we both planned on being back to work Tuesday.  So not only was the new honeymoon $1,000 + $400 more, add on top of that a hotel stay, food, and losing a day of work!  All in all, I will never use Bookit.com again!

Once the agent found us a resort she informed us of the $25 pp change fee and made the alterations for us (which was on a Sunday) and sent the updates via email. Monday I review the email and find that the new resort she booked us at was in Runaway Bay and not Negril (where the rest of our party was staying) I contacted customer services  and explained to them our request which was a different resort that was Adults only and in Negril and all inclusive deal was to remain(which we previously had)  and was told they would review the call and we should contact them within 24 hours. Called back Wednesday and was told they have not completed the review so they will contact us within 24 hours. 24 hours went pass and I Did not hear back so Friday we contacted them and they had review the call in questioned and they did apologize and the lady stated to me that “we are human it was a human error” however Friday night the gentleman we spoke to to rebook us rebooked us but now the room type I had originally was not available so he agreed to credit me $50 (what is that??) and now I am paying almost an extra $1,000 for their mistake.  Since Friday I have reached out numerous of times including sending 3 emails to someone who has not replied back to me to this day. I have inquired numerous of times about how my taxes and Service fees went from $65 to more than $421 for the same trip same hotel just a revision of the reservation. I have had two people tell me they (bookit) don’t charge services fees and one agent told me to send her what I see and after being put on hold for almost 20 mins as she finds an email I can send it to she came back and said that is the taxes the hotel is charging so I asked her if my room rate increased almost $400 how can anyone charge  more than 100% in taxes (no matter what country this is)? She had no answer but stated she will send me my agreement via email and she apologize and ended the call.*Please note that email was never received either!I leave in 8 days and so far (because of human error) I am paying an extra $1,000 was give a $50 refund (yes ONLY $50, was not even offer future credit at least) I also was given an apology and basically my taxes and service fees (keep in mind a service fee they say they do not charge) went for almost $65 to more than $421.This trip is suppose to be a celebration for my Sister’s 50th day and my daughters 30th bday and it is a complete nightmare!I have cried so much now I have to come up with almost an extra $1,000 for their (bookit) error or loss funds we have paid into it if I cancel.In addition to the email from the agent I am also still waiting for feedback from the operations supervisor in which I have emailed numerous of times and called and so far no one can at least tell me why I am paying an extra $350 in services fees when other individuals travel with my group services fees and taxes is only approximately $55-$65 and I also must add the other individuals travel with me is staying at the same hotel and same room type!!!I feel like I have been scammed and no one can help us!!!

title: We had never used BookIT.com until this…
text: We had never used BookIT.com until this trip.  We chose an all inclusive and paid for r/t transportation.  We landed in Puerta Vallarta and were met promptly by our transportation guide.  He shared with us that "Martina" would be our contact at our resort and we needed to meet with her to set up our return transportation.  No problem, he assured us she would be at resort when we arrived.  As we were driving to resort, she actually called the driver and asked to speak to me and told me that she in fact wouldn't be at resort today (Saturday) but would be there at 1130 on Sunday to meet us and assist us with any excursions or anything we may need.  Fast forward to Sunday.  We were enjoying our day at the pool and went to the lobby at about 1210 and Martina was no where to be found; another representative from another excursion company asked what we needed and we explained we were looking for Martina and she informed us that Martina 'had been there but had already left"  Really??? she was there all of 30 min?? Not to mention that she did not tell me when she spoke to me that she was only going to be at the resort for a few minutes. So not only did we still not have return transportation, but we missed out on any type of discounts for any excursions we may have wanted to do.  We expected a phone call from her to confirm our round trip transportation and it never happened.  We kept checking throughout the day and into Monday and never saw her or heard from her.  We had the desk clerk try and call her cell phone on Monday with no success.  Finally on Tuesday we asked the concierge to try and call again and she was able to get through to her and I finally was able to talk to Martina; she confirmed our transportation was set for Wed and that we needed to be in the lobby for pick up at 1129 am;  we were not picked up until 1150 am and there was no phone call telling us they were going to be late.  When they finally did arrive, they had no identification and the guy came to the resort and spoke to the bell man, and then still had to call a taxi for us.  Granted we did not have to pay for it, but it was stressful waiting and worrying if they were going to pick us up!  We were very disappointed in the return trip and trying to deal with "Martina";  so we would give her a very low score; however, the beginning of the trip, transportation from the airport to the resort was perfect and went off as expected.

text: UPDATE: a week passed.  Despite the response to this review, nobody contacted me, and to reach BookIt customer service, you have to stay on hold up to an hour. However, it's impossible to find out where the overcharge was, since in the package they do not give you details, just total (beware!)When I called to clarify, the agent was totally unprofessional.  She was trying to get rid of me, gave me multiple explanations, one contradicting the other, demonstrating how annoyed she was. Finally I requested to speak to a supervisor.  After a long hold I still didn't get the supervisor on the line, but the agent became more patient. It turned out that there were taxes included that I wasn't told about (ok, a few dollars - it didn't change the picture). She finally promised that they would review my phone conversation with the agent who was amending my reservation, so now I'm to call back in 24 hrs. text: When i first booked with a travel agent, he was the nicest person ever. His name was Rajay to be exact. He answered every question I had and reassured me that I was getting the best deal out there. One of the things I love about bookit is that it gives you the option to pay in increments, known as pay delay. I had 7 payments total. The destination i was traveling to was Dominican Republic. Unfortunately, unforeseen events happened as the months went by that caused myself and the other 3 ladies i was traveling with to become very weary of DR. Bookit didn’t seem to care about those events and insisted on that we had to keep our booking or else be charged a “change fee” of $500. I understand every company has a policy that has to be followed but in such circumstances, I feel as if when it comes to life and death situations the rules should be bendable. I explained to bookit that due to the recent events in the DR, that I am considering switching locations. Bookit didn’t seem to be phased by what I was saying and didn’t make it easy to switch destinations. Bookit basically gave me threeoptions: cancel and be charged a cancellation fee, change destinations and be charged a change fee or the worst, keep my reservations and risk my life. I felt defeated. Stuck. Helpless. It was until I waited two days to call back in and spoke with a very helpful young man who goes by the name of David. David wanted to help out any way that he could. David did not argue with me. He did not over-talk me nor did he seem aggravated with my rants. To make a long story short, David possibly saved not just my life, but my three other friends lives as well. David was able to switch our destination, and apply the difference in locations to the “change fee”. David is the ONLY reason Bookit gets three stars. If the second agent AND supervisor that I spoke to would have done their job like David did, maybe I wouldn’t of had a panic attack after all. So to Rajay who helped book the flight and to David who helped change the flight, you both ROCK!!!! Bookit does not deserve representatives like you both!!!! You both went above and beyond!!! And for that I humbly say THANK YOU!!!

Not to mention that my first phone call with Book It was an hour and a half long and I was on hold for 30 minutes straight at one point. Good thing I have patience, I think they were just waiting for me to hang up. So now, it is June 20th, FIFTEEN DAYS LATER, and Book It has not reached back out to us like they said they would.The employees and supervisors at BOOK IT have proved to be unethical and unprofessional. Unethical as they lied and said we could not cancel and get a full refund but then a few moments later admitted that we can. Then they said we just have to have Hard Rock approve of the cancellation. Hard Rock tried to help us because they said that if we did it through them, that they themselves would have easily canceled and refunded us… however BOOK IT is the only one that is able to. Therefore, BOOK IT has lied to us twice, proving to be an unethical and unprincipled business. Not only that, we started this entire process 15 days ago. It should not take 15 days to uphold on your word that your own employees and supervisors told us, which is that we are able to get the cancellation and full refund. text: I recently booked a trip to Jamaica with BookIt.com. The service provided was professional and all my questions were answered. My trip went smoothly until my confirmation of my return transportation from the resort to the airport. I booked roundtrip transportation with Bookit. The transportation company used is Island Routes. We selected the shared transportation. The night before my departure I called the front desk at my resort to find out if a representative for Island Routes was onsite. I was told that they had left for the day but we be back the next day at 8:30am. The next day I was at the Island Routes desk at 8:30am no representative at the desk. After waiting 15 min I left and came back a hour later still no one at the desk. So I called the Island Routes representative MALIKA direct number the day of my departure and spoke with her. She asked me a few questions and I informed her that I was at her desk waiting on her to just confirm my departure. She hung up on me! I called her right back, no answer. Finally she comes to the desk with a NASTY ATTITUDE!! She was beyond RUDE! Going on and on about how people blame her for things and that she called me back which was a lie! I told her i wasn't blaming her for anything and that all i wanted was conformation that i had transportation to the airport. I think her whole problem was that i didn't come to the Welcome Briefing Information my day after arrival. I'm on vacation! I'm not interested in attending some sales pitch. She was a terrible representative for Island Routes!

text: If I Could a Give Vayama ZERO Stars .... like many of you, my Int’l flights were Ultimately cancelled by the airline because of Covid.  Prior to my scheduled departure date, I had been calling and emailing Vayama and they just weren’t answering or responding.  So I called the airline and was (correctly) told that Vayama was the only one who could make changes or get a refund.  Vayama NEVER contacted me, they NEVER contacted the airline for my refund, and flat out LIED in response to my Better Business Bureau complaint.  Luckily, I purchased the tickets on a credit Card and contested it with the bank.  Vayama lied to the bank as well, saying that it was MY DUTY to contact the airline.My advice to you, 1). Don’t be tempted next time to buy through an outside of the USA virtual travel agency, just to save +/- $100,  2).  If you do, make sure you keep a transaction contact log including conversations, dates, times, and names.  3).  For your protection, and to retain your dispute rights, ALWAYS use a credit card, NEVER a debit card.    4).  Keep copies of all emails, save copies of screen shots.  Vayama underhandedly disabled the “send copy of email to myself” feature from their website, so unless you save a screen shot, you have no record and they will NEVER respond.In short, buy the ticket directly from the airline, or from a more reliable travel agent that is based here in the USA and who will actually answer the phone when you get stranded someplace, or if you need follow-up with your booking.

name: David Michael Mullins
title: Vayama: "Still Waiting!"
text: On April 5th, 2020, I received an email from Vayama notifying me that Aeroflot had cancelled my r/t flight from Los Angeles to Moscow. Since this was an involuntary cancellation and Aeroflot had suspended all flights from LAX, I was due a refund. Vayama instructed me to do nothing and not to contact them as they would be the ones initiating the refund request. However, 1 month later, I still had not received my refund so I sent Vayama an email asking why. Immediately, I received the same impersonal automated reply telling me to do nothing and that it may be weeks before I received a refund. The Department of Transportation rules for all airlines flying in or out of the United States in regards to tickets purchased by credit card, is very clear and that all travel agencies or airline ticket agents must refund the full amount of the ticket price, including any associated add-on fees within 7 days. Since the COVID-19 Pandemic, the DOP has publicly further clarified that those rules are still in effect and that neither the airline nor the travel agent may modify this. I spoke with Aeroflot's main office in Moscow who told me that Vayama must initiate the refund request since my purchase was done through Vayama. They also gave me a direct contact to an Aeroflot rep in Los Angeles who told me they have no record of Vayama ever initiating that refund request. Therefore she was unable to process my refund and could only offer me a travel certificate good for future travel on Aeroflot which I declined. She encouraged me to contact Vayama again to request my refund. The Aeroflot rep also told me that is a very simple process on the part of Vayama and that it only takes a few seconds to make the request. To date, I have not received a response from Vayama nor has my credit card been debited with the refund. Due to the circumstances arising from the pandemic, I have been patient and understanding but 6 weeks and counting is a lot more than 1 week. I am very disappointed at Vayama's lack of service to me especially since I even purchased their optional "service" package.

text: I always take things with a grain of salt and try to look into the positives of everything but I cannot find a single one with Vayama, unfortunately.It's a trying time with the uncertainty of Covid-19, and I get that. I didn't mind waiting on the phone for Air Canada's customer service for 2 hours, but at least they were able address my concerns and rebook me on a flight to Ho Chi Minh City from Portland, OR by way of Tokyo, Japan free of charge in accordance with their goodwill policy.When I had contacted Vayama's customer service to change my sisters flight to the same one I just rebooked with Air Canada to ensure my sister wouldn't have to travel alone. The Vayama customer service representative had stated that because there is no flight serviced by Air Canada from Tokyo to Ho Chi Minh City, we cannot rebook your flight. I get it, you're a travel agency which may limit what access you have in rebooking flights from different airlines, so I asked if the Vayama customer service representative would be able to find an Air Canada flight from Tokyo to Ho Chi Minh around the travel dates I laid out. The customer service representative said no there are not.So I reconfirmed that the two options Vayama would best support their customers with is to cancel a non-refundable ticket, wait to see if the flight gets cancelled in order to receive a refund or travel to South Korea, in which the United States CDC and State Department has a level 3 warning for (avoid all non-essential travel), she said yes and that has left me hopeless in Vayama's ability to support their customers in a trying time such as the Covid-19 outbreak.I express high disappointment with Vayama, and believe this may be my last time utilizing their service. It just bewilders me that in accordance to their goodwill policy that Air Canada is able to re-accommodate, while Vayama cannot honor such policy laid out by the airline through unforeseen circumstances.I hope whoever may be reading this reconsiders the next time they book through Vayama to hope for the best but prepare for the worst.

title: Vayama is a poorly managed company.
text: Vayama is a poorly managed company. I have to say that the customer service agents I spoke with were kind and needed some prodding at times, but were still helpful. However, the way that Vayama operates as a system results in a very poor customer service experience. They were great with the initial booking. I got the ticket number soon after I booked and was able to see the ticket on the airline's website. However, if you need any assistance after that, good luck! They advertise 24/7 customer service, but it appears that they cannot live up to that promise. Due to the Coronavirus outbreak, the CDC is advising against non-essential travel, and I have to cancel my flight. My doctor also wrote a formal letter advising against travel to this particular country. According to the Vayama website, you have to request a cancellation "quote" before you can cancel, and you are told to wait 2 days for a response via email. I have already requested a cancellation quote 3 times, and it has been 6-7 days. No response. I tried calling them 4 days ago, and I was placed on hold with a machine that kept repeating: "Due to circumstances, the waiting time is longer than usual. Currently, we are experiencing a higher call volume." No estimated wait time; no offer for a call back.After 30 minutes on hold, I did get to speak with someone, and he said that I can request to cancel up until 48 hours of departure. He recommended that I wait to cancel, as the airline could offer a full refund for this particular flight in a few days.After a couple of days, I got a response from Vayama through Trustpilot (not via email or phone) saying that I could request to cancel 1 week ahead of departure (note the discrepancy between what I was told earlier).Well, the 1 week deadline is coming up soon, and I will be very busy in the next few days, so I called them again today. I used two phones in case they hung up on me. After about 56 minutes, they finally answered one of the phones. The other phone they just hung up on after 1 hour, saying they would call me back (no call back received as of this time, it's been more than 5 hours since the call was initiated). In either case, because they answered the first phone, I was able to speak with an agent. He said he could cancel my ticket, but I would have to pay Vayama 100 dollars (extra payment needs to be made before they cancel)  and pay the airline cancellation fee, even though the airline website states that any refunds for flights from the US to all Asian destinations can be requested from the travel agency (screen shot sent via email to Vayama per their request). He said I could call the airline and ask them to place a note in my reservation to waive the cancellation fee, but why wouldn't Vayama (my "travel agency") make contact with the airline themselves? What use are they as a travel agency if I have to do everything myself? He said that they could reach out to the airline, but I would have to wait at least 5-6 hours and up to a 2 days for a response by email. But they had already ignored my email cancellation requests for 1 week. How can I trust that they will get back to me before the 1 week deadline to cancel? Also, I don't have all day to just sit around on the phone with them. I have to work and earn money so I can pay my "travel agency" to do this stuff for me. By the way, I did ask to speak with a supervisor but was refused.The administration of this company really needs to change their protocols. It seems like they are expecting their customer service agents to perform super human feats. They need to provide them the resources they need to communicate and reach out to the airlines so that they can take care of customers ethically and in a timely fashion. Charging customers for cancelling a flight to a region that the government and a person's own physician has advised against traveling to leaves a very bad image of the company.

title: Don't Trust the 5 Star Reviews and Check BBB Before Using Vayama!
text: Update 1.25.20As per Vayama's request in the response to this review, I've provided our booking reference number.UPDATE 1/14/20: Vayama has written to us by email saying that our tickets have been cancelled (we already knew that they were cancelled on December 18th) and that it can take up to 4 weeks for Cathay to refund the money. Previously Vayama said 10-14 business days. I get the sense that everything they say is arbitrary. Cathay has already told me that they will release the funds as soon as they get confirmation from Vayama. It's a circus!ORIGINAL POSTWe are currently involved in a two and a half month process of cancelling our tickets with Vayama. Back on November 4th, 2019 we called Vayama to cancel our flights when the times had been changed.We've gone through the same nightmare that many other reviewers have written. Vayama agreed to cancel the tickets that same day without any fees and said we should expect a confirmation in 24 hours. (If you ever speak to a Vayama representative and they tell you that you'll hear back from them in 24 hours that is the moment you will have officially entered the black hole of dealing with this business).We waited two days and called again. The new representative said they wouldn't honor the cancellation. When I mentioned that Vayama had already agreed, she said a manager would have to listen to the original phone call and get back to me in 24 hours. No response. I waited a few more days. Called again. This time the representative I spoke to insisted that I need to call Cathay Pacific directly to make sure they are willing to offer the full refund. That seemed easy enough so I called Cathay Pacific. What a breath of fresh air to speak to a professional, thoughtful call agent. Cathay confirmed that they will refund the ticket, no questions asked.I called Vayama again. The representative (who called herself a floor manager) told me that no one at Vayama can make an outgoing phone call to Cathay Pacific to cancel the tickets. She demanded that I collect a written permission from Cathay to prove to Vayama that the tickets would be refunded. At this point I'm feeling like I'm the travel agent! I call Cathay again and receive some commiseration from them at the ridiculous hoops I'm being made to jump through. This Cathay representative tells me that she speaks to Vayama people a few times a day. She can't imagine why they won't call to cancel these tickets. It would literally take a matter of moments. She puts a note in my file saying that the tickets will be cancelled once Vayama confirms the cancellation.I call Vayama again (we're already about 5 weeks into the process) but the next representative says that although they can see the note in my file, they actually need an email from Cathay. He again confirmed that Vayama simply can't call Cathay themselves. I call Cathay once more (really feeling bad for wasting their time at this point) and ask for an email. This is just not something they do. She has given Vayama everything they need to proceed with the cancellation. All they need to do is call.I finally figure out that people have had similar nightmares when I find the BBB complaints of Vayama. I currently have an open case with Vayama. This is literally the only way to get them to do anything.Very quickly after posting my BBB complaint a Vayama representative called me to confirm that I'd like to cancel my tickets. Oh boy. Yes, I would, please. I am told to wait 24 hours for a cancellation confirmation and my heart sinks. Amazingly I DO receive a confirmation. The tickets are officially gone.That was December 18th. Refunds can take awhile to process so we check occasionally and don't worry too much. On January 8th it feels like it's been too long, so I call Cathay again (I'll do anything to not speak to Vayama). Cathay confirms that the tickets have been cancelled on their end and they are waiting to get confirmation from Vayama to release the funds. They've been waiting since December 19th!I continue to write to Vayama on my open case with the BBB. No response.We continue to pay interest on our credit card purchase for these tickets.What is the benefit to Vayama for putting their customers through ordeals like this? I really can't figure it out.

Ultimately, we secured a new ticket, and she travelled on August 9th, missing her son’s wedding due to the two-day delay.This experience has been incredibly disappointing and has caused undue stress and emotional distress to our family. The lack of communication and the unprofessional handling of the situation by BudgetAir is unacceptable.I request a formal apology and compensation for the inconvenience and additional expenses incurred due to these changes.I hope BudgetAir will take this complaint seriously and improve its customer service to prevent such issues in the future.

title: No Customer Service When Anything Goes Wrong
text: I've been booking travel for my family for over ten years and used dozens of online travel agencies as well as booked directly with airlines. Budgetair is one of those companies where if you buy from them, you should expect absolutely zero customer service if anything goes wrong. If nothing goes wrong and you fly your original itinerary exactly as booked, you'll be just fine and might save some money. But as soon as something happens, even if it is out of your control like an airline schedule change, you will be completely left alone with no means to reach them, and in my case without a ticket even after paying them the full amount of the ticket. In my case, I booked a roundtrip and the airline changed the schedule of my return flight. Budgetair could not issue me a new ticket with the new itinerary for well over two weeks. While I was on my vacation, I had to use the silly online chat (they do not have a phone number) to contact them every day. The chat agents sounded like robots every time and would simply repeat the same thing over and over, telling me to keep waiting and be patient. When it was getting closer to my departure date, I got impatient and started asking them exactly when I can hear any update, they replied "in under 24 hours" a total of three times, but I never heard back any of these times. It is very weird to me how the chat agents cannot do anything and just keep saying they have "sent the request to the relevant team" but they cannot tell me what the problem was or why they were unable to issue the ticket. When asked how much longer I needed to wait (this was probably the 20th time I contacted them for this issue), one of the agents even said that the "team cannot provide a timeline" when it was 72 hours from my scheduled departure. Ridiculous. In the end I got in touch with the airline myself and begged the airline representative to take over the booking so that they can reissue my ticket without going through Budgetair's non-existent "team". Had I not contacted the airline, I would still not have a ticket on the day of my departure and would practically lose over 1000 dollars worth of a ticket and then need to buy a new ticket. I'm very sick of this company now and would probably never use them again. When you book with them you take a risk. If everything goes as planned you'll be fine. But if anything starts going wrong even when it's not your fault, their awful customer service means that you'll be left to your own devices to figure out how to get to your destination.

text: I originally wrote this for their UK website (.co.uk) Trustpilot board however the origination also appears to have a '.com' Trustpilot review board - its the same company and same website hence I thought I'd drop this here as well:*POTENTIAL FRAUD - USE AT YOUR OWN RISK*My dad contacted this organisation to buy tickets to India and was offered an incredibly cheap price with Emirates in comparison to all other travel agents. However multiple attempts to charge 3x different VISA Credit payment cards failed. The organisation appears to be using a money transfer service provider rather than an actual payment processing merchant as I received 3DS (Visa Secure) authorisation requests for 'NEC Money' and 'Remit Choice', both are money transfer providers. A legitimate company will never use a money transfer provider to receive payment and a customer should never receive a 3DS auth request (via mobile banking prompt or OTP - one time passcode sent via SMS/text) hence I question the legitimacy of this company despite their ATOL registration.The travel agent I talked to then attempted to persuade me into making a bank transfer or using a debit card which I respectfully declined. As a payment analyst myself looking after back office IT payment systems - I know better hence I would never use such means. You should only use a credit card when making purchases like this which gives you (the customer/consumer) protection under Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act.Just to add another point.... this organisation does not have a UK contact number (landline) which is another red flag. They use a WhatsApp business account which in itself is not an issue but the absence of a proper contact number does ring alarm bells. Use this company at your own risk.

title: This is a very fraudulent company
text: This is a very fraudulent company. If anyone is seeking to rent an RV, do not go thru the process of renting from RVshare. This company breaks its own rules to make money. I rented a camper in OK in Sept 2024 for 4 days. First of all when I went to pick up this camper, the owner never showed up to do the out paperwork to go over any damage before I rented it. Camper was stored at a public storage facility. I had to call him to find out about how to get in the camper. I checked the lights before pulling it away and the entire right side lights didn't work. No brake lights , no turn signal. I drove it away anyway because I already paid for it and there was no time to find another one. I returned the camper on the return day 4 days later and still the owner was not there to receive the camper so no in paper work was completed like he was supposed to do per rvshare rules. 3 days later I received an email from rvshare stating that owner found nothing wrong with the camper and was releasing my security deposit of $500 back to me and that this transaction was completed. A couple of weeks later I receive an email from rvshare that the owner filed a claim for damages and I was asked by rvshare what kind of damage there was. I didn't know of any damage. The only thing was that my wife found a piece of plastic molding on the floor when we picked it up. That was it. On Oct 10th I received an email from rvshare that they were charging my credit card $398 for damages. I looked at my credit card account and there was a pending charge for that amount. I immediately called a Claims adjuster for rvshare and she explained that was for some sort of damages when i had the camper. I had to pay for insurance when I rented the camper. Company policy. She never did tell me what the $398 was for and I never did revieve any claims paperwork showing what I was paying $398 for. I told her that I was cleared by the owner on Sept 5th and my security deposit was returned. She told me that there could be more charges later. I asked for what and she couldn't tell me. Later that afternoon I received an email from her saying this account has been closed. I called my credit card company and had my card locked and closed in case anymore fraudulent transactions occurred. I will never ever deal with this company again.

title: Disgusting, DO NOT USE.
text: Disgusting, AVOID at all costs as a renter. RV Share have perfected being an excellent scamming tool for RV owners to be able to fix up their broken, falling apart RV's by placing them in the hand of customers and waiting for something to (inevitably) go wrong so they can rinse them for RV repairs. AVOID at all costs, they ignore customers and don't look at any evidence. The RV we rented was run down, taped and zip-tied together, the owner wasn't present and provided old zoomed out photos to RV Share, within minutes of being on the freeway after collection the awning dangerously swung off, we pulled over to find it had only been propped on with one rusted threadless screw, had a number of holes where it had been reattached previously. We spoke to the owner immediately on the platform who was disinterested and told us to just 'screw it back on'. Upon return, we were later charged our entire deposit plus another $600 that they just took from my card without informing me. We sent time stamped photos as they requested, gave the full description of what happened showing all of the issues that the owner didn't disclose (with location and time stamps from collection) as well as the evidence of what had happened when we set off showing all of the holes where it had been screwed back on again previously. They didn't even look at any of it, they will take your money without informing you. Their 'customer service' is non-existaent and Kyla is one of the rudest people I have ever encountered. They did not send a breakdown of what was being claimed for, they did not send any documentation of any of it and just took money from my card. STAY AWAY FROM THIS SCAM AGENCY.
